[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-scholarship-finder-9141) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Ankurshukla18/AI-Scholarship-Finder-) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://ankurshukla18.github.io/AI-Scholarship-Finder-/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/4L7u28ZVXdk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> An scholarship finder platform.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI integration](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI%20integration-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**🎓 The Global Education Funding Crisis**

Every year, millions of students aspire to pursue higher education, yet a significant portion abandons their dreams due to financial constraints. While there are billions of dollars available in scholarships globally, an estimated $100 million in scholarship money goes unclaimed annually. Why? Because the bridge between deserving students and funding bodies is broken.

**🔍 Key Problems Students Face**

Current methods of finding financial aid are outdated and inefficient. Students encounter three major roadblocks:

Information Overload & Fragmentation: Scholarship information is scattered across thousands of disconnected websites, government portals, and private foundations. Searching manually feels like looking for a needle in a haystack.

Complex Eligibility Criteria: Students waste countless hours reading through requirements only to realize they don't qualify. The cognitive load of filtering through GPA requirements, demographic constraints, and essay topics is overwhelming.

The "Awareness Gap": Many students, especially from underprivileged backgrounds, simply don't know that funding exists for their specific profile (e.g., scholarships for specific hobbies, minority groups, or unique skills).

**💡 How ScholarPath Solves It**

ScholarPath revolutionizes this process by replacing manual searching with Intelligent AI Matching. We don't just list scholarships; we curate them.

1. Hyper-Personalized Matching Instead of a generic search bar, ScholarPath acts as a personal counselor. Users input their profile- grades, interests, background, and career goals- and our algorithm instantly filters through thousands of opportunities to present only those where the student has a high probability of success.

2. Time Efficiency & Focus We automate the discovery phase. What used to take weeks of research now takes seconds. This allows students to shift their energy from finding scholarships to winning them- focusing on writing quality essays and preparing strong applications.

3. Democratizing Access By aggregating verified scholarships from diverse sources (government, private, non-profit) into a single, easy-to-use platform, we level the playing field. ScholarPath ensures that financial aid is accessible to everyone, not just those with expensive career counselors.

**🚀 The Impact**

ScholarPath is more than just a search tool; it is a pathway to educational equity. By solving the discovery problem, we help students unlock their future, reduce the burden of student loans, and ensure that talent-not net worth-determines a student's success.

**Challenges we ran into**

**🛠️ How we built it**

We focused on creating a lightweight, fast, and responsive web application.

Frontend: We built the core structure using semantic HTML5 and styled it with custom CSS3 for a modern, responsive look.

Logic: We used JavaScript to handle form interactions and manage the user interface dynamically.

Version Control: We used Git for source control, managing branches to keep our features organized.

Deployment: The site is hosted live on GitHub Pages, ensuring it is accessible to anyone, anywhere, with zero downtime.

**🚧 Challenges we ran into**

The journey wasn't smooth, and we faced several technical hurdles:

Static Hosting Limitations: Since we deployed on GitHub Pages (a static host), we couldn't run server-side code (Node/Python). We had to refactor our form.js to handle validation on the client side instead of trying to hit a backend API, which initially caused server errors.

The "404" Deployment Error: We struggled with directory structures where GitHub couldn't find our index.html. We learned the hard way that file organization is key in production environments.

Responsive Assets: Integrating our custom logo and illustrations required fine-tuning our CSS Flexbox layouts to ensure images didn't break or stretch on mobile devices.

**🏆 Accomplishments that we're proud of**

Successfully Deployed: Moving from local development (localhost) to a live URL that we can share with the world.

Responsive Design: The site looks great on both desktop and mobile, thanks to our careful CSS adjustments.

Problem Solving: We hit a wall with the backend integration but successfully pivoted to a frontend-first approach to deliver a working prototype on time.

### BasePad
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/basepad-885b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/somewherelostt/BasePad) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://basepad.maazx.dev) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20Onchain%20with%20FBI-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://build-onchain-fbi.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Onchain bounty platform with x402 micropayments

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

BasePad solves the trust and payout problems that make traditional freelance platforms painful for both clients and builders.

### For Bounty Creators
- **Lock rewards onchain** instead of trusting a platform, the prize is committed upfront in **USDC on Base**, so there is no way to “ghost” after the work is done.
- **Simple, cheap bounty creation with x402 micropayments**, instead of complex checkout flows, creators pay a tiny **0.001 USDC x402 fee** to create a bounty.
- **Transparent, verifiable activity**, all payments, payouts, and receipts live on Base and can be inspected onchain.

### For Bounty Hunters
- **Instant, trustless payouts**, once a submission is selected, the payout is sent directly to the hunter’s wallet in **USDC on Base**.
- **AI-assisted review of submissions**, **Gemini 2.0** helps filter low-effort submissions so creators can focus on serious entries.
- **Onchain proof-of-work receipts**, hunters can download a neon **“bounty receipt”** that encodes the bounty ID, amount, hunter address, and transaction hash as portable proof of delivery.

### For Onchain Builders & Teams
- **Drop-in x402 demo**, shows how to use **HTTP 402 (Payment Required)** to gate features with onchain micropayments.
- **Better UX than typical Web3 dApps**, Privy embedded wallets remove the “install MetaMask first” friction, and the neo-brutal UI keeps the focus on bounties and payouts.
- **Template for onchain hackathons & micro-grants**, organizers can spin up bounties, collect submissions, and pay out transparently on Base using a familiar web-app flow.

> **In short:** BasePad turns bounty work from  
> “hope the platform or client pays me”  
> into  
> “terms are onchain, payouts are automatic, and everyone can verify what happened.”

**Challenges we ran into**

### A. Getting x402 Payment Verification Truly Trustless

At first, it was tempting to trust the client-side success state from the x402 flow, but that would defeat the purpose of building onchain.

The backend needed to independently verify that:
- The transaction actually happened on **Base Sepolia**
- The **real USDC contract** was called
- The **platform wallet** received at least **0.001 USDC**

The main hurdle was decoding **Transfer** event logs correctly and handling token decimals and edge cases.

**Solution:**
- Fetch the transaction receipt from a **Base Sepolia RPC**
- Use typed log decoding (via **Viem / Ethers**) to parse `Transfer(from, to, amount)`
- Strictly check:
  - `to === platformWallet`
  - `amount >= requiredAmount`
- Only then create the bounty

This transformed the x402 flow from a nice demo into a **fully trustless onchain payment gate**.

---

### B. Making x402 and Embedded Wallet UX Feel Like a Normal Web App

HTTP 402 responses, wallet popups, and onchain confirmations can easily feel clunky.

Early issues included:
- x402 errors surfacing as generic **500 errors** in Next.js route handlers
- Wallet prompts appearing at unexpected times
- No clear distinction between **draft bounty** and **ready-to-pay** state

**Solution:**
- Introduced a **two-step bounty creation flow**:
  1. Collect bounty details
  2. Explicit **“Pay 0.001 USDC via x402”** confirmation
- Normalized the x402 backend response into clean JSON:
  - `status`
  - `requiredAmount`
  - `targetAddress`
- Added clear neo-brutalist UI states:
  - **Awaiting payment**
  - **Verifying onchain**
  - **Bounty live**

This made the payment flow feel **predictable and web-native**, despite doing real onchain verification under the hood.

---

### C. Generating Onchain “Receipts” as Shareable Images

The goal was to give hunters a **downloadable, neon receipt** for every completed bounty.

Challenges:
- `html2canvas` does not play well with SSR and must run client-side
- Heavy neo-brutal styling with dynamic data such as addresses, hashes, and timestamps
- Consistent rendering across devices

**Solution:**
- Isolated the receipt as a `"use client"` React component
- Rendered it into a dedicated DOM node
- Used `html2canvas` with:
  - Fixed background
  - Controlled scale factor for crisp PNG output
- Pre-formatted data:
  - Truncated hashes and addresses
  - Normalized timestamps

**Result:**  
A one-click, onchain-verifiable receipt that hunters can share as **proof of work and payout**.

**Description of your solution**

VeriHub is an AI-powered fact verification platform that helps fight misinformation by checking both text and images in user claims.

For images, the system uses SerpAPI Reverse Image Search to find where an image has appeared before, and EasyOCR to extract any embedded text. This helps detect reused, out-of-context, or misleading visuals.

For text claims, VeriHub verifies information through Google Fact-Check databases, social media posts from verified accounts, and credible news portals.

At the core, Gemini-2.5-Flash analyzes and reasons over all the collected evidence, cross-checking both text and image results to provide a clear verdict: True, False, Misleading, or Unverified.

By combining multiple verification layers with powerful AI, VeriHub makes fact-checking faster, transparent, and trustworthy—helping people trust what they see and share online.

**Misinformation: Create an Agentic AI system that continuously scans multiple sources of information, detects emerging misinformation, verifies facts, and provides easy-to-understand, contextual updates to the public during crises.**

How VeriHub Aligns:

Agentic AI System – VeriHub uses Gemini-2.5-Flash as its reasoning engine, making autonomous decisions on how to gather, cross-check, and verify evidence without manual intervention.

Continuous Multi-Source Scanning – It integrates SerpAPI Reverse Image Search, Google Fact-Check API, social media APIs, and news portals, ensuring constant monitoring of diverse sources.

Detection of Emerging Misinformation – By comparing new claims with historical image usage, verified social media posts, and news reports, it can flag misleading or false narratives early.

Fact Verification – With EasyOCR for text extraction and multi-source evidence gathering, the system cross-validates both text and images to ensure credibility.

Contextual & Easy-to-Understand Updates – Gemini-2.5-Flash summarizes results into clear verdicts: True, False, Misleading, or Unverified, with reasoning that the public can easily follow.

Crisis Relevance – During events like natural disasters, elections, or health emergencies, VeriHub ensures people don’t fall victim to fake images or misleading news, providing real-time trustworthy updates.

Optimized Workflow: Focus on writing while Zenno handles link management, tracking, and updates.

All-in-One Platform: Combines blogging, monetization, and analytics into one easy-to-use interface.

Empowering Creators: Enables both beginners and experienced bloggers to maximize revenue without extra effort.

Save time managing affiliate links and tools

Increase earnings through data-driven insights

Simplify content monetization, making it accessible to everyone

Make blogging safer and more efficient by reducing manual errors

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges I Ran Into

While building Zenno Affiliate, I faced several technical and design hurdles:

Affiliate Link Management Complexity

Problem: Automatically inserting affiliate links into blog posts without breaking formatting or URLs was tricky.

Solution: Implemented a parsing algorithm that safely detects keywords and inserts links dynamically, ensuring post integrity.

Real-Time Analytics Performance

Problem: Tracking clicks and conversions in real time for multiple posts caused delays and occasional errors.

Solution: Optimized database queries, introduced caching, and used asynchronous API calls to handle high traffic efficiently.

Responsive UI Challenges

Problem: Designing a dashboard that works well on both desktop and mobile without clutter.

Solution: Adopted a mobile-first design approach and tested extensively across devices to ensure smooth UX.

Integration with Multiple Affiliate Programs

Problem: Different APIs and formats for various affiliate networks created inconsistencies.

Solution: Created an abstraction layer to standardize affiliate data and simplify integration.

✅ Lessons Learned

Importance of scalable architecture for real-time tracking

Value of thorough testing across devices

How to handle external API inconsistencies efficiently

Problem-solving under hackathon time constraints

> Click a picture and turn anything into a meme.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![cloudflare](https://img.shields.io/badge/cloudflare-333333?style=flat-square) ![Svelte](https://img.shields.io/badge/Svelte-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

I've always loved making memes, but honestly, it used to be a hassle. Finding the right template and coming up with the perfect caption would take forever, and half the time I'd just give up. 

That's why I built Memesnap. Now, you just snap a picture or upload one, add your context, and get a hilarious meme in seconds. 

No more overthinking or searching for templates. It's become my go-to way to make my group chats and stories way more fun, and it saves me so much time. 

If you love memes but hate the struggle, Memesnap makes it easy for anyone to create and share spot-on memes instantly.

⚠️ Disclaimer: You might end up as the most fun guy/gal at school or work ;)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Memesnap came with its fair share of challenges, especially since this was my first time creating a full stack product from scratch as a non-techie. I had to learn Svelte and SvelteKit on the go, figure out how to set up secure server-side APIs, and get Supabase Auth working smoothly for signups. Integrating Loops.so with Supabase to send auth emails was a bit tricky, and setting up the domain and server on Cloudflare took some trial and error.

I ran into bugs with authentication flows and some issues with deploying the AI backend powered by Google Gemini. Version control and managing multiple branches on GitHub was also new for me, but I got the hang of it after a few late nights.

What helped was breaking down the spec on Napkin.page, designing flows in Figma, and getting support from tools like Dia Browser, Windsurf, and v0 by Vercel. > Fighting misinformation with AI.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keras](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keras-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In an era of rampant misinformation and AI-generated content, it has become increasingly difficult for the average person to distinguish factual news from false narratives. This flood of "fake news" erodes public trust, influences opinions with incorrect data, and destabilizes a well-informed society.

Ethical Lens tackles this problem head-on by providing an accessible, easy-to-use tool for instant headline verification. It empowers users to take a questionable headline, check it against a vast database of recent, trusted news sources in real-time, and receive an immediate verdict on its authenticity. By leveraging the power of AI to fight AI-generated misinformation, Ethical Lens makes fact-checking simple and helps restore clarity and trust in the news.

**Challenges we ran into**

Model Deployment: Our initial Keras model architecture was incompatible with the Streamlit Cloud servers, causing persistent loading errors. We solved this by refactoring the model to use the more robust Keras Subclassing API.

Resource Limits: The deployment initially failed due to exceeding the server's 1GB memory limit. We fixed this by creating a highly optimized requirements.txt file that installs lightweight, CPU-only versions of TensorFlow and PyTorch.

Search Logic: The app initially failed to verify true news stories because the NewsAPI search was too restrictive. We overcame this by implementing a "cascading search" that combines results from multiple API endpoints to find evidence more reliably.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rapid API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rapid%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problems Tackled by आपकाPlatform

1. Lack of Real-Time Station Awareness

Issue: Many railway passengers—or especially those new to a station—struggle with dynamic details like which station is next, train–platform updates, or real-time arrival information.

Solution: The platform includes a live dashboard that shows upcoming stations and real-time arrival estimates. This helps commuters stay informed and reduces confusion. 


2. Uncertainty About Crowd Density and Station Facilities

Issue: Stations can become overcrowded, and travelers typically have little visibility into how congested areas like platforms, restrooms, or waiting areas are.

Solution: The system visualizes crowd density with dynamic graphics, enabling users to anticipate congestion. It also highlights availability of restrooms, food courts, ATMs, and other key amenities—reducing stress and helping passengers find facilities quickly. 


3. Navigation Difficulties on Large or Complex Platforms

Issue: Big railway stations often feel labyrinthine—locating exits, platforms, restrooms, or help points can be daunting.

Solution: By integrating AR-based navigation—leveraging Leaflet.js, OpenStreetMap, and routing tools—the platform offers a visual map with directional arrows, compass guidance, and estimated distances. Users can follow this augmented-reality overlay to navigate confidently. 


4. Accessibility & Multimodal Interaction Challenges

Issue: Not everyone can or wants to rely solely on text or visual cues—especially the visually impaired or people with mobility limitations.

Solution: The platform includes an AI-powered voice assistant, offering both speech synthesis and voice recognition. Users can ask about facilities (like restrooms, emergency support, food), schedules, or platform details using voice commands. The project also supports multiple languages—English, Hindi, and Bengali—enhancing inclusivity and accessibility. 


5. Alerts and Personalization

Issue: Staying alert about your stop or upcoming changes (e.g., delays) requires constant vigilance.

Solution: The platform features an alarm mechanism—letting users set destination alerts so they’re notified when their stop is approaching. This paired with the light/dark themes enhances usability across devices and conditions.

**Challenges we ran into**

🚧 Challenges Faced During Development

1. Data Availability & Real-Time Accuracy

Problem: Railway APIs in India are often restricted, paid, or unreliable. Getting real-time train data, crowd info, and platform changes is not straightforward.

Impact: Had to rely on mock data or simulated inputs for features like crowd density and train schedules instead of live railway databases.



---

2. Integrating AR with Web Technologies

Problem: Creating an AR-based navigation system with Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap is tricky:

GPS accuracy indoors (inside stations) is low.

Aligning directional arrows with real-world layouts is challenging.


Impact: Required simplification—AR simulation works for demonstration, but precise navigation inside large stations is hard.



---

3. Voice Assistant Development

Problem: Building an AI voice assistant in the browser has multiple issues:

Browser support for speech recognition and text-to-speech varies.

Handling multilingual input/output (English, Hindi, Bengali) reliably is complex.


Impact: Faced difficulties ensuring smooth voice recognition, especially with accents and noisy environments like railway stations.



---

4. Multilingual UI & Accessibility

Problem: Supporting multiple languages (English, Hindi, Bengali) and ensuring accessibility (for visually impaired users) required:

Translating UI elements.

Managing different fonts & Unicode rendering.


Impact: Increased UI complexity and maintenance overhead.



---

5. UI/UX Design for Usability

Problem: Designing a simple, responsive, and intuitive interface that works across mobile and desktop:

Needed to balance information density (maps, crowd info, facilities) without overwhelming the user.

Theme switching (dark/light) added extra CSS management.


Impact: Iterative testing needed to refine usability.



---

6. Resource Constraints

Problem: Since it’s a frontend-heavy project (HTML, CSS, JS), limitations arose:

No powerful backend for handling live queries.

Difficult to scale beyond a demo without cloud/database integration.


Impact: Some advanced features (real-time crowd tracking, actual train APIs) couldn’t be fully implemented.



---

7. Deployment & Browser Compatibility

Problem: Deploying AR + speech features consistently:

Some browsers block microphone access by default.

Map rendering issues on older devices.


Impact: Needed fallback mechanisms for non-supported devices.

**The problem it solves**

## 🛠️ The Problem It Solves

- **Tedious WiFi Onboarding:**  
  In public spaces like cafés, airports, or coworking spaces, connecting to WiFi is often slow and awkward. Users must ask staff for passwords, fill out lengthy captive portal forms, or struggle with inconsistent login methods. This wastes time and creates a poor experience.

- **Insecure WiFi Access:**  
  Traditional WiFi authentication methods (shared passwords, open networks) expose users to security risks such as eavesdropping, session hijacking, and unauthorized access. Passwords are often reused, shared widely, or left unchanged for long periods.

- **Privacy Risks:**  
  Many captive portals require users to hand over personal information (emails, phone numbers) which is often stored insecurely or sold to third parties, violating user privacy.

- **Payment Friction:**  
  Paying for premium or extended WiFi is typically clunky—cash counters, card swipes, or difficult online payment flows. Linking payment directly and securely to the user session is rarely done well.

- **Connectivity Interruptions:**  
  Travelers and commuters often lose their connection when moving between hotspots, passing through weak coverage areas, or when networks require frequent re-authentication. This disrupts productivity and can cause important data to be missed or lost.

---

## ✨ What People Can Use It For / How It Makes Life Easier and Safer

- **Instant, Hassle-Free WiFi Access**  
  Just scan a QR code or tap to connect—no passwords or forms. Users are online in seconds, improving satisfaction and reducing support workload for venue staff.

- **Private, Decentralized Authentication**  
  With Civic OAuth, users prove their identity securely without handing over sensitive data. They choose what information to share, and venues never store or see unnecessary personal details.

- **Seamless Digital Payments**  
  Users can pay for WiFi access or data top-ups using UPI, a fast and secure method familiar to millions. Payments are linked to their authenticated session, ensuring the right access level is granted immediately after payment.

- **Always-On Connectivity with AI**  
  Gemini AI predicts the user's likely travel route and potential connectivity blackspots. It pre-downloads key data (maps, emails, entertainment), so users stay productive and entertained even when moving between hotspots or through low-signal zones.

- **Safe, Role-Based Access**  
  The backend assigns network permissions based on user identity and context (e.g., guest, staff, admin), reducing the risk of unauthorized access and network abuse.

- **Better Analytics and Monetization for Venues**  
  Venue owners and IT admins can see anonymized usage analytics, automate payments, and customize access policies—all while respecting user privacy. This enables smarter marketing, better resource allocation, and new revenue streams.

- **Reduced Security Risks**  
  By eliminating shared passwords and using secure, token-based authentication, the system drastically reduces opportunities for credential theft, rogue access points, and other WiFi-related attacks.

- **User Empowerment and Control**  
  Users remain in charge of their data and identity. They can see what is shared, revoke access at any time, and trust that their privacy is protected by design.

---

**In summary:**  
This project transforms WiFi connectivity from a source of frustration into a seamless, secure, and intelligent user experience—benefiting both end users and providers, while setting a new standard for privacy and convenience in public and enterprise networks.

**Authenticate with Civic Auth**

### How Civic OAuth was use in Tap2Wifi
1. **User Authentication in Flutter App**  
   - The Flutter app integrates Civic’s OAuth SDK or uses Civic’s OAuth endpoints.
   - When a user logs in, the app redirects them to Civic for authentication and identity verification.
   - Upon successful authentication, Civic returns an OAuth access token (JWT or similar) to the Flutter app.

2. **Passing the Civic Token to the Backend**  
   - The Flutter app includes the Civic OAuth token in the `Authorization` header of each HTTP request to our Go backend:
     ```
     Authorization: Bearer <civic_oauth_token>
     ```

3. **Backend Middleware for Token Verification**  
   - The Go backend uses middleware (like our `RequireAuthRouter` or `RequireAuth`) to intercept incoming requests.
   - Instead of checking for a static token (`Bearer testtoken`), the middleware extracts the Civic token from the header.

4. **Validating the Civic Token**  
   - The middleware verifies the Civic token’s signature and validity.
   - This typically involves:
     - Decoding the JWT.
     - Fetching Civic’s public keys (JWKS endpoint) to verify the token’s signature.
     - Checking token claims (issuer, audience, expiry, etc.).
   - If the token is valid, the request proceeds; otherwise, it returns `401 Unauthorized`.

5. **Securing Endpoints**  
   - All protected routes use this middleware, ensuring only users authenticated via Civic can access sensitive resources.

6. **Web3 and Decentralized Identity Benefits**  
   - Civic’s identity system is Web3-ready, so in the future, we can:
     - Leverage decentralized identity features.
     - Allow users to prove ownership of blockchain wallets or credentials.
     - Integrate with smart contracts or other Web3 services.

**Best use of Gemini API**

# 🌐 Gemini AI Integration in Tap2Wifi

The backend leverages **Google Gemini AI** to suggest interesting stops—such as landmarks, attractions, or points of interest—between any two geographic coordinates. When combined with our service, it ensures users stay connected to the internet throughout their journey.

---

## 📡 Flexible API Endpoints

### `/api/gemini/recommendstops`
- Returns a list of **5 recommended stops** between a start and end coordinate.
- Utilizes Gemini AI for intelligent suggestions.

### `/api/gemini/recommendstopswifi`
- Enhances the above by also returning **available WiFi networks** near each recommended stop.
- Merges AI recommendations with your WiFi database.

### `/api/wifi/nearby/stops`
- Accepts a **custom list of stops** (in JSON).
- Returns WiFi networks near each location for flexible integration with frontends or third-party systems.

---

## 📶 WiFi Discovery

For each **recommended or user-supplied stop**, the backend:
- Queries the MongoDB WiFi collection.
- Returns all networks within a specified radius (e.g., **1 km**), including:
  - **SSID**
  - **Password**
  - **Location**
  - **Description**

---

## ✨ Seamless User Experience

Users can:
- **Plan routes**
- **Discover interesting places**
- **View available WiFi networks** at each stop  
All through a **simple and intuitive API**.

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

## MongoDB on Tap2Wifi

 We selected MongoDB Atlas for its managed cloud database service, allowing us to quickly set up a cluster on AWS without the hassle of server management. Also we got a generous free-tier to work through the project    
- **Integration with Go**: We connected Atlas to our Go backend using the 
  - official [MongoDB Go Driver](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver), which made secure connections and CRUD operations straightforward.
  - also used much packages to parse Objects
    
- **Data Storage for Flutter**: For our Flutter frontend, 
  - we stored user profiles, 
  - session tokens, 
  - and Wi-Fi hotspot details in MongoDB’s flexible document-based collections.
  
- **Authentication and Security**: We handled authentication by storing user credentials and OAuth tokens in Atlas, leveraging its field-level security to protect sensitive data.
    
- **Real-Time Updates**: We used change streams to push real-time updates
   - like new hotspot notifications—to the Flutter app,
   - keeping users engaged.
    
- **Geospatial Features**: Our Wi-Fi hotspot feature utilized geospatial queries 
  - to find nearby hotspots, 
  - adding a practical,
  - location-aware twist to the app.
    
- **Performance Optimization**: We relied on Atlas’s automatic scaling to handle load spikes and added indexes on key fields (e.g., user IDs, hotspot coordinates) to ensure fast queries.
- **Query Optimization through Indexing**: We significantly improved query performance by creating indexes on frequently queried fields. For example, 
  - we indexed `wifiID` and `userID` fields to accelerate user lookups, ensuring that authentication and profile retrieval were instantaneous.
  - Additionally, for our Wi-Fi hotspot feature, we implemented a geospatial index on the location field, allowing us to perform rapid proximity searches and deliver nearby hotspot results to users in milliseconds.

**The problem it solves**

Medical research and machine learning models in healthcare have been historically limited by access to diverse patient data. Due to strict privacy concerns, hospitals cannot share raw patient data. This leads to biased models trained on limited populations. A Secure Federated Learning (FL) System that allows hospitals to collaboratively train machine learning models without exposing raw patient data. Hospitals upload their datasets, train models locally, and share encrypted model weights for collective learning.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges Faced During MedHive Development

Building *MedHive* — a collaborative healthcare AI platform — brought unique challenges.

## 🚀 1. Designing the Federated Learning (FL) System
- *Multi-Modal Data:* Medical data includes text, prescriptions, PDFs, X-rays, and CT scans. Handling multiple formats securely was a complex task.
- *Device Variability:* Hospitals had diverse computing power, making consistent FL training difficult.
- *Secure Aggregation:* Merging encrypted model weights without leaking information required custom pipelines.
- *Continual Learning:* Healthcare evolves fast. We had to build systems ready for real-time updates.

## 🌐 2. Lack of Free Hosting Opportunities

- *GPU Shortage:* Deploying heavy models (X-ray classifiers, ECG analyzers) needed GPU-backed servers, rare on free tiers.
- *Scaling Limits:* FL relies on real-time client-server updates, leading to frequent timeouts and throttling on free hosting.
- *Uptime Reliability:* Free platforms couldn’t guarantee 24/7 availability, critical for federated learning sessions.

## 📚 3. Dataset Challenges

- *Privacy Constraints:* Access to diverse medical datasets is restricted by law (HIPAA, GDPR).
- *Data Diversity:* Models needed multi-language, multi-domain data — hard to source publicly.
- *Expert Annotations:* Properly labeling medical data (e.g., ECGs, X-rays) without experts delayed prototyping.
- *Federated Simulation:* Creating realistic, partitioned datasets to simulate real-world hospitals was non-trivial.

**Groq track**

1. MedHive powers a **real-time healthcare chatbot** using Groq’s ultra-fast inference, delivering instant, accurate responses to patient and clinician queries.
2. A Groq-optimized **navigation agent** ensures users can swiftly access medical models, upload data, and explore the platform without any delays.
3. **Dr. MedLiv**, our LLM-based symptom analysis agent, leverages Groq to provide rapid, conversational health insights, enhancing early detection and triage.
4. The **Data Upload Agent** uses Groq to enable hospitals to securely and quickly upload encrypted datasets, fueling continuous federated learning without bottlenecks.

**Challenges we ran into**

Only if we had a token for every challenge we faced.

In all honesty, we started thinking we had something to work with. Spoiler alert, we (really really) didn't. 
We found the leading repository in the field of token prediction. But guess what, it was just a linear hollow template that gave out random guesses in the name of token prediction. Wrong metrics, wrong formulas, wrong results.

So we did what all sane rising sophomores, complete beginners in AI/ML, heuristics and umm.. Hierarchical backoff with geometric shrinkage do. Which is of course using the power of 100dollars in OpenAI credits, to make everything - all prediction logic, all frontend, every metric - from scratch, on our own.

Our testing credit cards got exhausted after too many runs, so we spent hours on calls with the Prava team getting everything sorted. Shoutout to Shubham and Sushant for testing an unreasonable number of credit cards.

Shivam had to switch database setups multiple times before finally settling on the good old Supabase, and running like a 1000 tests (quite literally) . Tanay had to completely change the dashboard to be dynamic (update logs every 3 seconds), and homepage to be 3D. Shubh had to explain his screen time to his parents. Ammar had to figure out why the error margin of the autonomous feedback loop was rising from 49% to 200% before it finally started decreasing to within 10% in the final model.

All things considered, the worst challenge was still without a doubt running out of caffeine. BUT finallyyy seeing the 0% error rate on some of the runs reignited our will to sacrifice our sleep schedules.

**The problem it solves**

Companies spend thousands a month on LLM calls and can't tell you how quickly it went by, and when balance hits zero at mid project, production stops.

Meter is a drop-in proxy.
As soon as you use our integration, every call, attribute, feature is tracked. 
We predict your input and output tokens, something that no one else can do. Or at least not using the painstaking heuristics and self improving feedback loops we have in place (you really should go through the “how prediction works” section on the website)
When you're about to run out of tokens, we predict  how many you need within a really improved error margin (6.5x better), and then buy them for you, through our dearest Prava. 

They say the devil will burn all your credits, but guess what, now the devil wears prava. 

In the future, we plan to expand the type of prompts, which we define as feature-tags, that the prediction model can conquer. We also wish to expand to AI providers other than OpenAI. Further we wish to decrease the latency of the proxy and database. All this will help us progress to a point where we are ready to flawlessly ship to users and businesses.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

We built a dedicated agent called the Treasurer agent that autonomously holds a human-approved Visa mandate and spends against it with nobody present. VIC is what allows the automatic budget top ups to run.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

*We are not just startup ready, but also ready for startups to use.*
Meter ships as managed infrastructure or inside your own perimeter. The hosted stack runs the proxy on Render, the dashboard on Vercel and the ledger on Supabase against a single shared Postgres, while docker compose up deploys that same stack single-tenant inside your VPC, where your provider keys never leave your environment. And the product appreciates in place. Prediction accuracy is derived from your own accumulated per-feature history, so forecast quality improves the longer you run it - so not only can it handle users, but users make it better.

**OpenAI**

Firstly, Meter is a drop in proxy for live OpenAI traffic, the predictions our engine makes is for OpenAI, specifically the GPT 4o Mini model. Our entire prediction model is trained on actual token information from 1756 OpenAI requests for output token estimation, and uses OpenAI's own tiktoken for input token estimations.

**iMessage Agent**

We don’t only know when to use Prava, but also when not to because we have a circuit breaker that automatically blocks suspicious prompting activity to avoid your bank account from being empty due to leaked API keys. When that happens we immediately alert the user with iMessages via Linq. This keeps them always notified and their bank accounts always safe.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

The dashboard is live. The status ramp is colourblind safe and contrast was measured for this exact reason. The top-up renders as "dry run, no money moved”. We don't invent any payments or log lines, we only show states that exist in the ledger. And the dashboard shows user friendly live analytics and the entire site has clear navigation with creative 3D UI.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

We predict the cost before the call, not after the bill. We did deep analysis, check every research paper and repo we could find - but nothing exists for inspirations that can pass even remotely close benchmarks. Everyone else reports what you spent; we forecast it pre-flight and cut it off mid-flight - 70% error down to 11%, measured across 1,300 real calls, not asserted.
A real Visa settlement with no human present. Most agentic-commerce demos stop one step before the money moves. Ours has a transaction id. It's deployed, you can drive it yourself in ten minutes, and we publish what we haven't proven.

Daily commuters often face expensive and unreliable daily transportation, with limited connectivity to public transport. Many people travel along the same routes every day, yet there is no trusted platform that enables them to safely share rides.

 Existing ride-hailing services are designed primarily for commercial drivers and individual trips, leaving empty seats in private vehicles unused while others struggle to find affordable transportation. **Solution:**

**RideLink AI** enables daily commuters travelling in the same direction to share rides with one another.

Drivers can also earn by sharing their unused vehicle seats, while passengers enjoy safe and cost-effective transportation.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building **RideLink AI** involved solving several complex full-stack engineering challenges:

**Real-Time Multi-Client Synchronization:** Initially, ride data was stored in local React component state, causing data loss on browser refresh and preventing passengers from seeing new rides. We resolved this by re-architecting our Express backend to persist ride offers directly to MongoDB Atlas while emitting real-time WebSocket events via Socket.IO. This ensures every connected client receives instant UI updates across browsers without page refreshes.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/e222800fb6ea4528b1a8ea44eee1d520/be7e9c1b-8375-4b36-8344-813c6bf02535.png)


**Firebase OAuth Domain Authorization:** Deploying Google OAuth via Firebase triggered domain authorization errors due to cross-origin security policies. We resolved this by registering production domain origins in the Firebase Console and configuring custom provider parameters to explicitly force the Google account selection window every time.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/e222800fb6ea4528b1a8ea44eee1d520/7f9ab361-7167-4dc2-bf39-d865deafbc9c.png)


**Strict Document-Based Driver Authorization:** Early prototypes allowed drivers to gain verified status without submitting real identity documents. We hardened our Express validation middleware and MongoDB schemas to strictly verify Aadhaar Card and Driver’s License fields, locking ride creation endpoints until identity verification is completed.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/e222800fb6ea4528b1a8ea44eee1d520/1047c547-0041-4893-bccf-1190f7b7ea36.png)

**Atomic Inventory Control for Concurrent Bookings:** Simultaneous booking requests created race conditions where seats could be oversold. We implemented atomic MongoDB document updates and validation logic in our Express controllers to verify remaining seat capacity before confirming any booking

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/e222800fb6ea4528b1a8ea44eee1d520/35ba27e0-f0e3-4a77-bbb0-3c379c4a45d3.png)

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

## The Problem

Learning to invest is expensive, intimidating, and fragmented. New investors face several painful realities:

- **Real money means real fear.** Beginners hesitate to experiment because a single bad trade can wipe out weeks of savings. This kills the learning loop before it starts.
- **Tools are scattered everywhere.** You need one app for charts, another for news, a third for fundamentals, a fourth for an AI opinion, and a fifth to backtest an idea. Nothing connects.
- **AI advice is a black box.** ChatGPT can talk about stocks, but it doesn't see your portfolio, your risk exposure, or your live market data. Generic advice isn't actionable advice.
- **Strategies are untestable.** "Buy when RSI drops below 30" sounds smart, but without a way to simulate it on historical data, it's just a guess.
- **Markets never stop moving.** By the time a human spots a breakout or reversal pattern across 65 stocks, the opportunity is already gone.

---

## What TradeWise Solves

TradeWise is a unified, AI-native paper trading platform that turns market learning into a safe, hands-on experience, and gives users capabilities normally reserved for quant funds.

### For learners and students

- Start with **$100,000 in paper money** and trade without risking a cent.
- Every trade executes atomically against **real live prices** via Finnhub WebSocket, so you are learning on real market behavior, not a toy simulator.
- When markets are closed, simulated ticks keep the experience alive 24/7, so there is no waiting for Monday to practice.

### For people who want AI that actually understands their portfolio

- The **AI Advisor** is a ReAct agent with 7 tools. It pulls your live holdings, current quotes, technical indicators, fundamentals, news sentiment, ML predictions, and a financial knowledge base before answering.
- Ask *"Is my portfolio too concentrated?"* or *"Should I rotate out of tech?"* and get context-aware, explainable answers, streamed step-by-step so you see the reasoning.
- Type trades in plain English: *"Buy $2,000 of NVDA and trim 20% of my TSLA"*. The system parses, previews, and executes.

### For data-driven decision makers

- A **3-model ensemble** (XGBoost, LSTM, and Logistic Regression) votes on every prediction, with confidence capped at 85% so humility is built in.
- **Cascading sentiment analysis** runs FinBERT on news headlines, falling back to Gemini when confidence is low, balancing speed and accuracy.
- A **Monte Carlo risk engine** simulates 10,000 portfolio paths to compute Value-at-Risk and expected shortfall, so you know how bad a bad day could really be.

### For people who want a second (and third) opinion

- The **Swarm Debate** pits a Bull, a Bear, and a Fundamentalist agent against each other on any stock, running two rounds of arguments and rebuttals grounded in real indicators.
- An **episodic memory bank** powered by ChromaDB remembers past debates and actual outcomes, weighting each agent by its track record in the current market regime.
- The result is a final BUY, SELL, or HOLD decision with conviction level, fully explained.

### For active traders who cannot watch every ticker

- The **Signal Scanner** sweeps 65 symbols every 5 minutes, detecting 6 pattern types (ML consensus, breakouts, oversold, overbought, momentum, and reversals) with confluence scoring.
- Alerts stream live via Server-Sent Events, so you never miss a setup because you were in a meeting.

### For people who want automation they can trust

- **Autopilot** runs autonomous portfolio management in four modes: Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive, and Full Auto.
- Hard **guardrails** enforce max drawdown, daily loss limits, and position size caps. The bot cannot blow up your account.
- Every decision streams its reasoning in real time, so automation never feels like a black box.

### For strategy designers

- Describe a strategy in **plain English**, such as *"Buy when MACD crosses above zero and sell when RSI exceeds 75"*, and TradeWise parses it, simulates it over 1 month to 1 year of data, and returns the equity curve, Sharpe ratio, max drawdown, win rate, and every individual trade.
- Test an idea in seconds instead of learning Python.

### For portfolio risk managers

- The **Correlation Network** renders your holdings as a force-directed physics graph. Nodes are sized by allocation, colored by sector, and edges are weighted by correlation.
- Instantly see hidden concentration risk. If everything in your portfolio is correlated, you don't actually own a diversified portfolio.

---

## Who It's For

| User | What TradeWise does for them |
|---|---|
| **Students and beginners** | Learn markets risk-free with real data, real AI guidance, and real feedback. |
| **Self-directed investors** | Get institutional-grade analysis (ensemble ML, Monte Carlo VaR, multi-agent debate) in one place. |
| **Strategy hobbyists** | Prototype and backtest ideas in plain English without writing a l

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## 1. Finnhub Free Tier Rate Limits

The free tier caps at 60 API calls per minute. One dashboard refresh wanted quotes for 8 holdings, 5 watchlist symbols, news for 3 tickers, and historical OHLCV, which blew through the quota instantly and returned 429s.

**Fix:** Built a 3-layer cache (in-memory dict, then Redis, then Finnhub) in `app/core/cache.py`. Every market data call goes through a single `cache_get(key, ttl, fetch_fn)` helper. Finnhub usage dropped around 95%.

## 2. SSE Connection Storm

Autopilot's SSE endpoint closed immediately when idle. The browser's `EventSource` auto-reconnects every 3 seconds, AND our `onerror` handler was also reconnecting. Dozens of concurrent connections accumulated and starved the backend so badly that even `/api/autopilot/status` timed out. The page would spin forever.

**Fix:** Backend now polls for state every 5 seconds with heartbeats instead of closing. Frontend only opens SSE when the agent is actually running. Reconnects tracked in a ref so stale callbacks can't fire phantom reconnections.

## 3. Trade Race Conditions

A user spamming "Buy" twice in 100ms could end up with double holdings but one balance deduction. We hit this when autopilot fired trades in parallel with a manual trade on the same symbol.

**Fix:** Used SQLAlchemy's `with_for_update()` for row-level locks on both the User balance row and the Holding row before any calculation. Transaction either fully commits or fully rolls back.

## 4. Gemini Hallucinating Tool Outputs

Our first AI Advisor passed tool definitions to Gemini 2.5 Flash via system prompt. Gemini would confidently fabricate tool results instead of calling them. It once said a user owned 50 shares of AAPL when they owned nothing.

**Fix:** Abandoned function calling and built a manual ReAct loop. The prompt forces a strict `TOOL_CALL: tool_name(argument)` format. We parse that with regex, execute the tool ourselves, append results to context, loop up to 7 iterations. No tool call means no data to claim.

## 5. Vercel Build Failing on TypeScript

Hardcoded fallback data we added didn't match the `ParsedRules` interface. Local dev mode was lenient but production builds enforced types strictly, so `npm run build` failed on deploy.

**Fix:** Rewrote the fallback to match the exact nested shape (`entry: { conditions, logic }` instead of `entry: string[]`), and converted `equity_curve` from `number[]` to `{ date, equity }[]`.

## 6. Markets Closed During Demo

We tested the "live ticking prices" feature at 9 PM IST on a weekend. US markets were closed, Finnhub's WebSocket sent nothing, and every number on screen was frozen. Terrible look for a real-time trading app.

**Fix:** Added a `simulate_prices()` background task in `ws_manager.py` that kicks in when the real feed is silent. It applies a 0.05% random walk per second to 10 default symbols and broadcasts through the same pipeline. Frontend cannot tell the difference.

## 7. JWT Over Server-Sent Events

Browser `EventSource` cannot set custom headers, so our standard `Authorization: Bearer` pattern broke every SSE endpoint (advisor chat, autopilot stream, signals feed, backtest runner). They all returned 401.

**Fix:** Added a second FastAPI dependency `get_current_user_sse` that reads the token from a `?token=` query param instead of the header. Same validation, different source. Frontend appends the token to the SSE URL.

## 8. Scope vs Time

The biggest challenge was ambition. We wanted a trading platform, ML ensemble, AI advisor, multi-agent swarm, autopilot, signal scanner, backtester, correlation graph, and natural language commands, all in a hackathon window.

**Fix:** Built the shared layers first (cache, auth, trading engine, market data service) before any feature on top. That gave every feature a consistent base and let them interoperate cleanly. The autopilot uses the same ML predictions as the dashboard, the swarm reads the same cache as the backtester, the command palette executes through the same trading engine as the trade page.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/verix-19b1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Kutan-Fuiton/Verix) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Q32d-H6tXVE) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Q32d-H6tXVE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-BINARY%20v2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://binaryvtwo.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI System for Detecting Misinformation Risk

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today’s Indian digital ecosystem, information spreads rapidly through platforms like WhatsApp, X, and Telegram—often in code-mixed languages like Hinglish and Banglish that combine multiple languages, slang, and informal structure. Existing AI moderation systems are largely designed for clean English text and fail to accurately interpret these mixed-language messages. As a result, high-risk content—such as panic-inducing messages, unverified claims, and emotionally persuasive narratives—spreads unchecked, not because it is explicitly false, but because it is difficult to detect using traditional methods. This creates a critical gap where harmful information can influence public behavior and perception before any verification or intervention occurs.

Verix solves this problem by acting as a real-time intelligence layer over conversations, analyzing every message the moment it is sent. Instead of trying to fact-check content after it spreads, Verix uses a specialized AI model trained on code-mixed Indian language patterns to detect risk signals such as panic intent, unverified claims, and narrative bias instantly. Through a live chat interface powered by WebSockets, each message is evaluated, assigned structured risk scores, and visually highlighted for users, making hidden risks immediately visible. This proactive, scalable approach ensures that potentially harmful information is identified before it goes viral, especially in linguistic contexts where traditional systems fail

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges I faced was structuring the problem into a clean, learnable format for the model. Since the project involves multiple outputs like fear signal, misinformation risk, claim type, and more, designing a consistent labeling scheme and converting raw mixed-language text (Hinglish/Banglish) into structured data was tricky. Initially, the model performance was unstable due to inconsistent labels and limited data, so I addressed this by standardizing categories and generating more balanced synthetic data. Another major hurdle was building the chat interface that could seamlessly connect with the model in real time. Handling asynchronous responses, ensuring low latency, and displaying meaningful outputs (like risk scores and explanations) required multiple iterations. I overcame this by simplifying the backend pipeline, optimizing API calls, and gradually improving the UI to make the interaction smooth and intuitive.

**AI/ML**

This project aligns with the AI/ML track by leveraging transformer-based models like BERT to perform multi-label classification and risk prediction on real-world multilingual text. It applies machine learning to detect misinformation, analyze sentiment, and generate structured insights, showcasing practical AI deployment in social and communication systems.

**Smolify AI track**

We accquired datasets of code-mixed Hinglish and Banglish social media messages to train our text classification model.

### VÉSTRA
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vestra-d747) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/anshu-2007/vestra-luxury-aggregator) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Cross-Platform Luxury Aggregator & AI Stylist

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🔴 The Luxury Fragmentation Problem
The Indian luxury market is highly fragmented across platforms like Amazon Luxe, Myntra Luxe, Ajio Gold, and Flipkart Premium.

Price Disparity: The same watch or garment can vary by ₹2,000 to ₹15,000 across different apps.

Decision Fatigue: Users spend hours switching between apps to compare prices, delivery times, and bank offers.

Styling Anxiety: High-value purchases are risky; users often worry if a premium color palette (like Gold vs. Rose Gold) will actually suit their skin tone.

🟢 The VÉSTRA Solution
VÉSTRA serves as a centralized "Visual Intelligence" layer for the high-end shopper. It automates the research phase of luxury shopping through three core pillars:

1. Cross-Platform Price Synchronization
People use VÉSTRA to instantly see a 4-way price comparison. It eliminates the need to manually search multiple apps by identifying the "Lowest Price Platform" and highlighting real-time savings.

2. Aesthetic Risk Mitigation (AI Stylist)
Instead of guessing, users utilize our Visual Intelligence Engine. By inputting their skin tone and the desired "vibe" (e.g., Old Money or Global Business), the system filters the database using color-theory logic. This ensures that a ₹20,000 purchase is an aesthetic match, not just a financial one.

3. Optimized Financial Checkout
Existing tasks like calculating credit card discounts are manual and confusing. VÉSTRA makes this safer and easier by:

Automating Discount Logic: Real-time calculation of ROI for premium cards (HDFC Infinia, Amex, etc.).

Deep-Link Navigation: Securely routing users directly to the verified checkout page of the lowest-priced retailer.

🚀 Impact
VÉSTRA transforms a 30-minute manual search into a 30-second AI-curated experience, ensuring users never overpay for luxury again.

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges We Overcame
Building a luxury aggregator in a limited timeframe presented several unique hurdles. Here is how we navigated them:

1. The "Single Source of Truth" Data Mismatch
The Challenge: Every e-commerce platform uses different naming conventions. Amazon might list a color as "Midnight Black," while Myntra calls it "Obsidian." This made automated filtering and price comparison nearly impossible.

The Solution: We implemented a Canonical Data Schema. We built a middleware logic that maps these fragmented "Vendor Attributes" into a single "VÉSTRA Standard" (e.g., mapping all variants to a standard hex_code and category_id). This ensured that when a user filters for "Minimalist Black," they see matching items from all four platforms simultaneously.

2. Complex State Management (The "Filter Paradox")
The Challenge: Managing the intersection of multiple filters (Skin Tone + Vibe + Occasion + Price) caused "Prop Drilling" issues and sluggish UI re-renders.

The Solution: We moved away from basic component state and utilized React Context API combined with a Memoized Filtering Logic. By using useMemo, we ensured that the 60+ item database is only re-calculated when a filter actually changes, maintaining a "Luxury" feel with 60fps smoothness even on low-end mobile devices.

3. Science vs. Subjectivity in AI Styling
The Challenge: Mapping "Skin Tone" to "Clothing Color" is scientifically complex due to lighting variables. Initially, our recommendations felt too rigid or inaccurate.

The Solution: We integrated the Monk Skin Tone (MST) Scale logic. Instead of simple "Warm/Cool" labels, we built a Weight-Based Scoring Algorithm. Each clothing item is assigned a 'Compatibility Score' against different skin tones. If an item doesn't meet a 70% match threshold for the user's profile, it is gracefully hidden, ensuring the "Stylist" feels intelligent rather than random.

4. Handling CORS and Dynamic Redirects
The Challenge: Browsers often block direct redirects or data fetches from major retail sites due to CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) policies.

The Solution: We utilized Next.js API Routes as a proxy layer. Instead of the browser talking directly to the retailer, our server handles the handshake, ensuring a secure and uninterrupted "Deep-Link" experience for the user when they click the "Buy" button.

Team **HACTRIX** -- Nandini Kalia, Akshat Chouksey, ANSHU CHOWDHURY

> Coding ka Khel Khatam

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The primary problem this project addresses is breaking the language barrier (and the "seriousness" barrier) of programming by creating a coding environment based on Hindi/Urdu keyphrases.

It creates a bridge between a natural language (Hindi/Hinglish) and machine code (C++).

KhelKhatam is an educational and cultural tool. It solves the technical challenge of "How do I build a safe, web-accessible compiler for a custom language?" while serving the user goal of "I want to code in Hinglish."

**Challenges we ran into**

1. We thought about how to create the AST on our own so that we really challenging.
2.  Nesting of loops was very difficult to implement. As managing the pointer while nesting is difficult.
3. CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)
Issue: Browsers block requests from one Origin (e.g., frontend on port 8000) to another (backend on port 5000) for security reasons. Even with flask-cors, we faced persistent preflight errors.
Fix: We moved to a Single Origin Architecture. Instead of running two separate servers, we configured Flask (app.py) to serve the HTML/JS static files itself.

> A Gamified AI Platform for Concept-Driven Learning

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square) ![Phaser.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Phaser.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Traditional learning platforms rely heavily on memorization, passive content consumption, and high-pressure testing.**
Students often:

- Forget concepts quickly after exams
- Feel stressed by penalties and game-over systems
- Lack personalized guidance on what to learn next
- Practice without understanding why an answer is wrong
- Teachers, on the other hand:
- Have limited ways to track real conceptual understanding
- Spend time repeating explanations instead of improving content

****💡 How SkillQuest Solves It****

SkillQuest transforms learning into a concept-driven, AI-guided experience.

🎮 Game-based learning that tests understanding, not rote answers
🧠 Practice-first modes with no penalties → stress-free learning
🔥 Optional challenge modes for competitive learners
🤖 AI Mentor that explains mistakes and suggests next steps
📊 Visual progress analytics instead of raw scores
🧩 Daily AI-generated questions ensure fresh practice every day
🔒 Strict role separation keeps the platform secure and fair

****🚀 What People Can Use It For****
- Students → Learn concepts deeply through play
- Teachers → Share structured notes without admin overhead
- Beginners → Build confidence without fear of failure
- Competitive learners → Test skills under challenge mode
- Judges / Demo users → Experience learning instantly via Guest Mode

**🌱 Impact**
SkillQuest makes learning:
- More engaging
- Less stressful
- More personalized
- Concept-first, not exam-first

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Role security:** Preventing students from accessing teacher features.
      **Fix:** All role checks moved to backend with an authorized teacher list.

- **No-penalty learning design:** Making games educational without frustrating “game over” loops.
       **Fix:** Separated Practice Mode (feedback only) and Challenge Mode (scoring + game over).

- **Daily AI question growth:** Adding new questions daily without repetition.
       **Fix:** Stored questions with subject, game type, difficulty, and date.

- **Resume learning safely:** Restoring sessions without breaking when content changes.
       **Fix:** Used fallback redirection to Learning Zone if data is missing.

- **Guest demo limits:** Allowing instant access without saving data.
       **Fix:** Used temporary sessions with strict question caps.

### Zeke
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zeke-9a89) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/EchoWebLV/Zeek) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/ZekePrivacy) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1HnUIzfNYBY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Spreading the Gospel of Zero Knowledge.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twitter API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twitter%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![railway](https://img.shields.io/badge/railway-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Gemini 3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Gemini%203.0-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**ZEKE** is an AI-powered privacy advocacy engine that turns complex ideas into accessible content and proves private payments work by accepting them.

**ZEKE** generates fresh privacy content daily through 10+ rotating post types including tips, facts, predictions, hot takes, quotes, shoutouts, and recommendations. No more repeating the same talking points. Every second post pulls real-time news about Zcash, Starknet, NEAR, Mina, and the broader ZK ecosystem, keeping the community informed without manual curation. Anyone can send shielded ZEC with a topic in the memo to trigger an on-demand public analysis post. Pay privately, get public insight.

For the analysis under the hood, ZEKE watches for incoming shielded Zcash payments using a viewing key. When someone sends ZEC with a topic in the memo, ZEKE detects the transaction, decrypts the memo client-side using Zcash's native encryption (the same cryptography that protects all shielded transactions), and feeds the topic to AI for content generation. The sender stays anonymous, ZEKE only sees the memo and amount, never who sent it.

Each post comes with a unique AI-generated image featuring Zeke, a consistent retro mascot with a black censored bar. The character appears in scenes that match the content, making every post visually distinct while maintaining brand identity across all generated content.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Making Complex Topics Accessible**
Zero-knowledge proofs and shielded transactions make most people's eyes glaze over. The solution was baked into the system prompt: two short paragraphs max, 250-400 characters, no academic language, no jargon. The AI had to explain like a smart friend, not a textbook. Short sentences. Direct. If you only have two paragraphs, every word earns its place.
**Avoiding Content Fatigue with Rotation**
A bot posting the same content type gets boring fast. I built a two-layer rotation: every second post is live news from Google Search, and non-news posts cycle through 10+ types (tips, facts, predictions, hot takes, quotes, shoutouts.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/5d001a8c00934c5286199dc21ecbe878/60d46252-7c11-4b91-b3a1-37419e0782d7.png)

**Real-Time News Aggregation**
Live news sounds simple until search results return redirect URLs, old content gets recycled, and AI hallucinates sources. We used Gemini's Google Search grounding with strict freshness constraints, resolved redirect URLs to get actual sources, and included real links in every post so readers can verify.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/5d001a8c00934c5286199dc21ecbe878/5e63988c-218e-4ef9-a75a-ed7c91a54afd.png)

**Decrypting Shielded Memos**
Reading private Zcash memos isn't plug-and-play. The fast sync protocol strips out memo data to save bandwidth, giving you only a fraction of what you need. The fix was a two-step process: first detect that a payment arrived, then fetch the full transaction to actually read the memo. We built the decryption in pure Node.js so it runs anywhere without installing Zcash tooling. The sender stays anonymous. We only see what topic they requested, never who they are.

**Creating a Consistent Character with AI Image Generation**
AI image generators produce different styles with every prompt. Early mascot attempts gave us a completely different character each time. The fix was obsessive prompt engineering: defining Zeke with extreme specificity (retro Vault Boy style, black censored bar over eyes, monochromatic olive-green skin and clothes, yellow Z logo shirt). Keeping Zeke monochromatic while letting backgrounds stay vibrant anchors the character visually across hundreds of different scenes.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/5d001a8c00934c5286199dc21ecbe878/f8b10f98-83f5-4e8a-a6ad-24b5e43c30d9.png)

### Zord Protocol
