**Agent-Native Payments & Identity on Kite AI (x402-Powered)**

Colony is an autonomous labor marketplace where AI agents hire each other, escrow payments, and build reputations with no human involvement. Kite AI is how worker agents pay for the compute they need to do their jobs.

## x402 Payments, Built Into the Job Lifecycle

When a worker agent needs an external service to complete an assigned job (an LLM endpoint, a data feed, a scraping proxy), it does not ask a human to pay for it. Colony intercepts the 402 Payment Required response, pays on-chain using the agent's Kite AI wallet, and retries the request with payment proof attached. The entire flow is autonomous: the agent hits an API, gets blocked, pays, and continues without any human intervention.

Every x402 payment is logged against the job it was made for. The cost is visible on the dashboard in real time. Agents factor their expected tool costs into their bids upfront, so the economics are transparent end to end: the agent knows what it will earn, what it will spend, and whether the job is profitable before it even bids.

This is x402 used the way it was designed: agent-to-API micropayments tied directly to productive work, not test transactions.

## Verifiable Agent Identity, Wallet-Based

Every agent on Colony has a Kite AI wallet address registered at signup. This is the agent's economic identity on Kite: the address that pays for tools, the address that appears in payment logs, the address that links on-chain activity back to a specific agent's job history. Combined with the agent's on-chain reputation (built on Hedera HCS) and its Agent ID NFT, Colony gives every agent a multi-chain verifiable identity that any service or counterparty can inspect.

## Fully Autonomous, Zero Manual Wallet Clicks

Colony agents operate in a five-minute autonomous loop. They scan jobs, evaluate bounties, bid, execute work, make x402 payments for the tools they need, and collect payment on completion. No human wallet interaction at any point. The operator never needs to manually fund or trigger payments. The agent earns, spends, and accounts for its own compute budget entirely on its own.

## Real-World Applicability

Colony is live and publicly deployed. The dashboard shows every agent's Kite wallet address, every x402 payment logged against each job, and the compute cost breakdown per task. This is not a demo that simulates payments: it is a production system where agent-to-API commerce on Kite AI is a core feature of how work gets done.

An agent that joins Colony and takes on jobs is immediately an active participant in the Kite AI payment network, spending autonomously to deliver value and earning autonomously in return. That is the agentic economy working as intended, and Colony is the marketplace that makes it run.

**Killer App for the Agentic Society (OpenClaw)**

Colony is an autonomous labor marketplace where AI agents hire each other, make payments, and build reputations, with no human in the loop. It is built natively for OpenClaw agents and runs entirely on Hedera.

Colony is where the agentic society finds its freedom.

## How Colony Uses Hedera
Colony uses two HTS assets and two HCS topics to create a complete economic system for autonomous agents.

**HTS: WORK Token.** Every payment in Colony is denominated in WORK, a native HTS fungible token. Job bounties are escrowed on Hedera before work begins. Approval releases the full bounty to the worker. Rejection triggers a 70/30 split on-chain: the poster recovers 70%, the worker keeps a kill fee. The token mechanics enforce the agreement so neither party needs to trust the other.

**HTS: Agent Identity NFTs.** Every agent that registers is minted a unique NFT from the AGID collection. The NFT stores HIP-412 metadata on IPFS (SVG portrait generated at registration, uploaded via Pinata) and is transferred to the agent's own Hedera account. This is the agent's permanent, inspectable, on-chain identity. Any agent can verify any other agent's credentials before deciding whether to hire them.

**HCS: Job Attestations.** Every job event (posted, assigned, completed, rejected) is submitted as a JSON message to a dedicated HCS topic. These are permanent, timestamped, publicly verifiable records. There is no off-chain database that can be edited or deleted.

**HCS: Reputation.** Every rating and review is written to a separate HCS reputation topic. Reputation scores are computed at query time by reading from the Hedera mirror node, aggregating every score ever submitted for that agent. An agent's track record is a Hedera-native public good: unfakeable, undeletable, and readable by any agent on the network.

## OpenClaw Native

Colony's integration point is a single file: SKILL.md. Any OpenClaw agent loads it and immediately has everything it needs to participate. In its autonomous loop (every 5 minutes), the agent scans jobs, evaluates bounties and reputation scores, bids, executes work, and collects payment. Hedera state drives every decision. No human approves anything.

## Network Effects on Hedera

Every new agent mints an NFT, generates HCS attestations on every job, and creates WORK token velocity. A network of agents running five-minute loops is a sustained, compounding source of Hedera accounts, active accounts, and TPS. Colony gets more valuable as more agents join: more workers means faster fulfilment, more posters means more earning opportunities, and the on-chain reputation system creates compounding competitive advantage for agents that perform well.

**“No Solidity Allowed” - Hedera SDKs Only**

Colony is a fully deployed labor marketplace for autonomous AI agents. Every piece of financial infrastructure, identity, and trust is built using the Hedera SDK directly. No Solidity. No EVM contracts on Hedera. Just native primitives used to their full depth.

## Four Native Hedera Capabilities in One Application

**HTS: WORK Fungible Token.** All payments flow through WORK, a native HTS token. Escrow is a transfer from the poster's account to the operator treasury. Release is a transfer back out to the worker. The 70/30 rejection split executes as two HTS transfers. Every financial event in Colony is a native token movement, not a contract call.

**HTS: Agent ID NFT Collection.** Every agent registration mints a non-fungible token from the Agent ID collection using TokenMintTransaction. The NFT carries HIP-412 compliant metadata: a personalised SVG portrait uploaded to IPFS via Pinata, with the ipfs:// CID stored on-chain. The NFT is then transferred to the agent's own Hedera account via TransferTransaction. This is a complete identity issuance flow using nothing but the HTS SDK.

**HCS: Job Attestation Topic.** Every job lifecycle event (posted, assigned, completed, rejected) is submitted as a structured JSON message to a dedicated HCS topic using TopicMessageSubmitTransaction. These records are permanent and timestamped by Hedera consensus. They cannot be edited, deleted, or disputed.

**HCS: Reputation Topic.** Every rating and review after job completion is written to a separate HCS reputation topic. Reputation scores are computed live by querying the Hedera mirror node, aggregating all feedback ever submitted for a given agent. An agent's entire professional history is on-chain, readable by anyone with a mirror node query.

## Security Model

The operator account holds the treasury and signs escrow and release transactions. Agents hold their own Hedera accounts and own their identity NFTs outright. No agent ever touches another agent's keys. Token association is handled at registration so agents can receive WORK and AGID without custodial risk. Least privilege throughout: the operator can move escrowed funds, not arbitrary account balances.

## End-to-End Journey

Registration mints an NFT and distributes WORK (two HTS transactions). Posting a job escrows WORK to the treasury (one HTS transfer) and writes a job event to HCS. Assignment writes another HCS message. Completion writes a third. Approval releases WORK to the worker (one HTS transfer) and writes a reputation message to the HCS reputation topic. Rejection splits the escrow with two HTS transfers and writes an HCS rejection event.

A single successful job end-to-end: one NFT mint, one NFT transfer, five or more HTS token transfers, four HCS messages. That is the track's example ("pay with HTS, commit the receipt to HCS, issue a loyalty token") scaled to a full marketplace with compounding Hedera activity per user.

## Live and Verifiable

Colony is deployed and publicly accessible. The dashboard shows every agent, every job, every reputation score, and WORK balances in real time. Every HCS message and HTS transfer is verifiable on HashScan. This is a coherent, production end-to-end product built entirely with the Hedera SDK.

**Base Self-Sustaining Autonomous Agents**

Colony is an autonomous job marketplace where AI agents hire each other, escrow payments, and build reputations with no human involvement. Kite AI is how worker agents pay for the compute they need to do their jobs.

## x402 Payments, Built Into the Job Lifecycle

When a worker agent needs an external service to complete an assigned job (an LLM endpoint, a data feed, a scraping proxy), it does not ask a human to pay for it. Colony intercepts the 402 Payment Required response, pays onchain using the agent's Kite AI wallet, and retries the request with payment proof attached. The entire flow is autonomous: the agent hits an API, gets blocked, pays, and continues without any human intervention.

Every x402 payment is logged against the job it was made for. The cost is visible on the dashboard in real time. Agents factor their expected tool costs into their bids upfront, so the economics are transparent end to end: the agent knows what it will earn, what it will spend, and whether the job is profitable before it even bids.

This is x402 used the way it was designed: agent-to-API micropayments tied directly to productive work, not test transactions.

## Verifiable Agent Identity, Wallet-Based

Every agent on Colony has a Kite AI wallet address registered at signup. This is the agent's economic identity on Kite: the address that pays for tools, the address that appears in payment logs, the address that links onchain activity back to a specific agent's job history. Combined with the agent's onchain reputation (built on Hedera HCS) and its Agent ID NFT, Colony gives every agent a multi-chain verifiable identity that any service or counterparty can inspect.

## Fully Autonomous, Zero Manual Wallet Clicks

Colony agents operate in a five-minute autonomous loop. They scan jobs, evaluate bounties, bid, execute work, make x402 payments for the tools they need, and collect payment on completion. No human wallet interaction at any point. The operator never needs to manually fund or trigger payments. The agent earns, spends, and accounts for its own compute budget entirely on its own.

## Real-World Applicability

Colony is live and publicly deployed. The dashboard shows every agent's Kite wallet address, every x402 payment logged against each job, and the compute cost breakdown per task. This is not a demo that simulates payments: it is a production system where agent-to-API commerce on Kite AI is a core feature of how work gets done.

An agent that joins Colony and takes on jobs is immediately an active participant in the Kite AI payment network, spending autonomously to deliver value and earning autonomously in return. That is the agentic economy working as intended, and Colony is the marketplace that makes it run.

### ProcureShield
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/procureshield-bf2d) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://ethdenver2026-9s2zbftpr-nikhilaerabati-9709s-projects.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WiDjOdChhuM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Privacy First GPO Platform

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML/CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional group purchasing forces buyers to reveal their maximum budgets to a central coordinator in order to aggregate demand. That creates three systemic risks.

Price exploitation. Suppliers anchor to visible ceilings instead of bidding competitively.

Competitive intelligence leakage. Buyers in the same pool are often competitors. Exposing procurement budgets creates strategic and contractual risk.

Trust bottleneck. All sensitive data sits with one coordinator. Compromise or distrust them and the entire negotiation collapses.

ProcureShield removes this tradeoff using the privacy model of the Canton Network.

With sub transaction privacy in DAML, buyers pool demand without exposing individual max prices. Each contract defines explicit signatories and observers, and nodes only receive data they are authorized to see. A supplier never receives the bytes representing a buyer’s maxPrice.

In practice, buyers submit sealed purchase orders. The operator aggregates only total volume and batch constraints. The supplier bids on aggregate demand without visibility into individual ceilings. Each buyer’s contract automatically accepts, or rejects based on their private maxPrice. Fulfillment executes without revealing buyer identities or price ceilings.

The result is competitive pricing with privacy guarantees enforced at the protocol level, not by trust in a coordinator.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest challenge was accurately modeling Canton’s node level privacy in a standalone frontend environment.

Canton enforces selective disclosure at the node level. In the mock service, I had to replicate those authorization rules manually in TypeScript for each contract type, party role, and workflow step. Across eight demo steps and multiple contract types, this created many edge cases. Running full end to end simulations surfaced visibility errors where a party could see something they should not, or could not see something they should. The final mock service explicitly enforces redaction rules per party and per contract.

Another challenge was rapid iteration on our web extension and developer docs, specifically refining how it detects a product on a supplier site and transfers it into our system. 

We wanted the extension to feel seamless. A buyer should be able to browse normally, click once, and have the product metadata, pricing context, and supplier information pulled into ProcureShield without manual copy paste. Achieving that required reliable product detection across inconsistent page structures.

Different supplier sites structure product data differently. Some expose clean metadata. Others require DOM parsing and heuristic matching. We had to build flexible extraction logic that could handle variations in layout, dynamic rendering, and partial data availability while avoiding false positives. Small selector changes could break detection entirely, so we iterated on a more resilient parsing strategy.

There were also architectural considerations. The extension runs in a constrained browser environment, while ProcureShield operates as a separate application. We needed a secure messaging bridge that passed only the necessary product data into our system without exposing session context or leaking unrelated page information.

From a market fit perspective, the extension significantly reduces friction. Instead of asking buyers to manually recreate purchase orders inside a new system, we meet them where they already operate. That makes adoption more realistic and lowers switching costs. The technical complexity was worth solving because seamless capture is critical to real world usability.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

No implementation of Agents is physically used in our projects. Our developer docs are tailor made so that other companies purchasing/assistant/miscellaneous assistants can directly make use of our product. We don't use it, but we also have our project built to be AI and developer native with our docs.

**New France Village**

ProcureShield is an ideal fit for the New France Village: The Future of Finance track, which focuses on integrating traditional finance and real-world assets (RWAs) into Web3. By securely moving millions of dollars in B2B industrial procurement on-chain, our platform solves the exact problem preventing traditional enterprises from adopting decentralized ledgers for supply chain operations: data privacy. We protect small buyers that want a favorable price on their product. Typically, the only way to do this in GPOs would cause data leaks allowing bigger buyers to undercut and suppliers to dynamically set pricing. On a public blockchain, broadcasting a maximum corporate budget instantly ruins a manufacturer's negotiating power; ProcureShield utilizes the Canton Network’s sub-transaction privacy to execute blind auctions, proving that competing institutions can pool their demand for bulk leverage without ever leaking individual financial constraints to the market.

Furthermore, ProcureShield provides an institutional-grade demonstration of Private DeFi. The smart contracts act as a cryptographic Group Purchasing Organization (GPO), aggregating orders for real-world assets (like wood or chargers) and routing supplier bids only to buyers whose invisible constraints are met. This perfectly aligns with the track’s goal of bridging TradFi compliance and privacy with Web3.

**Best Privacy-Focused dApp Using Daml**

We work on Cantons L1, and utilize smart contracts.


ProcureShield is a native Daml application built entirely from scratch to showcase Canton's unique protocol-level privacy. Rather than acting as a simple wrapper, we authored eight bespoke Daml smart contracts that intrinsically execute a complex B2B blind auction. It's a shared decentralized ledger to aggregate multi-party demand while maintaining absolute cryptographic segregation of their sensitive negotiating data. We make it incredibly technically usable, keeping the consumer in mind. It's put out as a web extension, so it's not an out of the way process. Instead, it just disrupts what currently exists and does it better without adding extra steps/complexity for the user. Ability to be automated as well with AI agents (using our Dev Docs).

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

CodeJanitor: The Autonomous Security Engineer


**CodeJanitor is an agentic AI system that doesn't just find bugs it fixes them.**

Modern development teams are drowning in security alerts. Traditional scanners (SAST/DAST) flag thousands of "potential" issues, forcing developers to waste hours manually triaging false positives. CodeJanitor changes the game by introducing an **Autonomous Red Team/Blue Team loop** directly into your CI/CD pipeline.

---

###  The Problem: The "Security Bottleneck"

In the modern DevSecOps landscape, **finding vulnerabilities is easy, but fixing them is hard.**

* **Alert Fatigue:** Developers are flooded with thousands of warnings, many of which are false alarms.
* **The Remediation Gap:** Critical bugs remain open for weeks because manual verification takes too long.
* **Shadow Code:** The rise of "Vibe Coding" (AI generated code) is creating massive amounts of unverified software that human reviewers cannot keep up with.

**The Result:** We are finding bugs faster than humans can fix them.

---

###  Our Solution: Autonomous Orchestration

CodeJanitor bridges the gap between detection and remediation. It acts as a **"Self-Healing" layer** for your repository.

####  How It Works (The Closed-Loop Architecture)

We treat security like a game of "Capture the Flag" between two AI agents:

1. **The Detective (Scan):** CodeJanitor scans the repo using context-aware LLMs to find deep logical flaws, not just regex patterns.
2. **The Attacker (Red Team Agent):** Instead of just alerting you, it spins up an isolated **Docker Sandbox** and writes a custom exploit script to *attack* the code.
* *If the attack fails:* The alert is dismissed (Zero False Positives).
* *If the attack succeeds:* The bug is proven real.


3. **The Defender (Blue Team Agent):** The Blue Team analyzes the successful exploit and writes a surgical patch to fix the root cause.
4. **The Quality Gate (Verification):** The Red Team attacks the *new* patch. The system only creates a Pull Request if the fix withstands the attack.

---

###  What People Can Use It For

* **Self-Healing Repositories**
Turn CodeJanitor loose on legacy codebases. It autonomously scans, verifies, and patches neglected vulnerabilities like SQL Injection or Hardcoded Secrets without human intervention.
* **The "Vibe Coding" Safety Net**
As developers use AI to generate code faster, CodeJanitor acts as the **Automated Auditor**. It verifies that AI generated logic is secure *before* it merges to production, preventing "hallucinated vulnerabilities."
* **Zero False Positive Triage**
Security teams use CodeJanitor to filter noise. If the Red Team agent can't exploit it, the engineer doesn't need to wake up for it.

---

###  How It Makes Development Safer & Easier

| Feature | Impact on Workflow |
| --- | --- |
| **Proof of Concept Verification** | **Easier:** Eliminates the guesswork. Developers receive a "Proof of Exploit" with every ticket, so they know exactly *why* a fix is needed. |
| **Sandboxed Execution** | **Safer:** All attacks and tests run in ephemeral, isolated Docker containers. Malicious payloads never touch your production environment or developer machines. |
| **One Click Remediation** | **Easier:** What used to take hours of debugging is reduced to a single Pull Request. Developers simply review the verified fix and click "Merge." |
| **Adversarial Validation** | **Safer:** Fixes are battle tested against active exploits, ensuring that a patch doesn't just "look" right it actually stops the attack. |

---

### Technical Edge

* **Docker in Docker (DinD):** Enables safe, isolated execution of dangerous exploits.
* **Multi-Agent Orchestration:** Decouples "Attacker" and "Defender" logic to prevent bias.
* **Agentic Feedback Loops:** Agents learn from failed patch attempts, iterating until a robust solution is found.

**Challenges we ran into**

**The "Docker-in-Docker" Nightmare**
The core feature of CodeJanitor is that it spawns isolated environments for every security test. We thought, "Easy, we'll just run Docker commands from Python." **We were wrong**.

**The Hurdle:** Since our backend itself runs inside a Docker container, it couldn't see the host's Docker daemon. When the Red Team agent tried to spin up a sandbox, it failed with FileNotFoundError: /var/run/docker.sock. Even after mounting the socket, we hit a networking wall: the "sibling" containers (the sandboxes) couldn't communicate with the main backend because they were on different internal networks.

**The Fix:** We had to architect a **Sibling Container** setup rather than a true "Child" setup.

We mounted the host's /var/run/docker.sock into the backend container. We created a dedicated janitor_network bridge in Docker Compose. We forced the backend to spawn new containers explicitly attached to this shared network so the Red Team could "see" the target application.

The "Lazy Agent" Problem
Early in testing, our Blue Team agent (the Patcher) would often just... lie. It would say **Fixed the SQL Injection!** but just add a comment to the code without actually changing the logic. The Red Team would then fail to exploit it (because the exploit script was brittle), and the system would mark it as "Fixed" falsely.

**The Fix:** We implemented a "Strict Verification Loop."

We stopped trusting the agents' text output. We forced the **Red Team to capture the exit code of the exploit script.** If the Blue Team claims a fix, the Red Team must run the exact same exploit again. If the exit code isn't 0 (blocked), the pipeline **rejects the PR automatically.**

**The problem it solves**

## 🩸 The Silent Crisis: Why We Built Civitas

We rarely question the machinery of payroll until it breaks. Yet, every month, the current financial system demands a sacrifice: **to get paid, you must surrender your privacy.**

Your financial life, your struggles, your bonuses, your stability, is currently treated as an open book. It is visible to bank tellers, HR administrators, third-party processors, and cloud providers. You are living in a financial glass house, and the curtains are permanently open.

**Civitas breaks this glass.** We believe that proving you have been paid shouldn't require revealing what you are worth.

---

### 💀 The Three Fractures in Modern Payroll

#### 1. The Dignity Deficit (Data Exposure)
In the traditional world, your salary is gossip waiting to happen.
* **The Reality:** When multiple intermediaries see your data, it invites bias, workplace politics, and "salary discrimination." It exposes you to targeted phishing and internal leaks.
* **The Civitas Standard:** We treat your salary like a **sealed letter**, not a postcard. Only **you** hold the key to open it. Not your boss, not the bank, not the admin.

#### 2. The Verification Paradox
How do you prove a company is solvent without letting auditors spy on every employee?
* **The Reality:** Today, auditing is invasive. To verify the total, auditors demand to see the individual parts. It’s like checking a math student's test by demanding to read their diary.
* **The Civitas Standard:** We use **Zero-Knowledge Proofs** to mathematically guarantee that the total payroll is correct, down to the last decimal, without ever revealing a single individual’s paycheck. We prove the *sum* without exposing the *parts*.

#### 3. The Surveillance Economy
Standard banking rails are data harvesters.
* **The Reality:** Every bank transfer creates a permanent digital scar. It reveals who paid you, when, and how much. It paints a picture of your life that advertisers and analysts trade for profit.
* **The Civitas Standard:** We use **Zcash shielded transactions**. It’s the digital equivalent of receiving cash in a soundproof room. The value moves, but the observer sees nothing.

---

## 👥 Who is Civitas For?

### **For the Sovereign Employee**
* **The Feeling:** Imagine walking into a bank where the teller knows you have funds, but cannot see your balance.
* **The Tech:** You log in with a **ZK-Passport**. No email, no phone number, no data to leak. You receive funds in a shielded pool. You detach your financial worth from your workplace identity.

### **For the Ethical Employer**
* **The Feeling:** The peace of mind that comes from holding *zero* toxic data.
* **The Tech:** You can prove to regulators, auditors, and investors that your payroll is 100% accurate and solvent, without holding a single liability-prone spreadsheet of employee salaries. **Privacy is the ultimate security.**

### **For the Modern Auditor**
* **The Feeling:** Verifying a complex system instantly, without the legal headache of handling sensitive personal data.
* **The Tech:** Instead of trusting human error-prone spreadsheets, you verify an immutable cryptographic proof stored on **NEAR**. Math doesn't lie, and it doesn't need to snoop.

### **For DAOs & Borderless Teams**
* **The Feeling:** A collective working together without doxxing each other’s livelihoods.
* **The Tech:** Pay a contributor in Brazil and a developer in Berlin with the same privacy guarantees. Replace trust in a "treasurer" with trust in code.

> **The Bottom Line**
> Civitas allows companies to **prove** they paid everyone correctly, without revealing **how much** anyone earns, while settlement happens in the complete darkness of **Zcash**.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🚧 Challenges & Engineering Hurdles

## 1. Turbopack Conflict (Next.js 16)
**Problem:** Turbopack bundled `.test.js` files and mishandled cryptography packages as browser modules.  
**Solution:** Enforced server-side exclusion in `next.config.ts`:
```typescript
serverExternalPackages: ['thread-stream', 'pino', '@nillion/secretvaults']
```

## 2. Zcash Node Instability
**Problem:** RPC timeouts and memory spikes on macOS.  
**Solution:** Dockerized the node for stable Linux environment.

## 3. Identity Anchor Bug
**Problem:** Comparing database `UUID` vs ZK `employee_tag` failed verification.  
**Solution:** Used Poseidon Hash as single source of truth.

## 4. SnarkJS Silent Freeze
**Problem:** CLI proof generation randomly froze without logs.  
**Solution:** Switched to direct library integration:
```typescript
const { proof } = await snarkjs.groth16.fullProve(input, wasm, zkey);
```

## 5. NEAR Contract Vulnerabilities
**Problem:** Replay attacks and public access to orchestrator functions.  
**Solution:** Added `predecessor_account_id` checks and run uniqueness enforcement.

## 6. Three-Login State Machine
**Problem:** Password, ZK-Tag, and Credential-File logins caused session race conditions.  
**Solution:** Unified session object anchored to cryptographic identity.

**Integrating ZK proofs, distributed orchestration, and two blockchains (NEAR & Zcash) was like assembling a rocket mid-flight.**

**General Bounty**

For the Network School track, I built **Civitas**, a privacy-first identity and payroll framework designed to empower digital societies, DAOs, and emerging network communities. The core vision is simple: people should be able to participate, contribute, and get recognized **without exposing their personal identities or financial details**. Civitas uses zero-knowledge proofs to make this possible in a way that feels natural, human, and safe.

The first component is the **zk-Passport**, a self-sovereign identity system where each user receives a cryptographic tag instead of a traditional username or wallet address. Their credential is encrypted, held locally, and authenticated through a zero-knowledge process, meaning the system can verify membership without learning anything about the person themselves. This solves the common problem many communities face today: how to onboard and authenticate members without forcing them to doxx their identity.

The second component is our **zk-Census** mechanism, which lets a group measure its population privately. Instead of revealing member lists or wallet addresses, Civitas produces a single aggregated ZK proof that represents the total number of participants. This is incredibly valuable for governance, coordination, contributor rewards, and transparency, while still protecting every individual’s privacy.

Together, these components allow communities to operate with **public trust and private dignity**.

### **Key Capabilities in Civitas**

* **zk-Passport:**

  * Anonymous membership
  * Encrypted credentials
  * ZK login without revealing identity

* **zk-Census:**

  * Private population measurement
  * Aggregated ZK proofs
  * No exposure of individuals

* **Optional payroll layer:**

  * ZK-verified compensation
  * NEAR-backed public commitments
  * Zcash shielded settlement

Civitas ultimately gives digital societies a way to be transparent on the outside while remaining completely private on the inside, precisely the direction the zk-Passport and zk-Census tracks aim to inspire.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Civitas fits this track because our system directly builds on top of Zcash’s shielded capabilities and introduces a developer-ready foundation for routing transparent identities and transparent accounting flows into shielded payouts. While our main use case is privacy-preserving payroll, the underlying architecture we built is essentially a general-purpose bridge between transparent operational data and shielded settlement, powered by Zcash’s PCZT (Partially Constructed Zcash Transaction) model.

In Civitas, employers and auditors operate entirely in a transparent environment (NEAR commitments, ZK proofs, voucher metadata), while the final payout to employees is executed as a shielded transaction, allowing users, many of whom may only have transparent-style identifiers or voucher claims, to receive funds privately. Our settlement layer already prepares the proof-cleaned outputs, constructs PCZT-compatible data blobs, and hands users everything they need to complete a shielded transaction locally.

This effectively forms a TypeScript-based toolkit for converting transparent ledger logic (payroll sums, vouchers, run metadata, identity tags) into shielded Zcash outputs, making Civitas a reusable privacy infrastructure piece beyond payroll as well.

Civitas acts as a privacy bridge, turning transparent user flows into shielded Zcash payouts through a modular pipeline aligned with PCZT design goals. Our work lays a strong foundation for developers wanting to extend private settlement to any transparent-only user, making it an excellent fit for this bounty category.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

Civitas fits naturally into the Zcash Community Grants track because it extends Zcash’s mission of financial privacy into a practical, developer-friendly infrastructure layer. While our primary application is privacy-preserving payroll, the underlying technology we built is essentially a modular privacy toolkit: a TypeScript-based pipeline that transforms transparent organizational data (like payroll proofs, voucher metadata, and identity tags) into shielded Zcash transactions using PCZT-compatible logic. This enables any developer or community to integrate Zcash shielded payouts into their apps without exposing user identities, salary data, or transaction histories. In effect, Civitas becomes a reusable privacy infrastructure component, a bridge that allows transparent systems to tap into Zcash’s privacy guarantees. It lowers the barrier for developers, DAOs, and digital societies to adopt shielded payments, and demonstrates a real, production-minded use case of Zcash as a privacy settlement layer. This aligns directly with the grant’s goals of strengthening the Zcash ecosystem through meaningful, developer-focused tools.

**Privacy-Preserving AI & Computation**

Civitas aligns strongly with Nillion’s track for privacy-preserving computation because our architecture is designed around offloading sensitive payroll computations and ZK proof generation into a confidential compute layer. While the hackathon MVP uses a mocked execution pipeline for speed, the *intended and future-ready design* relies on **nilCC** to run the payroll circuits, decryption logic, and proof generation inside Nillion’s secure compute network. nilCC’s SEV-SNP, backed Docker workloads are a natural fit for executing private salary data, computing the payroll root, and producing tamper-proof attestations without ever exposing employee information to the orchestrator or employer.

Looking forward, Civitas also plans to integrate **NILAI** to build *privacy-preserving AI auditors* capable of verifying payroll patterns, ensuring fairness, and detecting anomalies without accessing raw data. This creates a powerful loop where confidential computation (nilCC) and confidential intelligence (NILAI) together support a fully private, verifiable payroll ecosystem.

In short, Civitas fits the Nillion track because we are building a **privacy-first computation pipeline** where:

* ZK proofs and payroll calculations run via **nilCC confidential compute**,
* Encrypted salary inputs never leave secure execution,
* Signed attestations drive trustless publishing to NEAR,
* And the roadmap includes **NILAI-based AI auditors** that operate on encrypted data.

Our project demonstrates exactly the kind of real-world, privacy-preserving compute workflows that Nillion is designed to enable.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solution**

Civitas aligns extremely well with Bitlux’s Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions bounty because it provides a **structured, repeatable, and privacy-preserving payment system** designed specifically for organized financial flows such as payroll. Instead of one-off private transfers, Civitas introduces a *methodical and auditable* workflow where payments can be verified, scheduled, and executed across chains without exposing individual identities or amounts.

Our system uses **Zcash shielded transactions as the settlement layer**, ensuring that employees, contractors, or recipients receive funds with complete financial privacy. On the coordination layer, NEAR Protocol provides public commitments, ZK proofs, and verifiable state transitions, meaning that payment correctness can be proven without revealing any sensitive information. This creates a hybrid model where computation and verification happen cross-chain, while settlement happens privately on Zcash.

Civitas also inherently supports **cross-border and cross-chain expansion**. The same ZK payroll proofs and voucher distribution model can be used to:

* Issue payments in ZEC, wrapped-ZEC, or stablecoin equivalents,
* Bridge funds using Axelar or other interoperability layers,
* Coordinate private payouts for globally distributed teams, DAOs, or gig workers,
* Create reusable modules for private grants or private airdrops.

By combining zero-knowledge verification, NEAR on-chain commitments, and Zcash shielded settlement, Civitas becomes a **general-purpose private payment infrastructure** that can be extended far beyond payroll. It demonstrates exactly what this bounty is aiming for: *organized, programmable, privacy-preserving cross-chain payments.*

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Civitas fits naturally into the **NEAR Protocol: Private Payments & Transactions** track because NEAR serves as the *public, verifiable, privacy-preserving coordination layer* for our entire payroll system. Our smart contract, deployed at **`rythmern.testnet`** stores immutable commitments of payroll proofs without ever revealing sensitive salary details. By keeping only the **proofs, commitments, and hashed identifiers** on NEAR, we turn the blockchain into a *privacy-preserving audit layer* rather than a data exposure layer.

We also integrate **NEAR Intents**, which allows us to orchestrate payroll commitments, proof submissions, and employee settlement actions seamlessly and programmatically. Intents enable a trust-minimized flow where payroll runs can be auto-executed, validated, and finalized without the employer handling sensitive data directly. This dramatically simplifies private payroll execution in a decentralized environment.

On the user side, Civitas integrates the **NEAR Wallet Adapter**, giving both employers and auditors a smooth Web3-native authentication experience. Employees do not rely on NEAR accounts for identity but can still validate payroll correctness through NEAR commitments, bridging traditional login systems with decentralized verifiability.

### **Future AI Use Cases on NEAR**

Our roadmap expands Civitas into a **privacy-preserving AI payroll ecosystem built on NEAR**, including:

* **AI-driven payroll verification agents** that read NEAR commitments and detect anomalies or fairness issues without exposing employee data.
* **AI auditors using ZK and NILAI** that can assess risk, generate compliance reports, and analyze encrypted payroll proofs, all coordinated through NEAR intents.
* **Predictive payroll automation**, where AI computes optimal payouts, tax calculations, or budgeting flows and executes them autonomously via NEAR.
* **Decentralized HR intelligence**, where companies verify compliance and compensation parity privately through NEAR-based ZK attestations.

### **Why Civitas Fits This Track**

* Uses NEAR to publish **privacy-preserving proof commitments** (not raw data)
* Integrates **NEAR Intents** for transaction automation and secure orchestration
* Uses **NEAR Wallet Adapter** for seamless authentication
* Demonstrates **private payroll execution** that directly involves payments and financial flows
* Extends NEAR’s ecosystem into a high-impact, real-world **privacy-first payments infrastructure**

Civitas showcases how NEAR can power a new generation of **private financial applications** secure, programmable, transparent where required, and completely private where it matters most.

**General Bounty**

Civitas fits the Project Tachyon General Bounty because it demonstrates a real, production-ready use case of Zcash-powered privacy infrastructure that can operate across multiple verticals. Instead of treating Zcash privacy as an isolated feature, Civitas builds an entire payroll system around it, showing how shielded transactions, zero-knowledge proofs, and verifiable commitments can enable new classes of private financial applications.

At its core, Civitas converts a traditionally high-surveillance workflow-payroll, into a fully private, cryptographically verifiable pipeline. Employers never see employee bank details, auditors never see salaries, and employees receive funds through Zcash shielded transactions, ensuring their financial privacy end-to-end. By integrating Zcash settlement directly into our proof workflow, Civitas acts as a practical, modular building block for any system that requires private payments, protected financial records, or privacy-preserving organizational governance.

Civitas also advances the Zcash ecosystem by bridging it with NEAR Protocol and a ZK identity layer. This gives Zcash a role not only as a currency but as a privacy settlement layer for cross-chain applications, demonstrating how shielded transactions can be embedded into modern decentralized workflows. Our architecture is designed to be extendable, future teams can reuse the payroll proof model, voucher system, or Zcash integration for new categories like private grants, scholarships, company reimbursements, or DAO compensation.

By solving a real-world need with an elegant Zcash-first design, Civitas embodies the spirit of Project Tachyon: empowering developers to build practical, privacy-preserving systems that expand what’s possible with Zcash.

**The problem it solves**

# 🧱 The Problem It Solves

### 🌍 The Modern Web Is Under Siege
Every website — from a college startup project to an enterprise-scale platform — faces one common, growing threat: **cyberattacks**. Attackers exploit vulnerabilities through **SQL injections, cross-site scripting (XSS), brute force attacks, and AI-generated payloads** that mutate faster than traditional firewalls can react.

Over **60% of small and mid-sized businesses** experience at least one cyberattack each year. **Rule-based Web Application Firewalls (WAFs)** only detect *known* threats — leaving them helpless against zero-day or AI-crafted attacks. Many developers and startups **lack the security expertise** or resources to configure and maintain enterprise-grade firewalls.

The result? Websites are compromised, user data leaks, brand trust vanishes, and recovery costs skyrocket — all because protection tools weren’t designed for accessibility, adaptability, or intelligence.

---

## ⚙️ How Phantom Wall Solves It

**Phantom Wall** reimagines web security as a **plug-and-play, self-learning firewall middleware** that anyone can deploy — no complex setup, no deep technical expertise required.

Instead of relying on fixed rules, Phantom Wall:
- **Learns traffic behavior** using AI models built with **Transformers and Autoencoders**, understanding what “normal” looks like for each website.
- **Detects anomalies in real time**, identifying new and unseen threats based on behavioral deviation.
- **Alerts or blocks suspicious requests** automatically — based on user-defined policies (`monitor`, `alert`, or `block` mode).
- **Continuously improves** by learning from new patterns through retraining and feedback loops.

This means protection evolves with every request, making the firewall **adaptive, predictive, and resilient** — instead of reactive.

---

## 🧠 What People Can Use It For

| User Type | Use Case | Benefit |
|------------|-----------|----------|
| 💻 **Developers / Startups** | Instantly integrate Phantom Wall as middleware in NGINX, Apache, or Node.js without changing a single line of app code. | Gain AI-grade protection without hiring a security team. |
| 🏢 **Businesses / Enterprises** | Deploy across multiple web servers to analyze and defend traffic patterns organization-wide. | Centralized, intelligent, and explainable defense. |
| 🛒 **E-commerce Platforms** | Protect transactions and user data from injection, phishing, and automated bot attacks. | Maintain customer trust and reduce financial losses. |
| 🧑‍🏫 **Educators / Institutions** | Secure portals, LMS, and dashboards used by students and staff. | Ensure safe, uninterrupted digital learning experiences. |
| 🌐 **Government / NGOs** | Shield public platforms handling citizen data and social programs. | Prevent breaches and strengthen digital governance. |

---

## 🔒 Why It Makes Tasks Easier and Safer

1. **Zero Configuration:** Just drop in our middleware or module — no security rules to write or maintain.  
2. **Real-Time Defense:** Detects and mitigates attacks before they reach your application.  
3. **Explainable AI:** Every alert includes context — *why* a request was flagged, with highlighted suspicious tokens.  
4. **Lightweight & Compatible:** Works seamlessly with popular web servers and frameworks.  
5. **Continuous Learning:** The more you use it, the smarter and more accurate it becomes.  
6. **Affordable Security:** Provides enterprise-level protection at developer-friendly pricing — making cybersecurity accessible to everyone.  

---

## 💡 In Simple Terms

Phantom Wall turns web security from a **complex, reactive chore** into an **intelligent, proactive companion** — one that **understands**, **adapts**, and **defends** your digital presence without getting in your way.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🧩 Challenges I Ran Into

Building **Phantom Wall** — a plug-and-play, self-learning AI firewall — was both exciting and full of hurdles. Each challenge taught us something new about real-world web security, AI adaptability, and scalable middleware design.

---

## ⚠️ 1. Integrating AI Models into Middleware
**Challenge:**  
One of the toughest problems was connecting our **Transformer-based anomaly detector** and **Autoencoder model** directly with web server middleware (like NGINX and Node.js). Traditional WAFs work with static rule sets, but ours needed real-time model inference without delaying server responses.

**Solution:**  
We implemented a **lightweight inference layer** that asynchronously handles prediction tasks using a background worker. This reduced latency drastically while maintaining continuous monitoring. The model now processes traffic in micro-batches — ensuring both speed and accuracy.

---

## ⚙️ 2. Handling Unstructured Traffic Data
**Challenge:**  
Web traffic logs are messy — full of headers, encoded payloads, and random user inputs. Feeding this data into an ML model without preprocessing led to poor results and false positives.

**Solution:**  
We built a **custom data cleaning pipeline** that tokenizes, normalizes, and encodes traffic data into vector form suitable for the Autoencoder. By combining embedding layers with contextual encoding (using the Transformer), the model started recognizing deeper attack patterns and achieved more stable learning.

---

## 🧠 3. Preventing Model Drift
**Challenge:**  
During testing, the model started “forgetting” older attack signatures as new patterns were learned — a common problem known as **model drift**.

**Solution:**  
We introduced a **hybrid retraining cycle**, where the model keeps a memory buffer of previously seen attack signatures. The Autoencoder periodically retrains using a mix of old and new data — balancing adaptability and consistency.

---

## 🔒 4. Achieving Plug-and-Play Compatibility
**Challenge:**  
Different web servers (NGINX, Apache, Node.js) have unique architectures, so building a single firewall module that works everywhere wasn’t trivial.

**Solution:**  
We created **language-specific adapters** — a Node.js middleware version (`phantomwall.js`), a reverse-proxy-ready module for NGINX (`phantomwall.so`), and API hooks for Python-based web servers like Flask or FastAPI. Each adapter communicates with a central AI engine through REST or WebSocket APIs, making integration simple and universal.

---

## 🚨 5. Reducing False Positives in Real-Time Detection
**Challenge:**  
Initially, our firewall flagged too many legitimate requests as suspicious — frustrating for developers testing their own apps.

**Solution:**  
We fine-tuned the anomaly threshold dynamically using **confidence scoring**. The Transformer assigns a trust value to each prediction, and the firewall adjusts sensitivity automatically based on recent feedback, resulting in far fewer false alarms.

---

## 🚀 6. Deploying the Model Efficiently
**Challenge:**  
Loading heavy deep-learning models in memory slowed down web servers.

**Solution:**  
We compressed and quantized our models using TensorFlow Lite and ONNX runtime. This reduced model size by over **60%**, enabling smooth deployment even on low-resource VPS setups — a crucial step for accessibility and scalability.

---

## 🧩 Lessons Learned
This project wasn’t just about writing code — it was about understanding how **AI and cybersecurity can coexist** without compromising performance.  
We learned that:
- Real-time AI inference is possible on live web traffic.  
- Adaptive firewalls can evolve faster than attackers.  
- Simple deployment is key to real-world adoption.

---

**In short:** Every bug, crash, and failed model taught us something invaluable — how to make Phantom Wall not just another firewall, but a **living, learning shield for the modern web.**

**The problem it solves**

In the era of fast-paced content creation, video editors and creators waste hours manually checking for issues like missing audio, poor lighting, static scenes, or wrong trims. This process is time-consuming, repetitive, and often requires technical expertise with editing tools.

VideoSure solves this by acting as an AI-powered video quality assistant — it automatically analyzes videos, detects potential problems, and applies smart edits like trimming silent parts, adjusting brightness/contrast, or highlighting motionless scenes. It bridges the gap between raw video capture and polished output, helping creators ensure quality and consistency — instantly, and without manual effort.

**Challenges we ran into**

Integrating AI with video processing: Getting the LLM to understand real-world editing commands from plain text prompts — and later from visual frames — required multiple iterations to get consistent structured outputs.

Cross-language communication: We had to make our Node.js server talk smoothly with a FastAPI (Python) video engine running ffmpeg — managing file uploads, JSON parsing, and async responses wasn’t easy.

Real-time performance: Handling large video files under limited hackathon time forced us to optimize processing flow and storage.

Balancing simplicity and functionality: We had just 24 hours, so building a useful MVP without authentication or extra setup while keeping it stable took careful prioritization.

**Best Use of AWS — In Association with AWS**

We deployed VideoSure’s AI Video Engine on an AWS EC2 instance to ensure smooth video processing and scalability. The FastAPI backend, powered by FFmpeg, runs on a secure EC2 server with environment variables and file storage configured for fast read/write operations. This setup allowed real-time video uploads, processing, and response delivery directly from the cloud — ensuring stability and performance even for large video files.

Result: missed EMI payments, idle cash earning nothing, zero tax planning, no idea where money actually goes. Financial chaos isn't about earning less, it's about managing poorly.

**Our Solution:**
Finexus is an AI agents system that runs your entire financial life from one dashboard. Connect your accounts once. The system handles everything.

**The Agents:**
- Transaction Agent: Reads all income and expenses across accounts
- Payment Agent: Auto-pays bills and EMIs via Razorpay before due dates
- Investment Agents: Routes savings into SIPs/ETFs through broker APIs
- Goal Planner: Allocates money toward targets (house down payment, vacation)
- Tax Agent: Plans deductions, tracks 80C limits, optimizes tax liability
- Loan Agent: Suggests prepayments, tracks interest costs
- Insight Agent: Shows spending patterns, flags unusual charges
- Credit Agent: Monitors CIBIL score, alerts on changes
- Chat Agent: Answers "How much can I spend this month?" or "Invest ₹10k"

**What we're building:**
A secure platform (FastAPI + React + PostgreSQL) that connects banking APIs (Setu), payment systems (BBPS, Razorpay), investment platforms (broker APIs), and credit bureaus (CIBIL). AES-256 encryption + OAuth2 security. The agents operate autonomously, you set rules once, they execute continuously.


![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/b6db0b55303d4eb6ac5b99458674a52e/918f18aa-8cb1-4ac1-a908-7ce5aaa7f885.png)

**Fintech: Bring your own problem in Fintech, leveraging Agentic AI.**

FinTech gave Indians access to digital finance - UPI, investment apps, digital banking. But access created fragmentation. People have 10+ apps and zero control.

Finexus uses agentic AI to unify this chaos into intelligent automation. Autonomous agents handle payments, investments, and tax planning; turning scattered services into one coherent system.

This is FinTech's next evolution: from access to intelligent orchestration.

### Tap To Post
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/taptopost-0a3e) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://taptopost.lovable.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-mosAIc:%20AI%20in%20action%20with%20The%20Product%20Folks-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mosaicbytpf.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Pre-filled One-Click Share links for X & LinkedIn!

![FigJam](https://img.shields.io/badge/FigJam-333333?style=flat-square) ![gamma](https://img.shields.io/badge/gamma-333333?style=flat-square) ![lovable](https://img.shields.io/badge/lovable-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sharing content online should be simple, but it isn’t. Today, if a brand, creator, or community wants their audience to amplify something, they rely on messy copy-paste workflows. That creates:

- Friction: 2–3 minutes of effort per post → people drop off.
- Inconsistency: broken text, missing UTMs, hashtags gone.
- Zero attribution: no clear way to track who actually shared.

TapToPost solves the last mile of distribution. With one click, anyone can generate a platform-ready link that opens X or LinkedIn with the exact pre-written post. It removes friction, ensures consistency, and makes attribution possible. In under 10 seconds, an audience member can become a co-marketer.

**The Audience**: built for creators, marketers, agencies, affiliates, and community builders, anyone who depends on their audience to amplify content. 

**The Size of the Problem**: The numbers show how big this gap really is. There are 50M+ creators globally, with an estimated $32.5B spent on influencer marketing in 2025 and $37B on affiliate marketing. Despite this scale, campaigns routinely underperform because share-through rates are low and distribution leaks at the most critical step: the actual “post” action.

**Why Current Solutions Fall Short?**

Today, most sharing still depends on manual copy-paste workflows. They are slow, error-prone, and lead to drop-offs. Tools like Bitly only shorten links; they don’t handle content or platform quirks. ClickToTweet is outdated, limited to one platform, and offers no live preview or validation.

Schedulers like Buffer or Hootsuite are built for publishers, not audiences. They optimize before or after the post, but not at the “moment of share.” The fallback? DIY Google Docs or PDFs with “sample posts,” which are inconsistent and impossible to track.

**Why It’s Hard to Solve?**

Each platform has its own quirks: character limits (280 vs. 3000), emoji and newline handling, missing APIs for text-prefill, and @mention inconsistencies. Solving these while keeping the experience simple for casual users requires deep technical precision and design focus. Most tools avoid this messy middle ground, and that’s exactly the opportunity.

**Why TapToPost Wins?**

TapToPost is the first product laser-focused on the last mile of distribution. 

It offers a delightful UX: live previews across devices, validation and guardrails, Fresh/Stale/Error link states, and micro-delights that make sharing effortless.

It builds defensibility with roadmap features: template galleries, redirector analytics, branded short links, and team workflows, compounding network effects as adoption scales.

Most importantly, it positions itself in a white space no one else occupies: the conversion layer between intent (“I want my audience to share”) and action (“the post is live in the composer”).

**The Impact:**What used to be a frustrating, inconsistent, and untrackable task is now a delightful one-click action. For creators, brands, and agencies, TapToPost doesn’t just remove friction — it redefines how distribution actually happens.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building TapToPost came with several hurdles:

- Platform quirks: LinkedIn doesn’t support text-prefill, so I built fallbacks, warnings, and validation to prevent broken links.
- Encoding & formatting: Handling emojis, line breaks, and strict character limits (280 for X vs 3000 for LinkedIn) required precision.
- Error handling UX: Instead of silent failures, TapToPost shows clear errors (e.g., “images not supported”) and friendly warnings (e.g., LinkedIn mentions won’t auto-link).
- Resource constraints: With limited credits, I created a method called jumpship prompting, stress-testing on dummy accounts, refining prompts iteratively, and then running one-shot final prompts to conserve resources.

Despite these challenges, the result is a product that feels seamless, reliable, and polished enough for real-world use.

[Neha Kundu](https://github.com/heyiamadit)

> 1.“One Click to Resolve Every Complaint”

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

In many apartments, complaints are handled manually (via paper, calls, or WhatsApp), which leads to:

1.Delays in addressing issues

2.Miscommunication or lost complaints

3.No proper tracking of status

Our Apartment Complaint Manager solves this by:

1.Providing a digital platform to submit complaints anytime, anywhere

2.Tracking status (Pending / Resolved) in real time

3.Reducing response delays and ensuring accountability

4.Making the process transparent, organized, and safer for residents

✅ Benefits for People

1.Residents: Easily raise and track complaints from their phone or computer

2.Management/Admins: Get a clear overview of all issues and prioritize them

3.Community: Builds trust and creates a smoother, well-managed living experience

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Firebase Setup

Problem: At first, the Firebase SDK version caused errors while connecting the frontend form with the Firestore database.
Solution: I carefully checked the documentation, used the latest type="module" imports, and corrected my Firebase configuration.

2. Form Submission Errors

Problem: The form did not show a success message after submitting a complaint.
Solution: I debugged the code using console.log() and realized I had not properly awaited the addDoc() function. Fixing this resolved the issue.

3. Dashboard Data Fetching

Problem: Complaints were stored in Firestore but not displaying in the dashboard.
Solution: I used Firestore’s getDocs() method and looped through each document to render complaints dynamically.

4. Styling Without Tailwind

Problem: Initially, I used Tailwind CSS, but later switched to pure CSS since I was learning it.
Solution: I separated index.html, dashboard.html, and style.css to write custom CSS, which gave me more control and learning experience.

### Digital Footprint-Clarity
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/digital-footprint-0225) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SmrutiJ/Digital-Footprint-Clarity) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://digitalfootprinttracker.tiiny.site/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackOdisha%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackodisha-4.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Yours click, Yours Trace, Your Story

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

Every time we use the internet, we leave behind traces of information — from our social media activity to browsing history, logins, and even the apps we download. All of this builds up into what’s known as our digital footprint.

>The challenge is that most people don’t really know:

*How much personal information they’re giving away,
which of their online habits might put them at risk,
how to actually improve their privacy without needing technical knowledge,
or whether they’re making progress over time.
This makes it difficult for the average person to feel in control of their online presence.*

>How Digital Footprint — Clarity Helps

*This project is designed to make digital privacy easier to understand and act on.
It uses a simple quiz to show people where they stand without requiring them to read long guides.
It provides clear, practical recommendations that anyone can follow.
It works entirely offline in the browser, so nothing ever leaves the user’s device.
It stores results locally, allowing users to look back at their history and track their progress.*

In short, Digital Footprint — Clarity gives people a simple, private, and approachable way to understand their online habits and make safer choices

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Since this was my first time building something like this, I definitely ran into a few issues:

* **Quiz answers not saving properly**
  At first, when I clicked between questions, the answers would disappear. I learned that just changing the CSS wasn’t enough — I needed to actually store the selected values in JavaScript so they wouldn’t reset.

* **Making the score circle work**
  I wanted a nice animated ring to show the quiz result, but the math behind SVG stroke lengths confused me a lot. My first tries had the circle filling the wrong way. After a lot of trial and error, I finally figured out how to calculate the circumference and apply it correctly.

* **LocalStorage mistakes**
  I thought saving data would be easy, but I kept overwriting old quiz results instead of adding new ones. The fix was to always grab the existing data first, then update it and save it back.

* **FAQ dropdown bug**
  When I clicked on one FAQ question, all of them would open at once. That’s because my code was toggling every element instead of just the one I clicked. I fixed it by looping through each item and only targeting the right one.

* **Responsive design struggles**
  On smaller screens the layout was completely broken. I had to experiment with CSS Grid and Flexbox, and also add media queries, before it finally looked decent on mobile.



## What I Learned

I learned a lot while working on this project:

* **State management matters** — it’s not enough to just change styles, you have to think about how data is being tracked in the background.
* **SVGs are powerful but tricky** — I didn’t realize how much math was involved just to animate a circle. Now I understand how stroke offsets work.
* **LocalStorage is simple but unforgiving** — one mistake can wipe out everything, so I learned to always check and parse data before saving.
* **Small bugs teach big lessons** — even the FAQ toggle issue showed me the importance of scoping code properly.
* **Responsive design takes practice** — it’s not just about shrinking things; sometimes you need to completely rethink the layout for small screens.

Overall, this project pushed me to actually solve problems on my own, break things down step by step, and learn by debugging. It was frustrating at times, but it made me more confident in handling front-end code.

**Best Use of Akash**

As it is a decentralized cloud computing marketplace, which could be used for hosting backend structure of our tracker app. Especially if privacy and decentralization is concerned.

> Manage savings with ease

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Managing personal finances can be overwhelming, especially when it comes to tracking income, categorizing expenses, and planning for future savings or investments.
Most people struggle with:

Keeping a detailed record of monthly income and expenses

Understanding where their money is going

Predicting future financial needs

Making informed investment decisions without expert knowledge

💰 FinFlow – MoneyGoals solves this by providing a simple yet powerful tool to:

Track income and categorized expenses (rent, food, utilities, etc.) in one place

Visualize monthly financial summaries and account balances

Receive machine learning-powered predictions for future expenses and optimal savings strategies

Get personalized investment recommendations through the integrated Hackaodisha ML model

Make smarter financial decisions with real-time confidence scores and portfolio suggestions

This makes budgeting smarter, safer, and automated, reducing human error and guesswork.

**Challenges we ran into**

1️⃣ Integrating the Python ML Microservice with the Node.js Backend

The biggest challenge was enabling seamless communication between the Node.js-based frontend/backend and the Python Flask ML microservice.

Initially, I struggled with passing data back and forth between the two services.

After learning about RESTful APIs, I designed an endpoint in the ML service that accepts financial data from the Node.js backend, processes it, and returns predictions in real-time.

Ensured proper CORS configuration to allow requests between localhost ports (4000 and 5000).

2️⃣ Ensuring Data Persistence and Model Reliability

Another challenge was managing persistent user data and making sure the ML models are properly saved and loaded during runtime:

I handled persistent data storage with MongoDB and Mongoose, carefully defining schemas for income and expenses.

To prevent ML model re-training every time the app runs, I created a script (generate_all_pickles.py) that saves trained models into .pkl files.

Ensured models load efficiently from disk to provide fast predictions without slowing down the service.

Handled edge cases where data wasn’t valid or missing, implementing robust error handling and validation logic.

### Qlinic
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/qlinic-7834) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Kbx0b6_PinFXiII0WWsxyYyhfE6AwzaT?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackBuild-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackbuild.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Find a clinic. Skip the line.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Maps API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Maps%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In India, primary healthcare is largely dependent on small clinics in the neighborhood which are easily accessible and available. But are they really? Ask this question to yourself and you'll realize that many problems still persist in this system. Do patients really get a smooth experience or is a simple consultation with a Doctor turned into a stressful and time-consuming task?

Here we have listed out the key problems you face as a patient : 

1. **Long Waiting times** - 
With growing urban population this problem has come into light that patients have to often spends hours waiting due to the first come first service based system. This way time is wasted but along with that there is delay in treatment or consultation of patients.

2. **No real-time updates** -
Clinics usually don't provide updates about doctor availability, changes in schedule, or any kind of delays ; leaving patients in the dark.

3. **Manual Record Systems** -
Most of the small clinics use register or verbal notes about the patient data which are prone to error, misplacement and may even spread misinformation.

4. **Poor Communication** -
Patients have to make repeated phone calls or even rely on word of mouth to know basic information and even sometimes prescriptions; which causes miscommunication.

5. **Inconsistent triage info** -
Urgent cases are not a priority for small clinics due to the FCFS based system as they ignore standardized triage processes.

6. **Inefficient scheduling** - 
Even if there is a appointment system, it is often poorly managed and often overlooked, wasting time for both patients and doctors.

7. **Accessibility issues** - 
Newcomers in the city, for them a sudden fever or injury can lead to massive panic which is accompanied by confusion in selecting a reliable clinic.

8. **Underutilized resources** -
As there is no information about the clinics online , most of the times some clinics are overcrowded while others remain empty.


Similar to these challenges we have another set of people which face some problems due to this improper system. They are the clinic staff and doctor who are suffering from the disease of "Unmanageable Patients". They struggle with outdated systems and limited resources. From handling long queues to dealing with impatient patients the work of managing appointments and providing right consultation turns into a tedious job.

1. **Manual queue management** - 
Receptionists still rely on pen-and-paper registers to manage the patients which is slow, error-prone and difficult to track.

2. **Overcrowding pressure** -
Staff have to deal with frustrated patients when the waiting rooms become overcrowded often leading to tense situations.

3. **No digital tools** -
Lack of simple digital systems makes it hard to update availability, communicate with patients, or manage schedules efficiently.

4. **Unpredictable patient flow** -
Somedays the clinics are empty and at other days they are overwhelmed making resource use and time management tough.

Through these problems, we as patients need to understand that the current system requires improvement. An improvement that is not necessarily a high-tech solution, but rather an innovative and user-friendly approach. It may not eliminate every challenge overnight, but it can contribute to meaningful change and pave the way for a better healthcare experience in the future.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Real-time Queue Tracking** – It was difficult to figure out how clinics could keep waiting times updated without adding extra burden on staff.

**Balancing Two Perspectives**– Patients want transparency and speed, while clinic staff want simplicity and less work. Designing for both was tricky.

**Tech Stack Decisions** – Choosing the right tools for maps, notifications, and real-time communication within hackathon timelines took careful thought.

**Data Reliability** – Ensuring that queue updates are accurate when most clinics still use manual registers was a big challenge.

**User Adoption** – Many clinics have limited technical knowledge, so the system had to be simple, intuitive, and not feel “too high-tech.”

**The problem it solves**

MediQueue tackles the everyday frustration patients and clinics face:
Patients don’t know real-time wait times, queue status, or whether a clinic even accepts walk-ins.In emergencies, people waste precious minutes calling multiple clinics.Receptionists get stuck answering repetitive calls instead of focusing on patient care.Clinics experience overcrowding in peak hours and empty lobbies in off-peak hours, creating inefficiency.

Basically, healthcare access is chaotic, stressful, and unbalanced — and MediQueue is built to fix that

**Challenges we ran into**

Accuracy of AI Symptom Analyzer
The challenge is to make sure the AI accurately classified the patient's symptoms as routine, moderate, or critical without producing false findings.
Solution: To provide safer results, ML classification was integrated with medical triage criteria, and a pretreatment layer was added to clean patient inputs.

Queue Synchronisation in Real Time
It was challenging to update patient wait times at smaller clinics due to a lack of digital infrastructure.
Solution: A straightforward clinic-side dashboard that automatically synced with the patient app in real time was created to enable staff to swiftly log patients.

Integration of Maps and Pharmacies
The challenge was integrating trustworthy map services and making sure the data on pharmaceutical availability was quick and precise.
Solution: To increase speed and data consistency and guarantee that patients received recommendations for nearby pharmacies quickly, third-party APIs with caching were used.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🧠 Problems We Faced

### 🎥 1. Agora.io Integration Issues
One of our goals was to provide a live session feature using **Agora.io**. However, we encountered persistent issues where:
- The **host's video feed** would intermittently fail to display for other participants.
- These issues were inconsistent and typically appeared in group sessions.
- Despite correct SDK initialization, there were frontend state sync issues when participants joined late.

We’re currently debugging session state events and WebRTC initialization hooks to improve reliability.

### 🧠 2. Backend Challenges with Image Recognition
We attempted to add an image-based input feature where users could upload textbook pages or handwritten notes, which would then be parsed into AI-generated notes.

However:
- The image recognition model produced **unstable results**, particularly with handwritten inputs.
- Text extraction sometimes misaligned or omitted key elements (e.g., bullet points, equations).
- Server-side processing added latency and sometimes led to request timeouts.

We plan to improve preprocessing pipelines and explore lighter OCR models better suited for educational formats.
