> From Crisis Response to Predictive Readiness

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![MQTT](https://img.shields.io/badge/MQTT-333333?style=flat-square) ![OAuth](https://img.shields.io/badge/OAuth-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square)

**Description of your solution**

1. What We Plan to Build

We plan to build MedIntel, an Agentic AI-powered hospital management system that enables healthcare institutions in India to predict, prepare, and proactively respond to sudden patient surges during high-risk periods such as major festivals, pollution peaks, and epidemic outbreaks.

MedIntel runs through a network of ten intelligent AI agents, each handling a specific hospital function. Together, they continuously analyze real-time data from hospital systems, IoT sensors, air quality indices, and health feeds to make predictive decisions and automate preparedness.

Forecasting & Resource Agent – Predicts patient inflow using time-series and environmental data.

Staff Optimization Agent – Recommends optimal shift plans using reinforcement learning.

Medical Supply & Inventory Agent – Forecasts shortages and automates reorders.

Equipment & Utility Agent – Triggers predictive maintenance for critical equipment.

Predictive Outbreak Agent – Detects early epidemic or pollution-related illness surges.

Telemedicine & Triage Agent – Routes mild cases to teleconsultation to reduce overcrowding.

Emergency Readiness Agent – Activates surge protocols and allocates critical care resources.

Coordination Agent – Synchronizes data between departments and ambulances.

Supply Chain Resilience Agent – Detects vendor delays and switches to alternates.

Community Health Agent – Sends verified advisories and health alerts in local languages.

By integrating with existing Hospital Management Systems (HMS) and IoT devices, MedIntel enables hospitals to move from reactive crisis management to predictive readiness — optimizing staff, supplies, and patient flow before emergencies occur.

2. What Specific Pain Points It Addresses

Indian hospitals often face chaos during patient surges caused by festivals, pollution spikes, or epidemics. These lead to overcrowding, shortages, and delayed care.

MedIntel addresses these real-world challenges through predictive analytics and automation:

Unpredictable patient surges: Forecasts demand using time-series and event data.

Staff shortages: Suggests balanced shifts and proactive scheduling.

Medical supply crises: Predicts consumption and triggers early reorder alerts.

Equipment breakdowns: IoT-based maintenance prevents ICU and O₂ failures.

Overcrowding: AI triage filters mild cases to teleconsultation.

Misinformation: Delivers verified multilingual health advisories.

Lack of coordination: Automates inter-department alerts and communication.

Fragmented data: Connects HR, patient, and inventory data into one knowledge graph.

Slow admin response: Provides predictive dashboards for quick, data-backed action.

Small hospital limitations: Modular cloud version supports resource-limited centers.

In short, MedIntel helps hospitals foresee, plan, and act early — preventing overload and improving patient safety during every crisis.

3. Who the Target Audience Is

The primary audience includes urban and semi-urban multi-specialty hospitals, district health centers, and state or municipal health departments that face operational strain during surges. These organizations need smart systems that integrate easily with their existing HMS and IoT infrastructure.

The secondary audience includes private hospital chains, NGOs, and telemedicine platforms aiming to enhance predictive healthcare management and crisis preparedness.

Ultimately, the end beneficiaries are citizens and patients who receive faster care, reduced wait times, and accurate health information. MedIntel strengthens India’s healthcare ecosystem — ensuring that no hospital is ever caught unprepared again.

4. What the GTM and Revenue Streams Look Like

MedIntel’s Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy follows a practical, phased approach.

In the first phase (0–6 months), we’ll pilot MedIntel in Delhi and other high-load cities, integrating with existing HMS and IoT systems to validate predictive accuracy, reduced wait times, and improved staff efficiency.

In the second phase (6–18 months), we’ll expand to State Health Departments and Smart City programs, providing real-time dashboards for hospital forecasting, outbreak detection, and regional coordination.

The third phase (18–36 months) will focus on a nationwide SaaS rollout, integrating MedIntel into popular hospital ERP systems such as eSanjeevani, Medanta HIS, and CareStack. Partnerships with government programs, insurance firms, and healthcare analytics companies will drive large-scale adoption.

Revenue Model:
The primary revenue stream will be a SaaS subscription (₹30–₹50 per bed/month). Additional sources include API integration fees, premium analytics dashboards for administrators, and Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) — anonymized health trends for insurers and research partners. CSR and government health grants will support subsidized rollout in public hospitals, ensuring inclusivity and large-scale impact.

**Healthtech: Manage unpredictable surges in patients during festivals, pollution spikes, or epidemics with an AI agent that autonomously analyzes data and recommends staffing, supply, and patient advisory actions in advance.**

The problem statement highlights how hospitals in India struggle with unpredictable patient surges during major festivals, seasonal pollution spikes, and epidemic outbreaks. These events lead to overcrowding, shortage of medical supplies, staff exhaustion, and delayed care. MedIntel fits this track perfectly because it is built specifically to solve these challenges through predictive hospital management. It enables hospitals to anticipate surges, plan resources in advance, and operate proactively instead of reacting after the crisis begins.

During high-demand periods like Diwali, pollution peaks, or epidemic outbreaks, hospitals are often unprepared because they lack forecasting and coordination systems. MedIntel addresses this through its Forecasting and Resource Agent, which studies hospital records, environmental data, and event patterns to predict patient inflow and bed demand. This allows administrators to plan staffing, allocate space, and secure supplies before the surge occurs. This predictive capability is at the core of the problem statement’s focus on readiness and prevention.

Staffing shortages and fatigue are common when patient numbers rise sharply. MedIntel’s Staff Optimization Agent uses data-driven scheduling to recommend shift rotations and staff allocations that maintain balance and prevent burnout. Hospitals can ensure that doctors and nurses are efficiently deployed where they are most needed.

Medicine and oxygen shortages often arise during crises. MedIntel’s Medical Supply and Inventory Agent tracks real-time consumption and predicts when supplies are likely to run low. It then alerts procurement teams to restock early. The Equipment and Utility Agent supports this effort by monitoring connected medical equipment and alerting staff before machines fail, improving reliability in intensive care units and oxygen systems.

Overcrowding and long waiting times are another major issue mentioned in the problem statement. MedIntel’s Telemedicine and Triage Agent helps reduce unnecessary footfall by screening mild or non-urgent cases online and guiding them to remote consultations. This ensures that hospital space and medical attention are available for those who need it most.

Coordination problems between departments and emergency units can delay treatment. The Coordination and Communication Agent solves this by sharing live updates between departments, laboratories, and ambulances, improving communication during peak load situations.

Epidemics and pollution-related illness surges often spread unnoticed until hospitals are overwhelmed. The Predictive Disease Outbreak Agent continuously analyzes health data, patient symptoms, and local conditions to identify signs of outbreaks early. This helps hospitals and authorities prepare and act before cases escalate.

Misinformation and panic also worsen situations during pollution peaks or epidemics. The Community Health Engagement Agent delivers verified health advisories and preventive messages in multiple languages, keeping the public calm and informed while reducing unnecessary hospital visits.

MedIntel also supports smaller and semi-urban hospitals that lack advanced digital infrastructure. Its cloud-based design allows such hospitals to access predictive insights and alerts through simple, cost-effective setups.

Overall, MedIntel fits this track because it addresses the exact issues described in the problem statement. It uses artificial intelligence to predict patient surges, prevent resource shortages, coordinate internal operations, and improve public communication. It transforms hospitals from reactive responders into proactive, prepared systems that can handle festival rushes, pollution-driven cases, and epidemic outbreaks with foresight and efficiency.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/weighnix-7768) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Abhivocopedia/Weighnix-DSUDEVHACK2.0/tree/main) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DevHack%202.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart LPG monitoring system

![MySQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino IDE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino%20IDE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart Programming Language](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart%20Programming%20Language-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL Server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL%20Server-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring tool suite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring%20tool%20suite-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We, **Team TheAPIcalypse**, have built a solution to one of the most common problems faced by the public — a **Smart LPG Monitoring System, WEIGHNIX.**

Many of us have experienced running out of gas in the kitchen during critical situations. **WEIGHNIX **solves this by sitting beneath your cylinder and continuously monitoring LPG usage through its weight.

But it’s not just a detection device — it’s smarter than that. WEIGHNIX is equipped with an LPG/Natural Gas sensor that immediately alerts you in case of gas leakage. It also notifies you when your cylinder is about to run out.

As it evolves into a pro version, WEIGHNIX will even be capable of automatically ordering and paying for a new cylinder, ensuring you never face such a problem again.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
Sensor & Frame Integration: Initially, the sensors and frame didn’t align properly, which caused hardware instability.

Debugging Issues: The debugging process turned out to be very time-consuming. Multiple bugs led to inaccurate values being displayed on the frontend.

Hosting Constraints: Due to technical issues with our sponsor’s platform (Vultr), we were unable to host and deploy the project there.

Live Demo Accuracy: The live demo values were not fully accurate because of complex calculations, wiring challenges, and circuit management.

Features : Adding too many features in parallel made the system more complicated than expected.
Simple Features were easy on paper but hard to implement in real world.

**Best build on Vultr Cloud**

It wasn't a very good experience because of them our cloud section in the plan came to an end

> Smart Knee Brace for Informed Rehab

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Un-informed knee-rehabilation. And if informed (usually through an MRI scan) is expensive. So, we introduce ortho onnect that measures the range of motion of knee and recommends rehab exercises. (Must be used under the guidance of a doctor).
Hence, ortho connect is not just a platform + equipment for knee injured people, but can be used by patients who can rely on lifestyle changes that  help in rehab.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Noise data from the MH6050 sensor - solved through preprocessing and training through ML model like Random Forest ALgorithm in google colab.
2. HC-05 cannot connect to modern browsers like chrome.(as they connect to BLE) - solved by assigning serial bluetooth port and enabling Experimental Web Platform Features in chrome.
3. n8n integration to a NoSQL type output - solved by creating csv output files of serial logs of output from json.
4 Migrating from local:5000 to firebase hosting - hosted MERN project to firebase through generated json
5. HC - 05 data send to in memory logs due to .env MONGODB_URI defined wrongly. - Created databse and cluster to use URI.
6. Creating recommended exercises for measured knee angle and other parameters - Connected to n8n workflow that takes serial input and gives json out of required data. This is stored in csv file. (use of python)

**Best Build for Kroolo**

Connected github repo to Kroolo and created plan for Project execution through AI for a span of 2 days.

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

MongoDB Atlas - NoSQL database created a collection in successful connection of HC-05 and MPU6050. Hence, being a scalable database that can store json files generated from sensor.

Homes
Get instant alerts if someone trespasses at night, with an automatic alarm or phone call to the owner.

Shops & Small Businesses
Detect break-ins or unusual activity after hours and trigger an emergency alarm or call the manager instantly.

Schools & Hostels
Monitor entry/exit points. If someone crosses restricted areas, staff are notified immediately via email or voice call.

Warehouses & Factories
Prevent theft or unauthorized access with real-time AI detection and sound an external siren.

Remote Locations (e.g., Farms, Construction Sites)
Stay connected even in areas with minimal human supervision. Hawkeye takes action on your behalf.

Hawkeye transforms surveillance from passive watching to proactive protection, giving users peace of mind with intelligent, immediate, and automated responses.

**The problem it solves**

RevvUp solves the problem of boring, scattered, and non-interactive ways of learning programming. Most learners struggle with retaining coding concepts, staying consistent, and tracking their progress. RevvUp gamifies the process by combining flashcards, quizzes, roadmaps, and progress analytics, making learning structured, engaging, and motivating. By introducing XP, CodeCoins, and achievements, it keeps learners hooked while also helping them focus on weak areas through analytics and practice tools.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the challenges I faced was figuring out how to take my project from a local environment to a live website. I had to understand how Vercel works, configure the project correctly for deployment, and ensure all the assets and routes worked after publishing. Another challenge was making sure the UI looked good across devices once it was online, since things sometimes displayed differently compared to local testing. Publishing on Vercel for the first time gave me valuable experience in deploying projects and making them production-ready.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🎯 **ReliefMap: Disaster Relief Platform Summary**

### **📋 App Overview**
- **Purpose**: Real-time disaster relief mapping and emergency response coordination platform
- **Target Users**: Disaster victims, first responders, volunteers, and emergency coordinators
- **Platform**: Desktop-only web application with mobile restrictions for optimal performance
- **Tech Stack**: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Firebase, OpenWeatherMap API, Google Maps

### **🚨 Problem Solved**
- **Real-time Disaster Coordination**: Provides live mapping of emergency reports, resources, and safe zones during disasters
- **Emergency Communication Gap**: Bridges communication between affected populations and relief organizations
- **Resource Allocation**: Helps coordinate volunteers, supplies, and emergency services efficiently
- **User Safety**: Delivers weather alerts, evacuation routes, and real-time safety information
- **Information Overload**: Organizes disaster data into actionable insights with visual mapping
- **Accessibility Issues**: Ensures desktop-optimized experience for critical decision-making during crises

### **⚡ Key Features**
- **Interactive Disaster Map**: Real-time visualization of reports, alerts, and resources using Leaflet
- **Emergency Alerts System**: Browser notifications with Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)
- **Weather Integration**: Live weather data and flood warnings via OpenWeatherMap API
- **Smart Navigation**: Google Maps directions from user location to emergency sites
- **WhatsApp Sharing**: Direct sharing of emergency reports with location and details
- **Authentication**: Google OAuth integration for secure user access
- **Performance Optimized**: Lazy loading, memoization, and responsive design for smooth UX


### **🌟 Impact & Value**
- **Emergency Response**: Enables faster coordination between victims and responders during disasters
- **User Safety**: Provides real-time weather alerts and evacuation guidance
- **Scalability**: Built with modern web technologies for high-traffic disaster scenarios
- **Accessibility**: Desktop-focused design ensures reliable performance in critical situations
- **Innovation**: Combines multiple APIs for comprehensive disaster intelligence
- **Production-Ready**: Optimized for deployment with security best practices

### **🚀 Technologies & APIs Used**
- **Frontend**: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet Maps
- **Backend**: Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Cloud Messaging)
- **APIs**: OpenWeatherMap, Google Maps, Nominatim Geocoding
- **Tools**: Vite, ESLint, PostCSS, Service Workers
- **Security**: Environment variables, secure API key management

**Challenges we ran into**

### **🔧 Challenges Faced**
- **API Authentication Issues**: OpenWeatherMap 401 errors due to incorrect API key configuration and endpoint changes
- **Performance Bottlenecks**: Slow loading of map components and report details due to unoptimized React rendering
- **Security Vulnerabilities**: Firebase API keys exposed in public service worker files
- **Mobile Responsiveness**: Balancing desktop-only restrictions with responsive design requirements
- **Real-time Data Integration**: Managing multiple APIs (Firebase, OpenWeatherMap, Google Maps) with error handling
- **Build Configuration**: Resolving TypeScript compilation errors and environment variable management
- **User Location Detection**: Handling geolocation permissions and fallback scenarios for directions

### **✅ Solutions Implemented**
- **API Fixes**: Switched to free-tier OpenWeatherMap endpoints, implemented proper error handling and fallbacks
- **Performance Optimization**: Applied React.memo, useMemo, useCallback, and lazy loading to components
- **Security Enhancement**: Removed hardcoded keys from service worker, implemented secure PostMessage communication
- **Desktop-Only Implementation**: Created device detection system with professional mobile restriction screen
- **Real-time Integration**: Built robust weather service with caching and graceful degradation
- **Build Resolution**: Fixed TypeScript errors, optimized bundle size, and ensured production-ready deployment
- **Location Handling**: Enhanced geolocation with permission management and coordinate validation

- **The overall setup of this project gets you feel that how real systems work like when we get notifications from government portal before severe crisis, floods, hurricane towards our state etc.**

### Med-Help
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/medhelp-e6b4) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://med-help.onrender.com/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/BOYvUA7qzWw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackOdisha%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackodisha-4.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Med-Help=Life Saving Platform

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In emergencies, people often struggle to find which pharmacy has the required medicine or which doctor is currently available. This leads to wasted time, stress, and even life-threatening delays. MedHelp solves this by providing real-time updates on medicine availability at nearby pharmacies and the current availability of doctors at clinics and hospitals.

It makes healthcare access faster, easier, and safer by:

Helping patients instantly locate the nearest pharmacy with the medicine they need.

Allowing users to see available doctors and book slots without confusion.

Reducing panic in critical situations through quick, reliable information.


This ensures people get the right treatment at the right time, ultimately saving lives.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced was integrating real-time updates for medicine availability and doctor slots. Ensuring that the data was accurate and refreshed quickly required us to carefully design the database and backend APIs.

We also struggled with connecting the frontend to the backend, especially while managing asynchronous requests from multiple users. Debugging database connection issues and handling authentication securely took more time than expected.

Another challenge was designing a user-friendly interface that works smoothly on both mobile and desktop, since in emergencies users cannot afford confusing layouts.

We overcame these hurdles through teamwork, dividing responsibilities between backend, frontend, and UI/UX design. We used MongoDB Atlas for cloud database, optimized API calls, and continuously tested the app to make sure it was reliable under real-world use cases.

# Elvo – Your AI-Powered Full-Stack Engineer

## 🚀 The Problem It Solves  
Building a new product is exciting—but let’s be real, it’s also painful.  
Developers waste countless hours setting up **frontend, backend, Docker, CI/CD, and deployment pipelines** before they can even test their core idea.  

**Elvo** fixes this. It’s a **full-stack + AI starter kit** that gets you from idea → prototype → production in record time.  

-  **Launch in minutes** – Pre-configured with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, Docker & Vercel.  
-  **AI-powered productivity** – Automates repetitive tasks, scaffolds boilerplate, and accelerates development.  
- **Production-ready out of the box** – No more wasting time on setup; focus on what makes your app unique.  
- **Safe & Reliable** – Opinionated defaults tested for full-stack harmony.  


---


## What You Can Use It For  
- **Hackathons & MVPs**: Turn your AI or web idea into a working app *same day*.  
- **AI Feature Testing**: Drop in your model endpoint, hook up the UI, and see it live instantly.  
- **Startups & Solo Builders**: Spend less time debugging config, more time building impact.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Keeping it Flexible but Opinionated** – Too many configs overwhelm developers, too few block creativity.  
  Solved by offering optional configs (Docker, CI/CD, etc.) while keeping defaults simple.  

- **AI Generation Consistency** – Early iterations of AI scaffolding produced inconsistent output.  
  Fixed with curated templates, prompt engineering, and logging for traceability.  

- **Smooth End-to-End Integration** – Ensuring Next.js, APIs, Docker, and Vercel deploys worked seamlessly.  
  Solved with end-to-end smoke tests and a modular architecture.

> AI-Powered Skilling & Employment Platform

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India faces a youth unemployment rate of ~15%, with 10–12 million new entrants joining
 the workforce each year. Existing platforms like the National Career Service (NCS) mainly
 provide job listings but fail to:
 Deliver accurate AI-based predictions on unemployment risks (mismatch >30%).
 Offer personalized skilling recommendations, leading to low user engagement.
 Ensure secure certification, as fake/duplicate certificates reduce employer trust.
 This results in a widening skill-job gap, underemployment, and growing social and
 economic pressures.

**Challenges we ran into**

During ML model training, I struggled with data quality issues (missing values, inconsistent formats) and low accuracy in early models (<65%). I solved this by applying feature engineering, cross-validation, and hyperparameter tuning, which improved accuracy to ~82%. Resume parsing with NLP was also challenging due to unstructured text, but I used TF-IDF and embeddings to extract skills. Finally, I optimized deployment by serving the model through a lightweight REST API, ensuring smooth integration with the MERN dashboard.

### DeployLite – Agentic AI-Powered Deployements
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/deploylite-agentic-ai-deployment-platform-272b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/BasirKhan418/status-code-2-deploylite.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://app.deploylite.xyz) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/1mfRNi50pBk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-StatusCode%202-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://statuscode-2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Deploy in few clicks

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Deploying applications today is often complicated and fragmented. Developers and small teams usually need to rely on multiple services to get a single product online hosting the frontend on one provider, the backend on another, and the database somewhere else. This fragmentation forces them to juggle credentials, configurations, and deployment pipelines, which can quickly become error-prone and time-consuming.

Another challenge is the DevOps overhead. Setting up CI/CD pipelines, managing containers, and configuring scaling rules typically requires significant infrastructure knowledge. Teams without dedicated DevOps engineers lose valuable time trying to solve deployment issues rather than focusing on building features.

Most existing platforms also create vendor lock-in, pushing developers into their own ecosystems and limiting flexibility. For indie developers, startups, and small businesses, this means higher long-term costs and less control. The complexity also discourages non-experts, who often find cloud deployments intimidating and inaccessible.

DeployLite addresses these problems by providing a single platform where web apps, databases, and even AI-powered chatbots can be deployed and managed seamlessly. It introduces AI-driven deployments, allowing developers to describe what they want in plain language instead of writing configuration files. The platform offers flexibility by supporting both managed infrastructure and direct deployment to services like AWS or Vultr, ensuring that teams retain control when needed. Every deployment comes with built-in CI/CD pipelines, reducing errors and saving engineering time, while the architecture is microservices-ready with isolated database instances for scalability and reliability.

In essence, DeployLite simplifies the deployment process, making it faster, safer, and more accessible without taking away the control and flexibility that modern teams need.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/fea484b6-5422-49a6-b8f6-44d8a6f17214.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/7a53398a-0314-432f-897f-4dca341b94c5.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/f67c85df-12e4-41d0-b8b1-bf6841a81c59.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/323f3f90-172a-40ca-bd99-cd56120e796e.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/0217f700-b3ac-46be-923b-096b27ef31d6.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles we faced was with the Vultr API. Since our deployment system was repeatedly hitting the same endpoint from the same IP address, Vultr’s security systems flagged the activity and temporarily blocked access. This not only broke our deployment flow but also made debugging difficult because the API responses stopped coming through. On top of that, their firewall blocked common ports like 80 and 443, which created additional issues during configuration and testing.

Another challenge came from working with multiple MongoDB instances for our microservices. Ensuring proper connection pooling and avoiding bottlenecks required careful configuration. A small mistake in the URI setup or resource allocation could bring down an entire service.

We also ran into containerization issues. Some images worked perfectly on local Docker setups but failed during production deployment due to differences in environment variables and networking rules. Tracking down these inconsistencies took time and forced us to refine our CI/CD pipeline with stricter validation checks before pushing anything live.

To overcome these challenges, we implemented rate-limiting and backoff strategies for API calls, carefully configured firewall rules, and added retry logic to handle transient network failures. For the database and container issues, we introduced stricter environment parity between local and production setups, along with automated health checks to catch failures early. These fixes not only solved the immediate problems but also made our platform more resilient for the long run.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/f26865a4-949a-424e-afcb-f25df2cd3985.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/e6f1c3cc-2c8b-4060-9ce4-469bae4ba4a4.png)

**Vultr Cloud Deployment Track**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/46e1e5be-1c2e-474a-bee6-a7913c8d7291.png)We used 5 Vultr servers to host 7 containerized microservices that power DeployLite’s core features deployment orchestration, CI/CD, AI chatbot, and workload management. Through Vultr’s API, our platform deploys user projects directly onto Vultr infrastructure, enabling seamless launches of web apps, databases, and chatbots on Vultr’s reliable compute.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/26d3074c-17a4-4143-823a-e4f4a909ffad.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/3f2d6d95-202a-47a0-947a-43604f5d5405.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/4004dda8-93a6-43cc-a2e7-8ec527546443.png)Our AI deployment agent is powered by the Gemini API, enabling users to provision and manage deployments entirely through natural language prompts. In addition, our chatbot builder leverages Gemini to generate vector embeddings from custom data sources, making it possible to build domain-specific conversational bots with minimal setup. Gemini is at the core of both our deployment automation and our chatbot intelligence layer.

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/faf2b6efe69f49b1ae0b8b15d35e7cbb/1ce4769d-525d-4913-9c95-50e7d208d3d0.png)Our entire platform is powered by MongoDB  all core application data is stored in MongoDB, making it the backbone of DeployLite. To support our microservices architecture, we use multiple MongoDB instances, each dedicated to a specific service, ensuring scalability, isolation, and high availability. MongoDB’s flexibility and performance are critical to handling deployments, user data, and real-time operations across our platform.

> Organize. Assist. Elevate

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square) ![MLflow](https://img.shields.io/badge/MLflow-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Dual-UI Website:**

- Admins → Upload public/private documents.
- Users → Access only public documents.

**Documents (PDFs, images → text extracted) stored in PostgreSQL + FAISS for semantic search.**

**LLM with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) for context-aware Q&A.**

**Voice Assistant powered by RAG → hands-free, interactive document exploration.**

**Real-Life Example:**

- A law firm → Admin uploads confidential case files (private) & legal precedents (public).
- Lawyers use voice assistant to quickly query “Show me similar precedents for contract disputes.”

**Challenges we ran into**

- CORS issues – frontend and backend origins didn’t match, needed explicit whitelisting.
- Environment variables – .env not loading properly on cloud (Railway/Render), had to set vars in dashboard.
- File handling – temp files not saved/removed correctly, caused parsing errors.
- Unsupported formats – API crashed on non-PDF/Image/TXT uploads, fixed with clear error response.
- Library deprecations – LangChain changed imports (FAISS, LLMChain), required code updates.
- OCR inconsistency – Gemini returned unwanted \n or formatting, needed cleanup.
- Frontend-backend integration – localhost vs 127.0.0.1 mismatch, HTTPS required in production.

**Open Innovation**

**External Collaboration**

- Involves partnerships with other companies, universities, startups, or the community.
- Example: Using external APIs, open-source tools, or research contributions.

**Knowledge Sharing**

- The project allows others to learn from, use, or improve your solution.
- Example: Publishing datasets, models, or methods for public use.

**User Engagement**

- Invites feedback or co-creation from users outside your core team.
- Example: Beta testers contributing to the system design or providing labeled data.

**Solving Broader Problems**

- The innovation addresses industry-wide or societal challenges, not just internal needs.
- Example: AI tool for document analysis usable by multiple organizations.

**Accessibility and Transparency**

- Makes the solution or framework accessible, modular, or adaptable for others.
- Example: Public APIs, open documentation, or plugin support for your system.

> In need of care? We'll get you there.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTTP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTTP%20server-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

What People Can Use Find My Clinic For

- Discover Nearby Clinics: Locate clinics on an interactive map with filters for services, insurance, and specialties.
- Check Real-Time Wait Times: See queue length and estimated wait before heading out.
- Book via QR Token: Scan a clinic’s QR standee to reserve your spot without waiting inside.
- Get a Dynamic Patient QR ID: Your encrypted pass for check-in, future bookings, and visit history.
- Chat with Clinic Staff: Confirm bookings, ask about services, and get delay updates.
- Receive Turn Alerts: Get notified when it’s almost your turn.

How It Makes Visits Easier & Safer

- Avoid Crowded Waiting Rooms: Join queues remotely to reduce exposure to illness.
- Faster Registration: QR IDs store your details, cutting paperwork.
- Save Time & Travel: Pick the least busy clinic using real-time info.
- Accurate Queue Data: Live updates from both patients and staff.
- Easy for Everyone: Works via app or QR scan—no installation required.
- Private & Secure: Encrypted data ensures privacy and quick access when needed.

**The problem it solves**

This project solves the problem of making traditional board games more engaging and educational by incorporating coding challenges and timed quizzes, turning a simple game of Snake and Ladder into an interactive learning experience that tests both knowledge and problem-solving under pressure.

**Challenges we ran into**

API Integration: Managing API calls and ensuring smooth integration for coding challenges or quizzes could be tricky, especially with rate limits or authentication issues.

Game Balance: Balancing the difficulty of coding challenges and quizzes to ensure they are engaging but not overly frustrating for players.

Multiplayer Mode: Implementing real-time multiplayer functionality, where players compete against each other, might present synchronization and latency issues.

Time Pressure: Ensuring that the time-based challenges feel intense yet fair could be tricky, as players might get frustrated if the time limits are too short.

User Interface: Designing an intuitive and visually appealing interface that integrates both the game elements (board, dice rolls) and the quiz challenges in a user-friendly manner.

Testing and Debugging: Given the interactive nature of the game, thorough testing will be crucial to ensure that the mechanics work smoothly across different devices and environments.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/dev-doodle-0f09) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dhrubojyot/Dev_Doodle) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zlaNZtr02xk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HexaFalls-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hexafalls.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Complete Platform for both Code & Sketch.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today’s fast-moving world of development and design, teams often use many different tools to work together. Coding tools usually only support sharing code, and drawing tools are only for sketching. This means teams have to switch between several apps to write code, test it, draw ideas, take notes, and talk to each other. Constantly jumping between tools wastes time, breaks focus, and makes work more confusing.

**Dev Doodle solves this problem by integrating all these essential collaborative workflows into a single seamless platform.**

In Dev Doodle developers no longer need to switch between **VS Code Live Share**, **Separate AI copilot tools**, **Sketching whiteboards for flowcharts**, and **Video & Audio calling apps**. Designers and Developers can work together in **real time** without compatibility issues or platform restrictions. Teams can **code**, **sketch**, **video & audio chat**, **auto generated ReadMe of code base with AI**, and execute code collaboratively from any location with minimal setup.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges we faced was implementing the **AI-powered README generator. **We used **Gemini 2.0 Flash** for generating the README file by scanning multiple files in the codebase. However, the API integration posed difficulties due to frequent failures and long response times, making the process unreliable during testing. To overcome this, we optimized our API call logic, improved request handling, and ensured stable integration to make the README generation feature functional and efficient.

Another significant hurdle was integrating real-time audio and video calling within the platform. Setting up seamless communication required complex implementation, and initially, we faced numerous errors with external services, compatibility issues, and unstable connections. We resolved this challenge by integrating **ZegoCloud**, which provided a stable and developer-friendly solution for real-time audio and video communication. After multiple testing iterations and error debugging, the feature is now working smoothly, enhancing the overall collaborative experience of our platform.

**The problem it solves**

# FitWise 🏋️‍♂️🤖

**FitWise** is an intelligent AI-powered workout assistant that combines **Agentic AI**, **RAG-enhanced knowledge**, and **MediaPipe pose detection** to create personalized workout routines and provide real-time form correction — designed for fitness enthusiasts at every level.

---

## 🚀 Core Features

### 🧠 **Agentic AI Workflow**
- **Intelligent Chat Assistant**: Natural language conversation for fitness advice and workout creation
- **Tool-Based Execution**: Uses specialized tools for workout generation, exercise config creation, and data persistence
- **Context-Aware Responses**: Maintains conversation flow with multi-step reasoning
- **User Session Management**: Personalized experience with login/logout functionality

### 🎯 **Dynamic Workout Generation**
- **Personalized Routines**: AI creates workouts based on goals, equipment, experience level, and duration
- **Unlimited Exercise Support**: No longer limited to predefined exercises - AI generates tracking configs for any exercise
- **Automatic Exercise Config Generation**: MediaPipe pose tracking configurations created dynamically using LLM analysis
- **Smart Caching**: Efficient reuse of generated configurations for performance
- **Database Integration**: Saves workouts with linked exercise configurations for future use

### 📚 **RAG-Enhanced Knowledge System**
- **Vector Database**: Qdrant-powered embedding storage of exercise science research
- **Relevance Filtering**: Only uses high-relevance content (70%+ similarity) for responses
- **Evidence-Based Recommendations**: Leverages latest research in biomechanics, anatomy, and exercise science
- **Source Citation**: References specific research sources in responses
- **LM Studio Integration**: Local embedding generation using text-embedding models

### 📷 **Advanced Pose Detection & Analysis**
- **MediaPipe Integration**: Real-time pose landmark detection via webcam
- **Multi-Joint Tracking**: Composite angle analysis from multiple body joints
- **Adaptive Peak Detection**: Intelligent rep counting with trend analysis
- **Target Angle Guidance**: ROM (Range of Motion) optimization with personalized targets
- **Bilateral Tracking**: Left and right side angle measurements for balanced analysis

### ✅ **Intelligent Real-Time Feedback**
- **AI-Powered Analysis**: LLM-based feedback generation considering form, tempo, and ROM
- **Configurable Performance Modes**:
  - **Fast Mode**: Quick text feedback for immediate responsiveness
  - **Enhanced Reference**: RAG-enhanced feedback with research backing
  - **Voice Feedback**: Spoken guidance in Bengali for hands-free operation
  - **Combined Mode**: Both enhanced reference and voice for comprehensive feedback
- **Scoring System**: 0-100 performance scores with "good/okay/bad" classifications
- **Progressive ROM Targets**: Adjustable range of motion goals (Low/Standard/High/Maximum)

### 🛠️ **User Interface & Experience**
- **Modern SvelteKit Frontend**: Built with shadcn/ui components for a clean, responsive design
- **Dashboard Overview**: Centralized view of workouts, progress, and AI interactions
- **Exercise Config Management**: Visual interface for viewing and testing generated configurations
- **Form Analysis Page**: Real-time pose detection with visual feedback
- **Workout Library**: Save, organize, and access personalized workout routines
- **Mobile-Responsive**: Works seamlessly across desktop and mobile devices

---

## 🤖 Agentic AI Workflow

FitWise implements a sophisticated agentic AI system that orchestrates multiple tools and knowledge sources to provide comprehensive fitness assistance:

![Editor _ Mermaid Chart-2025-06-22-011233](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccda9128-e5f2-4045-a161-aae3a73deae6)

### Agentic Components:

1. **Query Analysis Agent**: Determines if queries are fitness-related and routes appropriately
2. **RAG Retrieval Agent**: Searches vector database for relevant exercise science research
3. **Workout Generation Agent**: Creates personalized routines using evidence-based principles
4. **Exercise Config Agent**: Generates MediaPipe configurations for any exercise dynamically
5. **Persistence Agent**: Manages user data, workout storage, and exercise configurations
6. **Feedback Agent**: Provides real-time form analysis using pose detection data

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

Building FitWise presented several unique technical challenges that required innovative solutions:

### **MediaPipe Angle Data Preprocessing**
Transforming raw MediaPipe pose landmarks into meaningful angle data for LLM consumption was more complex than anticipated. The challenge involved:
- **Noisy Landmark Data**: MediaPipe outputs can be jittery, requiring sophisticated smoothing algorithms
- **Multi-Joint Coordination**: Creating composite angle signals from multiple body joints while maintaining biomechanical accuracy
- **Peak Detection Logic**: Developing adaptive algorithms to detect rep peaks/valleys across different exercise patterns
- **Angle Normalization**: Ensuring angle data is consistent and interpretable for downstream LLM analysis

**Solution**: Implemented weighted composite angle calculations with moving average smoothing and adaptive peak detection that considers exercise-specific movement patterns.

### **Real-Time Model Streaming with Minimal Latency**
Achieving fast response times while coordinating multiple AI models (LLM, RAG, TTS) proved challenging:
- **RAG Pipeline Bottleneck**: Vector search in Qdrant + embedding generation + LLM processing created latency spikes
- **Streaming Conflicts**: Balancing real-time pose feedback with chat-based AI responses
- **Memory Management**: Local models consuming significant RAM while maintaining smooth pose detection
- **Tool Coordination**: Managing sequential tool calls without blocking the UI

**Solution**: Implemented relevance thresholding (70%+) for RAG, aggressive caching of exercise configs, and background streaming with tool call optimization.

### **Quality Data Scraping for RAG Embeddings**
Building a robust knowledge base from exercise science content required careful data curation:
- **Content Quality**: Filtering scientific articles from fitness blog spam and misinformation
- **Source Diversity**: Balancing peer-reviewed research with practical training insights
- **Embedding Consistency**: Ensuring local embedding models produce meaningful vector representations
- **Data Structure**: Organizing scraped content for optimal retrieval performance

**Solution**: Focused on reputable sources (RPStrength, research papers), implemented content validation, and used proven embedding models like `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`.

### **Local Model Quality vs. Speed Trade-offs**
Running everything locally for privacy while maintaining performance created difficult compromises:
- **Model Size Limitations**: Smaller models (3B-4B parameters) vs. quality of larger cloud models
- **Hardware Constraints**: Balancing LLM inference, embedding generation, and MediaPipe processing on consumer hardware
- **Response Quality**: Local models sometimes producing less nuanced feedback compared to GPT-4 class models
- **Context Length**: Smaller models struggling with long conversation history and complex RAG context

**Solution**: Chose `qwen3-4b` for good instruction following, implemented smart context truncation, and optimized prompts for smaller model capabilities while maintaining acceptable quality.

**Progress made before hackathon**

Pre-Hackathon Foundation: While FitWise was built entirely from scratch for this hackathon, I brought valuable experience from previous hackathon projects where I had experimented with MediaPipe for basic pose detection. 

However, this project represents a significant evolution - the integration of agentic AI capabilities, RAG-enhanced knowledge systems, and dynamic exercise configuration generation were all novel implementations developed specifically for FitWise. 

No code was directly copied from previous projects; instead, the foundational understanding of MediaPipe's pose landmark system provided a launching point for building the sophisticated angle preprocessing, multi-joint tracking, and real-time feedback systems that make FitWise unique. 

The agentic workflow orchestrating multiple AI tools, the vector database integration, and the intelligent exercise configuration generation were entirely new challenges that pushed beyond simple pose detection into the realm of comprehensive AI-powered fitness assistance.

I’ve integrated Civic Auth into CVisionary to provide secure, password-less login  functionality in under five minutes. Using Civic’s React SDK, I wired up OAuth flows so users can authenticate with a single click—no usernames or passwords required—and chose to enable to authenticate

**The problem it solves**

# 💼 TaskFlow.ai — Intelligent Project & Workforce Management SaaS

> 🚀 Built in 36 hours to solve the chaos of project management, employee overload, and inefficient meetings.

---

## 🧠 The Problem

Modern IT companies rely on **fragmented tools** to manage people, projects, and productivity:

- HR systems to manage employees
- Separate project management tools (Jira, Trello)
- Time trackers (Toggl, Clockify)
- Manual spreadsheets to assign work
- Video calls with no action items
- Overloaded teams and unclear task ownership

This leads to:
- 💥 Work overload and burnout
- ❓ Tasks lost in conversation
- 🔁 Repetitive, manual work assignment
- ⚙️ Low efficiency and delayed projects

---

## ✅ Our Solution: TaskFlow.ai

**TaskFlow.ai** is a full-stack SaaS platform that:
- Centralizes company, employee, and project management
- Uses **AI to transcribe meetings and generate task summaries**
- **Auto-assigns jobs** based on availability, skill, and project priority
- Tracks work hours and load to prevent burnout
- Makes every meeting actionable — no wasted talk time

---

## 🎯 Who is it for?

- IT service companies
- Product teams
- Freelancing agencies
- Remote teams with recurring project work

---

## 🔧 Key Features

| Category | Features |
|----------|----------|
| 👥 Company Management | Register company, add employees, manage roles |
| 📁 Project & Task | Create projects, define priorities and deadlines, assign tasks |
| 🕒 Time Tracking | Start/stop work, manage time slots, prevent overload |
| 🎥 Meetings | Built-in video calls (Jitsi), auto recording |
| 🧠 AI Automation | Transcribe meetings, summarize key points, auto-create task list |
| ⚙️ Smart Assignment | Match tasks to best-fit employees by skill and availability |
| 🧑‍💻 Dashboards | Separate views for Admins, Employees, and Project Managers |

---

## 🧪 Demo Workflow

1. ✅ **Login/Register** as a company admin
2. 👥 **Add employees**
3. 📁 **Create a project** with priority and required skills
4. 🧑‍💻 **Start a meeting** → it records and transcribes the discussion
5. 🧠 **AI summarizes the meeting** and creates tasks
6. ⚙️ **System auto-assigns tasks** to the right team members

No more juggling 5 tools. No more overburdened teams.  
Just clear meetings, smart assignments, and balanced workloads.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges We Ran Into

### 1. ⏱️ Time Constraints with a Multi-Module System
We aimed to build a complete SaaS platform in just 36 hours — with modules for employee management, project tracking, AI transcription, smart task assignment, and real-time communication. Prioritizing what to build and what to cut was crucial.

### 2. 🤖 Whisper Transcription Setup
Setting up OpenAI Whisper locally proved difficult due to limited hardware resources. Transcription on CPU (no GPU available) was slow, and processing long meeting recordings within time constraints was a bottleneck.

### 3. 🧠 GPT-Based Task Extraction
Generating accurate and actionable tasks from raw meeting transcripts using GPT-4 required carefully crafted prompts. Mapping tasks to team members based on skill and availability had to be simplified due to time pressure.

### 4. 🖥️ Hardware & Resource Constraints
We worked on personal laptops and VMs with limited RAM and no GPUs. Running AI models (Whisper), Jibri (for recording), and PostgreSQL concurrently was resource-intensive. Some features had to be downscaled or mocked to avoid crashes and lag.

### 5. 🔌 Frontend & Backend Integration Bottleneck
Our frontend developer was limited to building UI only. This meant our full-stack member had to handle API integration, increasing their workload and introducing slight delays in completing the frontend flow.

### 6. 🎥 Jitsi + Jibri Integration
While Jitsi Meet integration via iframe was relatively straightforward, setting up **Jibri for auto-recording** introduced major challenges:
- High hardware demand (Jibri alone can consume 2–4 GB RAM).
- Lack of GPU slowed video encoding.
- Configuring audio loopback (using `snd-aloop`) in a VM environment was tricky.
- Docker container setup was not trivial and consumed valuable hours.

### 7. ⚖️ Smart Task Assignment Logic
Designing a logic that assigns tasks based on skill, availability, and project priority was complex under time constraints. We opted for a basic rule-based matching system with hardcoded skills and weights for the demo.

### 8. 🔄 Service Synchronization & Pipeline Orchestration
Moving data between modules — from Jitsi → audio → Whisper → GPT → backend → frontend — required careful coordination. Managing intermediate data, delays, and ensuring the right API trigger at the right time took multiple iterations.

### 9. 🧪 Testing Under Time Pressure
We focused on testing key flows like company registration, project creation, meeting → transcription → task flow. However, edge-case testing and performance checks had to be postponed to maintain delivery speed.

### 10. 🧠 Team Efficiency vs Feature Ambition
Not all teammates could contribute at full capacity due to complexity in unfamiliar areas. We had to downscale features like real-time transcription, advanced scheduling algorithms, and fancy dashboards to ship a working MVP.

**Authenticate with Civic Auth**

## 🔐 How Civic Auth Helped Us

Integrating authentication is one of the most time-consuming and error-prone parts of a hackathon project — especially when building a multi-tenant SaaS with role-based access (Admin, Project Manager, Employee).

Thanks to **Civic Auth**, we were able to:

### ✅ Simplify User Onboarding
- Civic’s identity verification allowed us to securely onboard company admins and employees without building a custom auth system from scratch.
- Saved us hours that would have gone into building login/registration, password hashing, and session handling.

### ✅ Enable Role-Based Access Quickly
- Civic’s user claims made it easy to distinguish between different roles (Admin vs Employee) and control access to different dashboards and actions.

### ✅ Ensure Security Without Extra Dev Time
- Civic provides built-in protection against common vulnerabilities like password leaks, session hijacking, and brute-force login — which is critical for a SaaS product, even in a hackathon demo.

### ✅ Focus on Core Product Logic
- Offloading authentication to Civic let our backend and frontend developers **focus on core features** like project/task management, AI transcription, and time tracking — instead of auth boilerplate.

> 🔐 In short, **Civic Auth gave us production-grade authentication with near-zero friction**, which helped us move faster, build smarter, and ship more in 36 hours.

**Best use of Gemini API**

## 🧠 How Gemini API Helped Us

Building an AI-powered productivity tool in a limited timeframe requires fast, reliable, and flexible language model capabilities — and that’s exactly where **Gemini API** came in.

We used **Gemini (by Google)** to power the natural language understanding and decision-making parts of our project, especially during the **meeting-to-task automation flow**.

### ✅ Meeting Summary Generation
- Gemini helped us process raw meeting transcripts (produced via Whisper) and **generate concise, structured summaries** that captured:
  - Key discussion points
  - Actionable decisions
  - Task ownership cues

### ✅ Task Extraction & Role Assignment
- Based on the summary, Gemini API enabled us to **extract tasks** and intelligently suggest:
  - Task descriptions
  - Required skill sets
  - Priority levels
  - Suggested assignees (based on role context)

### ✅ Prompt Flexibility & Fast Responses
- The flexibility of Gemini’s prompts allowed us to:
  - Fine-tune task generation behavior
  - Handle ambiguous transcripts gracefully
  - Iterate quickly on prompt logic during the hackathon

### ✅ Saved Dev Time & Improved Output Quality
- Without Gemini, we’d have to write custom NLP pipelines or rely on hardcoded keyword extraction — which would be far less accurate and extremely time-consuming.
- Gemini gave us **high-quality natural language understanding out of the box**, letting us focus on building core app logic.

> 🧠 In short, **Gemini API was our AI co-pilot**, helping us bridge the gap between unstructured meeting data and structured project workflows — all within the tight 36-hour hackathon window.

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

## 🗄️ How MongoDB Atlas Helped Us

Choosing the right database was critical for building a scalable, fast, and flexible multi-tenant SaaS platform in a short timeframe. **MongoDB Atlas**, with its cloud-native, fully managed environment, proved to be a perfect fit.

### ✅ Fast Setup & Zero Infrastructure Overhead
- Within minutes, we spun up a fully functional MongoDB cluster on Atlas — no server provisioning, no manual scaling.
- It eliminated the need to manage databases manually during the hackathon.

### ✅ Flexible Document Schema
- Our project involved dynamic data: users, companies, projects, tasks, time slots, transcripts — all with different shapes.
- MongoDB’s document-based model allowed us to **store flexible and nested data** (e.g., task status, transcript chunks) without rigid schemas or complex joins.

### ✅ Easy Integration with Backend (FastAPI)
- MongoDB Atlas came with native Python drivers (`pymongo`, `motor`) that seamlessly integrated with our FastAPI backend.
- Helped us move quickly and iterate over models with minimal refactoring.

### ✅ Built-in Tools & UI Dashboard
- The **Atlas web dashboard** helped us:
  - Monitor live data
  - Run test queries during development
  - View performance and logs in real-time

### ✅ Scalable & Ready for Production
- Even though it was a hackathon project, MongoDB Atlas gave us confidence that our backend could scale if this turned into a real SaaS product.

> 🗄️ In short, **MongoDB Atlas helped us go from zero to production-ready DB in minutes**, giving our team the flexibility and power to build fast, adapt quickly, and deliver a smart AI-based project management tool.

**The problem it solves**

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🛠️ Technical Challenges & Solutions  

#### 1. **LLM Response Inconsistency**  
**Challenge:**  
- Gemini/Llama APIs returned unpredictable JSON structures for auto-generated quizzes  
- Edge cases like code snippets in blogs caused malformed outputs (mixed Markdown/HTML)  
- Confidence scores fluctuated wildly for fill-in-blank questions  

**Solution:**  
```javascript
// Implemented multi-layer validation
const sanitizeLLMResponse = (rawData) => {
  // 1. Fallback parsing with regex for code snippets
  if (rawData.includes('<code>')) {
    rawData = extractCodeBlocks(rawData);
  }
  
  // 2. Schema validation with Zod
  const QuestionSchema = z.object({
    question: z.string(),
    options: z.array(z.string()).length(4),
    correctIndex: z.number().min(0).max(3)
  });
  
  // 3. Confidence threshold filtering
  return rawData.filter(q => q.confidenceScore >= 0.85);
};

**GEN AI&ML**

BrainBolt pushes generative AI beyond content creation into active skill transformation. Unlike basic AI tutors, our engine leverages Gemini/Llama to dynamically convert any passive content (videos/PDFs/blogs) into personalized, gamified learning experiences. By automating 90% of assessment generation with adaptive difficulty and neuroscience-backed spaced repetition, we turn raw information into retained competence – directly addressing GenAI’s mandate to solve real human problems (95% graduate unemployability). Our architecture embeds GenAI at every layer – from NLP-powered quiz generation to LLM-driven career path recommendations – creating an AI-native solution that doesn’t just assist learning but reinvents it as a competency-building engine.

**Challenges we ran into**

⚙️ Challenges We Ran Into
🧩 Integrating Real-Time Chat with Other Modules
Implementing Socket.IO for real-time chat while managing authenticated user sessions and syncing it with freelancing and event modules was tricky.
✅ Fix: We modularized the socket logic, used JWT for secure user identification in chat events, and established isolated namespaces for groups and DMs.

🌐 Database Structuring Across Multiple Domains
Managing a single database structure that could handle gigs, events, user chats, and community data was complex.
✅ Fix: We designed a modular schema in MongoDB with clear references and indexes, enabling better performance and query separation.

🎯 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Differentiating features for freelancers, clients, event organizers, and general users created logic conflicts in UI/UX flow.
✅ Fix: We implemented a centralized role-checking middleware on both backend and frontend routes to ensure smooth access handling.

🧪 Real-Time Updates on Gig Applications and Event Registrations
Getting changes to reflect live across dashboards without full page refreshes was a challenge.
✅ Fix: We combined WebSockets and React Query with cache invalidation strategies to keep UI updated dynamically.

📦 File & Media Upload Issues
Uploading user avatars, event banners, and media in chats to Firebase Storage while maintaining security and speed posed hurdles.
✅ Fix: We created signed upload URLs and restricted file types/sizes, ensuring reliable and secure uploads.

> A real-time 1v1 battle platform where competitive programming enthusiasts go head-to-head for glory.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![TailWindCSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/TailWindCSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Render](https://img.shields.io/badge/Render-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

While platforms like LeetCode and Codeforces are excellent for practice and contests, they lack real-time 1v1 competition, which many competitive programming enthusiasts crave. There's no easy way to instantly challenge another coder, solve the same problem in parallel, and truly compete.

Fleetcode solves this by offering:

Instant 1v1 matchmaking with a fair problem

A real-time synced timer

An integrated code editor and problem panel

Automatic winner declaration based on submission and correctness

This mirrors the thrill of a coding round — in a controlled, focused 1v1 format. No waiting for contests. No leaderboard grinding. Just raw competition, anytime.

It transforms passive practice into engaging duels — ideal for those preparing for coding competitions or simply looking to sharpen their edge.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Fleetcode, a real-time 1v1 competitive programming platform came with multiple technical hurdles. The platform is still in its development phase, with core systems implemented and integration underway.

1. WebSocket Synchronization
Early issues with timers and game state desync led to confusion during matches. We solved this by creating a centralized timer on the backend that broadcasts updates every second via WebSockets to both players.

2. Matchmaking System
We initially faced problems like self-matching and stalled queues. We implemented a FIFO-based matchmaking queue using a /match/find API. The logic is written, and frontend integration is ongoing.

3. Code Editor Isolation
Using a shared or global editor state caused unexpected behavior. We integrated Monaco Editor and scoped it per user session to maintain isolated environments.

4. Winner Declaration Logic
Edge cases like simultaneous submissions or no submissions required special handling. Backend logic now tracks valid submissions and determines winners or declares a draw if time runs out.

5. UI/UX Challenges
Dark theme design needed multiple iterations to balance readability and focus. We used TailwindCSS to build a responsive, distraction-free interface suitable for high-stakes 1v1 battles.

We’re actively integrating the judge system, completing matchmaking UI flow, and adding user stats, rankings, and match history.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Modular Backend Structure
Since the project combines multiple domains — freelancing, event management, and real-time community features — designing a clean and scalable backend architecture was a major challenge. Merging all services into one monolithic structure would have made debugging and future scaling difficult.

Solution:
We created separate folders for each major module (/freelance, /events, /realtime-services) with independent route, controller, and model files. This kept each service isolated and easier to manage and scale independently.

2. Real-Time Messaging Logic
Setting up real-time messaging with Firebase Realtime DB involved handling message delivery, group chats, and 1-on-1 conversations, while maintaining sync across clients.
 Solution:
We implemented Firebase listeners and structured our database to support fast message queries. We also tested different data models before finalizing the one that supports both performance and scalability.

3. Authentication & Role Handling
Managing multiple user roles (freelancers, startups, admins) across all modules was tricky, especially when restricting certain features to specific roles (e.g., only clients can post gigs).

 Solution:
We used Firebase Auth with role-based middleware, which ensured that each route and action had proper access control without hardcoding logic.

4. Frontend-Bound Feature Synchronization
With parallel development between frontend and backend teams, keeping APIs and UI behavior in sync was initially a hurdle.

 Solution:
We created a shared documentation (OpenAPI format) and used Postman collections, which ensured that frontend could test APIs as soon as they were ready, reducing dependency delays.

5. Time Constraints & Feature Prioritization
Being a hackathon, time was limited. Balancing quality while delivering all major features was tough.

 Solution:
We followed an agile approach, delivering MVP versions of each module first and then progressively enhancing them base

> "Schedule appointments with just your voice - no apps, no clicks, just conversation."

![•	JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![•	Vapi AI - Voice conversation engine and natural language processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	Vapi%20AI%20--%20Voice%20conversation%20engine%20and%20natural%20language%20processing-333333?style=flat-square) ![•	n8n - Workflow automation and A2A (Application-to-Application) logic orchestration](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	n8n%20--%20Workflow%20automation%20and%20A2A%20(Application--to--Application)%20logic%20orchestration-333333?style=flat-square) ![•	REST APIs - Service integration and data exchange](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	REST%20APIs%20--%20Service%20integration%20and%20data%20exchange-333333?style=flat-square) ![•	Webhooks - Real-time event notifications](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	Webhooks%20--%20Real--time%20event%20notifications-333333?style=flat-square) ![•	OAuth 2.0 - Secure API authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	OAuth%202.0%20--%20Secure%20API%20authentication-333333?style=flat-square) ![•	Node.js - Custom function development in n8n](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	Node.js%20--%20Custom%20function%20development%20in%20n8n-333333?style=flat-square) ![•	Google Calendar API - Availability checking and existing event management](https://img.shields.io/badge/•	Google%20Calendar%20API%20--%20Availability%20checking%20and%20existing%20event%20management-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional appointment booking systems create friction in customer experience through multiple steps: downloading apps, creating accounts, navigating complex interfaces, selecting times from dropdowns, and filling out forms. This process is particularly challenging for elderly users, people with disabilities, or those uncomfortable with technology. Businesses lose potential customers due to booking abandonment, while customers face frustration with complicated scheduling systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

Major Challenge: Real-time Calendar Synchronization and Conflict Resolution
The biggest technical challenge was ensuring real-time synchronization between multiple calendar systems (Google Calendar, Cal.com) while preventing double-bookings during concurrent voice conversations.
The Problem: When multiple customers called simultaneously, there was a race condition where two people could book the same time slot if their conversations overlapped. The voice AI would check availability, confirm the slot was free, but before booking completion, another conversation might book the same slot.
Our Solution: We implemented a distributed locking mechanism within the n8n workflow:
1.	Temporary Reservations: When availability is confirmed verbally, we create a 5-minute temporary lock on that time slot
2.	Atomic Operations: Used Airtable's API with conditional updates to ensure only one booking can succeed per slot
3.	Real-time Webhooks: Implemented instant calendar sync using webhooks between all integrated services
4.	Graceful Failure Handling: If a conflict occurs mid-conversation, the AI immediately offers alternative slots without requiring the customer to restart
This taught us the importance of designing for concurrency from the beginning and implementing robust error handling in voice-based systems where users can't easily retry operations.
