> Making Orcyon more stable and contributor-friendly

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prisma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prisma-333333?style=flat-square) ![Turborepo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Turborepo-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

College societies and student organizations often rely on multiple disconnected tools to manage events—such as spreadsheets for attendance, messaging apps for coordination, separate platforms for content and social media, and manual processes for logistics and onboarding. This fragmentation leads to poor coordination, duplicated work, errors in attendance tracking, and difficulty onboarding new team members.

Orcyon solves this problem by providing a single, centralized platform that brings together event planning, attendance management, content creation, social media scheduling, logistics coordination, and student onboarding. It streamlines workflows for different teams (organising, content, social media, logistics, and admins) while giving students a simple and reliable way to register for events and mark attendance.

In addition, Orcyon addresses the challenges faced by contributors and maintainers of such systems by focusing on a scalable architecture, clear role-based access, and improved developer experience. By unifying operational workflows and reducing manual overhead, the platform makes event execution more efficient, transparent, and reliable for college communities.

**Challenges we ran into**

While contributing to the backend, I faced several setup and configuration challenges that initially blocked local development. One of the main issues was related to missing and undocumented backend dependencies, which caused the server to fail during startup. Identifying these issues required carefully tracing runtime errors, reviewing import usage, and validating the backend package configuration.

Another challenge involved database setup and Prisma integration. The backend relies on Prisma with MongoDB, which introduces specific requirements such as proper schema configuration and database compatibility. Since these details were not clearly documented, running write operations initially resulted in failures. I addressed this by investigating Prisma’s requirements, testing different local configurations, and discussing the findings with other contributors and maintainers.

Additionally, working within a monorepo setup using Turborepo and Bun required understanding how multiple packages interact during development. Debugging issues across the frontend, backend, and shared configurations helped me gain a deeper understanding of the project architecture.

By systematically debugging errors, communicating through issues and pull requests, and validating fixes locally, I was able to resolve blocking problems and contribute toward making the backend more stable and contributor-friendly.

### OWASP Nest: Contributor Discovery & Automation
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/owasp-nest-contributor-discovery-and-automation-bc2f) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eH_spxEHEaOl9__L1da-xm1LV-zLkf1h/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=118049866034390141386&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Making OWASP contributions easier to discover

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![GraphQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/GraphQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

OWASP has a large and diverse ecosystem of projects, but new and existing contributors often struggle to discover the right issues, understand how to get started, and navigate contribution workflows efficiently.

OWASP Nest addresses this by acting as a centralized contribution gateway. This project enhances OWASP Nest by improving contributor onboarding, enabling skill-based issue discovery, and introducing automation to reduce manual mentor effort. By simplifying how contributors find and engage with projects, the platform improves contribution quality, reduces friction, and supports sustainable open-source growth within the OWASP community.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the key challenges was understanding and aligning with an existing large-scale open-source codebase while ensuring changes remained incremental and review-friendly. Balancing backend API design with frontend usability also required careful planning to avoid overengineering.

Another challenge was scoping automation features realistically within the Winter of Code timeline. I addressed this by breaking features into smaller milestones, prioritizing an MVP-first approach, and actively seeking mentor feedback early to validate assumptions before implementation. This approach helped reduce rework and ensured steady, reviewable progress.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aleithiaai-2079) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Weekend%20of%20Code%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://weekendofcode2k26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Intelligence that Adapts. Reliability that Lasts.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Alethia.ai redefines the future of quantitative trading by solving the critical "silent failure" problem in financial AI through a multi-modal, research-backed architecture that prioritizes mathematical truth over raw probability. By engineering a shared latent space where FinBERT-driven textual narratives are cross-verified against temporal Transformers and fundamental MLPs, the system moves beyond traditional forecasting into a realm of verifiable intelligence. This innovative approach utilizes the Zhang et al. (2024) consistency framework to detect "narrative drift"—the gap between institutional messaging and empirical market data—effectively eliminating the fragility of legacy models that crash during regime shifts. Ultimately, we have inculcated the precision of quant trading with a resilient, self-healing pipeline that doesn't just predict market trends but dynamically validates the structural reality of the global economy, setting a new paradigm for institutional-grade reliability.

**Challenges we ran into**

The most formidable technical hurdle encountered during development was the Encoder Dimensionality Schism, where a critical misalignment between the training checkpoint and the production inference pipeline caused a system-wide failure. Specifically, the system triggered a RuntimeError due to a size mismatch in the tabular_encoder, which expected an 11-feature input from the legacy checkpoint while the optimized real-world dataset had evolved to 13 features, including advanced technical indicators like RSI and MACD. This resulted in a recursive 503 Service Unavailable state on the dashboard, which was ultimately mitigated by engineering a Dynamic Feature Interceptor and a self-healing model-loading utility. This layer enabled the system to automatically prune input vectors to match the pre-trained weights while simultaneously triggering a background retraining task to reconcile the new data dimensions. Furthermore, resolving infrastructure bottlenecks—such as the ReadTimeoutError during the containerization of the PyTorch-heavy ML service—required a surgical optimization of the Docker build process, ensuring that the platform achieved the high-availability and operational resilience necessary for institutional-grade financial intelligence.

**The problem it solves**

**Project Overview**
Gram Vikas is a comprehensive agricultural marketplace platform designed to bridge the gap between rural farmers and urban buyers. The platform provides real-time analytics, multi-role dashboards, and innovative features tailored for agricultural communities in India.


**Key Features**

- Agricultural Marketplace

    Product Listings: Farmers can list agricultural products with detailed descriptions
    Bidding System: Real-time auction system for fair price discovery
    Search & Filter: Advanced product search with categories and filters
    Order Management: Complete order processing workflow
    Payment Integration: Secure Razorpay payment gateway

- Multi-Role User Management

    Buyer Dashboard: Purchase analytics, order tracking, spending patterns
    Farmer Dashboard: Sales analytics, listing management, revenue tracking
    Admin Dashboard: Platform-wide analytics, user management, system monitoring
    Hub Operator Dashboard: Hub-specific analytics, logistics management
    SHG Leader Dashboard: Group analytics, member management, collective sales

- Real-time Analytics

    Live Charts: 4 chart types (line, bar, pie) updating every 5 seconds
    User Growth Tracking: Monthly user registration trends
    Transaction Volume: Real-time transaction monitoring
    Revenue Analytics: Category-wise revenue breakdown
    User Distribution: Role-based user analytics

- Rural Technology Integration

    USSD Support: Mobile USSD integration for feature phones
    OTP Authentication: SMS-based verification for rural users
    Offline Capability: Designed for low-connectivity areas
    Multi-language Support: Hindi and English interface

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. **CORS Configuration Issues**
- **Challenge**: React (localhost:3000/5173) and Django (localhost:8000) cross-origin requests
- **Solution**: Added multiple allowed origins in `settings.py` and set `CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = True` for development
- **Evidence**: Multiple ports listed (3000, 3001, 3002, 5173) in CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

### 2. **JWT Token Authentication & Refresh Flow**
- **Challenge**: Auto-refresh expired tokens without disrupting user flow
- **Solution**: Axios interceptors in `api.ts` to:
  - Attach tokens to requests
  - Catch 401 errors
  - Refresh and retry original request
  - Redirect to login on refresh failure
- **Complexity**: Preventing refresh loops with `_retry` flag

### 3. **Frontend-Backend Integration**
- **Challenge**: Connecting React TypeScript frontend to Django REST API
- **Issues**:
  - Different ports and protocols
  - Type mismatches (TypeScript vs Python types)
  - Async/await handling for API calls
  - State management across components

### 4. **Offline-First Data Synchronization**
- **Challenge**: Sync data for rural areas with unreliable connectivity
- **Issues**:
  - Timezone parsing (`timezone.datetime.fromisoformat()` with 'Z' format)
  - Role-based data filtering (COWORKER vs DOCTOR vs ADMIN)
  - Incremental sync with `last_sync` timestamps
  - Conflict resolution when uploading offline data
- **Note**: Upload endpoint is a placeholder

### 5. **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**
- **Challenge**: Permissions by user role
- **Implementation**:
  - Custom User model with role field
  - Different data access per role
  - Filtering patients/vitals/consultations by role
- **Complexity**: Ensuring users only see/modify permitted data

### 6. **Database Migrations & Setup**
- **Challenge**: Setting up database on Windows with SQLite
- **Issues**:
  - Migration conflicts
  - Database locking errors
  - Custom User model requiring early migration order
  - Switching between SQLite (dev) and PostgreSQL (production)

### 7. **Windows-Specific Setup Challenges**
- **Challenge**: Windows environment setup
- **Issues**:
  - Virtual environment activation (`venv\Scripts\activate`)
  - Path separators in batch files
  - Port conflicts (multiple processes on 8000/3000)
  - Node modules installation issues
- **Solution**: Multiple batch scripts for setup/startup

### 8. **Port Conflicts**
- **Challenge**: Ports 8000 (backend) and 3000 (frontend) already in use
- **Solutions**:
  - Multiple fallback ports configured (3001, 3002, 5173)
  - Instructions to change ports in README
  - Development server port configuration

### 9. **TypeScript Integration with React**
- **Challenge**: Type safety with API responses
- **Issues**:
  - No explicit API response types
  - Type inference challenges with Axios
  - Ensuring component props match API data structures

### 10. **Error Handling & User Feedback**
- **Challenge**: Clear user feedback for API errors
- **Implementation**:
  - Token refresh retry logic
  - 401 handling with redirect to login
  - CORS error handling
  - Network error handling for offline scenarios

### 11. **Timezone Handling in Sync Views**
- **Challenge**: Converting ISO datetime strings with timezone info
- **Issue**: Parsing `last_sync` parameter with 'Z' (UTC) notation
- **Solution**: `timezone.datetime.fromisoformat(last_sync.replace('Z', '+00:00'))`
- **Complexity**: Handling multiple timezone formats

### 12. **BMI Calculation Logic**
- **Challenge**: Calculating BMI from weight (kg) and height (cm)
- **Implementation**: Converting cm to meters in property method
- **Edge Case**: Division by zero if height is 0

### 13. **Multiple Build Tools & Configuration**
- **Challenge**: Vite for frontend, Django for backend
- **Issues**:
  - Different development servers
  - Configuration synchronization
  - Hot reload coordination

### 14. **Authentication State Management**
- **Challenge**: Persisting auth state across page refreshes
- **Solution**: localStorage for tokens
- **Concern**: Security implications of client-side token storage

### 15. **Dependency Management**
- **Challenge**: Managing Python and Node.js dependencies
- **Issues**:
  - Version conflicts
  - Virtual environment isolation
  - Package lock file synchronization
  - Windows-specific package installation issues

### 16. **Offline Data Upload Implementation**
- **Challenge**: Bulk upload of offline-recorded data
- **Current Status**: Placeholder implementation in `sync/views.py`
- **Complexity**: Conflict resolution, duplicate detection, transaction handling

### 17. **Production vs Development Configuration**
- **Challenge**: Different settings for dev and production
- **Configuration**:
  - DEBUG mode toggle
  - Database switching (SQLite → PostgreSQL)
  - CORS settings (permissive vs restricted)
  - Secret key security

> Deployment at the speed of thoughts

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**OPSonic** is an autonomous **AI-powered DevOps** agent that transforms raw developer code into live cloud deployments without manual infrastructure work. Through a chat-based interface, users can upload **ZIP files, folders, or GitHub repositories**, and Opsonic automatically reviews the code, understands its structure and framework, and deploys it to the optimal **AWS service**. Frontend applications are built and hosted via AWS Amplify, backend services such as JAR files or APIs are provisioned on EC2 with correct runtimes and networking, and **CI/CD pipelines** are set up automatically for GitHub-based workflows. By abstracting cloud complexity, and using ephemeral credentials that are never stored, OPSonic enables secure, zero-configuration deployments—allowing developers to focus on building software instead of managing servers.

**Challenges we ran into**

We encountered a major deployment challenge with the “Zip-in-a-Zip” problem, where uploaded ZIP files often contained an extra folder layer, causing build scripts to fail when expected files like package.json were not found at the root. We solved this by implementing a smart recursive search that automatically locates the true project root and runs build commands in the correct directory, making uploads robust regardless of how they were zipped. Another challenge was browser security blocking HTTPS frontends from calling HTTP backends; this highlighted the need for SSL-enabled backends in production to ensure secure end-to-end communication.

**The problem it solves**

Mentora uses Generative AI to solve critical career development challenges:

**🤖 AI-Generated Personalized Roadmaps**
Problem: Career counseling costs ₹5,000-10,000/session with generic advice. 82% of students lack guidance.
**GenAI Solution:**

- Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite generates 15-25 node personalized roadmaps in 10 seconds by analyzing your skills, goals, and timeline with natural language processing
- Intelligent prerequisite mapping and dynamic difficulty progression (Beginner → Intermediate → Advanced) ensures optimal learning sequences

**📄 Intelligent Resume Analysis**
Problem: 75% of resumes rejected by ATS with zero feedback.
**GenAI Solution:**

- Multimodal AI processes PDF text + layout to provide 6-dimensional scoring with contextual improvement suggestions
- AI generates before/after examples specific to your content while extracting missing keywords from millions of job descriptions



**🧠 AI-Driven Skill Gap Analysis**
Problem: Students don't know what skills they're missing.
**GenAI Solution:**

- AI tracks progress and infers skill proficiency automatically, generating insights like "Strong in React, need Hooks practice"
- Predicts completion timelines based on learning velocity: "Master Node.js in 3 weeks at current pace"

**Challenges we ran into**

**🤖 Inconsistent AI Roadmap Generation**
Problem: Initial prompts gave 5-40 nodes randomly, broken links, arbitrary difficulty levels.
**GenAI Fix:**

- Engineered structured prompts with JSON schema enforcement and few-shot learning examples showing ideal roadmap structures
- Built AI self-validation layer where Gemini checks its own output for prerequisite logic and link validity → 95% consistency achieved

**📄 Multimodal PDF Understanding Failed**
Problem: Complex resume layouts confused AI—fragmented text, missing sections (70% accuracy).
**GenAI Fix:**

- Developed preprocessing pipeline with semantic chunking that breaks resumes into logical sections before Gemini multimodal analysis
- Implemented confidence scoring and fallback strategies (text-only if multimodal fails) → 95% parsing success rate

**⚡ 8-12 Second AI Response Latency**
Problem: Users thought app was frozen during roadmap generation.
**GenAI Fix:**

- Implemented streaming responses showing roadmap nodes progressively as AI generates them with optimistic UI
- Built smart caching system where similar goals return modified roadmaps in <2 seconds + token optimization reduced API time by 40% → <3 seconds perceived latency

**🧠 AI Hallucinated Fake Resources**
Problem: Gemini invented course names or suggested outdated 2018 resources.
**GenAI Fix:**

- Added validation layer with RAG approach that cross-references AI suggestions against Coursera/Udemy APIs and curated verified resource lists
- Built user feedback loop that flags suspicious patterns + recency filtering ("Only 2023+ resources") → 98% resource accuracy


**🎯 No User Profile = Poor Personalization**
Problem: New users had no data—AI couldn't personalize roadmaps.
**GenAI Fix:**

- Created conversational onboarding with zero-shot learning where AI asks clarifying questions and guesses level from goal phrasing
- Implemented implicit preference learning that analyzes resource click patterns + adaptive roadmaps adjust difficulty in real-time → 85% first-time user satisfaction

**Generative AI**

Mentora leverages Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite to revolutionize career guidance through intelligent AI features:

**🤖 AI-Powered Roadmap Generation**

- Gemini analyzes user goals, skills, and timelines to generate personalized 15-25 node learning paths in under 10 seconds with natural language processing
- Implements structured prompts with JSON schema enforcement and few-shot learning for 95% consistent output quality

**📄 Multimodal Resume Analysis**

- Processes PDF resumes using Gemini's multimodal capabilities (text + layout understanding) to provide 6-dimensional ATS scoring
- Generates contextual before/after improvement examples specific to each user's content with intelligent keyword extraction

**🧠 AI-Driven Insights**

- Semantic chunking and map-reduce patterns handle complex documents while maintaining context window efficiency
- Predictive analytics forecast learning timelines and identify skill gaps automatically based on progress patterns

**⚡ Optimization Innovations**

- Smart caching layer with streaming responses reduces perceived latency from 12 seconds to <3 seconds
- RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) approach validates AI outputs against verified resource databases, achieving 98% accuracy
- Token optimization reduced API costs by 40% while maintaining response quality

**The problem it solves**

## What can people use it for?

Our system is designed to help **children living away from home** stay connected to and informed about their parents’ health—without constant calls, anxiety, or false alarms.

### 🧓 Remote Parental Health Monitoring
- Allows children to **passively monitor parents’ health** through wearable-driven data.
- Reduces the need for frequent check-in calls while still staying informed.

# Why ArthSethu? The Solution to Startup Failure

ArthSethu is not just another fintech app; it is a **Financial Intelligence Platform** designed to solve the two biggest killers of early-stage startups: **"Estimation Paralysis"** and **"Financial Blindness."**

We bridge the critical gap between having an ambition and securing the capital to execute it. Here is how we solve the problem:

## 1. Solving "Estimation Paralysis" (The Reality Check)
**The Problem:** Students and aspiring founders often have brilliant ideas but fail to start because they cannot accurately calculate the cost of execution. They get stuck in the "dreaming" phase because they lack real-world data.

**The ArthSethu Solution:**
* **Adaptive Profiling:** We replaced generic business forms with a smart **Decision Tree**. The system adapts to the user—asking a *Cloud Kitchen* about "Packaging Costs" while skipping irrelevant questions like "Seating Capacity."
* **Hyper-Local Accuracy:** We eliminate guesswork by integrating with **Government Open Data Repositories**. The platform fetches live, real-time costs for specific cities—including Commercial Rent, Labor Wages, and Commodity Prices (like Milk or Steel).
* **The Result:** A student can generate a professional **Feasibility Report PDF** with one click, complete with Break-even graphs and CAPEX/OPEX charts, ready to present to any mentor or incubator.

## 2. Curing "Financial Blindness" (Operational Intelligence)
**The Problem:** Many founders focus entirely on product and sales, ignoring unit economics. They don't realize they are bleeding money on hidden leaks like wastage until the capital runs out.

**The ArthSethu Solution:**
* **The "Health Score" Dashboard:** We simplified complex accounting into a single **0-100 Speedometer Gauge**.
* **Instant Feedback Loop:** By tracking just three simple metrics—**Sales, Expenses, and Wastage**—the system monitors margin stability.
* **The Result:** If "Wastage" spikes, the Health Score drops immediately. This visual alert acts as an early warning system, allowing founders to fix operational leaks before they become financial disasters.

## 3. Removing Strategic Fear (The AI CFO)
**The Problem:** Small business owners often make decisions based on "gut feeling" because hiring a financial consultant is too expensive. They fear expanding because they don't know the financial consequences.

**The ArthSethu Solution:**
* **Context-Aware AI:** We provide an **AI CFO** (powered by Llama 3.2) that "knows" the user's specific business context.
* **"What-If" Simulations:** Users can run risk-free simulations. A user can ask, *"What if I hire one more barista?"* and the AI will calculate the exact impact: *"Your monthly cost increases by ₹18,000. To break even, you must sell 12 extra cups per day."*
* **The Result:** Users make data-backed decisions with the confidence of a seasoned CFO.

---
**ArthSethu empowers the next generation of entrepreneurs to stop guessing and start calculating.**

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest technical hurdle was integrating the **Local LLM (Llama 3.2)** with our **Java Spring Boot backend**. We faced persistent "Connection Refused" errors because the Dockerized backend could not communicate with the **Ollama** instance running on the host machine.

We overcame this by configuring **Docker networking** to utilize `host.docker.internal`, creating a seamless bridge between the container and the local AI. Additionally, to ensure **Contextual Awareness** without hallucinations, we used **LangChain** to dynamically inject specific user data (like rent and sales) from **PostgreSQL** into the prompt context.

**Best Innovation**

ArthSethu deserves "Best Innovation" because it redefines fintech, moving beyond simple lending to create a new category: the Financial Intelligence Platform. It solves the true root causes of startup failure—"Estimation Paralysis" and "Financial Blindness"—acting as a "Digital Co-Founder"

Its innovation lies in two key breakthroughs:

Hyper-Local Precision: It replaces guesswork by integrating Government Open Data to calculate exact real-world costs (rent, wages) for specific cities.

Democratized Strategy: It provides an AI CFO (Local Llama 3.2) that allows students to run complex "What-If" simulations, giving them the strategic foresight usually reserved for large corporations.

**AWS**

ArthSethu leveraged Kiro not just as an IDE, but as an architectural accelerator. We used Kiro to design our robust Spring Boot backend structure and validate the complex local AI orchestration flow (LangChain + Ollama) before implementation. Kiro efficiently automated our GitHub workflows and generated the foundational boilerplate code for our "Health Score" algorithms. This reduced weeks of structural planning into days of execution, allowing the team to bypass setup fatigue and focus entirely on building our core "Financial Intelligence" features, ensuring the platform was scalable and hackathon-ready from day one.

## The Problem It Solves

Small and medium grocery stores struggle with **manual inventory management** and **poor sales visibility**, leading to:

- **Lost Revenue**: Out-of-stock items and overstocking tie up cash flow
- **Manual Processes**: Spreadsheet-based tracking is time-consuming and error-prone  
- **Poor Decision Making**: Lack of real-time sales insights and profit analysis
- **Inventory Waste**: No demand forecasting leads to expired products and dead stock
- **Missed Opportunities**: Unable to identify best-selling products and optimize pricing

### What Our Platform Does

**Sales and Prediction Platform** transforms CSV sales data into actionable business intelligence:

 **Real-time Inventory Management** - Modern card-based interface shows stock levels, profit margins, and reorder alerts instantly

 **Profit Analysis** - Automatically calculates cost vs selling price, profit margins, and total inventory value from uploaded CSV data

 **Sales Analytics** - Visual dashboards track revenue trends, best/worst performing products, and category performance

 **Smart Alerts** - Automated notifications for low stock, out-of-stock, and dead stock items

 **Demand Forecasting** - Predictive analytics help plan inventory purchases and avoid stockouts

 **Mobile-First Design** - Responsive interface works on phones, tablets, and desktops for on-the-go management

### Target Users
- **Grocery Store Owners** managing 20-500 products
- **Small Retail Businesses** needing better inventory control
- **Shop Managers** wanting real-time sales insights
- **Business Owners** seeking to improve profit margins through data-driven decisions

The platform eliminates manual tracking, reduces inventory costs, and increases profitability through intelligent analytics - all from simple CSV data uploads.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. **Real-time Data Synchronization**
**Challenge**: Keeping inventory data synchronized across multiple components (Dashboard, Inventory, Alerts) when CSV data updates.

**Solution**: Implemented WebSocket connections with Socket.io to broadcast real-time updates. Each component listens for specific events (`inventoryUpdate`, `salesDataUploaded`) and updates state accordingly.

### 2. **Mobile Responsive Design Complexity**
**Challenge**: Creating a sidebar navigation that works seamlessly on desktop (always visible) and mobile (hamburger menu) without breaking the layout.

**Solution**: Used CSS media queries with transform animations and proper z-index management. Added mobile overlay backdrop and state management for sidebar visibility across all components.

### 3. **CSV Data Processing & Profit Calculations**
**Challenge**: Processing uploaded CSV files and automatically calculating profit margins, total values, and inventory statistics in real-time.

**Solution**: Built a robust backend parser using `csv-parser` that validates data, calculates derived fields (profit = sellingPrice - costPrice), and generates comprehensive inventory statistics before sending to frontend.

### 4. **Modern Card Layout vs Table Performance**
**Challenge**: Initially used traditional tables, but user wanted a modern card-based grid layout. Challenge was maintaining performance with 25+ products while keeping it responsive.

**Solution**: Replaced table with CSS Grid layout, implemented efficient React rendering with proper key props, and used CSS transforms for smooth hover animations without affecting performance.

### 5. **State Management Across Components**
**Challenge**: Managing complex inventory state (products, categories, filters, search) while ensuring data consistency and avoiding prop drilling.

**Solution**: Centralized state management in each component with proper useEffect hooks for data loading, and WebSocket listeners for real-time updates. Used React's built-in state rather than external libraries to keep it simple.

### 6. **Dynamic Category Generation**
**Challenge**: Hard-coded categories didn't match CSV data. Needed dynamic category filtering based on actual uploaded products.

**Solution**: Implemented dynamic category extraction using `Set` to get unique categories from CSV products: `['All Categories', ...new Set(products.map(p => p.category))]`

### 7. **Loading States vs Instant Display**
**Challenge**: Balancing between showing loading states and providing instant user experience with sample data.

**Solution**: Implemented a hybrid approach - show sample data immediately for instant UX, then load real CSV data in background and seamlessly update the interface without jarring transitions.

### 8. **Cross-Component Navigation Consistency**
**Challenge**: Maintaining identical sidebar navigation across 5 different page components without code duplication.

**Solution**: Created consistent navigation structure with proper active states, mobile responsiveness, and logout functionality. Used identical JSX structure across components to ensure consistency.

The biggest learning was balancing **user experience** (instant loading, smooth animations) with **real functionality** (live data, accurate calculations) while maintaining **clean, maintainable code**.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mapbox](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mapbox-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Global maritime navigation still relies heavily on static routing heuristics, fixed shipping lanes, and manual planning tools that fail to account for continuously changing ocean conditions, environmental regulations, and real-world operational risks. This results in inefficient fuel usage, higher carbon emissions, unsafe route selections during storms and piracy threats, and poor adaptability to last-minute changes in weather and congestion. Existing systems largely optimize for a single metric, typically distance or time, while ignoring the multi-objective trade-offs that define real maritime decision-making.

Navix AI solves this by introducing a real-time, multi-objective AI routing engine powered by HACOPSO (Hybrid Adaptive Chaotic Opposition-based Particle Swarm Optimization). It simultaneously evaluates fuel efficiency, safety, carbon emissions, travel time, and comfort to generate Pareto-optimal routes rather than a single rigid path. This allows ship operators to dynamically select the best route based on their operational priorities, automatically avoid hazardous zones, comply with emission regulations, and significantly reduce fuel consumption and carbon footprint.

For shipping companies, port authorities, logistics firms, and maritime startups, NaviX AI transforms route planning into an intelligent, visual, and explainable process. What previously required hours of manual planning and guesswork becomes a few-click operation backed by transparent AI reasoning, live environmental data, and interactive visualizations. The platform makes global shipping safer, greener, and more economical, while enabling data-driven fleet management and future-ready compliance with international maritime standards.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the most significant technical hurdles was designing a multi-objective optimization engine that remained both computationally efficient and numerically stable while operating on real-world geospatial grids. Early versions of the HACOPSO implementation frequently converged too quickly to suboptimal solutions due to chaotic parameter sensitivity, leading to unstable Pareto fronts. This was resolved by introducing adaptive inertia scheduling, bounded chaotic maps, and a controlled opposition-based reinitialization strategy, which stabilized convergence while preserving the exploration capability of the swarm. Extensive benchmark testing against classical PSO and genetic algorithms validated both performance and robustness improvements.

A second challenge was integrating dynamic environmental data, particularly storm fields and current vectors—into the routing fitness model without significantly degrading response time. Naively querying spatial layers caused unacceptable latency and inconsistent results under load. To overcome this, I implemented a pre-interpolated ocean grid layer and cached spatio-temporal weights at the cell level, allowing the optimizer to evaluate thousands of route candidates per second while still reflecting real-world ocean dynamics. This design preserved realism while keeping the system responsive and scalable.

Finally, deploying an AI-heavy backend to a cloud environment introduced reliability and cold-start issues, especially for long-running optimization jobs. Render’s ephemeral containers would occasionally terminate active jobs, risking partial results. This was mitigated by implementing checkpoint-based job persistence and resumable swarm execution, enabling interrupted optimization processes to resume seamlessly. Together, these solutions transformed NaviX AI from a fragile prototype into a production-ready, fault-tolerant platform suitable for real-world maritime use.

**Best Innovation**

NAVIX-AI represents a fundamentally new class of maritime intelligence platforms by introducing Hybrid Adaptive Chaotic Opposition-Based Particle Swarm Optimization (HACOPSO) into real-world ocean navigation — an approach that has not previously been implemented as a fully deployable, end-to-end decision system. Instead of generating a single “shortest” route, NAVIX-AI produces multi-objective Pareto-optimal route universes that simultaneously balance fuel efficiency, safety, weather risk, carbon emissions, and voyage comfort. This allows operators to make informed trade-offs based on real operational priorities, replacing rigid heuristic routing with intelligent, adaptive decision-making.

The innovation lies in NAVIX-AI’s fusion of chaotic swarm intelligence, opposition-based learning, explainable AI, and spatio-temporal ocean modeling into one scalable platform. By modeling the ocean as a living digital grid and continuously learning from historical voyage performance, NAVIX-AI evolves its optimization strategy over time — transforming routing from a static computation into a self-improving intelligence layer. The built-in “Why-this-route?” explainability further advances transparency, trust, and adoption in regulated maritime environments.

Beyond algorithmic novelty, NAVIX-AI delivers product-level innovation through its cloud-deployable architecture, carbon-aware compliance modeling, interactive Pareto exploration, and high-fidelity visualizations. This combination of research-grade optimization and real-world usability positions NAVIX-AI not merely as a smarter routing tool, but as a next-generation maritime decision platform — making it a strong and natural fit for the Best Innovation track.

**The problem it solves**

###  Problem Statement

**DevOps today is under pressure to ship fast, stay reliable, and scale across clouds.** Yet the tooling around it is still fragmented and manual.

- **What teams are up against**
- **Complex, provider-specific CI/CD setups**
    
    Each cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, Vercel, etc.) needs its own YAML, credentials, and deployment logic.
    
- **Slow, painful debugging of failed deployments**
    
    Engineers sift through long GitHub Actions logs and cloud error messages to find a single misconfiguration.
    
- **Fragmented visibility across tools**
    
    Build status, runtime logs, metrics, and alerts live in different dashboards, with no single source of truth for "Is production healthy?".
    
- **Manual, repetitive remediation work**
    
    The same classes of issues (env vars, ports, versions, secrets) are fixed by hand over and over, increasing MTTR and burning engineer time.

---

###  Solution Overview

**DevOps Insight Engine** is an intelligent, AI-powered platform designed to **democratize DevOps**. It automates CI/CD setup, centralizes monitoring, and uses AI agents to **analyze, recommend, and self-heal** deployment issues.

### Core Value Propositions

- **Unified DevOps Command Center**
    
    A single pane of glass to monitor deployments, statuses, error trends, and MTTR across multiple cloud environments.
    
- **One-Click Deployment**
    
    Automatically generates and pushes CI/CD workflows for GitHub-based projects with minimal input.
    
- **AI-Powered Log Analysis**
    
    Turns noisy build and runtime logs into clear, human-friendly diagnoses and actionable suggestions.
    
- **Self-Healing Pipelines**
    
    Agents can automatically apply safe patches or configuration fixes for common issues.
    
- **DevOps-as-a-Co-Pilot**
    
    Developers get an intelligent assistant that guides them step-by-step instead of relying on a dedicated DevOps specialist for every project.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges & Learnings

- **CORS & Cross-Origin Security**
    
    Secure communication between Next.js (e.g., Vercel) and Express (e.g., Render / Docker) required careful CORS + token handling.
    
- **State Management & Real-Time UX**
    
    Deployment polling and log streaming were handled with React hooks and tools like React Query to keep UI responsive.
    
- **AI Integration & Prompt Design**
    
    Prompts were tuned to reduce hallucinations and keep the AI focused on concrete logs and reproducible fixes.
    
- **Database Connectivity & Environments**
    
    MongoDB Atlas connectivity across local, staging, and production highlighted the importance of robust environment variable and connection management.
    
- **Observability & Feedback Loops**
    
    Tracking which suggestions are accepted or rejected creates a feedback loop to iteratively improve AI quality.

**The problem it solves**

## 🚨 The Problem

In today’s campus hiring ecosystem, referrals are one of the most powerful ways to secure job opportunities — yet the system is fundamentally broken.

### ❌ Problems for Students
- Students rely on **cold messages** on LinkedIn or email to ask for referrals
- No clear way to identify the **right alumni for the right role**
- High rejection or no‑response rates due to spam‑like outreach
- Fake or exaggerated profiles reduce overall trust, even for genuine candidates

### ❌ Problems for Alumni
- Alumni hesitate to give referrals due to **reputation risk**
- Difficulty verifying whether a student’s skills match their resume
- Time‑consuming to screen large volumes of unverified applications
- No structured way to mentor or support juniors effectively

### ❌ Problems for Colleges
- Lack of visibility into real referral activity and employability
- No centralized platform to manage alumni–student engagement
- Placement outcomes depend heavily on informal, untracked networks

---

## ✅ How NextRef Solves This

NextRef replaces unstructured, spam‑prone referral requests with a **trusted, college‑verified referral pipeline**.

### 🔐 Trust & Verification
- College‑wise closed networks prevent random or external spam
- Student resumes are verified by college authorities
- Alumni interact only with verified candidates

### 🤖 Skill & Communication Validation
- AI‑based **audio interviews** assess communication, clarity, and confidence
- ML‑based resume parsing and skill matching
- Alumni receive interview scores, not just resumes

### 🎥 Human Interaction Before Referral
- Alumni can conduct **real‑time video interviews** using WebRTC
- Referrals are given after actual interaction, not blind trust

### 📊 Transparency & Tracking
- Students track application status clearly
- Alumni manage applications efficiently
- Colleges gain insights into placements and engagement

---

## 🎯 Result

NextRef transforms referrals from:
> **Cold requests → Verified, interview‑ready opportunities**

It makes the hiring process:
- Safer
- Fairer
- More transparent
- More effective for all stakeholders

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🧱 Challenges Faced & How We Solved Them

Building NextRef involved solving several technical and product‑level challenges, especially within a hackathon timeline.

---

### 1️⃣ Building Trust Without Adding Friction
**Challenge:**  
Too much verification can discourage users, while too little creates spam.

**Solution:**  
We designed a **layered trust pipeline**:
- Resume verification by colleges
- AI‑based audio interview before application
- Alumni video interviews only after shortlisting  
This balanced trust with usability.

---

### 2️⃣ AI Audio Interview Implementation
**Challenge:**  
Creating a scalable, unbiased, and realistic interview experience without manual intervention.

**Solution:**  
- Used **ElevenLabs** for natural, human‑like AI voice interviews
- Built an agentic AI interviewer to ask role‑specific questions
- Generated interview scores to assist alumni decision‑making

---

### 3️⃣ Real‑Time Video Interviews
**Challenge:**  
Integrating video interviews without relying on external tools or links.

**Solution:**  
- Implemented **WebRTC‑based in‑platform video interviews**
- Ensured secure, college‑scoped communication
- Reduced dependency on third‑party meeting platforms

---

### 4️⃣ Testing Complex Referral Workflows
**Challenge:**  
Simulating multiple referral states (shortlisted, referred, rejected) without redeploying backend services repeatedly.

**Solution:**  
- Used **Requestly Redirect Rules** to reroute API calls
- Simulated real‑world backend responses
- Tested frontend logic in production‑like conditions efficiently

---

### 5️⃣ Maintaining UI Quality Under Time Constraints
**Challenge:**  
Ensuring the platform looked professional and trustworthy within limited time.

**Solution:**  
- Used **Magic UI** for polished components and smooth interactions
- Maintained consistency across dashboards
- Focused on clarity and usability over visual clutter

---

### 6️⃣ Deployment & Scalability
**Challenge:**  
Building something that goes beyond a prototype and feels production‑ready.

**Solution:**  
- Used **AWS‑backed infrastructure**
- Developed and deployed using **Kiro IDE**
- Designed the system to scale across multiple colleges

## 🧠 Key Learning

The biggest challenge wasn’t just technical — it was designing **trust at scale**.  
Every architectural and product decision in NextRef was guided by one principle:

> **Referrals should be earned through credibility, not requested through noise.**

**Build with ElevenLabs**

## 🎙️ Build with ElevenLabs — Voice‑Enabled AI Interviews

NextRef integrates **ElevenLabs** as a core part of its trust and verification pipeline through **AI‑driven voice interviews**.

Before a student can apply for an alumni referral, they must complete a **short AI‑based audio interview** conducted by an **agentic AI interviewer** powered by ElevenLabs’ high‑quality text‑to‑speech and voice capabilities.

### How ElevenLabs is Used
- AI interviewer asks **role‑specific questions** using natural, human‑like voice
- Students respond verbally, simulating a real interview experience
- The interaction feels authentic, professional, and engaging due to ElevenLabs’ voice quality
- Audio interviews are consistent, unbiased, and scalable across colleges

### Why ElevenLabs Matters for NextRef
- **Enhances trust**: Alumni receive an interview score instead of just a resume
- **Reduces spam & fake profiles**: Only serious, prepared candidates pass voice screening
- **Scales interviews**: Eliminates the need for manual pre‑screening
- **Improves candidate evaluation**: Assesses communication clarity, confidence, and relevance

### Impact
By using ElevenLabs, NextRef ensures that referrals are based on **verified skills and communication ability**, not cold messages or unproven claims.  
This transforms referrals from guesswork into **informed, trust‑driven decisions**.

> ElevenLabs enables NextRef to bring **human‑like interviewing at machine scale**, making campus referrals credible, fair, and future‑ready.

## 🔁 Build with Requestly — Simulating Real‑World Referral Workflows

NextRef leverages **Requestly Redirect Rules** to power and demonstrate critical workflows in our alumni–student referral platform.

Our platform involves multiple referral states such as application review, shortlisting, referral confirmation, and rejection. During development and testing, we used Requestly’s redirect capabilities to **simulate real‑world backend responses without modifying or redeploying server code**.

### How We Used Requestly
- Redirected API calls related to:
  - Viewing applications
  - Shortlisting candidates
  - Marking referrals
  - Handling rejection or alternate outcomes
- Dynamically rerouted requests to different endpoints to mimic:
  - Successful referrals
  - Failed or rejected applications
  - Alternative application states
- Validated frontend behavior under multiple backend scenarios in a production‑like environment

### Why Redirect Rules Were Chosen
We intentionally focused on **Requestly Redirect Rules**, as other features like script injection fall under premium offerings. By building entirely within the **freely accessible feature set**, we demonstrate how Requestly can still deliver **high practical value** for developers.

This approach allowed us to:
- Test complex user flows quickly
- Debug referral logic without backend changes
- Validate UI and state management reliably
- Speed up development and iteration

### Impact
Using Requestly, NextRef was able to simulate and validate complex alumni referral workflows efficiently, ensuring a smoother and more reliable user experience.

> Requestly enabled us to test, debug, and validate real‑world referral scenarios with zero backend redeployment — proving its power even within the free feature set.

## ☁️ Build with AWS — Scalable, Production‑Ready Infrastructure

NextRef is built and deployed using **AWS‑backed infrastructure**, with **Kiro IDE** as the primary development and deployment environment. AWS enables NextRef to operate as a **scalable, secure, and production‑ready alumni referral platform**, capable of handling real‑time interviews, ML workloads, and high user concurrency.

### How AWS is Used in NextRef
- **Backend API Hosting**: Scalable deployment of Node.js + Express backend
- **Database Layer**: Cloud‑hosted MongoDB (via managed cloud infrastructure)
- **File & Media Handling**: Resume uploads, audio interviews, and assets stored securely
- **ML Services Support**: Python‑based ML services for resume parsing and AI interview scoring
- **High Availability**: Cloud infrastructure ensures reliability across colleges and users
- **Secure Networking**: Environment‑based configuration and access control

### Role of Kiro IDE
We used **Kiro IDE** to:
- Develop and manage the full‑stack codebase
- Configure and deploy cloud‑based services
- Handle environment variables, builds, and production workflows
- Maintain a smooth developer experience while working with AWS‑hosted services

Kiro IDE allowed rapid iteration while ensuring the system remained **deployment‑ready and cloud‑native**.

### Why AWS Matters for NextRef
- **Scalability**: Easily supports growth across multiple colleges and thousands of users
- **Reliability**: Stable infrastructure for critical features like interviews and referrals
- **Security**: Protects sensitive user data and resumes
- **Future‑Ready**: Ready for expansion into real‑time analytics, notifications, and cross‑college referrals

### Impact
AWS enables NextRef to move beyond a prototype into a **real‑world, deployable platform**.  
By combining AWS cloud capabilities with Kiro IDE, NextRef delivers a robust foundation for **trust‑driven, AI‑powered campus hiring at scale**.

> AWS provides the backbone that allows NextRef to scale trust, intelligence, and impact across institutions.

**Problem**
Traditional artisans create high‑quality, culturally rich handmade products but struggle to succeed in the digital marketplace. Most lack access to simple tools for marketing, storytelling, pricing, and online presentation. As a result, they depend on middlemen, face unfair pricing, poor visibility, and language or literacy barriers that prevent them from reaching customers directly.

**Solution**
ArtisanVerse empowers artisans to sell digitally by providing AI‑powered tools that simplify the entire process. Artisans can create professional product listings using voice or simple inputs, enhance images for online marketplaces, receive fair pricing suggestions, and access content through text or voice—making digital selling easy, inclusive, and safe.

**Impact**
Enables direct digital selling without middlemen
Reduces pricing and product listing errors
Makes online selling less intimidating and more inclusive
Helps artisans earn fair value while preserving cultural identity

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blender](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Unity 3D](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity%203D-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
1. Bridging the Gap Between Civilians and Defense Tech Most people never get the chance to see heavy military assets (like warships, submarines, or battle tanks) up close. They are restricted, dangerous, or located in specific bases. This app democratizes access, allowing anyone to bring these massive assets into their living room or classroom to explore them safely and in detail.

2. Transforming Passive Learning into Active Exploration Traditional methods of learning about the Indian Army—textbooks, 2D photos, or video clips—are passive. They don't convey the true scale or complexity of the machinery. This AR application solves this by providing immersive, spatial visualization. Users can walk around a tank, inspect a ship from different angles, and understand the scale of the equipment relative to their own environment.

3. Zero-Cost, Risk-Free Training & Education For students, cadets, or defense enthusiasts, examining real equipment is expensive and logistically difficult. This app solves the logistical nightmare of physical field trips. It serves as a safe, portable digital museum, making defense education accessible without the need for physical travel or security clearance.

4. Inspiring the Next Generation By making the Indian Army's assets interactive and "gamified" through Augmented Reality, the app engages younger audiences in a way that static images cannot. It acts as a modern tool for inspiration and recruitment, sparking curiosity about engineering and defense careers among youth.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
1. The "Grey Screen" Configuration Nightmare One of the biggest hurdles was getting the AR camera to actually render on the device. After building the APK, the app would launch but only show a static "grey skybox" instead of the camera feed.

The Bug: The app was treating the project as a standard 3D game rather than an AR experience.

How I Solved It: I dug into Unity's XR Plug-in Management and realized the "Google ARCore" provider wasn't explicitly enabled. Additionally, I discovered that the Vulkan graphics API was causing crashes on Android. Switching the graphics API to OpenGLES3 and enabling the ARCore plugin instantly fixed the feed.

2. The "Infinite Clones" Logic Error Initially, my TapToPlace script was too simple. Every time I tapped the screen to move the 3D model, it would Instantiate (spawn) a new copy of the tank/ship. Within seconds, my room was filled with overlapping models.

How I Solved It: I refactored the C# script to check if the object already exists (spawnedObject != null). If it does, the code now simply updates the position of the existing object to the new raycast hit point, rather than spawning a new one.

3. The "Invisible Model" (Pivot Point Offset) When I imported my .glb models from Blender, the AR placement felt broken. I would tap the floor, but the tank would spawn 3 meters to the right or behind a wall, making it look like the app wasn't working.

The Bug: The pivot point (origin) of the model in Blender wasn't set to (0,0,0), and the export had a massive transform offset.

How I Solved It: I learned to "freeze transformations" in Blender before exporting. In Unity, I created a parent prefab to zero out the position (0,0,0) and standardized the scale to 0.1 so the heavy machinery fit realistically inside a room without clipping through the ceiling.

**Challenges we ran into**

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Database-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Ai Phishing solves the problem as it detects hidden pattern and tells us whether the email is spam or not.
NLP- AI reads the email/message content:
Urgency words: “Verify now”, “Account blocked”
Threat language
Grammar & tone inconsistencies
 Phishing messages follow emotional manipulation → AI identifies this.
Real-Time Detection
AI checks:
Links before clicking
Emails when received
Websites during browsing

**Challenges we ran into**

1) One of the major challenges was finding a large, balanced, and reliable dataset of phishing and legitimate emails/URLs.
Many datasets were either outdated or highly imbalanced, which affected model accuracy.
2)Identifying the right features (URL length, special characters, keyword frequency, sender patterns) was challenging.
Too many features increased complexity, while too few reduced detection accuracy.

### Ops Monitor
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ops-monitor-459a) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://devops-project-quzm.onrender.com/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XLXosi4LvcA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeQuest%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codequest-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Secure, Zero-Persistence Infrastructure Monitoring

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem Statement

In modern development workflows, sensitive environment variables are frequently hardcoded or stored in .env files that are accidentally committed to version control. Key issues we solve:

Credential Exposure: Hardcoded secrets in GitHub/GitLab lead to massive security breaches.

Infrastructure Cross-Contamination: Many monitoring dashboards use a single global database connection, creating vulnerabilities in multi-tenant environments where one user's leak could compromise others.

Deployment Friction: Internal tools often require complex local setups, preventing quick stakeholder reviews or guest access.



## Core Solution: Volatile-Session Architecture

Ops Monitor solves these issues through a Volatile-Session Architecture:

In-Memory Parsing: Users upload their .env file via a secure UI. The multer middleware processes the file buffer in-memory. The contents are parsed and stored in an encrypted session that expires after 30 minutes of inactivity.

Cryptographic Multi-Tenancy: The application establishes isolated MongoDB connection pools per user session. Using mongoose.createConnection(), we ensure that User A's infrastructure data is physically and logically separated from User B's.

Diskless Operation: No sensitive configuration data or configuration files are ever written to the server's persistent storage. The server remains "clean" at all times.

4. Key Features & UX

Real-Time Health Monitoring

The system pings configured server URLs at regular intervals (or on-demand) and reports status (Up/Down) with specific HTTP diagnostics, such as HTTP 500 Internal Server Error or Connection Timeout.

Render API Integration

We provide a first-class integration with the Render API. Users can:

View live deployment statuses (Live, Building, Failed).

See commit messages and IDs for the latest builds.

Check service types and environment labels (Production/Staging).

Zero-Config Guest Mode

A sandbox environment that uses a Map-based in-memory storage. This allows stakeholders to demo the full dashboard functionality instantly without providing any credentials or having a database ready.

Automated Audit Logs

Captures health check snapshots and manual deployment triggers. These are stored within the session-isolated database, providing a temporary but reliable audit trail for the developer's session.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a multi-tenant dashboard without a persistent central database presented several technical hurdles:

The "Global Connection" Trap

The Bug: Initially, the app used a standard mongoose.connect() call. This created a global connection shared by all users. If User A uploaded their .env, it would overwrite the connection for User B, causing massive data leaks and session hijacking.
The Fix: We pivoted to a Connection Pool Manager. Instead of a global state, we implemented a Map that stores mongoose.createConnection() instances keyed by sessionId. This ensures physical isolation between users.

Zombie Connections & Memory Leaks

The Hurdle: Creating a new database connection for every session led to "Zombie Connections"—idle database tunnels that stayed open long after the user closed their tab, eventually crashing the server with EMFILE (too many open files) errors.
The Fix: We implemented a Scheduled Cleanup Routine using setInterval. Every 5 minutes, the server scans the connection pool and forcefully closes any connection that doesn't have an active session, ensuring memory and socket health.

Webhook Statelessness

The Hurdle: External webhooks (like Render's deployment notifications) arrive without a user session cookie. Since our app is "Zero-Persistence," the webhook had no way to know which database to save the data to.
The Fix: We recognized this as a fundamental limitation of the "Zero-Persistence" model and documented a transition strategy involving Webhook Secret Headers to route notifications to the correct temporary database instance.

**The problem it solves**

# 🧠 Neuromo

> **Focus, but for real.**

![Neuromo Banner](https://i.ibb.co/CxLmfQj/image.png?text=NEUROMO:+AI+Focus+Assistant)

---

## 📖 About Neuromo

Neuromo is a focus and attention monitoring tool built for people who want to **actually work** — not just sit in front of a screen with a timer running.

Most productivity tools assume you’re focused just because the clock is ticking. Neuromo doesn’t. It measures **real attention** using computer vision and gives you immediate feedback when your focus drifts or when fatigue kicks in.

---

## 🚨 The Problem

We live in an **attention economy**, but our productivity tools still run on the **honor system**.

1.  You start a Pomodoro.
2.  You stare at the screen.
3.  You scroll.
4.  You zone out.
5.  The timer ends.

**It feels productive, but very little real work happened.** Neuromo exists to fix this "illusion of productivity."

---

## 💡 What Neuromo Does

Neuromo uses your device’s camera (with permission) to understand whether you are **actually engaged**, not just present.

### 🧿 Attention Tracking
If your gaze drifts away from the screen for too long, Neuromo gently alerts you and visually signals the loss of focus. It ensures that 25 minutes of work means **25 minutes of focus**.

### 😴 Drowsiness Detection
Using **Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR)**, Neuromo detects when your eyes stay closed beyond a safe threshold and triggers a loud alarm. This isn’t to shame you — it’s a **circuit breaker for burnout** and fatigue.

### 🧑‍💻 A Digital “Body Double”
For people who struggle with self-regulation (especially those with **ADHD**), Neuromo acts like a quiet presence that keeps you accountable — without judgment.

### 📊 Focus Over Time
Neuromo doesn’t just track time. It tracks **time spent focused**, helping you understand your real work patterns and quality of attention.

---

## 🛠️ How It Works
* **Computer Vision:** Powered by MediaPipe and OpenCV to detect facial landmarks in real-time.
* **Privacy First:** All video processing happens **locally** on your device. No video is ever sent to a server.
* **Smart Feedback:** Instant visual cues (Green = Focused, Red = Distracted) to retrain your brain.

---

> *"What gets measured, gets managed." — Neuromo ensures you are measuring the right thing.*

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

Building **Neuromo** wasn't smooth sailing, and honestly, that's where most of the learning happened. Here are the real engineering hurdles I faced and how I solved them.



---

## 1️⃣ The "Cloud Camera" Paradox (Deployment)

> **⚠️ The Problem:** I initially tried deploying this like a typical web app (Vercel/Netlify style). That failed immediately. I learned the hard way that Python-based computer vision apps (using OpenCV/MediaPipe) cannot run on serverless platforms that lack GPU/Webcam access.

> **✅ The Fix:** I realized that **languages and architecture matter**. A Python CV backend requires a different environment than a JS frontend.
> * I pivoted to a **Local-First / Containerized** approach.
> * I created a **Docker setup** so anyone can run the full app locally with one command.
> * This completely changed my understanding of "deployment"—it's a design decision, not an afterthought.

---

## 2️⃣ Streamlit Was a Trap

> **⚠️ The Problem:** I started with **Streamlit** to move fast. It was great for a prototype but terrible for a product. It limited my control over the UI, animations, and the "Glassmorphism" aesthetic I wanted. The app felt clunky and restricted.

> **✅ The Fix:** I made the tough decision to **rewrite the entire frontend** using HTML, CSS (Tailwind), and Vanilla JavaScript, connected to a Flask backend. It delayed the project by days, but the result—a custom, responsive, high-performance UI—was worth the pain.

---

## 3️⃣ Low-Light Detection Failure

> **⚠️ The Problem:** The AI worked perfectly in daylight but failed at night. In dim lighting, the landmark detection became noisy, causing the "Sleep Alarm" to trigger falsely even when I was wide awake.

> **✅ The Fix:** I stopped trying to "over-fix" hardware limitations with software. instead, I added basic **frame preprocessing** (brightness normalization) and implemented a **dynamic threshold** system. The app now waits for consistent data over several frames before triggering an alarm, drastically reducing false positives.

---

## 4️⃣ The "Z-Index War" (UI Glitches)

> **⚠️ The Problem:** The live webcam feed kept rendering *on top* of my Settings Panel, blocking the buttons. No matter what I did, the video canvas ignored the layout boundaries.

> **✅ The Fix:** I had to dive deep into **DOM Layering**. I restructured the HTML container hierarchy and strictly managed the `z-index` values (Settings: 60, Camera: 50) to ensure the UI components stayed isolated and layered correctly.

---

## 5️⃣ Dependency Hell (MediaPipe)

> **⚠️ The Problem:** Different versions of MediaPipe silently broke function behaviors. Code that worked in one tutorial failed in my environment because of version mismatches.

> **✅ The Fix:** I learned that dependency locking is non-negotiable. I pinned specific versions in `requirements.txt` and stopped relying on undocumented behaviors, ensuring the app runs reliably on any machine.

---

## 6️⃣ The "Ghost Audio" Bug

> **⚠️ The Problem:** The Lofi music or Alarm would sometimes keep playing even after I closed the tab or paused the timer. It was a small bug, but it ruined the user experience.

> **✅ The Fix:** I implemented proper **cleanup logic** and event listeners in JavaScript to forcibly stop audio playback and clear buffers on page unload or session termination.

---



## 🧠 What This Taught Me



* **Deployment is architecture:** You can't just "host" a CV app; you have to design for the hardware.
* **UI Frameworks matter:** Ease of use (Streamlit) often comes at the cost of flexibility.
* **State Management is key:** Most bugs were actually architecture mistakes where frontend and backend states fell out of sync.

*Every problem forced me to rethink my assumptions — and that made **Neuromo** much stronger.*

[Rajdeep Saha](https://github.com/C0D3K0NG)

**The problem it solves**

FIRST BUILDER PPROJECT

During disasters like **floods**, **earthquakes**, **tsunamis** or **fires**, the biggest challenge isn’t just the event itself — it’s how prepared people are to respond. In many regions, disaster training programs happen across different districts, but -

**1.** Disaster training data is often scattered across sheets, messages, or paper.
**2.** No easy way to track district‑wise training status in real time.
**3.** Hard to know which areas are prepared and which are still at risk.
**4.** Report generation takes time and lacks transparency.

**SafeStep** offers a central live dashboard where training records with photos can be uploaded and mapped — making disaster preparedness organized, visible, and easy to monitor.

This is our first project that we build from scratch, hope you will find it helpful towards society. We can take this project to big level if we get your support and guidance.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Handling image uploads and preview within the frontend gave UI issues at first — solved it by using controlled file input and testing with different image sizes.
- Displaying markers dynamically on the map required converting data into lat‑lng format — debugging through console and sample datasets helped fix it.
- Styling the dashboard and making it responsive took extra work — refined the UI using components and tested on multiple screen sizes.
- Connecting all components (form → storage → display → map) was tricky initially, but breaking tasks into small modules helped me solve them one by one.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves
Poor road conditions, especially potholes, lead to accidents, vehicle damage, traffic congestion, and slow emergency response. Manual inspection by authorities is time-consuming, expensive, and often inaccurate. Most cities lack a real-time system to monitor road health and prioritize repairs.
Our solution automatically detects potholes and road damages using AI/ML from images and location data, then maps them on a dashboard for authorities and citizens. This makes road monitoring faster, smarter, and automated, helping city authorities:
identify damaged roads instantly
prioritize repair work based on severity
reduce accidents and improve public safety
save time and cost spent on manual surveys
improve traffic flow and emergency routing
For citizens, it provides safer travel routes and allows them to report road issues digitally.
Overall, it transforms traditional road inspection into an intelligent, automated, and real-time smart city solution.

**Challenges we ran into**

(First Hackathon)
1.Integrating Different Data Sources
Our project required combining image data, GPS location, and road-condition metadata. Each data type came in a different format, and aligning them correctly was challenging.
How we solved it:
We standardized all inputs into a unified JSON structure and performed pre processing before sending data to the ML model.
2. Accuracy Issues in Pothole Detection
Initially, the ML model was detecting random dark patches as potholes, reducing accuracy.
Fix:
We improved the dataset, added more real-world samples, and applied data augmentation. After retraining, the model performance increased significantly.
3. API & Backend Deployment Errors
Deploying the backend on the cloud caused CORS errors and API timeouts.
Fix:
We configured proper CORS policies, optimized API routes, and used cloud-based storage for faster image handling.
4. Frontend Build & NPM Errors
While running the frontend, we faced npm installation issues and build failures.
Fix:
We reinstalled Node.js, updated environment paths, and cleaned the project dependencies (npm cache clean --force).
5. Real-Time Map Rendering Problems
Displaying pothole locations on the live map was slow and inaccurate at first.
Fix:
We switched to lightweight map libraries and optimized the geo-coordinates we were plotting.
6. Team Collaboration & Version Conflicts
Multiple developers working on the same code caused merge conflicts.
Fix:
We created a proper Git branching strategy and used issue tracking to avoid overlapping tasks.

**Duality AI Track**

Our project uses AI/ML to automatically detect potholes and road damages from images and geolocation data. This aligns directly with the Duality AI Track as it focuses on applying artificial intelligence to solve real-world problems at scale.
We use machine learning models for image classification, object detection, and severity analysis to identify road hazards in real time. The system processes visual data securely, converts it into actionable insights, and supports safer urban mobility.
By combining AI with smart-city data, our solution demonstrates how intelligent automation can improve public safety, enhance urban infrastructure monitoring, and reduce manual effort—perfectly matching Duality’s focus on impactful AI-driven innovations.

> Learn until it clicks.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

Parents and teachers struggle to help young learners understand math word problems.  
Most kids don’t fail because of the arithmetic — they fail because they can’t decode the *language structure* of the story.

This leads to:
- Guessing instead of reasoning  
- Adults repeatedly explaining the same patterns  
- No clear data on *where* the child got stuck  

Traditional worksheets and drill apps don’t expose the child’s reasoning path.  
They show answers, not understanding.

---

## How this app helps (Current Capabilities)

**Until You Understand/WAKARUMADE** breaks each word problem into small, guided steps so children understand *how* to think, not just what the answer is.

Current users can:
- Follow a step-by-step scaffold tailored for early elementary level  
- See the problem decomposed logically, one decision at a time  
- Receive immediate feedback that nudges them back on track  
- Have new similar problems automatically generated based on what they struggled with  
- Benefit from backend logs that analyze **which step caused confusion**, and receive **new variants targeting the same reasoning gap**

This makes word problems:
- Less intimidating  
- More predictable  
- More accessible to ESL families  
- Easier for parents/teachers to support without re-explaining everything

---

## Future Directions (Not yet implemented)

Planned enhancements:
- Highlight key linguistic triggers in problems (e.g., “altogether”, “left”, “in total”) to teach the link between language and operations  
- A parent dashboard showing:
  - what patterns the child has mastered  
  - where they repeatedly get stuck  
  - simple explanations of the child’s reasoning weaknesses  
- Progress tracking for logged-in students  
- Personalized practice sets generated automatically from each child’s error patterns  
- A library of problem types categorized by cognitive skill (comparison, combine, separate, equal groups, etc.)

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

- Implementing **voice input for kids** was tricky — raw speech is messy, so I built a pipeline that cleans and structures it before sending it to the AI.
- Designing **persistence without login** (kid-friendly, zero friction) required balancing simplicity with data-structure needs.
- Structuring logs so the system can **detect where kids struggle** and use that data for future problem generation was harder than expected.

**Best Use of GitHub**

## GitHub & Eligibility

My repository(https://github.com/MakikoOhashi/wakarumade) is fully public and all commits were made strictly within the hackathon window.  
The project was built from scratch during the event, including frontend, logic, and AI integration.


## How It Meets the Judging Criteria

- **Creativity:**  
  I built a math word-problem tutoring app for early learners that generates adaptive explanations and new practice questions using LLMs — a niche that is rarely explored for young kids.

- **Effort:**  
  The entire flow (voice input → AI correction → reasoning → dynamic hints → similar-problem generation) was designed and implemented during the hackathon.

- **Medium:**  
  Instead of a slide video or static assets, I created a functional interactive web app that can run on any device without installation. The demo video showcases the live behavior.

I focused on building something simple but genuinely useful and technically complete within the hackathon time.
