> AI-Powered Student Performance Prediction Tool

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Most learning environments have difficulties defining the performance of a student before final exams or evaluations. Teachers, mentors, and parents often need to guess, take incomplete observations, or wait for exam results to understand which students need their assistance.

This leads to:

❗ Late Identification of struggling students

❗ No customized learning path

Outcomes not easily predicted early on.

❗ Inefficient decision-making for educators

❗ Students not getting support at the right time

How this project helps the community.

This Student Performance Prediction System predicts the academic outcome of a student using Machine Learning based on several variables, including:

Study time

Preparing for tests

Parental education

Attendance

Past scores

Learning habits

Based on these predictions, the following makes existing tasks easier and wiser:

Early Risk Detection

Educators can identify low-performing students before the exams and take early action.

???? Personalised Learning Support

Students will receive guidance based on their weak points.

Data-Driven Decision Making

Removes guesswork: Teachers and institutions can rely on ML-backed insights.

Improvement in Academic Performance

This helps a student to modify their learning habits and increases their chances of scoring better.

???? User-Friendly Streamlit Interface

The web app allows any teacher, tutor, student, and parent to use the model without coding.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

Working on this project was exciting, but honestly, it wasn’t smooth all the way. I faced several challenges that really tested my patience — and helped me grow as a developer.

🔹 1. Dealing With Messy Data

The dataset wasn’t clean at all — missing values, inconsistent entries, and weird formatting.
Because of that, my model’s accuracy dropped heavily in the beginning.

How I fixed it:
I spent time cleaning and preprocessing the data properly — filling missing values, encoding categorical columns, and scaling numerical features. Once the data was clean, the model started behaving much better.

🔹 2. Confusion About Which ML Model to Choose

This was one of the trickiest parts.
Every model gave different results — some overfitted badly, and some gave very low accuracy.

What I did:
I experimented with multiple models and compared them using accuracy, F1-score, and confusion matrix.
After many trials, Random Forest turned out to be the most stable and reliable.

🔹 3. Understanding Which Features Actually Matter

Initially, I just threw all the features into the model without thinking much.
Later, I realized not all of them were useful, and some were even confusing the model.

How I solved it:
I used feature importance and correlation heatmaps to identify what actually impacts student performance.
This made the model cleaner and more interpretable.

🔹 4. Streamlit Not Running on My System

This was the most frustrating challenge.
Even after installing Streamlit, the terminal kept saying:

"streamlit is not recognized as a command"

I spent hours trying different solutions.

How I fixed it:
I finally set up Python PATH correctly, reinstalled Streamlit, and created a new virtual environment.
After that, everything worked smoothly.

🔹 5. Creating a Simple, Clean & User-Friendly UI

Even after the ML part was done, designing a UI that feels simple for teachers/students was tough.

How I solved it:
I used Streamlit widgets like sliders, dropdowns, and columns, and focused on keeping the layout minimal and easy to understand.

🔹 6. Connecting the Project to Real-Life Use

As a student, it was honestly challenging to understand how my model would help in real educational scenarios.

What helped:
I tried to think from a teacher’s perspective —
Which students need help? What study habits improve performance? What factors matter most?
This approach helped me bring real meaning to the predictions.

Anyone can access attendance registers physically; no authentication or privacy exists.

Organizing and preparing the student list with names, roll numbers, branches, and batches took time and required careful formatting.


2. Bulk Uploading Data to Firebase
Firestore does not support direct Excel uploads, so I had to format the data into JSON and upload it using scripts/tools.


3. Creating a Clean Login System (Teacher + Student)
Setting different login credentials and permissions for teachers and students was a bit tricky.


4. Ensuring Secure Authentication
Managing email/password-based login and preventing unauthorized access required careful configuration.


5. Designing a Beautiful UI
Making the dashboard both functional and visually appealing with animations took extra time.


6. Filtering by Branch, Batch, and Date
Getting Firestore queries right and efficiently filtering data was challenging.


7. Real-Time Attendance Updates
Setting up Firestore listeners to instantly update the UI when attendance was marked.


8. Managing Multiple Collections
Separating "students", "teachers", and "attendance" collections cleanly without confusion.


9. Deploying the Web App
Deploying on a professional domain and ensuring Firebase hosting worked smoothly.


10. Time Constraints
Completing the entire project (UI, backend, Firestore setup, data entry) within a short deadline.

### RFP Response Agent
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/rfp-response-agent-a369) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackBIOS%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackbios2k25.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> B2B RFP response process for a leading industrial

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![Webhook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Webhook-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTTP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTTP%20server-333333?style=flat-square) ![GOOGLE GEMINI API](https://img.shields.io/badge/GOOGLE%20GEMINI%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![n8n](https://img.shields.io/badge/n8n-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project focuses on optimizing the B2B RFP response process for a leading industrial 
manufacturer using Agentic AI. We designed a multi-agent system that automates RFP 
identification, product matching, and pricing estimation to improve response speed and accuracy. 

About our ideal client/user (Business) 

A large Industrial products manufacturing firm (client) with a business across Fast moving electrical 
goods (FMEG), Wires and Cables has seen considerable growth over the last 5 years. The growth has 
been driven by large Business to business (B2B) Request for proposals (RFPs) and tenders from 
infrastructure build out in India. The client wishes to further develop the B2B business by increasing 
the number of RFP qualifications and responses.  

Context on B2B RFPs 

Typically, large projects – e.g., government projects are launched by government departments or 
public sector undertakings (PSUs). These projects are executed by lumpsum turnkey (LSTK) project 
executors (PSUs or private enterprises). The LSTK project executors in raise RFPs for material 
supplies – e.g., wires, cables, other materials as RFPs to be supplied by Original Equipment 
Manufacturers (OEM) vendors.  
A typical RFP consists of technical scope of supply (quantity of wires / cables), technical specification 
(for wires and cables), test requirements and acceptance tests to be conducted before accepting the 
delivery of wires and cables (refer sample RFP). OEM vendors bid for these tenders and lowest 
priced tender is awarded the contract. The client is one of the large wires and cables OEM in India, 
who regularly bid for such RFPs.  

B2B RFP response process

* Once the RFP is received to the client Sales Team, they qualify the RFP based on the date for 
submission, past experience and product coverage.  
* Qualified RFPs are passed on to the Product Technical Team to match the client product 
SKUs to RFP product requirements. Refer sample of product specs.  
* The Product Technical Team finalizes the client product SKUs, which are the closest 
matches.  
* This is then worked on by the Pricing Team, which estimates the price of the products and 
additional costs required to meet the testing and acceptance test requirements at project 
site.  
* The Sales Team consolidates the inputs from Product Technical Team and Pricing Team to 
submit the RFP response to the LSTK project executor.  
* In case the client product SKUs has a low match for RFP product requirement, an internal 
request for new made to order SKUs is prepared to meet the RFP product requirements.  
Bottlenecks in the B2B RFP Response 
* The entire RFP response process is manually driven – with manual handoff between each 
team. 
* In many cases the Sales Team may not be aware of the release of RFPs by LSTK project 
executors on time. These are typically released on LSTK project executor’s website, received 
on emails. Delay in initiating response to RFPs would certainly mean lower chances of 
winning.  
* The technical matching of RFP requirements to Product SKUs is manually done. This requires 
knowledge of technical standards, specifications, and product knowledge.  
* While standards, specifications and product details are well documented, the technical team 
is often concurrently managing multiple RFPs and takes a lot of lead time to turn around 
their response. The Pricing Team can work on the price only after technical team’s 
responses.

**Challenges we ran into**

While the overall architecture from the solution plan was sound, I encountered several critical data-handling and integration bugs during the build. The main hurdles were not in the core AI logic, but in the "plumbing"—ensuring data was in the correct format as it passed between agents.

1. Technical Agent: PDF Parsing & Inconsistent AI Output
The plan to use standard nodes for PDF reading and JSON parsing proved to be fragile.

Challenge: The standard Read PDF node was unreliable. For the specific RFP files, it either failed or output text with poor formatting, which confused the Gemini AI.

Solution: I replaced the Read PDF node with a Code node. This new node directly uses the pdf-parse library to extract text, which proved tobe far more consistent and robust.

Challenge: The Gemini AI model, despite the prompt, would inconsistently wrap its JSON output in markdown (e.g., ```json ... ```). This caused the standard Parse JSON node to fail.

Solution: I replaced the simple Parse JSON node with another Code node. This node acts as a "safe parser"—it checks multiple possible output paths from the AI, strips any markdown wrappers, and then parses the clean text. This made the AI integration resilient to formatting errors.

2. Pricing Agent: Data Type Mismatch & Parallel Data Flow
This agent had the most significant bug. The plan assumed the Pricing_Agent's Code node could access data from both the initial Webhook and the parallel Google Sheets nodes, which isn't how the data flow works.

Challenge: The Technical_Agent was passing the sku_list and test_list as simple strings (e.g., "SKU1,SKU2" or "Test1\nTest2") instead of the JSON arrays the Pricing_Agent's code was built to expect.

Solution: I had to add a major fix (labeled // --- START FIX --- in the priceAgent.json) inside the Code node. This new logic checks if the incoming data is a string or an array. If it's a string, it manually splits it by commas or newlines and trims the results to build the clean array needed for the price lookup.

Challenge: The original plan's Code node couldn't get data from the Google Sheets nodes running in parallel.

Solution: I introduced a Merge node (not in the original plan) to wait and collect the outputs from all three branches (Webhook trigger, Product Prices, Service Prices) before sending them all to the final Code node for calculation.

3. Sales Agent: Web Scraping & Date Parsing
The plan for scraping the mock website was inefficient and the date logic was brittle.

Challenge: The original plan used three nodes (HTML Extract > Spreadsheet File > Set) to get the link text and URL. This was clunky.

Solution: I replaced this entire chain with a single HTML node using the extractHtmlContent operation, which can grab both the element's text and its href attribute in one step.

Challenge: The plan's date-parsing regex (/Due: (.*)/) was too simple and broke if there was an extra space after the colon (e.g., "Due: ").

Solution: I updated the regex in the Code node to /Due:\\s*(.*)/i to make it case-insensitive and, most importantly, handle any amount of whitespace after the colon.

Team **Robin** -- [Manotosh Kumar Phade](https://github.com/manotosh33), Chhayanka Dewangan, bhupesh verma, [Aditya Mishra](https://github.com/git-adityamishra)

> SIMPLIFYING LAWS FOR INDIANS

![Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Database-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML/CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML/CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
Many people in India struggle to understand legal rights and court procedures. Legal help is costly, processes are slow, and citizens don’t have access to expert advice or case histories. Judges also waste time organizing paperwork and searching for old cases.

What People Can Use It For
Understand Your Rights: Anyone can enter their problem (like dowry, property, or job harassment) and get an instant, AI-powered legal explanation in simple language.

Find Similar Cases: Citizens see real or AI-generated cases like theirs, including outcomes and the main reasons for winning or losing.

Get Legal Steps: The platform suggests clear, practical next steps for your situation—what documents you’ll need, which offices to visit, and how to start.

Ask for Help Safely: No need to visit a lawyer for every question—first advice comes within seconds, anonymously and for free.

For Judges: Judges can quickly organize case summaries, check document lists, and find relevant court precedents in one place.

How It Makes Life Easier & Safer
Saves Time: No endless Google searches, visits to lawyers, or confusing paperwork.

Reduces Mistakes: AI ensures you know your basic legal rights and required steps, reducing costly errors.

Safer for Vulnerable People: Victims of domestic abuse or fraud can get fast, private guidance.

Faster for Courts: Judges are less likely to miss documents or make avoidable delays.

Fairer Access: Makes legal help available to everyone, not just experts or the rich.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
1. Handling Undefined or Missing Data
Many functions were failing because input variables like problem or lawCategory were sometimes undefined.

Trying to call methods like .toLowerCase() on undefined caused runtime errors.

How I solved it: Added robust safety checks and default empty strings ("") before using variables. Added .toString() conversions to avoid non-string errors.

2. Parsing AI Responses from Gemini API
Gemini API returns free-text responses; sometimes it included extra text or formatting around JSON arrays.

Extracting AI-generated case JSON reliably was hard due to unstructured responses.

How I solved it: Used regex to extract JSON arrays from API text, added try/catch error handling to prevent crashes, and fallback default cases.

3. "Could Not Generate" AI Explanation
Sometimes the AI API returned no useful explanation due to API key, quota limits, or prompt design.

How I solved it: Improved error handling to show detailed API error messages in logs and UI. Also rewrote prompts to be more explicit and detailed to generate better AI output.

4. Deployment Issues With Google Apps Script
Received errors like “Script function not found: doGet” when deploying web app.

How I solved it: Added mandatory doGet() and doPost() functions with safe error handling. Ensured these functions were saved and deployed with the latest code.

5. AI and Database Integration Logic
Balancing between returning database matches and AI-generated fallback cases was tricky.

How I solved it: Clearly defined fallback logic where if the database returns no matches, AI generates realistic hypothetical cases dynamically.

**The problem it solves**

# Snipmatic

An AI-powered platform that converts YouTube videos into viral short clips using intelligent content analysis.

## Live Demo

Visit [Snipmatic](https://snipmatic.online) to see the application in action.

## Overview

Snipmatic is an innovative AI-powered video processing platform that automatically identifies and extracts the most engaging moments from YouTube videos to create viral short clips. Using advanced machine learning algorithms, Snipmatic analyzes video content, identifies viral moments, and generates perfectly formatted short-form content for social media platforms.

## Problem We Solve

Snipmatic solves the problem of turning long YouTube videos into engaging short-form content quickly and intelligently. Instead of creators manually searching through hours of footage to find interesting moments, Snipmatic uses AI to automatically detect the most viral-worthy segments based on audio, visuals, and engagement patterns. 

It then generates polished, platform-ready clips in multiple aspect ratios with optional subtitles. This saves creators significant time, boosts content output, and helps them repurpose their videos for platforms like TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts without any technical expertise.

With built-in social media integration, creators can seamlessly post their generated clips directly to their favorite platforms, eliminating the need for manual downloads and uploads. This end-to-end workflow transforms content creation from a time-consuming process into an efficient, automated system.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Deployment Complexity
Managing multiple services (FastAPI, Celery workers, Redis, PostgreSQL, Go email server) made deployment challenging, especially ensuring all containers communicate properly in different environments.

### Scaling Workers Efficiently
Handling high video-processing loads required tuning Celery concurrency, optimizing FFmpeg operations, and preventing Redis from becoming a bottleneck.

### Multi-Platform Integration
Integrating posting workflows for different social platforms (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts) is difficult due to varying APIs, rate limits, authentication flows, and upload requirements.

### Long Video Processing Time
Processing long YouTube videos with Whisper, FFmpeg, and AI analysis often caused delays, timeouts, and heavy CPU/GPU usage.

### Queue Orchestration Issues
Managing task dependencies (download → transcribe → clip) required careful orchestration to avoid dropped or duplicated jobs.

### Error Handling & Retries
Network failures, yt-dlp errors, or corrupted media files required robust retry logic and fallback mechanisms.

### Real-time Status Updates
Keeping the frontend synced with backend progress across multiple distributed workers was challenging.

### Storage & Cost Management
Handling large temporary video files and frequent S3 uploads increased both storage complexity and operational cost.

### Cross-service Communication
Ensuring smooth communication between FastAPI, workers, Prisma, and the Go email service required consistent interfaces and shared models.

### AI Model Accuracy & Optimization
Training and fine-tuning viral moment detection models to identify high-engagement segments reliably was time-consuming and resource-intensive.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Snipmatic uses the Gemini API to enhance the AI-powered clip generation workflow by analyzing transcripts and identifying the most engaging moments in a video. After WhisperX generates a highly accurate timestamped transcript, the text is sent to the Gemini model, which evaluates factors such as emotional intensity, key insights, humor, and audience-engaging patterns. Gemini then returns structured suggestions, including potential clip timestamps, relevance scores, and short descriptions of why each moment is likely to perform well on social platforms. These insights are fed into the clip-worker service, which then extracts the recommended segments using FFmpeg. By integrating Gemini, Snipmatic transforms raw transcription data into intelligent, meaningful clip choices—making the viral moment detection far more accurate and context-aware.

**Cybercrime Detection & Prevention**

Our project, CYBER-TRACE, is a direct and advanced solution for the Cybercrime Detection & Prevention track.

While the problem statement focuses on detecting phishing links, fake calls, and fraudulent transactions, our platform addresses the root problem: criminal anonymity.

Instead of just blocking a threat (which is reactive), CYBER-TRACE is an integrated OSINT and Threat Intelligence platform built for Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) to proactively investigate and identify the humans behind the crime.

It directly solves the track's challenges and goes further:

Beyond Phishing/Link Detection: Our tool not only detects malicious links but actively footprints the scammer's infrastructure, uncovers their real IP (even behind VPNs), and links it to other assets.

Beyond Fake Call/Message Flagging: We turn a scammer's phone number or UPI ID into a rich investigative lead. Our advanced OSINT modules link these identifiers to associated PII, social media accounts (like Telegram), and vehicle data.

Proactive Dark Web Investigation: We don't wait for a crime. Our platform actively unveils hidden illegal websites on the Dark Web, scrapes data breach forums, and fetches PII of scammers before they can attack.

In summary, CYBER-TRACE moves beyond simple "prevention" and gives law enforcement a powerful correlation engine to connect the dots, unmask the criminal, and build actionable intelligence reports to stop cybercrime at its source.

**Best Cybersecurity in Emerging Tech**

CYBER-TRACE is a prime example of leveraging Emerging Tech to solve a critical cybersecurity problem. Traditional cybercrime solutions are reactive and fail to identify the anonymous criminals. Our platform uses a stack of innovative technologies to build a proactive, next-generation investigative tool for Law Enforcement.

Here's how we fit this track:

Graph Database Correlation Engine (Neo4j): Instead of using traditional relational databases (which are slow and inefficient for this task), we built our core on an Emerging Tech graph database. This allows us to find complex, hidden relationships between disparate data points (a phone number, a breach-data PII, and a dark web forum post) with a speed and accuracy that is impossible with old tech.

Automated Dark Web & Breach Data Analysis: We've engineered an autonomous Dark Web crawler and PII fetcher. This system navigates the Tor network, bypasses anti-bot measures, and automatically extracts actionable intelligence from hidden illegal sites and data breaches. This automated intelligence gathering is a cutting-edge field.

Advanced OSINT & ML Automation: Our platform integrates and automates complex OSINT tasks (for Telegram, UPI, Phone) that are normally done manually. We also use Machine Learning models to power our real-time phishing and spam link detection, ensuring we can identify zero-day threats.

In short, CYBER-TRACE is not just another cybersecurity tool; it's an integrated intelligence platform that uses the next generation of database, automation, and AI technology to find the human behind the crime.

**The problem it solves**

In today’s digital world, reporting cyber incidents is often confusing and inaccessible to general users. Many victims of phishing, online fraud, or harassment don’t know where to report or how to provide evidence.
CyberSentinel solves this by providing a simple, secure web portal for reporting cyber incidents. It bridges the communication gap between users and authorities, allowing quick data collection, evidence uploads, and automatic categorization of threats — leading to faster action and a safer online environment.

**Challenges we ran into**

Integrating multiple components (Flask backend, SQLite DB, and file uploads) smoothly was challenging within a limited time.

Initially, I faced compatibility issues with Flask 3.x since before_first_request was deprecated — I had to update the logic to use a custom database initialization method.

Managing environment variables using .env was tricky at first, but I resolved it using python-dotenv.

Dockerizing the application took some trial and error to ensure the correct Flask environment and port configuration.

How I overcame them:

I carefully read the Flask 3.x documentation, tested locally in a virtual environment, and incrementally containerized the app. Each problem taught me something new about modern web deployment practices.

**Cybercrime Detection & Prevention**

CyberSentinel aligns with the Cybercrime Detection & Prevention track by providing a user-friendly and secure platform for reporting cyber incidents such as phishing, online fraud, and digital harassment.
It helps detect and categorize the nature of reported crimes through an intelligent keyword-based classification system, assisting authorities in identifying and prioritizing threats.
By simplifying cybercrime reporting and ensuring quick, structured data collection, CyberSentinel contributes directly to the prevention and early detection of emerging cyber threats in society.

**The problem it solves**

## Devfolio Profile - Reimagined

A different take on the Devfolio profile page with drag-and-drop widgets and customizable layouts.

## What's Different

- I reimagined the Devfolio profile page as an interactive dashboard where you can drag widgets around and customize your layout. The whole thing uses Devfolio's actual fonts and colour palette to keep things consistent with their design.
- The tabs have also been replaced to keep a dock at the bottom, in my opinion, it is a lot simpler and one can navigate to a particular widget directly from the dock itself
- The main addition here is drag-and-drop functionality - you can rearrange widgets on your profile, resize them, and the layout saves automatically. I also added the ability to reorder projects and Medium articles within their respective widgets, which isn't available in the current Devfolio version.

## Features

- Drag and drop widgets to rearrange your profile layout
- Resize widgets (small, medium, large)
- Reorder projects and Medium articles
- Responsive design that works on mobile, tablet, and desktop
- Layout persists across sessions (saved to local storage)

## Tech Stack

- Next.js 16 with React 19
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS v4
- @dnd-kit for drag-and-drop
- Recharts for analytics

**Challenges we ran into**

I implemented a v0 of the requirements by around lunch, showed it to Pratham(the frontend lead), and received the following feedback:
- Add visual drop indicators during drag operations - show highlighted zones for valid drop targets and a preview box indicating where the widget will land
- Improve widget resizing UX - while the fullscreen button works properly, there are 3 sizes - small, medium and large, so a more intuitive way of showing them was needed

The main challenge was handling all the drag-and-drop edge cases, especially when swapping widgets of different sizes. While dragging and dropping works perfectly between widgets of the same size (small-to-small or medium-to-medium), it doesn't work as smoothly when swapping between small and medium widgets.
Specifically when swapping between medium to small widget.

The grid layout struggled to recalculate positions correctly when widgets of different sizes were swapped, sometimes causing overlaps or awkward gaps. I spent a lot of time debugging the collision detection and position logic, but getting it to feel truly seamless proved trickier than expected.

The app is about 90-95% ready - the core functionality works, but the mixed-size swapping may still need some polish to reach the level of smoothness, but this can be a version that can be merged to prod I would say.

### Campus Unite

> One Campus. One Platform. Endless Opportunities.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Campus Unite addresses the challenges of scattered communication and low engagement in campus environments. Traditionally, students miss out on important workshops, seminars, hackathons, and networking events because information is distributed across multiple channels like emails, WhatsApp groups, notice boards, and social media. Event organizers face difficulties reaching the right audience, and campus authorities struggle to monitor activities and track complaints efficiently.

**Key Benefits and Use Cases:**
- **Centralized Event Discovery:** Students can easily find, filter, and register for relevant events in one platform, reducing missed opportunities.
- **Streamlined Complaint Management:** Students can submit issues or feedback directly, and authorities can track and resolve them efficiently.
- **Efficient Event Management:** Organizers can post, update, and manage events with better visibility and analytics on student engagement.
- **Personalized Recommendations:** AI-powered suggestions help users discover events aligned with their interests, skills, and academic goals.
- **Enhanced Transparency:** Authorities can monitor ongoing activities, approve events, and access actionable insights, making campus operations smoother and more accountable.

Campus Unite makes campus life more organized, transparent, and user-friendly by reducing information clutter, improving engagement, and enabling smarter decision-making for all stakeholders.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building Campus Unite, several challenges arose during development:

1. **Integrating Frontend with Backend:** Initially, the deployed frontend could not communicate with the backend due to CORS and environment variable misconfigurations. This was resolved by properly setting up CORS in the backend and using a `.env` file in the frontend to store the backend URL securely.

2. **Role-Based Authentication:** Implementing JWT-based authentication for multiple user roles (Student, Organizer, Authority) was complex. The hurdle was ensuring that each role could only access its respective dashboard and APIs. This was solved by creating middleware functions to validate tokens and roles before granting access.

3. **Dynamic Event Recommendations:** Designing AI-powered personalized event suggestions required careful mapping of user interests to event tags. Initially, recommendations were generic and not relevant. This was overcome by refining the AI integration and improving user profile data collection to generate meaningful suggestions.

Despite these challenges, iterative testing, debugging, and structured problem-solving ensured a fully functional and robust platform.

> Ai platform for smart study and career success

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Eduverse** is an AI-powered all-in-one career preparation ecosystem that solves the problem of unstructured and confusing self-learning for students and aspiring engineers. It uses Gemini-based AI to generate personalized, day-wise learning roadmaps for domains like DSA, full-stack, and AI/ML, adapting dynamically based on test performance. Learners can practice coding through a built-in LeetCode-style environment, take daily and weekly quizzes, and receive instant AI-driven feedback and concept explanations. The platform includes an AI chatbot mentor for continuous guidance, an interview prep suite with mock interviews, and an AI resume builder for ATS-optimized career profiles. A progress analytics dashboard tracks skills, accuracy, and consistency, while gamified rewards, leaderboards, and streak systems boost motivation. Eduverse integrates supabase authentication, Email JS for automated communication, and a time-limited access system for premium users. It also offers community discussions, mentorship networks, and company-specific question sets to make preparation structured, measurable, and engaging—all in one seamless, intelligent learning environment.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building the **Interview Prep** and **Coding Practice **modules in Eduverse, one of the toughest challenges we encountered was ensuring real-time AI feedback accuracy during coding and mock interviews. Initially, the Gemini AI often provided generic explanations or incomplete code feedback, which didn’t match the user’s actual code or interview answers. This made the guidance feel inconsistent and unreliable.

To overcome this, we refined our prompt engineering pipeline — we started passing structured code snippets, user errors, and context (like the topic or difficulty level) directly into the AI request, forcing the model to respond with precise, context-aware explanations. For interview prep, we built a question-level context handler that tracked the conversation flow so the AI could follow up naturally, assess answers, and give targeted suggestions instead of restarting the mock each time.

Another hurdle was test data synchronization between the coding practice results and the AI roadmap progress tracker. Initially, solved problems didn’t reflect in the user’s progress summary. We fixed this by linking the coding test database with the user’s learning record in Supabase, updating their roadmap completion dynamically after every test submission.

These improvements made both the coding and interview modules far more intelligent, interactive, and reliable — ensuring users receive accurate, adaptive feedback throughout their preparation journey

✅ **Track trends** in real-time

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges & Solutions

## 🚧 Problems I Encountered

### 1. **The Loneliness of Solo Building**

**Problem:** I've been building WarpSeek alone for almost a year now (started November 2024). No co-founder, no team, no funding. Just me, my laptop, and countless cups of coffee at 3 AM.

**Reality:** Some nights I question if anyone even needs this. I win **1st place at Bitget Women hackathon**, get excited, then... nothing changes. I'm still coding alone, still figuring out every problem by myself.

**What I learned:** 
- Small wins matter. That hackathon win reminded me someone *does* see the vision
- The Telegram bot version actually works great - users love it
- But I know Farcaster integration is where the real magic happens, and I'm not skilled enough to do it justice yet

**What I need:** Teammates. People who *get it*. Someone who can push this project to the next level while I'm stuck debugging API calls.

---

### 2. **The Monetization Mystery**

**Problem:** I genuinely don't know how to make money from this. Free tier? Premium? APIs for devs? I've built something valuable but can't figure out the business model.

**Reality:** 

- I  make $0 revenue
- Every Web3 project seems to "figure out tokenomics later" - is that the answer?
- I'm a builder, not a business person. This gap keeps me up at night.

**What I'm struggling with:**
- Do I charge users? Most Farcaster tools are free
- Do I sell data? That feels wrong and against decentralization principles
- API access for developers? But who would pay?
- Maybe I just need someone who understands Web3 business models to join me

---

### 3. **Farcaster Integration: My Technical Ceiling**

**Problem:** The Telegram version is polished. The Farcaster integration? It's... okay. Not great. I hit my skill ceiling.

**Reality:**
- Farcaster's architecture is complex: Hubs, Neynar API, frames, actions, channels
- I can make it *work*, but not *shine*
- I see other Farcaster bots that are slicker, faster, more integrated
- I know my limits - and I've reached them here

**What frustrates me:**
- I have the vision but lack the execution skills for Farcaster-native features
- Users tell me "it's good for Telegram but feels clunky on Farcaster"
- I watch other projects nail the UX while I'm still debugging webhook handlers

**What I need:** A Farcaster expert. Someone who lives and breathes that ecosystem. I'll handle the AI and graph analysis - just need someone who can make it *feel native*.

---

### 4. **Rate Limits When You're Broke**

**Problem:** Neynar API free tier = 150 requests/min. Paid tier = $200/month minimum. I have $0 budget.

**Reality:**
- I built elaborate caching systems because I literally can't afford more API calls
- Sometimes the bot is slow because I'm working around limits with duct tape and prayer
- I know paying $200/month would solve this, but where do I get $200/month with no revenue?

**Creative solutions I tried:**
- Multi-level caching (Redis + in-memory + disk)
- Request batching and prioritization
- Asking users to wait 30 seconds instead of instant results
- It works... but it's not the experience I want to deliver

---

### 5. **Imposter Syndrome at 2 AM**

**Problem:** Sometimes I think I'm not good enough to pull this off.

**Reality:**
- I see VC-backed teams building similar things with 10 engineers
- I'm one person with Google, Stack Overflow, and determination
- Some days I ship features I'm proud of
- Other days I can't figure out why the graph algorithm returns empty results and I want to quit

**What keeps me going:**
- That **Bitget Women 1st place** - someone believed in this
- Users who message "this actually helped me find the right people!"
- Stubborn pride - I'm almost at one year, I can't give up now

**What I'm afraid of:**
- That I'll never find the right people to help scale this
- That the opportunity window will close while I'm still learning Farcaster internals
- That in 6 months, a funded team will build this better and I'll have wasted a year

---

### 6. **The Skills I Don't Have (Yet)**

**What I'm good at:**
- AI integration and prompt engineering
- Graph analysis and algorithms  
- Python backend development
- Building scrappy MVPs that work

**What I'm NOT good at:**
- Frontend/UI design (my interfaces are... functional)
- Farcaster-native development (I'm learning but slow)
- Marketing and growth (I have 47 Twitter followers)
- Business models and monetization strategy
- DevOps at scale (it works on my machine!)

**The gap:** I need people who are strong where I'm weak. Not just contractors - *partners* who believe in the vision.

**What they do:** Keyword search for casts  
**Our code difference:**

**What they do:** OpenRank reputation protocol  
**Our code difference:**
- They calculate one score (OpenRank)
- We combine **multiple graph metrics**: betweenness centrality, clustering coefficient, engagement patterns
- Our AI layer synthesizes these into human-readable insights

> AI Agent Platform for Programmable Money on Base.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WalletConnect](https://img.shields.io/badge/WalletConnect-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![paymaster](https://img.shields.io/badge/paymaster-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gemini API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gemini%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Nekoma simplifies how people interact with **programmable money** on the blockchain.
Today, managing on-chain funds, permissions, and transactions securely often requires deep technical knowledge, multiple wallets, and manual verification steps. Nekoma solves this by acting as a **secure, AI-powered delegated agent** that can manage permissions, execute on-chain actions, and automate workflows safely.

**People can use Nekoma to:**

- Automate **on-chain transactions** like transfers or swaps without exposing private keys.
- **Set spending limits and delegate control** to AI agents or smart accounts for recurring payments or automation.
- **Bridge on-chain and off-chain workflows** using natural language—e.g., “Send $5 to 0xabc” or “Swap 10 USDC for ETH.”
- **Enable gasless transactions**, making blockchain interactions accessible even to non-crypto users.

In short, Nekoma makes blockchain interactions **smarter, safer, and frictionless** eliminating the need for manual signing, complex UIs, or gas management.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was implementing secure delegation of spend permissions while maintaining a smooth user experience.
Balancing **security, flexibility, and automation** required a fine-tuned system that could:

- Verify permissions both on-chain and in the backend.

- Prevent over-spending or unauthorized actions by the AI.

- Maintain seamless chat-to-action flows without lag or repeated wallet prompts.

Another big hurdle was **tool invocation through the AI** ensuring the Gemini API-generated toolcalls were properly structured, validated, and safely executed by the backend.
To overcome this:

- We built a schema-based tool validation system that parses and sanitizes every toolcall.

- Added retry and fallback mechanisms for network reliability.

- Integrated on-chain permission checks before any transaction execution, ensuring full compliance with user-set limits.

**Link to the GitHub Repo of your project**

https://github.com/YadlaMani/Nekoma

**Live URL of your project**

https://nekomaa.vercel.app/

**What is your product’s unique value proposition?**

Unlike traditional wallet automation tools or AI bots, Nekoma combines **secure delegation, AI-driven tool execution, and gasless transactions** into one unified platform.

Its unique value lies in being:

- **Programmable yet safe** — users set daily spend limits and permissions, enforced both on-chain and off-chain.

- **AI-native**— actions are triggered conversationally through Gemini-powered chat, not rigid UIs.

- **Developer-extensible** — new tools can be added easily, enabling cross-protocol automation and integration.

- **Frictionless** — users never worry about gas fees or private key exposure.

The **alpha build** validates this by showcasing:

- Secure login with Base and CDP smart wallet creation.

- On-chain permission enforcement.

- AI chat-to-action system performing real transfers and swaps.

- A modular backend that bridges natural language with blockchain actions.

**Who is your target customer?**

Nekoma primarily targets:

- Developers & advanced users who need programmable agents for on-chain automation.

- DeFi power users who manage multiple wallets, subscriptions, and recurring payments.

- Builders & protocols seeking AI-driven wallet management for users.

Early feedback from Base and developer communities confirmed a strong need for **trusted on-chain delegation and AI-assisted fund management**, especially for tasks that are repetitive, time-sensitive, or require multi-step execution.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

Main competitors:

- Safe Global (safe.global)  - Multi-signature wallet for secure fund management.

- Coinbase Smart Wallet  - Simplifies wallet UX, but lacks AI automation.

- OpenAI GPT Actions / AutoGPT Agents - Enable automation but aren’t integrated with on-chain permission systems.

Nekoma’s differentiation:

- **AI-driven but chain-native** - directly connects Gemini to Base blockchain via structured toolcalls.

- **Permission-bound execution** - enforces daily spend and delegation limits on-chain.

- **Gasless UX** -  powered by CDP paymaster integration.

- **Extensible tool system** - enables rapid addition of both on-chain and off-chain actions.

In essence, Nekoma merges Safe’s trust model, Coinbase’s UX, and AI autonomy into one programmable agent layer.

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

Primary strategy:

- **Community-driven growth** through Base and Solana dev communities, hackathons, and open-source collaboration.

- **Developer adoption** by releasing SDKs and templates that allow easy integration of Nekoma agents into other apps.

- **Partnerships** with Base ecosystem projects to embed delegated agents for transactions, automation, and analytics.

Why this fits:
Because Nekoma is a developer-first infrastructure product, **bottom-up adoption**through dev communities and open-source visibility will create organic traction.
Once validated by early adopters, broader expansion to DeFi, wallet providers, and automation tools can follow via integration partnerships.

**The problem it solves**

Creators often struggle with fragmented platforms, delayed payouts, and lack of direct control over monetization. Fans, on the other hand, want easy access to premium content and a safe, convenient way to support the creators they love. Tingle solves this by giving both sides a single, streamlined platform.

**Challenges we ran into**

One big challenge I ran into was setting up payment gateways, especially getting crypto payments to work alongside regular ones. Each provider had its own way of handling authentication and callbacks, and half the time, the test environments didn’t behave like the real thing. It took a lot of trial and error to get them to talk to each other properly.

In the end, I created a kind of middle layer to handle all the payment logic in one place. That made it easier to debug, switch gateways, and keep everything stable. It was frustrating at first, but once it clicked, the system became way easier to manage.

**Link to the GitHub Repo of your project**

https://github.com/AsukuOnukaba/tingle

**What is your product’s unique value proposition?**

Tingle gives creators real earning power by making payments simple, transparent, and fair. With a built-in wallet for instant top-ups and withdrawals, creators don’t have to jump through hoops to get paid. The platform puts full control in their hands — from setting prices to deciding who sees what — while fans enjoy a premium, secure, and genuinely engaging experience. Everything about Tingle is built to make financial and creative interactions feel effortless and trustworthy.

**Who is your target customer?**

Primary Target:
Digital creators, influencers, and entertainers who want to monetize their content directly and fairly.
These include models, lifestyle influencers, musicians, fitness coaches, and independent entertainers — basically, anyone who builds a personal brand online and wants more control over earnings and audience relationships.

Secondary Target:
Fans and followers who value premium, exclusive access to their favorite creators in a secure, ad-free environment.
These users are willing to pay for authenticity, direct interaction, and curated experiences rather than the chaos of mainstream social platforms.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

Our closest competitors are:

1. Patreon

 (https://www.patreon.com/)
 – A strong global platform, but it’s not built for African creators. Payment options are limited, and withdrawals can be complicated for this region.

2. Fanfix

 (https://www.fanfix.io/) – Focused mostly on Gen Z creators in the US. It’s selective about who joins and doesn’t support easy local payouts.

Dating Platforms

1. Bumble and Tinder

 (https://bumble.com/) and Tinder (https://tinder.com/) – Both strong globally but not tailored for African users or creator monetization. They focus purely on matching, not on helping users build and earn from real engagement.

How Tingle is different:
Tingle is built for African creators and fans. It supports both fiat and crypto payments, instant withdrawals, and a transparent commission model. With a built-in wallet and flexible pricing control, creators earn fairly while fans enjoy a premium, secure, and personal experience.

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

Our main growth strategy is community-driven. We’re starting by working directly with African creators and influencers who already have loyal audiences. When they earn and share their experience on Tingle, their fans naturally follow — it’s the most genuine form of marketing.

We’re also partnering with local fintech and crypto-payment providers so payments feel simple and familiar. As we grow, we’ll mix in targeted social media campaigns, but the real power will come from word-of-mouth and creator referrals.

This approach fits our audience because in Africa, people trust people — not ads. When creators show they’re actually earning and enjoying the platform, others want in.

**The problem it solves**

**HypeScan solves**

Meme coin trading is currently dominated by uncertainty and **FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)**. 
Traders often make decisions based on random social media tips or chase trends after they've already peaked. This leads to many people buying at the top of pumps and losing money when the coins inevitably dump.

Meme Coin Trading has no textbook, traders rely on guesswork. Maybe, we can do better?

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles in building HypeScan AI was **making the project live**. The tool requires the X (Twitter) API for real-time social sentiment data, but we didn’t have the budget to access it at scale.

To work around this, we developed **novel scraping methods** to collect the necessary data. While this allowed us to continue testing, it introduced significant risk; we’ve already had **11 accounts banned** in the process of validating the system.

Because of these constraints, our **landing page remains static**, and the live, fully automated version isn’t public yet. Despite this, we were able to test the core predictive and analytical features effectively.

**HypeScan AI - Why It’s Different**

Most people trading meme coins are chasing the next viral coin, buying at the top, and complaining when it dumps. I built HypeScan AI to cut through all that noise. It doesn’t show charts it predicts moves before they happen.

The alpha proves it:

**Price Trends**: We pull historical DEX data, so you see patterns, not just numbers.

**Market Insights:** GMGN and BitQuery surfaces trends before the hype hits.

**Social Signals**: Scraping X (Twitter) for mentions and hashtags means you catch the wave before everyone else.

**Account Profiling**: PCA highlights who’s actually moving the market, maybe whales, bots, and the sneaky players.

Bottom line? HypeScan turns chaotic market noise into actionable intelligence. The alpha shows that with the right signals at your fingertips, you don’t have to guess, panic, or FOMO; you trade smarter.

**Who is your target customer?**

Our users are serious meme coin traders; the ones scrolling X at 2 a.m, chasing trends, and tired of buying at the top. 
We’ve confirmed this audience through feedback and alpha testing: early users loved that HypeScan combines price history, social sentiment, and market analysis in one actionable dashboard. They reported being able to make faster, more confident decisions; exactly the problem our product solves.

**In short: traders who want an edge, not another chart**.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

**Token Metrics**

Website: https://www.tokenmetrics.com/
Token Metrics is an AI-powered platform offering crypto trading research, indices, and analytics.

Differentiation: HypeScan AI focuses specifically on meme coins, utilizing AI models to predict price movements using social sentiment as the core driver of the analysis, whereas Token Metrics provides broader crypto market analysis

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

HypeScan AI reaches users where they already trade and hang out. 
We aim to build a frontend on Base, therefore putting predictive meme coin insights directly in the hands of active traders on DEXs, wallets, and community platforms.

Growth is driven by crypto communities, strategic Base partnerships, and targeted social campaigns around airdrops and perks will make adoption easy, viral, and highly engaged.

> Social Coin

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Database-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The central issue GoodCoin addresses is the absence of a measurable, investment-backed framework for rewarding genuine social good in online communities.

Traditional social platforms reward engagement with superficial “likes” or reactions, which lack real-world significance. GoodCoin transforms that system by introducing $GOOD, a tokenized utility that attaches tangible economic value to altruistic acts and meaningful contributions.

By requiring users to invest in order to reward good deeds, GoodCoin transitions social engagement from passive consumption to intentional, value-driven participation, creating a sustainable economic incentive for people to amplify positivity both online and offline.

**Challenges we ran into**

Developing GoodCoin involved two main challenges: one technical and one conceptual.

The technical challenge came from working with an unfamiliar framework and developing our first smart contract. Managing secure on-chain transactions, ensuring accurate balance updates, and maintaining performance all required time, research, and experimentation.

The conceptual challenge was genuinely defining what “value” meant for a socially positive app. We knew we wanted to make goodness profitable, but the real breakthrough came during in-depth design discussions focused on aligning altruism with market incentives. Once we established a model where moral and financial value could reinforce each other, the entire product vision became clear.

**Link to the GitHub Repo of your project**

https://github.com/leonritz/goodcoin

**Live URL of your project**

https://goodcoin-henna.vercel.app/

**What is your product’s unique value proposition?**

GoodCoin is the first on-chain social platform where financial growth is directly earned by rewarding acts of kindness. It’s not just another social app or token, it’s an economic system that connects moral behavior with market value.

Two mechanisms make this possible.

1. Gated Utility Model:
Users must acquire $GOOD tokens to use the Donation feature, ensuring that every reward represents a genuine, deliberate investment in a positive action. This keeps the community focused on meaningful contributions rather than empty engagement.

2. Reputational Asset System:
The token’s worth grows in proportion to the community’s verified altruism. As users perform and reward good deeds, both the social and economic value of the token increase, creating a self-sustaining “Value Flywheel” where doing good naturally drives growth.

Our alpha build demonstrates that this concept works in practice. It provides instant, reliable on-chain tracking, real-time transactions, and a dedicated donation interface integrated directly into Farcaster, proving that a seamless, monetized altruism ecosystem is possible.

**Who is your target customer?**

GoodCoin is built for anyone who believes that doing good should be both rewarding and accessible.

Through our practical understanding of how people behave online and what motivates meaningful participation, we identified several groups most aligned with our vision:

- Crypto-native communities who value purpose-driven engagement and want their on-chain activity to reflect positive impact.
- Web3 social users seeking authentic, reputation-based interactions within ecosystems like Farcaster.
- Everyday individuals who want to make a real difference while participating in an open, transparent system that rewards altruism.

Our approach is grounded in how people naturally respond to recognition, reciprocity, and reward. By connecting these universal motivations with verifiable blockchain mechanisms, GoodCoin transforms everyday good deeds into shared economic and social growth.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

We recognize two primary categories of adjacent projects:

- Alternative social reward tokens, such as Degen (https://www.degen.tips).
- Farcaster engagement applications that incentivize user activity.


GoodCoin stands apart because it’s not just about engagement — it’s about intentional social good. Our mandatory utility model requires users to purchase and spend $GOOD to reward others, ensuring that every act of generosity has real weight and value.

In addition, our Value Alignment principle ensures that the token’s price and reputation grow only through verifiable altruism. This alignment between ethical action and financial reward turns GoodCoin into more than a product — it becomes a statement about what value in Web3 should represent.

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

GoodCoin’s growth is entirely community-driven, powered by token utility and organic engagement within the Farcaster ecosystem. Because the miniapp operates natively inside Farcaster, user onboarding is instantaneous.

When users purchase $GOOD to make donations, they create both demand for the token and positive social visibility. Each act of generosity amplifies community energy, attracts new users, and fuels the Value Flywheel: more users lead to more good deeds, which in turn strengthen the token and the brand.

To deepen engagement, GoodCoin will also host exclusive community events and real-life meetups for top contributors, reinforcing the non-monetary social value of the token.

By connecting the token’s value to acts of kindness, GoodCoin creates an ecosystem where doing good is the most profitable behavior possible, aligning ethics and economics in a single self-reinforcing system.

Team **GoodCoin** -- [Damian Mayr](https://github.com/mayrdamian), [Leon Ritz](https://github.com/leonritz)

**Description of your solution**

SureSignal 
 -- AI Agent for Detecting and Verifying Misinformation 

   In today’s fast-moving digital world, misinformation spreads faster than the truth, especially during times of crisis — such as natural disasters, pandemics, or political unrest. This spread of false or misleading information often creates panic, confusion, and distrust among the public. Our project, VeriPulse, aims to solve this by creating an AI-powered verification agent that detects, verifies, and explains misinformation trends across multiple online platforms in real time.

VeriPulse continuously scans public content streams such as Twitter (X) and Reddit, identifying emerging misinformation patterns or trending crisis-related claims. Once a potential false claim is detected, the system automatically cross-references multiple trusted and verified sources, such as official government portals, recognized news outlets, and open fact-checking databases (like Snopes or FactCheck.org).

The verification engine then evaluates the credibility of each claim using advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and AI-based entailment models, which check whether the information is supported, contradicted, or unverifiable based on available evidence. Each verified output is accompanied by a confidence score, clear explanation, and authentic references to support the verdict.

To make verification accessible to everyone, we’ve designed two key interfaces:
Taggable Bot for Twitter and Reddit:
Users can simply tag our bot (@VeriPulseBot) under a tweet or comment and use the hashtag #VeriCheck. The bot will analyze the content, verify the claim, and reply within seconds with a clear verdict — True, False, Misleading, or Unverified — along with verified sources.
Example:
   “Verdict: MISLEADING (78% confidence). Claim: ‘Tsunami warning issued in Mumbai.’ — Verified reports from IMD and NDMA show no official warning. Sources: [IMD Report], [NDMA Update].”

Web Application for General Users:
For users who want to verify claims outside social media, we built a web portal where anyone can paste a news link or text and instantly check whether it’s true or false. The portal provides: A detailed verdict and confidence score
Contextual explanation (with “Explain Like I’m 12” mode for simpler language)
A list of verified, authentic sources ,Option to save or share results
The agent architecture is modular and scalable. It consists of: Stream Monitoring Module — continuously collects trending crisis-related content.
Claim Extraction & Normalization — processes unstructured text into meaningful claims.
Evidence Retrieval Engine — searches multiple sources using semantic similarity and entity matching.
Verification & Scoring Module — runs entailment checks to determine truthfulness.
Explainability Module — converts AI reasoning into human-readable summaries.
Web & Bot Interfaces — for user interaction across platforms.

**Misinformation: Create an Agentic AI system that continuously scans multiple sources of information, detects emerging misinformation, verifies facts, and provides easy-to-understand, contextual updates to the public during crises.**

Our project, SureSignal, perfectly fits into the Misinformation track as it directly addresses the challenge of identifying and verifying false information during global or local crises. In today’s fast-paced digital era, misinformation spreads faster than facts, especially on social platforms like Twitter and Reddit,often leading to panic, confusion, and mistrust.

SureSignal aims to counter this by building an AI-driven agentic system that continuously scans multiple information streams to detect misleading or potentially false claims as they begin to trend. Once a claim is identified, SureSignal uses advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and fact-verification algorithms to cross-check the information with trusted and authoritative sources, such as verified government portals, reliable media outlets, and public fact-checking databases.

What makes SureSignal unique is its two-way accessibility:
   On social media, users can simply tag our verification bot to check if a piece of news is true or false. The bot replies with a verdict, confidence score, and links to verified sources.
For the general public, we provide a web platform where users can paste any claim or news article link to instantly verify its authenticity.

Beyond just saying “true” or “false,” SureSignal goes a step further, it provides clear, contextual explanations that help users understand why a claim was classified that way. This makes information not only accurate but also easy to comprehend, even for non-technical audiences.

By combining real-time monitoring, AI-based fact verification, and explainable results, SureSignal fulfills the track’s objective: to create an agentic AI system that detects emerging misinformation and delivers accessible, contextual updates to the public during crises. It’s built with the goal of restoring digital trust and empowering communities to act on verified, factual information when it matters mos

Hospitals often collapse under sudden patient surges during epidemics, pollution spikes, or public events, leading to overcrowding, delays, and preventable deaths. **Description of your solution**

Title
Hack Project Analyst


Problem Statement / Challenge Addressed
In today’s information ecosystem, misinformation can proliferate rapidly — especially during crises or trending events — confusing the public, spreading false narratives, and undermining trust. MumbaiHacks’ Misinformation track calls for an AI-powered solution that can continuously monitor, verify, and clarify content across multiple sources to help people discern fact from fiction.

Hack Project Analyst tackles this problem by offering an AI-based web platform that processes incoming content (project descriptions, news, GitHub data, etc.), analyses for inconsistencies or misleading statements, and delivers clear, contextual 
insights or verifications.


Solution Overview
Hack Project Analyst is a web-based system designed to:
- Ingest & analyse text sources (e.g. project descriptions from GitHub, news snippets, user-provided text)
- Detect potential misinformation or inconsistencies using AI
- Provide summaries, insights, and verifications in simple language
- Help users understand whether a claim or piece of information is trustworthy, with supporting evidence or explanations

It acts as an “analyst layer” over textual data — helping users and developers see at a glance whether content seems reliable, and where potential red flags lie.


Key Features & Functionality
1. Source Input / Upload
Users can submit project descriptions, readme files, news text, or repository metadata for analysis.
2. Content Parsing & Preprocessing
The system cleans, tokenises, and organises incoming data (detecting sections, claims, entities, etc.). 
3. Misinformation Detection & Verification
The heart of the system: using AI models (and selective external reference checking), it flags statements with low confidence or that conflict with known sources.
4. Summarisation & Insight Generation
For each input, it produces a digestible summary of key points, highlights suspicious bits, and gives a verdict—“Likely accurate”, “Needs verification”, or “Potentially misleading.”
5. Explanatory Feedback
Alongside the verdict, the system offers supporting evidence (references, alternative sources) and contextual notes (why a claim is flagged).
6. User Interface
A clean, responsive web UI where users see input text, results side-by-side, and can drill down into flagged items for more detail.

Technology Stack
Layer(Frontend):Technologies / Tools(Vite + TypeScript (React))
Layer(Backend):Technologies / Tools(Node.js (TypeScript))
Layer(Database / Storage): Technologies / Tools((Assuming from your zip) could be a lightweight DB / file store for user inputs, logs)
Layer(AI / Model Layer):Technologies / Tools(Pretrained language models + custom verification logic)
Layer(Infrastructure & Hosting):Technologies / Tools(Assume deployment via standard Node host / cloud)


Target Users / Audience
- Hackathon participants/developers who want to validate or refine their project claims
- Writers/content creators who wish to check if their statements might be misleading
- Researchers / fact-checkers seeking a quick AI assistant to flag suspicious claims
- Educated readers / general public who want clarity on whether information is trustworthy


Unique Innovation / Edge
- Multi-source intelligence: Unlike many static fact-checkers that check only news, this system can interpret technical descriptions, GitHub metadata, project proposals, and general news text.
- Contextual reasoning instead of binary judgment: It doesn't just mark “true/false”—it provides insight, explanations, and confidence levels so users understand why a claim is flagged.
- Real-time and adaptive: The system is designed to quickly process new inputs on the fly.
- User-centric clarity: The UI is minimal but effective—non-technical users can interpret the output without needing deep AI knowledge.


Alignment with MumbaiHacks Misinformation Track
MumbaiHacks 2025’s Misinformation track asks for an AI agent that:
- “continuously scans multiple sources of information, detects emerging misinformation, verifies facts, and provides easy-to-understand, contextual updates to the public during crises.”
Hack Project Analyst fits this guiding statement by focusing on scanning, verification, and providing contextual clarity over user-submitted content — especially in high-risk or ambiguous contexts.


Team & Responsibilities
We built this as a team (2–4 members). Some roles we handled:
- Frontend / UI development
- Backend API and orchestration
- AI model integration, prompt engineering, validation logic
- Data parsing, preprocessing, and evidence retrieval
- Testing and UI refinement 


**What’s Next & Potential Extensions**
- Automated source crawling & monitoring (news, social media) to proactively detect misinformation without user input
- Multi-lingual support to handle local languages
- Deep integration with fact-checking databases or knowledge graphs
- User annotations/feedback loop (users can correct or comment on flagged )

**Misinformation: Create an Agentic AI system that continuously scans multiple sources of information, detects emerging misinformation, verifies facts, and provides easy-to-understand, contextual updates to the public during crises.**

Hack Project Analyst fits the Misinformation track by using AI to analyse and verify information from multiple sources. It identifies misleading or inconsistent data, summarises verified insights, and helps users easily understand what’s accurate — ensuring clarity and trust during critical situations.

**Description of your solution**

The Problem: A System in Reactive Chaos
During crises in India—be it a festival surge, a pollution wave, or an epidemic—our critical infrastructure operates in silos, leading to catastrophic failure. Hospitals are overwhelmed by unpredictable patient surges, critical supply chains break, and misinformation spreads faster than the truth, causing public panic and preventable harm.

Our Solution: SentinelEdge AI, an Autonomous Command Center
SentinelEdge AI is not another dashboard. It's a unified, multi-agent AI system that works 24/7 to manage a crisis autonomously, turning chaos into automated, life-saving action.

Our system deploys a team of specialized AI agents that work in concert:

⚕️ Health Agent: Predicts patient surges by analyzing real-time data (AQI, weather, local events). It proactively recommends optimal staffing levels and bed allocations to nearby hospitals.

📦 Logistics Agent: Monitors the medical supply chain across the city. It flags potential shortages of oxygen or medicine and can autonomously draft procurement alerts before a crisis hits.

📢 Info Agent: Scans social media and news to detect and neutralize harmful misinformation in real-time. It generates verified, easy-to-understand counter-messaging and distributes it through official channels.

Advanced Features:
Multi-Agent Coordination: A sophisticated framework where agents collaborate to make holistic decisions.

"What-If" Simulation Engine: Allows authorities to simulate disaster scenarios to test and refine their crisis response plans.

Autonomous, Multilingual Citizen Alerts: Proactive health and safety advisories sent via WhatsApp and SMS in English, Hindi, and Marathi.

SentinelEdge AI is the future of proactive crisis management—a system designed to predict, prepare, and protect.

**Healthtech: Bring your own problem in Healthtech, leveraging Agentic AI.**

SentinelEdge AI is a Healthtech platform at its core, engineered to make our healthcare system resilient during crises.

Its primary function is to directly manage and optimize healthcare operations. The Health Agent achieves this by:

Predicting patient surges using real-time health indicators like pollution levels (AQI), local event schedules, and epidemic alerts.

Providing actionable recommendations for hospital staffing, bed allocation, and resource management to prevent overcrowding and save lives.

The other agents directly support this core health mission. The Logistics Agent solves a critical healthtech supply chain problem by ensuring hospitals have the life-saving medicines and supplies they need before a surge hits. The Info Agent acts as a public health tool, protecting the integrity of the healthcare system by fighting dangerous misinformation during a health emergency.

In essence, SentinelEdge AI unifies predictive health analytics, medical supply chain management, and public health communication into a single, autonomous system designed to safeguard our nation's healthcare infrastructure.

Fact-Strip is an Agentic AI system that combats misinformation by verifying facts and transforming them into visually engaging, easy-to-understand narratives. The platform continuously analyzes user-submitted statements, authenticates them using OpenAI’s NLP models, and leverages Replicate’s generative AI to create contextual, comic-style visuals that simplify factual information for the public.

Developed with React, Flask, OpenAI, and Replicate, Fact-Strip detects misinformation, performs sentiment and bias analysis, and assigns confidence scores to enhance transparency. During crises or rapidly evolving events, it helps users differentiate truth from falsehood through clear, visual storytelling.

Goal: To make fact-checking accessible, transparent, and interactive, empowering digital citizens to navigate the information ecosystem responsibly and stay resilient against misinformation.

**Misinformation: Create an Agentic AI system that continuously scans multiple sources of information, detects emerging misinformation, verifies facts, and provides easy-to-understand, contextual updates to the public during crises.**

Fact-Strip aligns directly with the Misinformation track by acting as an Agentic AI system that continuously verifies information, detects emotional bias, and presents verified facts through visually clear explanations. It uses OpenAI models for fact verification and mood detection, and Replicate AI to generate contextual visuals in three selectable styles — Comic, Newspaper, and Normal Image — making factual information easy to understand and engaging for the public.

The system analyzes user-submitted statements and provides a comprehensive result panel that includes:

A verdict (True/False) with confidence score, ensuring transparent fact verification.

A detailed description explaining the reasoning behind the result, bridging AI prediction with real-world logic.

Mood detection, which identifies emotional tones such as neutrality, positivity, or negativity to detect potential bias.

A visual fact-strip, where verified facts are transformed into a 4-panel comic-like visual explanation — combining education with creativity.

By merging fact verification, emotional analysis, and AI-generated visual storytelling, Fact-Strip empowers users to discern truth from misinformation quickly. It not only combats false claims but also makes complex facts accessible to a wider audience through clear, engaging, and contextualized visuals.
