> Transform your notes into confident speeches

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![ElevenLabs API](https://img.shields.io/badge/ElevenLabs%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**What is it?**

Monologue is a simple tool that turns messy notes into an eloquent speech you can voice out loud. It uses an advanced language model to polish your notes, and lets you edit the text before reading it back in a natural voice powered by ElevenLabs, including your own voice! It is freely available on both on desktop or mobile without any signups or downloads.

**Who is it for?**

Monologue is for anyone who wants to speak with confidence. This includes leaders rehearsing talks, employees preparing presentations, and individuals looking to polish a short speech.

**The problem**

When you need to speak, it is hard to turn rough notes into something clear and natural. Reading your notes out loud feels awkward, and switching between different apps to write, record, and listen takes too long. Most people give up before it sounds good.

**How it solves the problem**

With Monologue, you paste your notes and pick a style: TED-style talk, business pitch, or stand-up comedy for fun. The tool uses a smart language model to turn your notes into a short speech. You can edit as you please, then press play to hear it in your own voice or a sample voice. It shows you exactly how you would sound, so you can use it as inspiration to practice and get there. Everything happens on one page, it only takes a few minutes, and you can practice privately until you feel confident.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Bolt platform issues** I got stuck in a groundhog day loop, where Bolt:

- repeatedly showed out-of-order steps or revealed later steps prematurely, making it difficult to enforce a strict, stepwise user flow (input → style → preview → voice → playback)
- claimed to make changes without it reflecting in the actual updates. 

For both I used a combination of Claude 4.0, ChatGPT and Perplexity Pro to debug. I eventually had to force a complete reset and start over. I also found that big and complex instructions often broke Bolt’s editor, so I made edits in small, homogenous prompts, applied one at a time. 

**Selecting the LLM under the hood** I considered the following options and tradeoffs:

- Initially I wanted to integrate with OpenAI's GPT 3.5 or 4 API at the backend due to its reputation for quality and reliability. However, as OpenAI has changed their free credits policy to require payment method from new accounts, it became a nonstarter for hackathon prototyping. It is also a blocker for a frictionless, account-free experience and at $0.002 per 1,000 tokens, can get costly quickly.

- Next, I considered one of the Hugging face models, but ultimately decided against it for this MVP. Even though these are open source and low cost, the output is less polished vs proprietary models. Since Monologue’s core value is generating speeches that sound professional, I prioritized rewrite quality. 

- For this hackathon, I integrated Google’s Gemini Flash 1.5, which delivers excellent text rewriting quality. The generous free tier (15 API calls per minute) is ideal for demos and testing, and allows rapid iteration without worrying about credit card bills. I currently cap usage at 1,600 characters per request (700 for input, 900 for output), balancing user needs with model/token limits and keeping response times fast. Post prrof of concept, I will re-evaluate paid options for upgraded versions.

**Voice AI & Conversational Products | Powered by Elevenlabs**

This product demonstrates the power of voice AI. Public speaking is one of the world’s top anxieties. Most people dread turning messy notes into a confident, engaging speech, and traditional tools don’t help bridge the gap between writing and real-life delivery. Monologue solves this through ElevenLabs’ voice cloning. Users write their raw ideas that Monologue instantly turns into polished speech using a large language model, and then brings it to life in their own synthetic voice via the ElevenLabs API.

Whilst polishing writeup with AI is no longer a novelty, Monologue’s unique value lies in letting users actually hear themselves speak at their very best. This transforms abstract feedback into tangible, personal audio inspiration. Users can practice with the “best version” of themselves, internalize it, and gain the confidence to deliver it in real life. By giving immediate, realistic voice feedback, Monologue makes practicing public speaking faster, more motivating, and truly personal.

Neelanjana Basu

**The problem it solves**

That’s where our app comes in — your AI-powered project whisperer 🤖✨

In short → We take the boring parts of meetings and turn them into actionable, listenable, and lovable insights 💜

**Challenges we ran into**

🐞 Challenges I Ran Into

Building this project solo meant I wore all the hats, dev, designer, debugger, and occasional therapist for my own sanity. Here’s what tripped me up along the way:

🔐 Auth0 Adventures
Getting authentication right wasn’t easy. Between localhost vs Render hosting configs and trying to make the default UI look less… 2005, I spent a good chunk of time convincing Auth0 to behave. Eventually, I tamed it but not without some late-night head-scratching.

🤔 API Identity Crisis
OpenAI turned into a bit of a rabbit hole. Should I use completions? Or responses? (Spoiler: I wanted insights, not essays.) I spent a lot of time tinkering, only to feel like I was fighting the tool. The escape hatch came when I switched to Gemini, it gave me more structured, concise outputs and felt like the right fit for digging out action items and project details. That shift was the breakthrough I needed.

🎙 Getting Voices to Talk
Connecting Gemini insights with ElevenLabs voice output was like making two new friends work together on day one of class. At first, silence. Then, robotic gibberish. After a lot of trial and error, I finally had transcripts turning into natural, human-like audio.

🤖 Prompt Engineering the Builder
Since I used Windsurf AI to generate much of the scaffolding, I had to learn how to ask it the right way. A vague prompt gave me boilerplate, but a detailed one gave me a multi-page, Tailwind-styled, TypeScript app with a floating navbar + Auth0. Basically, I became a prompt whisperer.

🚧 The Big Roadblock
Here’s the honest bit, I wasn’t able to publish this web app in time. Coming from a data science background, I wasn’t fully comfortable handling API requests and deployment quirks on Render. Combine that with the hackathon clock ticking ⏰, and I had to leave deployment unfinished.

⚡ Being a one-person team meant every hurdle was mine to clear but it also meant every win was mine to celebrate. Even though I couldn’t push it live, I walked away with a working local prototype, deeper API knowledge, and a battle-tested mindset.

**Challenges I Ran Into**

Building Meera Clinic AI came with its own set of hurdles:

*Real-time voice interaction*
- Challenge: Integrating the OpenAI Realtime API for smooth, low-latency conversations was tricky, especially with handling interruptions while the user was still speaking.

*Multilingual understanding*
- Challenge: Ensuring the AI could handle multiple Indian languages (Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu) along with English and foreign languages without confusion.

*Doctor availability & scheduling*

*Voice call integration*
- Challenge: Connecting the AI with a real call interface (so users could actually talk to it) required handling WebRTC/audio streaming smoothly.

**The problem it solves**

He basically just faked his resume, vibe, coded his way through interviews, and just, well, did all the jobs at the same time until he got busted by one company. So in a world where remote work is becoming the norm and where vive coding is flooding our repos, how do you keep track of these bad hires? And let's be real, background checking tools are just, well, a nightmare right now. They're very clunky, they're very expensive, and they're just way too slow for our fast startup lives. This is why we've decided to build Unmask

Unmask is your tool to bust unauthentic candidates by cross referencing their CV, their LinkedIn, GitHub, calling references, and also giving you notes during interviews so that you can bust fake, fake questions. But enough talking from me.

Unmask is an intelligent hiring verification platform that helps you verify candidate authenticity through comprehensive analysis of CVs, LinkedIn profiles, GitHub accounts, and automated reference calls. Built for **mosAIc: AI in action with The Product Folks 2025

Windsurf

**Challenges we ran into**

🔐 Supabase Storage Configuration
Problem: Bucket not found errors in fresh environments.
Solution: Added storage bucket creation to migrations with RLS policies.

🔑 Authentication State Management
Problem: JWT errors after database resets with cached tokens.
Solution: Implemented proper session cleanup workflow.



⚡ ElevenLabs Integration Complexity
Problem: Multi-step setup with poor documentation caused delays.
Solution: Built comprehensive setup validation and guides.

🔄 Concurrent Webhook Processing
Problem: Race conditions causing duplicate API calls to Ashby.
Solution: Used PostgreSQL locks (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) for atomic processing.

### Crowd Management and Abnormality Detection
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/crowd-management-and-abnormality-detection-66dd) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/allamsettykruthika/crowd-management) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackOdisha%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackodisha-4.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Predict. Prevent. Protect.

![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Colab](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Colab-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![SMTP](https://img.shields.io/badge/SMTP-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ultralytics YOLOv8](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ultralytics%20YOLOv8-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

With the advancements in computer vision and Artificial Intelligence, crowd management has become an extremely complex field. Traditional surveillance methods are being replaced by intelligent systems that can monitor and understand crowd behavior in real time. For instance, the deep graph convolutional networks have made it possible to analyze interactions between individuals within a crowd which allows more accurate behavioral characterization . Simultaneously, the hybrid approaches that combine object detection with motion tracking—such as those built on YOLOv4—are estimating the number of people, their speed, and direction with exceptional precision, making the real-time crowd monitoring more efficient . Beyond detection, researchers have started applying the formal concept analysis alongside machine learning to capture a better structure and context of crowd movements .These advancements have real-world impact, which include the high-density environments like Hajj and Umrah, where AI technologies are being used to enhance both crowd safety and the overall experience of pilgrims . From a broader perspective, the deep learning models enable the prediction of crowd density and flow across the cities, helping authorities to prepare and manage public events or rush-hour surges . Furthermore, recurrent neural networks have improved these models by detecting the temporal patterns in crowd transitions across different city zones. Explainable AI ensures that the systems will remain clear and interpretable as models grow more complex, especially when they are used in critical surveillance scenarios . At the cutting edge, attention-based bilinear convolutional networks are being used to more reliably flag anomalies and estimate crowd density at the same time . Research work in  has concentrated on preventing stampedes by detecting sudden surges in crowds using dense optical flow. Studies [ shows the necessity of a robust anomaly detection framework that integrates deep learning with motion and texture-based features. These innovations reflect a growing commitment to safer, smarter crowd management systems that can adapt to the dynamic nature of public spaces. In real-time crowd management scenarios, the goal is to ensure that information is delivered to decision-makers allowing them to assess the situation before it worsens.Our system uses an email alert mechanism to inform the on-site security teams, that are responsible for managing crowd in that region whenever crowd thresholds are exceeded or any abnormal activities like running, kicking, or crawling are detected. An important advantage of this system is that it doesn’t need continuous human monitoring, which is often error-prone and inconsistent in traditional surveillance setups. Moreover, it also reduces the communication delay that typically occurs when alerts are routed through control rooms before reaching the concerned security incharges. By directly giving alerts to the respective authorities, response time gets faster and is more efficient crowd management. Also these alerts act as early indicators to the authorities to take timely action before the situation goes out of control.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges I encountered during the development of this project was differentiating between "running" and "kicking" activities. Both involve rapid motion of the lower body, which initially caused frequent misclassifications.
How I Solved It:-
Running Detection:
I refined the detection by setting correct speed thresholds. By repeatedly experimenting and tuning these thresholds, I was able to reliably classify continuous forward motion as "running".
Kicking Detection:
For kicks, I focused on the leg region and applied Optical Flow (Farneback method). This allowed me to capture the distinct, localized burst of movement typical of a kick, which is different from the consistent motion seen in running.
Outcome
By combining speed-based thresholds for running with region-specific optical flow analysis for kicking, I achieved a more accurate classification system. This significantly reduced false positives and improved the reliability of abnormal activity detection.

**Use Gofr (A Golang Framework)**

Our project fits into the GoFr track as we can leverage GoFr’s efficient API framework to handle the backend of real-time alerting. Crowd monitoring detections (running, kicking, crawling, overcrowding) can be exposed as REST APIs using GoFr, which allows fast, scalable, and low-latency communication between the AI detection system and the alert delivery module. This makes the solution more reliable for high-density environments where quick response is critical.

**Build with Orkes Conductor in the AI Track**

Our project leverages AI-driven crowd monitoring and abnormal activity detection (running, kicking, crawling) in real-time. Using Orkes Conductor, the system can orchestrate workflows for automated alerts, where detections immediately trigger email notifications to security teams without manual intervention. This ensures faster decision-making, reduced response time, and a scalable workflow that adapts to high-density environments such as public gatherings, festivals, or pilgrimages.

**The problem it solves**

- Mailbox often load slowly or get cluttered.
- Important mails get buried under irrelevant ones.

**Challenges we ran into**

- My deployed n8n Docker instance on initially lost workflows and nodes credentials after restarts. I solved this by connecting an external database for **persistent storage** and setting a **fixed ENCRYPTION_KEY** to preserve credentials.

- One challenge was that the Outlook trigger provided the email body in **raw HTML**, which included tags, styles, and extra spaces, making it hard to work with. I solved this by writing a **Code node** that stripped out HTML tags, removed script/style sections, and normalized whitespace, giving me a **clean text** version (body_clean) that was consistent and easy to use.

- The AI sometimes returned unstructured text, so I used a **Structured Output Parser** with a JSON schema to ensure the output could be saved directly to Google Sheets.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional crowdfunding platforms often face issues such as :
1. **Lack of Trust:** Donors hesitate because campaigns are often unverified.
2. **Low engagement:** Users typically make a one-time contribution and do not return.
3. **Organizer difficulties:** Creating and managing campaigns efficiently is often tiresome.

Our platform, Benevo, addresses these challenges by :
1.  **Verification-first Approach:** Every campaign will be verified through a review and approval process, ensuring authenticity and building donors' confidence in the campaign.
2. **Gamified Donor Experience:** Contributors can earn badges, which will help in encouraging repeated donations, and contributors can showcase their badges.
3. **Organizer-friendly tools:** Campaign creators can track donations, monitor progress, and manage fund withdrawals efficiently.
4. **Transparent giving:** Donors can see exactly where their contributions go, fostering trust and long-term support.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of the crowdfunding platform, we as a team faced a few hands-on challenges:

1. **Bug with campaign display**  
   - **Problem:** Initially, the campaigns were not showing up correctly for new users due to a database query issue.  
   - **Solution:** We debugged step by step, checking the API response and fixing the query to fetch correctly and filter campaigns.

2. **Integrating leaderboard logic**  
   - **Problem:** Ranking users based on points and badges caused errors when multiple users had the same score.  
   - **Solution:** We added tie-handling logic and thoroughly tested edge cases to ensure leaderboard accuracy.

3. **Simplifying the website flow**  
   - **Problem:** Trying to reduce the number of pages led to confusion in navigation, and some links broke.  
   - **Solution:** We mapped the **user journey carefully**, restructured navigation, and tested each path to simplify it for users.

4. **File upload issues**  
   - **Problem:** Image uploads for campaigns sometimes failed due to incorrect server handling.  
   - **Solution:** I debugged the upload middleware and added error handling to make the process smooth, and also used MongoDB for storing these image uploads.

These experiences taught us **patience, debugging skills, and the importance of testing every feature thoroughly, and how much can be learned through hands-on project building**.

> Predict. Prepare. Perform.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Students often struggle to understand how their daily habits—like study hours, attendance, sleep, extracurricular activities, or screen time—impact their academic performance. Many students prepare without clear direction, leaving them unsure whether their current efforts will lead to good results or if adjustments are needed.

Teachers and parents also lack data-driven insights to guide students. Most feedback is either subjective or comes too late, after exams, when it’s difficult to make improvements.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Faced

Data Preparation & Encoding
Handling categorical features like school type required one-hot encoding, which created mismatches between the training data and the input features from the frontend.
Ensuring consistent preprocessing between training and prediction was tricky.

Frontend–Backend Integration
Mapping the frontend form inputs to the exact feature names the backend model expected.
Encountered issues where the React form was sending different field names than the Flask API, causing prediction errors.

Error Handling & Null Values
At one point, the frontend crashed (result.predicted_marks was null) because the app didn’t handle empty or failed API responses gracefully.
Had to add safeguards (result && result.predicted_marks) before rendering.

CORS & API Requests
Faced cross-origin request (CORS) issues when trying to connect React with Flask. Had to configure flask_cors properly to allow requests from the frontend.

Model Accuracy vs. Interpretability
Choosing the right features and balancing accuracy with understandable results. Some features (like social media time) had less obvious weight in predictions, so explaining results to users was a challenge.

> One Click Digital Badges for Real-World Events.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Organizing events whether it’s a small club meeting or a large conference often feels stressful and inefficient. That’s because most people are still using tools that don’t really fit the job.

The Common Problems Today:

Messy RSVP Tracking: Names and emails scattered across spreadsheets, Google Forms, and inboxes. Things easily get lost or outdated.

Paper Sign-In Sheets: Slow, wasteful, and hard to read later. Someone always ends up typing everything into a computer afterward.

No Proof of Attendance: After the event, attendees get nothing meaningful beyond a generic thank-you email.

Disconnected Communities: Once the event ends, people disperse. There’s no simple way to keep them connected or reward loyal participants.

How EventProof Solves This:
EventProof brings everything into one simple platform that makes events easier to run, more engaging for attendees, and more rewarding for communities.

Streamlined Invites & Tracking: Upload a CSV file or share a registration link. All responses are automatically organized in one place.

Digital, Verifiable Attendance: Instead of paper sheets, attendees get a personalized digital badge. It’s a permanent and secure record of their participation that they can save, share, or even add to their professional profile.

Effortless Rewards: With one click, you can send unique badges to every attendee. What used to take hours now takes seconds.

Lasting Community Engagement: Badges can unlock perks like private groups, discounts, or exclusive content giving people a reason to stay connected long after the event ends.

In short: EventProof simplifies event management, eliminates wasteful manual work, and helps build stronger, lasting communities.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building EventProof as a solo full-stack project presented several significant technical hurdles that I had to overcome. The main challenge was designing an efficient and reliable system to handle the entire minting workflow from start to finish.

A major hurdle was managing the backend process after the user clicks the "Send Badges" button. The system needed to fetch the list of attendees, generate a unique personalized image for each one using the Python script, and then make a series of API calls to Verbwire to mint each NFT individually. Initially, this process would time out or fail if the list was too long, as the backend could not handle the large number of sequential operations.

I overcame this by completely restructuring the minting logic into an asynchronous and batched process. Instead of trying to do everything at once, I implemented a system where the backend creates a queue of minting jobs. It processes a small batch of attendees at a time, patiently generating images and calling the minting API for each batch. This prevents server timeouts and ensures that even if one mint fails, the entire process doesn't halt and can be retried. This solution required a deep dive into asynchronous programming and careful error handling to ensure reliability from the frontend user click all the way to the blockchain transaction.

**Verbwire API Challenge**

My project, EventProof, is a direct implementation of the Verbwire API Challenge. The entire core functionality of minting and airdropping NFTs is built exclusively using the Verbwire API.

Specifically, I leveraged the /nft/mint/mintFromMetadata endpoint to handle the individual minting of each personalized attendance badge as a unique NFT. For efficiency and scalability with larger events, the system is also designed to utilize the /nft/mint/batchMintFromMetadata endpoint, allowing for the seamless airdrop of multiple NFTs in a single, streamlined operation.

This use of the API is fundamental to the project. It abstracted away the immense complexity of blockchain development, allowing me to focus on creating a smooth user experience and solving the real-world problem of event management, rather than wrestling with smart contracts, gas fees, or wallet infrastructure. The Verbwire API provided the secure, reliable, and powerful blockchain backbone that makes the one-click "Send Badges" feature possible.

**The problem it solves**

The problem DeployLite – Agentic AI-Powered Deployements solves
Deploying applications today is often complicated and fragmented. Developers and small teams usually need to rely on multiple services to get a single product online hosting the frontend on one provider, the backend on another, and the database somewhere else. This fragmentation forces them to juggle credentials, configurations, and deployment pipelines, which can quickly become error-prone and time-consuming.

Another challenge is the DevOps overhead. Setting up CI/CD pipelines, managing containers, and configuring scaling rules typically requires significant infrastructure knowledge. Teams without dedicated DevOps engineers lose valuable time trying to solve deployment issues rather than focusing on building features.

Most existing platforms also create vendor lock-in, pushing developers into their own ecosystems and limiting flexibility. For indie developers, startups, and small businesses, this means higher long-term costs and less control. The complexity also discourages non-experts, who often find cloud deployments intimidating and inaccessible.

DeployLite addresses these problems by providing a single platform where web apps, databases, and even AI-powered chatbots can be deployed and managed seamlessly. It introduces AI-driven deployments, allowing developers to describe what they want in plain language instead of writing configuration files. The platform offers flexibility by supporting both managed infrastructure and direct deployment to services like AWS or Vultr, ensuring that teams retain control when needed. Every deployment comes with built-in CI/CD pipelines, reducing errors and saving engineering time, while the architecture is microservices-ready with isolated database instances for scalability and reliability.

In essence, DeployLite simplifies the deployment process, making it faster, safer, and more accessible without taking away the control and flexibility that modern teams need.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest hurdles we faced was with the Vultr API. Since our deployment system was repeatedly hitting the same endpoint from the same IP address, Vultr’s security systems flagged the activity and temporarily blocked access. This not only broke our deployment flow but also made debugging difficult because the API responses stopped coming through. On top of that, their firewall blocked common ports like 80 and 443, which created additional issues during configuration and testing.

Another challenge came from working with multiple MongoDB instances for our microservices. Ensuring proper connection pooling and avoiding bottlenecks required careful configuration. A small mistake in the URI setup or resource allocation could bring down an entire service.

We also ran into containerization issues. Some images worked perfectly on local Docker setups but failed during production deployment due to differences in environment variables and networking rules. Tracking down these inconsistencies took time and forced us to refine our CI/CD pipeline with stricter validation checks before pushing anything live.

To overcome these challenges, we implemented rate-limiting and backoff strategies for API calls, carefully configured firewall rules, and added retry logic to handle transient network failures. For the database and container issues, we introduced stricter environment parity between local and production setups, along with automated health checks to catch failures early. These fixes not only solved the immediate problems but also made our platform more resilient for the long run.

> Deploy. Debug. Deliver - Server powered by Agent.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket Programming](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket%20Programming-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ZeroShell transforms server management from a complex, command-line-driven chore into a simple, intuitive conversation. It acts as an intelligent AI agent for your server, making complex DevOps tasks accessible, faster, and safer for everyone from solo developers to large teams.

## The Problem ZeroShell Solves

In today's development world, managing a server is a significant bottleneck. Developers, who should be focused on creating innovative solutions, are often forced to switch contexts and spend countless hours on tedious, error-prone server administration. The command line is an intimidating barrier for many, and a single typo can lead to hours of painful debugging. DevOps, in its current state, is a landscape of friction.

ZeroShell eliminates this friction.

## How ZeroShell Makes Server Management Easier and Safer

People can use ZeroShell to manage the entire lifecycle of their applications simply by talking to it. It makes existing tasks easier and safer in several key ways:

* ### One-Command Deployments
    Instead of manually cloning a repository, installing dependencies, configuring environment variables, setting up a process manager, and editing Nginx files, a user can simply say: **"Deploy my project from this GitHub link on port 3005."** ZeroShell understands the intent, analyzes the code, and handles the entire deployment pipeline automatically, turning a 30-minute, multi-step process into a single command.

* ### AI-Powered Debugging and Self-Correction
    When a deployment fails, the traditional debugging process is a painful loop of sifting through logs and searching for cryptic error messages. With ZeroShell, if a command fails, the agent automatically analyzes the error, generates a fix, and retries the command on its own. It can solve common issues like missing dependencies, incorrect start commands, or permission errors without any human intervention, dramatically reducing downtime and developer frustration.

* ### Natural Language Server Administration
    Routine but essential tasks are simplified from complex commands into simple requests.
    * **Instead of:** `crontab -l | grep -v 'my-app' | crontab -`
    * **A user can say:** **"Remove the cron job for my-app."**
    * **Instead of:** `sudo sed -i '/location \/my-app\//,/^ }/d' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default`
    * **A user can say:** **"Delete the Nginx proxy for my-app."**

* ### Real-Time Monitoring and Insights
    ZeroShell provides a simple way to understand server health without needing to remember a dozen different commands. A user can ask, **"How is the server doing?"** and receive a clean, structured summary of CPU load, memory usage, disk space, and top running processes, making server monitoring accessible to everyone, not just specialists.

By translating human intent into precise server actions, **ZeroShell makes DevOps safer by minimizing the risk of human error, faster by automating entire workflows, and easier by breaking down the command-line barrier for good.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## The Challenge: The Deceptive Simplicity of a Remote Shell

The single greatest hurdle we faced while building ZeroShell was the surprising fragility of executing complex commands on a remote server. What seems simple when typed manually into a terminal becomes a minefield of hidden issues when automated through a script. This problem manifested most severely when trying to programmatically edit the Nginx configuration file.

The goal was simple: **insert a new multi-line `location` block just before the final closing brace `}` of the main `server` block.**

-----

### The Initial Attempts and Failures

1.  **Attempt \#1: The Simple Append**
    Our first approach was to use a basic `echo` command combined with `tee -a` to append the new block to the configuration file.

    ```bash
    echo '{nginx_block}' | sudo tee -a /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/auto-server
    ```

    This failed immediately. It appended the block to the *end of the file*, outside the `server {}` scope, resulting in a syntactically invalid Nginx configuration that would not reload.

2.  **Attempt \#2: The File Rebuild**
    Our next idea was to rebuild the file logically. The script would use `head -n -1` to copy the file *without* its last line (`}`), then append the new `location` block, and finally append the closing brace back.

    ```bash
    # 1. Copy top part
    sudo head -n -1 {config_path} > {temp_path}
    # 2. Add new part
    printf '%s\\n' '{nginx_block}' | sudo tee -a {temp_path}
    # 3. Add last line back and replace
    echo '}' | sudo tee -a {temp_path} && sudo mv {temp_path} {config_path}
    ```

    This also failed, but in a much more confusing way. The commands would appear to run, but the file would end up truncated or unchanged. We discovered that the combination of multi-line strings, special shell characters (`>`, `|`, `}`), and the way our Python script was sending these commands was causing the remote shell to misinterpret or break them apart. The commands were failing silently.

-----

## The Solution: Bypassing the Shell's Ambiguity

We realized the core problem wasn't our logic, but that we were trusting the remote shell to correctly interpret our increasingly complex command strings. The solution was to stop fighting the shell and instead use methods that were immune to its interpretation rules.

1.  **For Nginx: Direct, In-Place Editing with `sed`**
    We switched to using `sed`, the standard Linux tool for in-place stream editing. Instead of rebuilding the file, we crafted a single, precise command to find the exact line to edit and insert our new block.

    ```python
    # Prepare the block to be safe for sed
    sed_safe_block = nginx_block.replace('\\', '\\\\')... 
    # The command finds the last '}' and inserts our block before it
    edit_command = f"sudo sed -i '/^\\s*}}\\s*$/i{sed_safe_block}' {nginx_config_path}"
    run_command(edit_command)
    ```

    This was far more direct and reliable. It treated the file as a stream and performed a single, atomic edit.

2.  **For Cron/Screen Commands: The "Sealed Envelope" Method (`base64`)**
    For other complex commands (like the full start command containing `&&` and environment variables), we used an even more robust method. We essentially put our command in a "sealed envelope" by **Base64 encoding** it.

      * **In Python:** The command `cd ~/my-app && npm start` was encoded into a simple, safe string like `Y2Qgf...`.
      * **On the Server:** We sent this safe string and had the server decode it and execute it.

    <!-- end list -->

    ```bash
    # The command sent to the server looks like this
    bash -c 'eval "$(echo 'Y2Qgf...' | base64 --decode)"'
    ```

    This completely eliminated any chance of the shell misinterpreting the command's content, as the special characters were safely hidden inside the encoded string.

Overcoming this hurdle was a crucial lesson: **when automating a remote shell, never trust it with complex strings.** Instead, use tools and techniques (`sed`, encoding) that bypass its interpretation quirks to ensure commands are executed exactly as intended.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

ZeroShell is fundamentally a project built on the capabilities of a Large Language Model, making it a perfect fit for the **Gemini track**. It moves beyond simple text generation and uses Gemini as the central "brain" for a sophisticated, autonomous agent that interacts with a complex, real-world environment—the server command line.

***
## Core Reliance on Gemini for Intelligent Automation

At its heart, ZeroShell is a natural language interface for DevOps. Every core feature relies on Gemini's advanced reasoning and code intelligence to function.

* **Translating Human Intent to Machine Code:** The primary task of the agent is to take a high-level human request like, *"Deploy my new e-commerce backend and set it up for production,"* and translate it into a precise sequence of Linux commands. This requires Gemini to understand the user's intent, analyze provided context (like a `package.json` file), and generate syntactically correct, logical commands.
* **Code Analysis and Generation:** ZeroShell doesn't just run commands; it understands code. It uses Gemini to analyze a project's file structure to determine the tech stack, find the entry point file, and construct the correct installation and start commands. When asked to make a project "production-ready," it again uses Gemini to generate new commands that incorporate process managers like `pm2`.

***
## Sophisticated Agentic Workflow

This project is a prime example of an **agentic AI**, a key theme of the Gemini track. ZeroShell operates as an autonomous agent that can perceive its environment, make decisions, and take actions.

* **Multi-Turn Reasoning and Self-Correction:** The agent doesn't just execute a command and stop. Its "self-correction" loop is a sophisticated, multi-turn process. When a command fails, the agent **perceives** the error message from the server, **reasons** about the cause by feeding the error back to Gemini, and **acts** by executing the newly generated, corrected command. This demonstrates an autonomous problem-solving capability.
* **Tool Use:** The agent uses the entire Linux command line as its toolkit. Gemini's role is to decide which tool to use (`git`, `sed`, `crontab`, `screen`, `npm`) and with what parameters, based on the user's high-level goal.

***
## Potential for Multimodal and Advanced Capabilities

The Gemini track emphasizes the future of AI, including multimodal interactions. The ZeroShell architecture is perfectly positioned for such extensions.

* **Voice Prompting:** The project's initial proposal included voice commands. This would directly leverage multimodal capabilities, where Gemini would process spoken language to trigger complex deployment workflows.
* **Visual Analysis:** A future version could allow a user to upload a screenshot of a terminal error. Gemini's multimodal vision capabilities could be used to analyze the image, extract the error text, and generate a fix, further simplifying the debugging process.

In summary, **ZeroShell is not just a project that *uses* an LLM; it's a project that embodies the core principles of the Gemini track: building intelligent, autonomous agents that solve complex, real-world problems through advanced reasoning and interaction.**

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

## Seamless Integration with a Serverless Data Backend

ZeroShell is a stateless AI agent that requires a persistent, scalable, and flexible database to manage its users, servers, and configurations. **MongoDB Atlas** serves as the ideal serverless data layer for this project, allowing the agent to focus on its core DevOps tasks without worrying about database administration.

* ### **Flexible Document Model for DevOps Data**
    The project's data is varied and semi-structured, which is a perfect use case for MongoDB's flexible document model.
    * The `users` collection stores user credentials.
    * The `servers` collection stores a list of servers associated with a user, each with its own unique credentials (`ssh_host`, `ssh_ip`, `ssh_password`).
    This structure can easily be expanded in the future to store deployment logs, project configurations, or even user preferences without requiring schema migrations, showcasing the agility of the document model. 

* ### **Leveraging the Atlas Developer Data Platform**
    The project directly utilizes the core features of the Atlas platform. The `db_data_push.js` script demonstrates how easily a Node.js application can connect to an Atlas cluster using the official MongoDB driver. The script performs atomic `updateOne` operations with `upsert:true`, which is an idempotent and robust way to populate and maintain data, preventing duplicates and ensuring data integrity. This highlights the developer-friendly nature of the Atlas ecosystem.

***
## A Foundation for Advanced, Data-Driven Features

While the current implementation uses Atlas for core data storage, the architecture is designed to grow by leveraging more advanced Atlas features, turning the simple database into an intelligent data platform.

* ### **Potential for Atlas Search**
    As the number of managed servers and deployment logs grows, **Atlas Search** could be integrated to provide powerful, full-text search capabilities. A user could ask the agent, *"Find all deployments that failed in the last week with a 'permission denied' error,"* and Atlas Search would instantly query and return the relevant logs stored in the database.

* ### **Future Integration with Atlas Vector Search**
    To make the AI agent even smarter, **Atlas Vector Search** could be used to implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). We could store documentation, best practices, and past deployment error resolutions as vector embeddings in Atlas. When the agent encounters a new, complex error, it could perform a vector search to find the most relevant historical solutions, providing Gemini with richer context to generate a more accurate fix.

In essence, ZeroShell uses MongoDB Atlas not just as a simple database, but as a strategic component of its intelligent, data-driven architecture, with a clear roadmap for leveraging its more advanced features to create an even more powerful AI agent.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Hackathon Challenge Log: AI Admissions Co-pilot

This document outlines the key challenges we faced and the pragmatic strategies we adopted to build our AI platform within the tight constraints of a hackathon.

---

## ## Challenge 1: Collecting University Data

The data on university admissions is scattered and inconsistent across thousands of websites, making live collection impossible during a hackathon.

**Hackathon Strategy:**
Instead of building a complex web scraper, we created a **static JSON file or CSV** to act as our database. We manually collected data for about 10-15 well-known universities. This allowed us to build and test our recommendation logic with clean, predictable data without wasting precious hours on scraping.

---

## ## Challenge 2: Designing the Recommendation Logic

Building a machine learning model that is both accurate and personalized requires significant time for training and tuning, which we didn't have.

**Hackathon Strategy:**
We implemented a simple but effective **rule-based recommendation engine**. Our logic uses basic filters (e.g., `if user_gpa >= 3.5 and user_interest == 'Computer Science'`) to categorize our static list of schools into "Ambitious," "Target," and "Safe." This approach is transparent, easy to implement in a few hours, and perfect for a proof-of-concept demo.

---

## ## Challenge 3: Making SOP & Resume Optimization Adaptable

Fine-tuning an AI model to handle diverse student backgrounds and maintain an authentic voice is a long-term research project.

**Hackathon Strategy:**
We leveraged a powerful, pre-trained Large Language Model (LLM) via an API (like Google's Gemini). Our innovation was focused on **prompt engineering**. We designed a single, sophisticated prompt that includes context about the user's background and the target university, instructing the AI to act as a "creative assistant" rather than a writer. This delivers impressive results instantly.

---

## ## Challenge 4: Building Trust in the AI

We couldn't rely on long-term trust-building methods like user testimonials or case studies. We had to earn the judges' trust in under 3 minutes.

**Hackathon Strategy:**
Our focus shifted to **UI transparency and a compelling demo script**. In our UI, we explicitly state *why* a school was recommended (e.g., "Recommended because your GPA is a good match for their average"). Our demo script clearly explains the logic, showing that the AI is a well-designed tool, not an uncontrollable "black box."

---

## ## Challenge 5: Affordability and Cost Management

While production costs are a major concern for a real SaaS product, the challenge in a hackathon is simply getting access to powerful tools quickly and for free.

**Hackathon Strategy:**
We relied exclusively on the **generous free tiers** offered by cloud and AI providers. We obtained a free-tier API key for Google Gemini, which was more than enough for our development and demo needs. This allowed us to use state-of-the-art AI without any financial cost.

---

## ## Challenge 6: Deploying the Backend on Vultr

Deploying a multi-agent microservice architecture with heavy AI models on an IaaS platform like Vultr is extremely complex and time-consuming. Attempting a full Kubernetes setup in a hackathon would have been a critical mistake.

**Hackathon Strategy:**
We drastically simplified our deployment to focus on functionality.

* **Single Instance, Simplified Orchestration:** We provisioned a **single, powerful Vultr instance**. Instead of Kubernetes, we used **`docker-compose`**. This allowed us to define all our containerized agents (`ResumeAgent`, `GitHubAgent`, etc.) in one simple `YAML` file and launch them with a single command (`docker-compose up`). This gave us the microservice feel without the DevOps nightmare.

* **No Self-Hosting for LLMs:** Self-hosting a heavy LLM is not feasible. Our "deployment" of the LLM was simply making an **API call** to the external Gemini service. This offloaded all the complexity of GPU management and model inference.

* **Local Development as a Fallback:** Our primary plan was to run the `docker-compose` setup on the Vultr instance. Our backup plan was to run the exact same `docker-compose` setup on a local machine and use a tool like **`ngrok`** to expose our local server to the internet for the final demo. This provided a crucial safety net.

**Vultr Cloud Deployment Track**

Scalable AI Workloads: Our platform runs ML models for resume parsing, profile evaluation, and global university matching. Vultr’s compute instances let us deploy and scale these services seamlessly.

Always Accessible: Students across India and beyond can access AcademiaAI without hardware constraints since everything runs on the cloud.

Rapid Deployment: Vultr enables us to quickly deploy APIs and backend systems powering SOP optimisation, recommendation engines, and application tracking.

Handles Growth: As more students join, Vultr’s infrastructure scales smoothly to meet increasing demand.

Secure & Reliable: Sensitive student data like grades, test scores, and personal details stay protected on Vultr’s secure cloud.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Smart SOP & Resume Drafting: Leveraging Gemini’s advanced LLM capabilities to generate well-structured, personalised SOPs, essays, and resumes tailored to specific universities.

Context-Aware Guidance: Gemini processes diverse inputs like academic scores, extracurriculars, and career goals to provide contextually relevant suggestions instead of generic outputs.

Interactive Career Counselling: Students can chat with an AI mentor powered by Gemini to clarify doubts about applications, scholarships, or global opportunities.

Profile Gap Analysis: Gemini identifies weak areas in a student’s profile and recommends actionable improvements to increase admission chances.

Natural Multilingual Support: With Gemini’s multilingual understanding, we can guide students in English, Hindi, and other Indian languages, making the platform inclusive.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Database-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Accessing local clinics for urgent or routine care is often stressful due to unclear wait times, inconsistent information, and a lack of trusted, real-time updates. Patients waste time traveling to overcrowded clinics or making multiple unanswered calls, while smaller clinics struggle with manual queue management, peak-time congestion, and underutilization during off-peak hours.

CareBuddy solves this by providing a map-first, real-time platform where patients can instantly see nearby clinics, live wait times, service availability, and triage categories. It includes in-app chat for direct communication, AI-based wait-time predictions, and community-verified check-ins to keep data accurate. Clinics benefit from efficient queue management, reduced repetitive calls, and better patient flow. The result is a connected, transparent healthcare network that saves time, reduces stress, and improves the quality of local healthcare for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was maintaining accurate real-time queue data for all clinics. Smaller clinics often lacked the staff or infrastructure to manually update wait times consistently, which risked outdated or misleading information.
To solve this, we implemented a multi-source data update system:
1. Clinic Staff Updates via the admin panel.
2. Community Check-Ins from patients already at the clinic to verify or refresh data.
3. AI Wait-Time Predictions using historical trends and current booking load to fill in      gaps.

## **CareQueue: Smarter Access to Local Clinics**

**Overview**  
CareQueue improves the frustrating and inefficient experience of visiting local clinics—for both **patients** and **clinic staff**.  

---

## **What CareQueue Offers**

### **For Patients**  
- Instantly view **all nearby clinics** on a single **map interface**  
- See **real-time wait times, triage categories, and availability** before leaving home  
- **Request a slot** in the virtual queue and receive confirmation  
- **Track your status** and get notified when it’s your turn  
- Get **walking or driving directions** to the clinic through the app  

### **For Clinics**  
- Provide **live queue updates** and **real-time availability**  
- Reduce **overcrowding** at peak hours and underuse at others  
- Streamline **patient flow** with transparent digital management  

### **Communication Made Easy**  
- Use **integrated chat** to connect patients and clinic staff instantly  
- Ask quick questions (e.g., confirm services, update arrival time)  
- Reduce unnecessary **phone calls and visits**

**Challenges we ran into**

## **Challenges We Ran Into (As a Team)**

- **Coordinating MERN + Flutter**  
  Backend (MERN) and frontend (Flutter) teams had trouble syncing data.  
  We fixed this by creating a **clear API contract** and sticking to it.  

- **Real-Time Queue Updates**  
  At first, REST polling caused delays in showing live clinic queues.  
  We switched to **Socket.IO** for smooth real-time updates.  

- **Map & API Integration**  
  Integrating Google Maps across iOS/Android broke a few times.  
  Standardizing on the **Google Maps Flutter plugin** solved it.  

- **Deployment Hiccups**  
  Render (backend) + Vercel (frontend) sometimes had **CORS and env issues**.  
  We resolved this by **configuring CORS properly** and using **shared env vars**.

> Empowering Rural Art with One Click and One Voice

![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![fast.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/fast.ai-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🛠️ The Problem

India—especially Bengal—is a land of artists
Today’s generation—people like us—have access to social media. We click, we post, we go viral. We get likes, we get recognition.

But what about the countless rural artisans of Bengal?
What about the housewives who create magic with clay, or the grandfather carving wood dolls in silence?

- ❌ They are incredibly talented, yet invisible. 
- ❌ They don’t know how to post. They can’t write captions.
- ❌ They don’t know hashtags. Most don’t even know how to type
- ❌ Their art often goes unseen and uncredited  

---

## ✅ What *ShilpoSphere* Does

🎨 **ShilpoSphere** helps rural artists:

-  Speak product details in Bengali  
- Snap a photo of their handmade art  
- Auto-generate captions + hashtags  
- Post on Facebook in **one tap**

---

## 🚀 Why It’s Powerful

- No typing needed — just voice  
- Empower rural women & homemakers  
- Reach more people, earn more  
-  Preserve local art, proudly shared

---

**From local to Global**

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🐞 Challenges We Ran Into

### 🔐 1. Facebook Page Integration
We faced issues with **Facebook Graph API authentication**, especially while posting on behalf of users.  
**Fix:** We resolved this by setting up proper developer roles, switching to Facebook test users, and ensuring the Instagram/Facebook pages were linked to Business accounts.

---

### 🗣️ 2. Bengali Voice Input Accuracy
Translating **spoken Bengali into clean text** was tricky — regional dialects and accents caused misinterpretations.  
**Fix:** We fine-tuned the voice recognition using **Whisper API** and filtered common Bengali phrases with custom post-processing.

---

### 📱 3. Simplifying the UI for Non-Tech Users
Our target users are often **first-time smartphone users**. Too many steps or buttons caused confusion.  
**Fix:** We designed a **minimal one-screen flow** with voice-only input, preview, and post — all in **Bengali language** with large icons.

---

> On-Demand Local Services Platform

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Leaflet](https://img.shields.io/badge/Leaflet-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Imagine being stranded on a highway with a dead car, facing a flooded kitchen from a burst pipe, or needing an immediate fix for a critical home appliance. In these moments, the universal need is for a fast, reliable solution. However, the current service landscape is ill-equipped to handle such on-demand emergencies.

Core Problem:
Access to immediate, reliable professional services—spanning automotive, plumbing, electrical, home maintenance, and even personal grooming—is critically flawed. Consumers consistently encounter a frustrating set of obstacles during urgent situations.

Key Pain Points:

Service Scarcity: The vast majority of skilled professionals are not available for immediate dispatch, especially outside of standard business hours.
Protracted Delays: The industry standard involves wait times of two hours or more, which is untenable in an emergency.
Lack of Reliability and Transparency: Finding a trustworthy technician is a significant challenge. Users struggle with a lack of real-time tracking, opaque pricing structures, and inconsistent service quality.
The "Emergency" Premium: When immediate service is available, it often comes at an exorbitant cost, penalizing consumers for their urgent needs.

Our solution is engineered to eliminate these inefficiencies. By creating a dependable, on-demand network of vetted professionals, we provide a seamless and immediate response to life's unexpected challenges, transforming moments of crisis into opportunities for swift, effective resolution.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a platform this ambitious in such a short time meant we had to tackle some serious challenges head-on. Here are a few of the biggest hurdles we faced and how we solved them:

1. The Real-Time Matching Conundrum

The Challenge: The core of our app is speed. But connecting the right available professional to a user's exact location in real-time is incredibly complex. We were dealing with constantly moving parts, and any lag would defeat our entire purpose.

How We Tackled It: We couldn't just poll for locations every few seconds; it had to be instant. We engineered a solution using WebSocket connections, which keep a live, open channel for data. This allowed us to get a constant stream of location updates, which we managed with a high-speed Redis system to instantly match the closest, most qualified worker using PostGIS spatial queries.

Translating "Panic" into Actionable Data
The Challenge: When your basement is flooding or your car is smoking, you're not thinking like an engineer. A user in a panic won't use perfect keywords. We needed a way to understand their problem from fragmented, emotional descriptions and even a blurry photo.

How We Tackled It: We integrated the Google Gemini API to act as our "AI diagnostician." We trained it with specific prompts to analyze user input—whether it's text or an image—and intelligently categorize the emergency, identify the required skills, and even suggest potential parts needed. This turns a frantic message into a structured job for our professionals.

3. Building a Foundation of Trust in a Weekend

The Challenge: Our platform is based on trust. You're letting a stranger into your home or trusting them with your vehicle. How do you build that confidence? We knew we had to address payment security and worker reliability from the very beginning.

How We Tackled It: While a full implementation takes time, we laid the groundwork for trust. For our proof-of-concept, we architected a system using smart contracts on the Aptos blockchain. This creates an immutable, tamper-proof record of agreements and payments, ensuring that transactions are secure and transparent for both the user and the service provider.

4. Balancing Our Grand Vision with a Hackathon Reality

The Challenge: We had a massive vision—disrupting a $400 billion industry. But in a hackathon, you have to be realistic. Our biggest strategic challenge was deciding what to build now to prove our concept, versus what to plan for the future.

How We Tackled It: We focused relentlessly on the core user journey: The Emergency. We prioritized the real-time matching and AI diagnosis because they solve the user's most immediate pain point. We then mapped out the other critical features—like the franchise model for expansion and advanced worker incentives—as a clear and viable roadmap for scaling post-hackathon. This showed we could not only build a product but also think like a business.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
Mobile app testing is slow, brittle, and requires constant maintenance. Scripted automation breaks with every UI change, and manual QA doesn't scale. Existing tools are complex, fragmented, and not built for how modern teams work.

What Can You Use Orbis For

- Automate iOS app testing without writing a single line of code
- Run tests on real and virtual devices simultaneously
- Generate synchronized video logs for every test session
- Use agents that understand UI context and adapt to changes
- Replace fragile test scripts with resilient, AI-driven workflows

Orbis simplifies testing, speeds up releases, and removes the need for traditional QA overhead.

**Challenges we ran into**

Getting WebSockets to behave was a mess at first. I needed real-time log streaming from the backend to the frontend for agent logs, but juggling async FastAPI with persistent socket connections wasn’t as clean as I expected.

Setting up the agentic framework using Facebook's idb was probably the trickiest. The iOS simulator isn’t exactly cooperative, and chaining commands while keeping state consistent across test steps needed a custom wrapper around idb.

**Progress made before hackathon**

Research on what idb is and researched best tools to use for building agents.

**Sarvam AI Track**

India’s mobile app ecosystem is massive. With apps in dozens of languages and used by millions. But testing is still either manual, expensive, or just skipped because existing tools aren’t built for this scale or diversity.

This project flips that. You just say what to test, and it does it across real simulators, no scripts, no setup. What makes it a perfect fit for Sarvam is that it’s language-agnostic. Most models fail outside English, but with Sarvam, this system can understand Indian languages. Whatever the app speaks, the agent speaks too.

It’s fast, affordable, and built to serve developers in India without compromising on depth or reliability.

> "Empowering Safe Commutes, One Student at a Time."

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embedded C](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embedded%20C-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP-32 WiFi Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP--32%20WiFi%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Location services](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Location%20services-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In many rural and tribal regions, school buses lack a real-time student monitoring system. Parents and school authorities often have no visibility into student attendance, location, or safety during transit. Traditional systems are either too expensive, unavailable in government fleets, or dependent on unreliable manual logs.

**✅ What People Can Use It For
📍 Live Bus Tracking**
Track the real-time GPS location of school buses from a mobile or web dashboard.

**Student Attendance Logging**
Automatically record each student’s presence using RFID tags — no manual roll call needed.

**📊 Centralized Data in Google Sheets**
All attendance and location data is instantly logged and stored in Google Sheets, making it accessible for parents, teachers, and administrators.

**📱 SMS Alerts to Parents**
Parents receive instant SMS notifications when their child boards or exits the bus.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into**
**1. Secure Communication with Google Sheets**
Initially, I struggled with getting the ESP8266 to send attendance data to Google Sheets via a secure HTTPS connection. The SSL certificate validation was failing, and I wasn't receiving any response.

**Solution:**
I resolved this by using client->setInsecure() in the Arduino code to bypass SSL certificate checks, which allowed smooth communication with the Google Apps Script Web App.

**2. Real-Time GPS Data Integration**
Streaming live GPS coordinates from the ESP32 to Firebase and displaying them on a web dashboard using Leaflet.js was a new challenge.

**Solution:**
I explored Firebase Realtime Database structure and learned how to push and pull live data. I used JavaScript + Leaflet.js for front-end map rendering and tested Firebase integration thoroughly.

**3. RFID Tag Reading Consistency**
The MFRC522 RFID module sometimes failed to detect tags reliably during initial testing, causing missed attendance logs.

**Solution:**
I refined my code to improve read stability and added feedback in the Serial Monitor to debug detection issues.

**4. SMS Notifications**
Integrating Twilio for SMS alerts was tricky due to authentication and webhook setup.

**Solution:**
I connected Google Sheets to Twilio using Pabbly Connect, which allowed me to trigger SMS alerts without complex back-end setups.

**IoT and Embedded System**

My project, Smart School Bus Monitoring System, is a perfect example of a real-world IoT + Embedded Systems solution.

**📶 IoT Integration:**
The system uses ESP8266 and ESP32 microcontrollers to connect hardware devices (RFID reader and GPS module) to the internet.

Attendance data is captured using RFID and pushed to Google Sheets via Wi-Fi, making it instantly accessible to schools and parents.

GPS data from ESP32 is streamed in real-time to a Firebase Realtime Database, which is then visualized on a web dashboard using Leaflet.js.

Twilio and Pabbly Connect are used to send SMS alerts to parents when a student boards or exits the bus.

**⚙️ Embedded Systems:**
The core hardware logic is programmed using Arduino C++, making full use of the ESP microcontroller’s capabilities.

Real-time RFID data reading and GPS coordinate logging are handled at the firmware level.

All components (GPS, RFID, Wi-Fi) are tightly integrated into a low-power, embedded system that runs independently on a moving bus.

> An AI-Powered Learning Platform

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bootstrap](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bootstrap-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Pymongo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pymongo-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Education is undergoing a massive transformation with the rise of digital learning platforms like YouTube, Coursera, and Udemy. While students now have access to endless learning resources, career guidance and skill development systems have not kept pace. Many students struggle to find personalized learning paths that align with their strengths and aspirations. They are often unsure which skills are actually relevant to the careers they want to pursue, and lack structured mentorship or systems to track their progress. Even after years of education, a large number of graduates end up without any industry-relevant experience. Traditional guidance methods such as counseling sessions and career fairs adopt a one-size-fits-all approach, which fails to serve the individual needs of students. This happens primarily because one mentor is often responsible for hundreds of students, making it difficult to provide customized support. Additionally, university curricula remain rigid and slow to evolve, making them disconnected from current industry needs. Meanwhile, self-learning via online platforms lacks real-time feedback, structured progress tracking, and mentorship—leaving students overwhelmed, directionless, and underprepared.

**Challenges we ran into**

PBSC-Ignite is designed to solve these challenges by introducing an AI-powered, personalized career readiness platform that guides students through every stage of their learning journey. The platform uses a Multi-Agent AI system that adapts to each student's learning speed, interests, and career goals. It builds a personalized roadmap, provides interactive daily mentoring through AI chat sessions, and aligns learning paths with real-time industry trends. PBSC-Ignite also tracks student progress across learning platforms, analyzes profiles like GitHub and LinkedIn, and recommends relevant internships and opportunities. By doing so, it ensures that every student—regardless of their college tier or location—receives quality guidance and practical direction. The platform contributes directly to the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education for All) by making personalized learning and career development accessible to all.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Handling ZIP File Cleanup in Synapse

One of the trickiest issues we faced while building Synapse was **cleaning up temporary ZIP files** generated by the DevBot after they were downloaded by users.

## The Challenge

Initially, we tried to delete the ZIP file right after triggering `FileResponse` in our FastAPI endpoint. But due to FastAPI’s asynchronous nature and how file streaming works, this led to several problems:

- **Race Conditions**: The file could get deleted *before* the download finished, leading to broken or incomplete downloads.
- **Permission Errors**: Sometimes the OS still had the file in use, so trying to delete it caused a `PermissionError`.
- **Silent Failures**: If anything went wrong while sending the file, the cleanup step might be skipped—leaving orphaned files behind and wasting disk space.

## The Solution

We solved this by using FastAPI’s `background` task mechanism, which runs cleanup logic *after* the response is fully sent to the client.

Here’s how we implemented it:

```python
# In app.py

# A safe file cleanup function with error handling
def cleanup_zip_file(zip_path: str):
    try:
        if os.path.exists(zip_path):
            os.remove(zip_path)
            print(f"Successfully cleaned up: {zip_path}")
    except OSError as e:
        print(f"Error cleaning up {zip_path}: {e}")

# Create the response and attach the cleanup as a background task
response = FileResponse(path=zip_path, media_type='application/zip', filename=fn)
response.background = lambda: cleanup_zip_file(zip_path)  # or use functools.partial

**The problem it solves**

Traditional interviews and evaluations rely heavily on subjective human judgment, making the process prone to bias, inconsistency, and inefficiency. Recruiters often struggle to objectively interpret non-verbal cues such as stress, engagement, or confidence, especially in virtual interviews where many human subtleties are lost. This creates gaps in decision-making and can lead to poor hiring choices.InsightHire AI offers an intelligent solution by automatically analyzing behavioral cues from video interviews. It scores candidates based on real-time facial expressions, eye contact, posture stability, speech pitch variation, and anxiety indicators such as blinking or face-touching. These metrics are visualized and quantified, giving recruiters a clear understanding of how a candidate performs emotionally and non-verbally.It enables data-driven shortlisting and flags signs of nervousness or disinterest and highlights soft skills like confidence or professionalism. The platform improves transparency, reduces bias and helps identify high-potential candidates who may not excel in conventional verbal responses.InsightHire bridges the trust and insight gap by offering consistent, unbiased behavioral analytics.It can also be used for:
Measuring stress levels,can be used by therapists to
analyze their patients in online
mode only.
Can be used in online classes by teachers to check the
focus level and attention span
of students.
Can also be used in medical field for detecting signs of
stress,depression or other
diseases.
Can also be used for lie detector tests.

**Challenges we ran into**

Environment Discrepancies Between Google Colab and VS Code: Initially, we developed and tested our code in Google Colab because many libraries and dependencies were preconfigured. However, when we migrated the project to a local development environment using VS Code, we encountered differences in command behaviors and module availability. These discrepancies led to intermittent errors and unexpected behaviors.We created a dedicated virtual environment and mirrored the Colab setup using a well-maintained requirements.txt file and a Pipfile.
Several libraries used in the project such as OpenCV, MediaPipe, and Librosa imposed conflicting version requirements. Some libraries required a version greater than a specific threshold, while others needed a version lower than a particular release to function as expected.We systematically reviewed the release notes and compatibility documentation for each library.We incrementally integrated each library into our local setup, using unit tests to ensure that each piece functioned correctly before moving on to the next.
Combining several libraries each with its own API quirks into one cohesive system presented integration challenges. For example, certain MediaPipe functions had some differences in behavior depending on the version used and integrating these functions with OpenCV sometimes required additional modifications.This was resolved by seeking help from opensource communities and youtube videos.

**The problem it solves**

### 🧠 Problem It Solves

The **AI-Powered API Monitoring and Anomaly Detection System** tackles performance issues in large-scale, distributed API platforms spread across on-prem, cloud, and multi-cloud environments.

---

### 🚀 Key Features & Benefits

#### 🤖 AI Phone Alert & Automation System  
Sends **automated phone alerts** triggered by logs, metrics, and traces. It can **automate recovery tasks** and deliver **Root Cause Analysis (RCA)** reports to engineers.

#### 🔍 Root Cause Analysis Engine  
Correlates logs, metrics, and traces to **identify the root cause** of issues — including predicted anomalies — enabling faster fixes.

#### ✅ Real-time Monitoring  
Monitors **response times**, **error rates**, and **uptime** across environments in one unified system.

#### 🔥 Anomaly Detection  
Detects **latency spikes** and **error anomalies** in real-time with **environment-aware alerts**.

#### 🧭 End-to-End API Tracking  
Tracks complete **API request journeys**, even when spanning multiple environments.

#### 📉 Predictive Analytics  
Forecasts potential failures using historical trends in logs and metrics.

#### 📊 Centralized Visualization  
Dashboards (**Grafana**) provide a single view of platform health.

---

### 💡 Value

- Reduces **MTTD** and **MTTR** with AI alerts and RCA.  
- Improves **system reliability** through proactive insights.  
- Simplifies debugging with **cross-environment correlation**.  
- Minimizes disruptions by **predicting and resolving issues early**.

> Acts as the intelligent core of your distributed API system — alerting, analyzing, and automating for a seamless experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

###  Challenges I Ran Into

One major challenge was **generating meaningful datasets**. The initial Python script produced poor-quality log data, which led to **undertrained ML models** and unreliable anomaly detection.

To overcome this, I explored better data generation strategies and came across **Locust**, a traffic simulation tool. It allowed me to generate realistic API traffic across services. I then introduced **`sleep()` functions and randomized timeouts** in certain services to create **variable response patterns** and simulate real-world latency and error behavior.

This approach helped generate a **diverse and representative dataset**, which significantly improved the performance and accuracy of the ML models.
