![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Managing hackathons and competitions using forms, spreadsheets, and manual evaluation is time-consuming, error-prone, and lacks transparency. This platform provides a centralized system where competitions can be created, projects can be submitted, judges can evaluate digitally, and leaderboards are generated automatically. It simplifies management, ensures fair judging, reduces manual effort, and makes the entire competition process faster, safer, and more transparent.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was designing the database relationships between students, projects, judges, and scores. Initially, incorrect foreign key mappings caused issues like duplicate submissions and scores not appearing correctly in the leaderboard.

Another hurdle was automatically generating the leaderboard in real time. Calculating scores manually worked, but updating rankings dynamically required careful query optimization and validation.

How I Overcame Them

Re-structured the database schema with proper relationships and constraints

Added validation checks to prevent duplicate entries

Implemented backend logic to recalculate scores and update the leaderboard automatically after each evaluation

These fixes improved data accuracy, system reliability, and overall performance.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

While Duality AI focuses on advanced AI model development, our platform serves as the competition and evaluation framework where such AI projects can be submitted, reviewed, scored, and ranked. It supports hosting AI challenges, managing submissions, and generating leaderboards for models like semantic scene segmentation systems.

### WallGodds-Web
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/wallgoddsweb-6219) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vivekyadav-3/WallGodds-Web) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> WallGodds-Web is a high-performance wallpaper disc

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem: Code Duplication & Maintenance Nightmares
The current WallGodds codebase has three separate components for the exact same image card (`ImgCardMobile`, `ImgCardTablet`, `ImgCardDesktop`). This "Copy-Paste Architecture" means:
1. **Triple the Bugs:** Every feature (like downloading images) has to be fixed in 3 different places.
2. **Bloated Bundle:** The code size is 30% larger than necessary, slowing down load times.
3. **Fragile Code:** Without TypeScript, simple type errors can crash the app in production.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9d1c73f9534243dfb60dc6de87295b32/4efb45a9-6e77-49fb-93c7-62a8da0409f6.jpeg) Solution: Component Unification & TypeScript Migration
My proposal solves this by:
1. **Refactoring Architecture:** Creating a single, responsive [ImageCard](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/KIIT/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/WallGodds-Web/Frontend/src/Components/CommonModule/ImageCardModule/ImageCard.tsx:22:0-155:2) component that handles all screen sizes automatically using CSS Modules.
2. **Migrating to TypeScript:** Rewriting core modules in [.tsx](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/KIIT/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/Rocket.Chat/apps/meteor/client/providers/ToastMessagesProvider.tsx:0:0-0:0) to enforce type safety, catch errors at compile time, and provide better tooling for future contributors.
3. **Enhancing UX:** Implementing "Shimmer Loading" and reliable "One-Tap Downloads" to make the app feel premium and native-like.

**Impact:** A cleaner, faster, and more robust application that is easier for new open-source contributors to work on.

**Challenges we ran into**

Determining the Best Abstraction
The biggest challenge was identifying the common patterns between the Mobile, Tablet, and Desktop components. Initially, they seemed very different because they had different CSS layouts (Flexbox vs Grid).
How I overcame it:
1.  **Isolated Logic:** I extracted the core functionality (Downloading, Liking, Saving) into a custom hook (future plan) or shared state logic.
2.  **CSS Modules:** I used CSS Modules to handle the responsive differences cleanly without cluttering the JavaScript.
3.  **Variable Props:** I designed the `UnifiedImageCard` to accept a `variant` prop (`'mobile' | 'tablet' | 'desktop'`), allowing a single component to adapt its styling dynamically while keeping the core logic identical.

Another challenge was setting up **TypeScript** in an existing JS Vite project. I had to carefully configure [tsconfig.json](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/KIIT/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/WallGodds-Web/Frontend/tsconfig.json:0:0-0:0) to allow mixed [.jsx](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/KIIT/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/WallGodds-Web/Frontend/src/Components/GalleryModule/Gallery.jsx:0:0-0:0) and [.tsx](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/KIIT/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/Rocket.Chat/apps/meteor/client/providers/ToastMessagesProvider.tsx:0:0-0:0) files so the app wouldn't break during the incremental migration.

### Complete CI Testing for OpenPrinting Projects
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/complete-ci-testing-for-openprinting-projects-ba86) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_mbRa_8ubxyulhArF8djGNenlqUDbuM2/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=111523583523038117403&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Standardizing CI for OpenPrinting

![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square) ![Github Action](https://img.shields.io/badge/Github%20Action-333333?style=flat-square) ![Shell/Bash](https://img.shields.io/badge/Shell/Bash-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The "Works on My Machine" Crisis
Currently, the OpenPrinting ecosystem is migrating to a new modular architecture. While the core cups repository has a mature CI pipeline, critical components like libcupsfilters (the new library), cups-filters (legacy), and cups-snap lack consistent automated testing.  
This project solves three key problems:
High Barrier to Entry: New contributors struggle to build the software because dependencies aren't documented or automated.  
Manual Testing Burden: Maintainers have to manually verify PRs, which is slow and prone to human error.  
Packaging Instability: There is no automated check to ensure that code changes don't break the final Snap/Docker packages for end-users. 
By implementing standardized GitHub Actions workflows, this project moves the ecosystem to a robust "Linux-First" CI pipeline that verifies builds, code quality, and packaging integrity on every single commit.

**Challenges we ran into**

Unmanaged Dependencies
When I conducted my initial audit to simulate a clean build environment, the build failed immediately. I encountered cryptic errors like error: autopoint not found and configure: error: Required cups-config is missing.  
The Fix: I had to reverse-engineer the build system to identify the exact missing packages (gettext, libcups2-dev, libqpdf-dev) and script their installation into the CI runner.  
2. Legacy vs. Modern Architecture
A major challenge is creating a unified strategy for both the legacy cups-filters (which relies on older standards) and the modern libcupsfilters.  
The Approach: I designed a modular build.yml workflow that can be adapted for both, using a Build Matrix to test across different Ubuntu LTS versions to ensure backwards compatibility.

### Project
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/foodline-cf83) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sF5yAcO9YZvARCxXIsEKfzavb-Z2EaCh/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=103290745075963808410&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> 1. Mixxx 2.Mixxx 3.Opstree

![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kubernetes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kubernetes-333333?style=flat-square) ![Qt](https://img.shields.io/badge/Qt-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. MIXXX
- When live streaming/broadcasting, Mixxx currently updates “Now Playing” metadata by selecting the deck with the highest volume every second, with a hardcoded “audible” threshold.
- During long blends (techno/minimal style), this causes metadata to rapidly flip between tracks and spam incorrect titles in stream/chat.
- This project adds a robust, user-controlled metadata update policy (Auto stable handover + optional Manual update/Lock) under Preferences: Live Broadcasting, so metadata updates are stable and predictable.

Issue link: mixxxdj/mixxx #15869 (https://github.com/mixxxdj/mixxx/issues/15869)

2. MIXXX
Mixxx currently routes audio to outputs like Main, Headphones, and Booth, which are typically already occupied by physical devices during a gig/stream setup. When DJs want to capture Mixxx audio in OBS (or other recording/streaming tools), they often have to rely on virtual audio cable/routing tools to duplicate the Master output.
This project adds a dedicated Record Output in Preferences: Sound Hardware that sends a duplicate of the Master mix to a separately selectable device/output. This makes streaming/recording setups:
- Simpler: no extra third-party audio routing required in common cases
- Safer: fewer moving parts that can fail during a live set
- More flexible: users can keep Main output for speakers/mixer and use Record output specifically for OBS/recorders

Target issue: mixxxdj/mixxx #15775.
https://github.com/mixxxdj/mixxx/issues/15775

3. OPSTREE
Adds clear health reporting for Redis Replication and Sentinel in redis-operator so users can instantly see readiness and failure reasons via kubectl, and adds kind-based CI smoke tests to prevent regressions.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. MIXXX
- Getting productive in a large C++/CMake codebase: setting up the Mixxx build environment (vcpkg buildenv, CMake generator) and reproducing issues reliably on Windows.
- Addressing maintainer review feedback: adjusting the ordering of checks, making error messages cross-platform, and handling path separator formatting differences (Windows vs CMake’s “/” paths).
- I handled this by reproducing the issue with minimal commands, iterating quickly with small commits, and validating output on Windows before updating the PR.

PR link: my open PR: #15899 (https://github.com/mixxxdj/mixxx/pull/15899#pullrequestreview-3703887841)

3. OPSTREE
- Setting up a reproducible local dev environment (kind + CRDs + operator). Solved by scripting setup and documenting common failure cases.
- Making status/conditions stable (no flapping) and meaningful. Solved by using standard Kubernetes Conditions and adding tests.
- Avoiding flaky e2e tests in CI. Solved with robust wait checks, timeouts, and debug logs on failure.

**AOPS**

- Open Source Contribution (C++/Qt)
- Systems / Desktop Application Development
- CMake / Build Systems (vcpkg buildenv)
- Audio Software / Live Broadcasting (metadata updates)
- Networking / Streaming (broadcast pipeline)
- Testing & Tooling (unit tests, CI-friendly changes)

**The problem it solves**

I am submitting 3 distinct proposals for Winter of Code 5.0:

1. OpsTree Global: Redis Operator Enhancements
Problem: The current operator lacks automated disaster recovery and auto-scaling.

Solution: Implementing a RedisBackup CRD for S3 snapshots and integrating Kubernetes HPA for dynamic scaling of Sentinel pods.

2. OWASP Nest: Backend Microservices Refactor
Problem: High latency during data ingestion due to synchronous processing.

Solution: Refactoring the backend into an async microservices architecture using Celery, Redis, and Docker to handle heavy loads.

3. OpenPrinting: CI Infrastructure Modernization
Problem: libcupsfilters lacks a standardized CI pipeline, risking regressions.

Solution: Implementing robust GitHub Actions workflows for cross-platform builds, static analysis (CodeQL), and containerized testing.

### Strengthening Open Source Infrastructure
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/building-reliable-performant-and-developerfriendly-open-source-systems-31ac) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/135jQriggD0-KC7BgMHXeApXFzdAkMPKf/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=105713651815631722856&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Prevent performance regressions in Kornia

![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Github Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/Github%20Actions-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kornia](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kornia-333333?style=flat-square) ![CUDA (GPU benchmarking)](https://img.shields.io/badge/CUDA%20(GPU%20benchmarking)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern computer vision systems rely heavily on **image augmentation pipelines** for training robust models. While Kornia is designed as a **high-performance, GPU-accelerated augmentation library**, there is currently **no standardized or automated way to measure, compare, or track its performance over time**.

This creates several problems:

* Performance regressions can be introduced unknowingly in new pull requests
* Maintainers lack objective, reproducible benchmarks to guide optimization decisions
* Users cannot make data-driven comparisons between Kornia, torchvision, and Albumentations
* Contributors have no clear performance baseline to validate changes

This project solves these issues by introducing a **reproducible, CI-driven benchmarking framework** for Kornia’s augmentation pipeline.

### What users can do with it

* **Automatically detect performance regressions** before code is merged
* **Compare Kornia’s augmentation speed** against torchvision and Albumentations
* **Measure CPU vs GPU throughput** and single-image vs batched execution
* **Make performance a first-class, testable property** of the library

By integrating benchmarking into the CI pipeline, this project helps Kornia **maintain its core promise of speed**, while making performance **transparent, measurable, and reproducible** for maintainers, contributors, and users.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Fair Cross-Library Benchmarking

Different libraries follow different assumptions for:

* Input formats (NumPy vs Tensor, channel order)
* Memory layouts
* CPU vs GPU execution paths

**Solution:**
A standardized input pipeline was designed to normalize:

* Image sizes, batch sizes, and dtypes
* Tensor layouts and device placement
* Equivalent augmentation parameters

Where exact output equivalence was not possible, fairness constraints were documented explicitly to ensure meaningful comparisons.

---

### 2. Benchmark Noise and CI Stability

Performance benchmarks are inherently sensitive to:

* System load
* GPU warm-up behavior
* Short-running timing instability

This makes CI-based benchmarking especially challenging.

**Solution:**

* Used `torch.utils.benchmark` for statistically robust timing
* Added warm-up iterations and minimum run durations
* Focused on **relative regression thresholds**, not absolute timings
* Ensured benchmarks were **non-flaky and deterministic** before CI integration

---

### 3. Balancing Coverage vs Execution Time

Benchmarking many operators, batch sizes, and devices can easily exceed CI time limits.

**Solution:**

* Carefully selected a **representative subset** of augmentations
* Designed benchmarks to be **parameterized and extensible**
* Split “full benchmarks” (local / scheduled) from **CI-safe regression checks**

---

### 4. Avoiding Misuse of AI-Generated Code

While AI tools can accelerate development, they can also introduce:

* Incorrect benchmarking logic
* Unfair comparisons
* Performance anti-patterns

**Solution:**
AI assistants were used **only for scaffolding and refactoring**, while:

* Benchmark design
* Performance analysis
* Validation decisions
  were done manually with careful review and local testing.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/transcribeit-and-scan-api-and-owasp-nest-bceb) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jqIl7b_DT9SR5tEFyoCxbYJ4MUwHtW0e/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=115075849863232515707&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> ENGINEER

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/pytest-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Project 1: TRANSCRIBEIT
The problem it solves

TranscribeIt powers video accessibility, but a powerful backend is useless if the user interface leaves users in the dark. Currently, users upload videos and face a static screen with no feedback, leading to uncertainty about whether the process has failed.

This project solves the "Feedback Loop" problem. By implementing a Real-Time Job Status Dashboard, users will see exactly what is happening (Pending -> Processing -> Done). Additionally, it solves the Exclusion Problem by auditing and fixing accessibility violations (WCAG), ensuring that the "hard of hearing" community—the primary target audience—can actually navigate the tool using screen readers and keyboards.

Project 2: SCANAPI 
The problem it solves

APIs are the backbone of modern software, but maintaining them is difficult without robust testing. ScanAPI automates this, but it currently suffers from a lack of comprehensive unit tests and a steep learning curve for new contributors.

My contribution solves the "Stability vs. Agility" trade-off. By increasing unit test coverage with Pytest, I ensure that future changes don't break existing features. Furthermore, by introducing Docker support, I solve the "It works on my machine" problem, allowing any developer to set up the project in minutes, regardless of their operating system.

Project 3: OWASP NEST
The problem it solves

OWASP Nest is the central hub for the global security community, but its user experience (UX) on mobile devices and Windows environments creates a barrier to entry.

This project solves the "Onboarding Friction" problem. By polishing the mobile UI, I ensure that security professionals can access resources on the go. More importantly, by documenting the Docker Setup for Windows (WSL2), I open the door for thousands of developers who were previously unable to contribute due to complex setup requirements.

**Challenges we ran into**

Project 1: TRANSCRIBEIT
Challenges I ran into

1. Understanding the Async Flow: The biggest hurdle was mapping out how the frontend should communicate with the backend's asynchronous processing. Since the transcription happens in the background, a simple HTTP request/response cycle doesn't work.

How I got over it: I analyzed the API documentation and determined that a Polling Strategy (using SWR or React Query) is the most robust solution for this architecture. I prototyped a small polling hook to verify I could fetch status updates without flooding the server.

2. Accessibility Testing: I realized that "visually working" doesn't mean "accessible." How I got over it: I set up lighthouse-ci locally to run audits. I identified that the current color contrast was insufficient for visually impaired users and planned a theme update using Chakra UI's token system to fix it.

Project 2: SCANAPI
Challenges I ran into

1. Dependency Conflicts: During my local setup, I faced issues with conflicting Python package versions on my Windows machine, which prevented the project from running.

How I got over it: This challenge actually inspired my proposal! I realized that containerizing the application with Docker would eliminate this issue entirely. I drafted a Dockerfile that isolates the environment, ensuring a consistent setup for everyone.

2. Testing Edge Cases: Understanding the complex validation logic in evaluator.py was difficult. How I got over it: I used pytest to run small, isolated experiments on the code. I learned how to use pytest.mark.parametrize to test multiple input scenarios efficiently, which will be the core of my contribution.

Project 3: OWASP NEST
Challenges I ran into

1. Docker on Windows: Getting the development environment running on Windows was non-trivial due to file permission issues and volume mounting differences in Docker Desktop.

How I got over it: I spent time researching WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux) best practices. I successfully documented the exact commands needed to run the project on Windows, which forms the basis of my "Documentation" milestone.

2. Mobile Layout Shifts: I noticed that the "Project Cards" broke the layout on smaller screens, causing horizontal scrolling. How I got over it: I inspected the CSS using Chrome DevTools' mobile simulator. I identified the specific Tailwind CSS utility classes causing the overflow and planned a refactor using Flexbox/Grid to make the layout truly responsive.

**AOPS**

This project Transcribeit fits the "Art of Problem Solving" track because it addresses two critical disconnects in the current system: User Uncertainty and Digital Exclusion. The core problem isn't just "displaying data"; it is solving the asynchronous gap between a long-running backend process and a synchronous frontend user experience. My solution involves architecting a Polling Mechanism that elegantly bridges this gap without overloading the server. Furthermore, by implementing WCAG 2.1 compliance, I am systematically dismantling the barriers that prevented the target audience from using the software.

This project SCANAPI fits the "Art of Problem Solving" track because it tackles the fundamental problem of Software Entropy—the tendency for code to break and environments to drift over time. My contribution solves the "It works on my machine" dilemma by introducing Docker Containerization. Additionally, by implementing Parameterized Unit Tests, I am solving the problem of "Regression Risk," replacing manual verification with automated mathematical certainty to ensure the API validator behaves consistently across thousands of edge cases.

This project OWASP NET fits the "Art of Problem Solving" track because it focuses on removing Onboarding Friction, which is the single biggest bottleneck for open-source communities. The problem is that complex setup requirements and poor mobile UX act as "Gatekeepers." My solution applies Documentation as Code and Responsive Design Patterns to lower this barrier, analyzing layout shifts and reverse-engineering Docker volume issues to transform the platform from an "exclusive" club into an inclusive hub for the entire global security community.

### Academic Performance Intelligence System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/academic-performance-intelligence-system-0a9d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/atharvakhotaig-boop/Academic-Performance-Intelligence-System) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Stop tracking. Start deciding.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## ❓ Problem Statement

Students are expected to maintain attendance, track assignments, and predict internal assessment (ISA) scores across an entire semester. In reality, this information is **fragmented, time-dependent, and cognitively demanding**. Most students either:

- Track data manually (notes, spreadsheets, memory)
- Use basic CRUD apps that only store inputs
- React too late after attendance or marks have already dropped

Existing systems **record the past** but do not help students **decide the future**.

---

## 💡 What Problem APIS Solves

APIS solves the problem of **academic uncertainty and decision fatigue**.

Instead of asking students to:
- Count lectures
- Calculate percentages
- Predict outcomes manually

APIS does this automatically and **converts academic data into decisions**.

---

## 🛠️ What People Can Use APIS For

### 🎓 Attendance Decisions
- Know **whether you can safely skip a lecture**
- Understand **how many classes you must attend to recover**
- Get guidance even if you **join mid-semester**
- Automatically account for **holidays and cancelled lectures**

### 📝 Assignment Planning
- Track assignment progress without spreadsheets
- See how remaining assignments affect final scores
- Compare best, worst, and target outcomes

### 🎯 ISA Marks Forecasting
- Predict ISA marks before evaluations end
- Understand how attendance and assignments combine
- Reverse-calculate what a percentage actually means in lectures or marks

---

## ⚙️ How APIS Makes Existing Tasks Easier

| Traditional Approach | With APIS |
|---------------------|----------|
| Manual attendance counting | Automatic lecture prediction |
| Percentage calculations | Instant decision outputs |
| Spreadsheets & guesswork | Scenario-based planning |
| Daily tracking | Event-based confirmation |
| Reactive recovery | Goal-oriented planning |

---

## 🧠 Why This Matters

Students don’t fail because they lack data.  
They fail because they **don’t know what to do next**.

APIS removes ambiguity by:
- Reducing human error
- Minimizing manual input
- Making academic outcomes predictable
- Helping students act early, not late

---

## ✅ Outcome

APIS turns attendance and assessment tracking from a **passive record-keeping task** into an **active academic intelligence system** that helps students stay compliant, strategic, and stress-free throughout the semester.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🔴 The Core Problem  
The biggest hurdle was that **the app initially loaded as a blank white screen**, even though the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript were present and error-free at first glance.

This happened because:
- The app used a **multi-page SPA-like structure** (`.page` sections toggled via JavaScript)
- No page was being explicitly activated on first load
- Rendering depended on `localStorage` state and URL hash
- A missing initialization flow caused *nothing to be shown*

In short: **logic existed, but nothing told the browser what to render first.**

---

### 🧠 Why This Was Tricky  
- There were **no visible console errors**
- CSS was working, but everything was hidden by default
- The bug only appeared on fresh loads or Live Server
- It involved **state, routing, and rendering order**, not syntax

This made it harder than a typical “missing semicolon” bug.

---

### 🛠️ How It Was Fixed  

We introduced a **deterministic initialization pipeline**:

1. **Central `init()` function**
   - Loads all data from `localStorage`
   - Determines the correct starting page:
     - Setup → Subjects → Intelligence

2. **Explicit page activation**
   - Ensured exactly one `.page` is active at all times

3. **Defensive rendering**
   - All render functions now validate required data before running
   - Graceful fallbacks if data is missing or corrupted

4. **State-safe navigation**
   - Added controlled page transitions and history handling

---

### ✅ Outcome  

- The app now **never loads blank**
- Works reliably on:
  - First open
  - Page refresh
  - Live Server
  - Direct URL access
- Improved overall architecture and stability

---

### 🧩 Key Learning  

> In logic-heavy frontend systems, **rendering order and state initialization matter more than UI code**.

This fix pushed the project from “working UI” to a **robust, production-ready system**.

**AOPS**

**APIS fits squarely under the Student Productivity + EdTech track**, with strong overlap into **Smart Systems / Applied Intelligence**.

It is not a generic tracking tool — it is a **decision-support system for students**, solving real academic workflow problems using logic, time-awareness, and structured intelligence.

---

## 🧩 Problem Area (What APIS Targets)

- Academic overload due to:
  - Manual attendance tracking
  - Assignment mismanagement
  - Unclear ISA/assessment rules
- Decision paralysis:
  - “Can I skip?”
  - “How many do I need to attend?”
  - “Am I safe or already late?”

These are **systemic student problems**, not UI problems.

---

## 🧠 How APIS Fits the Track

### ✅ Student Productivity
- Reduces cognitive load by eliminating manual calculations
- Replaces spreadsheets, notes, and guesswork
- Converts academic data into *actionable advice*

### ✅ EdTech (Beyond LMS)
- Complements college LMS systems instead of duplicating them
- Works independently of institution infrastructure
- Adapts to **any college’s rules**, not just one syllabus

### ✅ Smart / Applied Intelligence
- Timetable-driven prediction engine
- Time-aware logic (lecture cutoff, holidays)
- Scenario analysis (best / worst / target)
- Goal-oriented planning instead of passive tracking

---

## 🚀 Why It’s a Strong Hackathon Fit

- Solves a **real, universal student pain point**
- Goes beyond CRUD into **logic + reasoning**
- Fully working, offline-first system
- Scalable idea (college-agnostic, rules-driven)
- Clear differentiation from “attendance tracker” projects

### libpdfrip
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/libpdfrip-c6c1) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1z7l0YT8f83R-VYxHysIOdOsCXIZudWRC/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=116128124606971856116&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> High Performance PDF Rendering and Analysis Tool

![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square) ![GNU Make](https://img.shields.io/badge/GNU%20Make-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cairo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cairo-333333?style=flat-square) ![PDF](https://img.shields.io/badge/PDF-333333?style=flat-square) ![Pdfio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pdfio-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many real-world PDF documents rely on Form XObjects to represent reusable vector graphics such as logos, icons, stamps, and repeated UI elements. These objects are referenced through content streams to avoid duplicating graphical data and are essential for correct and efficient PDF rendering.

Currently, libpdfrip does not support Form XObject rendering. As a result, PDFs that depend on these constructs are rendered incorrectly or incompletely, limiting libpdfrip’s ability to handle production-grade documents.

This project addresses this gap by implementing Form XObject rendering support in libpdfrip, including correct resource lookup, graphics state handling, transformations, and recursive interpretation. This enables libpdfrip to render a wider range of real-world PDFs accurately, improving its reliability and usability as a fully open PDF rendering engine for the OpenPrinting ecosystem.

**Challenges we ran into**

While exploring the OpenPrinting stack, one challenge was building pdfio from the development branch due to issues with the bundled ttf submodule. I resolved this by switching to the stable v1.6.1 release, building it locally, and validating functionality using the provided examples.

Another challenge was understanding and tracing PDF content stream execution and graphics state handling in libpdfrip, especially for complex real-world PDFs. I addressed this by running the existing pdf2cairo test suite in verbose mode, analyzing the generated PNG outputs, and stepping through the interpreter logic to understand operator handling and rendering flow.

These steps helped me gain confidence in the codebase and clearly scope the proposed implementation work.

> Precision in Rendering, Accuracy in Data, Clarity

![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/pytest-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square) ![CMake](https://img.shields.io/badge/CMake-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1) libpdfrip – Improved PDF Rendering

Problem it solves: - Current versions of libpdfrip cannot render Form XObjects, which are widely used in modern PDFs to represent logos, stamps, icons, and reusable UI elements. This makes it impossible to accurately display production PDFs that rely on these objects.

How it helps / Use cases:- 

- Enables accurate rendering of complex PDFs for viewing, printing, or conversion.

- Supports applications in document processing, digital publishing, and PDF verification.

- Reduces errors and inconsistencies when displaying PDFs, improving reliability and user trust.

2) Open World Holidays Framework – Accurate Holiday Data

Problem it solves:- Existing holiday libraries often have inaccuracies in dates, regional names, or localization, which can cause scheduling conflicts in real-world applications.

How it helps / Use cases:

- Provides reliable, region-specific holiday data for applications in finance, HR, travel, and calendar systems.

- Simplifies global scheduling by automatically accounting for local holidays.

- Improves data integrity for applications relying on date-sensitive operations, reducing costly errors.

3) Exsh – Educational Unix-like Shell

Problem it solves: - Students and learners often lack a clear understanding of low-level shell mechanics, as most shells abstract away system calls, process management, and command execution.

How it helps / Use cases:

- Serves as a learning platform to understand core Unix concepts like process management, I/O redirection, and system calls.

- Enables hands-on experimentation with shell behavior and operating system fundamentals.

- Improves educational outcomes by making OS internals accessible, safe, and reproducible.

**Challenges we ran into**

1) libpdfrip – Improved PDF Rendering

Challenges:

- Form XObject Complexity: Handling nested and recursive content streams required careful management of transformation matrices and graphics states.

- Resource Resolution: Accurately locating and linking fonts, images, and other resources within Form XObjects.

- Bounding Box Calculations: Correctly computing the boundaries of Form XObjects to prevent clipping or misalignment during rendering.

- Integration with Existing Codebase: Ensuring that improvements didn’t break other PDF rendering functionality or introduce regressions.

2) Open World Holidays Framework – Accurate Holiday Data

Challenges:

- Regional Variations: Accounting for local variations in holiday observance, including exceptions and unofficial holidays.

- Data Accuracy: Verifying official sources and correcting inconsistencies in existing holiday data.

- Localization: Providing accurate holiday names in different languages while maintaining consistency across regions.

- Testing: Writing robust test cases to ensure correctness for multiple countries and edge cases, like leap years or movable holidays.

3) Exsh – Educational Unix-like Shell

Challenges:

- Process Management: Implementing fork/exec correctly, including handling of background processes and process termination.

- Command Parsing: Building a reliable parser to interpret complex commands, pipes, and redirection.

- State Management: Maintaining the shell’s internal state while safely executing user commands.

- Error Handling: Preventing crashes or undefined behavior while providing informative error messages to users.

### High-Performance Augmentation Benchmarking
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/highperformance-augmentation-benchmarking-71bb) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18mWIdqcafDl1kzRmjU2vww8_4o4Qx31R/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=114742060332178760042&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> Detecting performance regressions in Kornia

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

As computer vision pipelines grow in complexity, image augmentation becomes a critical performance bottleneck. While Kornia provides highly optimized augmentation operators, there is currently no standardized way to continuously measure performance changes or detect regressions as the codebase evolves.

This project addresses that gap by introducing a structured benchmarking framework for Kornia’s image augmentation pipeline. It enables maintainers and contributors to measure throughput and latency across different configurations and automatically detect performance regressions early in the development process.

By providing reproducible benchmarks and CI-based performance tracking, the project helps ensure that Kornia remains fast, reliable, and scalable for real-world machine learning workloads.

**Challenges we ran into**

Since this project is currently in the proposal and planning phase, the main challenges so far have been related to understanding the problem space and designing a realistic approach. One challenge was gaining clarity on how performance benchmarking should be structured to ensure results are reproducible and meaningful across different environments.

To address this, I reviewed existing benchmarking practices in similar libraries and studied Kornia’s current augmentation pipeline and CI setup. This helped me refine the scope of the project, identify feasible milestones, and design a plan that balances learning with practical contributions. I expect additional technical challenges during implementation, which I plan to address through incremental development, testing, and mentor feedback.

> “The One-Stop Platform for military"

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blender](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Unity 3D](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity%203D-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
1. Bridging the Gap Between Civilians and Defense Tech Most people never get the chance to see heavy military assets (like warships, submarines, or battle tanks) up close. They are restricted, dangerous, or located in specific bases. This app democratizes access, allowing anyone to bring these massive assets into their living room or classroom to explore them safely and in detail.

2. Transforming Passive Learning into Active Exploration Traditional methods of learning about the Indian Army—textbooks, 2D photos, or video clips—are passive. They don't convey the true scale or complexity of the machinery. This AR application solves this by providing immersive, spatial visualization. Users can walk around a tank, inspect a ship from different angles, and understand the scale of the equipment relative to their own environment.

3. Zero-Cost, Risk-Free Training & Education For students, cadets, or defense enthusiasts, examining real equipment is expensive and logistically difficult. This app solves the logistical nightmare of physical field trips. It serves as a safe, portable digital museum, making defense education accessible without the need for physical travel or security clearance.

4. Inspiring the Next Generation By making the Indian Army's assets interactive and "gamified" through Augmented Reality, the app engages younger audiences in a way that static images cannot. It acts as a modern tool for inspiration and recruitment, sparking curiosity about engineering and defense careers among youth.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
1. The "Grey Screen" Configuration Nightmare One of the biggest hurdles was getting the AR camera to actually render on the device. After building the APK, the app would launch but only show a static "grey skybox" instead of the camera feed.

The Bug: The app was treating the project as a standard 3D game rather than an AR experience.

How I Solved It: I dug into Unity's XR Plug-in Management and realized the "Google ARCore" provider wasn't explicitly enabled. Additionally, I discovered that the Vulkan graphics API was causing crashes on Android. Switching the graphics API to OpenGLES3 and enabling the ARCore plugin instantly fixed the feed.

2. The "Infinite Clones" Logic Error Initially, my TapToPlace script was too simple. Every time I tapped the screen to move the 3D model, it would Instantiate (spawn) a new copy of the tank/ship. Within seconds, my room was filled with overlapping models.

How I Solved It: I refactored the C# script to check if the object already exists (spawnedObject != null). If it does, the code now simply updates the position of the existing object to the new raycast hit point, rather than spawning a new one.

3. The "Invisible Model" (Pivot Point Offset) When I imported my .glb models from Blender, the AR placement felt broken. I would tap the floor, but the tank would spawn 3 meters to the right or behind a wall, making it look like the app wasn't working.

The Bug: The pivot point (origin) of the model in Blender wasn't set to (0,0,0), and the export had a massive transform offset.

How I Solved It: I learned to "freeze transformations" in Blender before exporting. In Unity, I created a parent prefab to zero out the position (0,0,0) and standardized the scale to 0.1 so the heavy machinery fit realistically inside a room without clipping through the ceiling.

**AOPS**

our Military Educator chatbot fits the AOPs (Art of Problem Solving) track in Winter of Code on Devfolio through its algorithmic foundation for solving complex military training queries.
​

Core Algorithmic Mapping
The chatbot processes aspirant queries across army, navy, and air force domains using discrete algorithms:

Graph Search: Tactical pathfinding (e.g., optimal troop routes avoiding obstacles) via Dijkstra/A*—core to NDA physical/spatial reasoning problems.

Dynamic Programming: Resource optimization for logistics (e.g., min cost ammo/supply deployment under constraints), mirroring CDS optimization puzzles.

Tree/Trie Structures: Efficient multi-domain knowledge retrieval (e.g., branching queries on joint operations), achieving O(n log n) response times.

AOPs Track Alignment

![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem statement 1(TranscribeIt):
Many people face difficulty accessing video content because accurate transcriptions are either missing or poorly generated. This especially affects people who are hard of hearing, have sensory processing issues, or prefer reading over listening. Live streams and long videos make this problem worse, as captions are often unavailable or unreliable.

Even when transcription tools exist, they are hard to set up, poorly documented, or not beginner friendly for contributors who want to improve them. TranscribeIt aims to solve this by providing an open-source, well-structured video transcription system with clear documentation, reliable backend workflows, and accessible transcript outputs, making both usage and contribution easier for users and developers.

Problem Statement 2(OWASP Nest):
OWASP Nest is a comprehensive platform designed to enhance collaboration and contribution within the OWASP community. The application serves as a central hub for exploring OWASP projects and ways to contribute to them, empowering contributors to find opportunities that align with their interests and expertise.

Problem Statement 3(ScanAPI):
APIs are a core part of modern software systems, but keeping API behavior, testing, and documentation aligned is still a major challenge. Many teams rely on manual testing or fragmented tools, which leads to unreliable integrations, outdated documentation, and poor developer experience. ScanAPI addresses this problem by providing automated API integration testing and live documentation based on OpenAPI specifications. It validates real API behavior against the specification, helping teams detect breaking changes early and improve reliability.

### OpenPrintGuard: Multi-Arch CI Security
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/openprintguard-multiarch-ci-and-security-for-core-libraries-c841) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1e_w5deqLCrz6n7nvb6MK4VwPmXU0mfkf/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=116429206810151611923&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co)

> CVE Prevention Through Multi-Arch CI Excellence

![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

OpenPrinting's CUPS repository has world-class CI infrastructure, but critical projects like **libppd**, **libpappl-retrofit**, and **cpdb-libs** lack comprehensive testing. 

**3 Critical Problems:**
1. **No Multi-Architecture Testing** → ARM/ARM64 bugs ship undetected (explains CVE-2024-47175)
2. **Inconsistent Test Frameworks** → Contributors unclear how to validate changes
3. **No Integration Testing** → Dependency breaks surface post-release, not at code review

**Impact:** Security vulnerabilities reach production. Recent RCE flaws (CVE-2024-47175, CVE-2024-47076) trace directly to CI gaps. OpenPrinting's printing stack serves millions of Linux systems—vulnerabilities propagate ecosystem-wide.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Architecture Complexity**
GitHub Actions runners are x86_64-only. Solution: Docker buildx + QEMU for ARM64/ARM32 emulation (<10min overhead).

**2. Polyglot Ecosystem**
C (libppd), Go (goipp), Python (pycups) needed unified CI patterns. Solution: Language-specific templates with shared matrix strategies.

**3. Existing Bugs vs Test Bugs**
Discovered real vulnerabilities during test development. Solution: Prioritized regression tests first, documented findings for maintainers.

**4. CUPS Pattern Adaptation**
CUPS CI is excellent but project-specific. Solution: Created generic templates adaptable to 43+ OpenPrinting repos.

**Key Insight:** OpenPrinting's strength (mature ecosystem) became challenge (inconsistent infrastructure). Solution required both deep analysis + pragmatic engineering.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/miraya-eec4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Weekend%20of%20Code%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://weekendofcode2k26.devfolio.co)

> Many forms. One soul.

![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern digital platforms are flooded with images. The same image often appears multiple times—cropped, resized, compressed, filtered, or slightly edited—creating a web of visual duplicates that traditional systems struggle to identify.

These near-duplicate images cause serious challenges:

- Wasted storage due to redundant image uploads

- Spam & repost abuse by bots or malicious actors

- Copyright violations, harming original creators

- Poor search and feed quality, showing the same image repeatedly

- Misinformation amplification, where the same visual spreads across contexts

Conventional pixel-level comparisons or simple hashes fail once images are altered even slightly.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Corrupted dataset downloads**: INIRIA dataset was corrupted and not getting downloaded.
Solution: Verified archives and re-downloaded using streamed downloads with integrity checks

- **CLIP model loading issues**: Network timeouts during startup 
Solution: Rebuilt ground truth using only images actually present in the index

- **Evaluation showing F1 = 0**: Queries not present in index 
Solution: Rebuilt ground truth using only images actually present in the index

### CityIQ — Smart Emergency Response Platform
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cityiq-smart-emergency-response-platform-5252) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/CyberMohit-sys/cityIQ.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://cityiq-devfest-2026.lovable.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co)

> Smart emergency alerts for safer cities

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Cities today face a critical gap in real-time emergency awareness and response.
When accidents, medical emergencies, fires, floods, or public safety incidents occur, people often:
Don’t know what is happening nearby
Can’t quickly find nearest hospitals, shelters, police or fire stations
Waste precious time switching between multiple apps or searching online
Receive no reliable fallback when live systems or APIs fail
Emergency response systems are usually fragmented, static, or designed only for authorities — not for citizens on the ground.

💡 How CityIQ Helps?
CityIQ is a real-time, location-aware smart emergency response platform that helps citizens and communities act faster and safer during critical situations.
People can use CityIQ to:
🚨 View live emergencies happening around them on an interactive map
📍 Instantly discover nearby hospitals, police stations, fire stations, shelters, and aid centers based on their GPS location
📝 Report emergencies with severity, description, and location in seconds
🤖 Prioritize incidents intelligently using AI-based urgency scoring
👥 Enable community response, allowing nearby volunteers to assist
📱 Access everything as an installable PWA, even with poor connectivity
🛡️ Built for Real-World Reliability
CityIQ is designed for real-life conditions, not perfect lab environments:
Works in real-time mode using live location and open data
Includes a Demo / Fallback mode to ensure functionality during API limits, network issues, or high-traffic scenarios
Continues to provide nearby resources even when live data is unavailable
This makes CityIQ suitable for hackathon demos, real deployments, and disaster scenarios alike.

🌍 Why It Matters
By reducing response time, improving situational awareness, and empowering citizens with actionable information, CityIQ helps save lives and makes cities safer.
It bridges the gap between people, emergency services, and real-time data — turning smart city technology into real impact.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Nearby Resources Not Matching User Location
Problem:
In real-time mode, the app was sometimes returning hospitals and shelters from distant locations (e.g., Goa or Mumbai) instead of truly nearby resources.
Why it happened:
API credit limits caused incomplete responses from the OpenStreetMap Overpass API
In some cases, location permissions were delayed or cached coordinates were used
When the API failed silently, fallback logic wasn’t triggered early enough
Solution:
Added explicit GPS refresh control to force re-fetching live coordinates
Implemented distance-based filtering to discard resources beyond a fixed radius
Built a smart fallback system that injects realistic nearby simulated resources when live APIs fail or return insufficient results
This ensured the app always shows relevant nearby resources, even under API or network constraints.
2. Balancing Real-Time Functionality with Demo Reliability
Problem:
Hackathon demos must never fail, but real-time systems depend on APIs, permissions, and network stability.
Solution:
Introduced a dual-mode architecture:
Demo Mode → Stable, seeded data for smooth judging
Real-Time Mode → Live Supabase + GPS + OpenStreetMap
Added a clear UI toggle so judges can instantly switch and understand both modes
Included a guided tour explaining the system flow during demos
This allowed CityIQ to be both technically real and demo-safe.
3. Real-Time State Synchronization
Problem:
Handling live emergency updates, UI animations, and map markers together caused race conditions and inconsistent state.
Solution:
Centralized state management using React Context + reducer pattern
Normalized emergency data structures between demo and live modes
Ensured map layers re-render only when necessary to maintain performance
This improved stability, responsiveness, and clarity.
4. PWA & Permissions Edge Cases
Problem:
PWA installability, push notifications, and GPS permissions behave differently across browsers and devices.
Solution:
Added graceful permission fallbacks with clear UI messaging
Ensured the app remains usable even when permissions are denied
Tested flows in both browser and installed PWA modes
🔍 Key Takeaway
The biggest challenge was building a system that is real-time, reliable, and demo-proof at the same time.
By designing for failures instead of ignoring them, CityIQ became more robust, realistic, and production-ready
CityIQ is a Progressive Web App (PWA), installable on mobile or desktop. For optimal demo experience, judges can view it in desktop site/full-screen mode.

**Software Development**

CityIQ is fundamentally a full-stack software system designed to solve a real-world urban safety problem at scale.
From a software development perspective, the project demonstrates:
End-to-end system design — frontend, backend, realtime data, and external APIs working together
Production-grade architecture using React + TypeScript, Supabase (PostgreSQL, realtime, storage), and PWA standards
Real-time data handling for live emergency reports, location updates, and resource discovery
Offline-first engineering with graceful fallbacks (demo mode, cached data, permission handling)
Cross-platform delivery via a Progressive Web App that runs on Web, Android, and iOS without separate codebases
Robust UX under constraints (GPS permissions, API limits, network failures)
CityIQ is not a prototype or static demo — it is a working software product that focuses on reliability, scalability, and real-world usability, which aligns directly with the goals of the Software Development track.

**AI**

How CityIQ fits the AI track?

CityIQ integrates AI to improve decision-making during emergencies, where speed and prioritization are critical.
The platform uses AI-driven logic to:
Analyze emergency reports (type, severity, location, time, and context)
Generate an urgency / priority score to help surface the most critical incidents first
Reduce human overload by automatically triaging multiple incoming reports
Support smarter responses by guiding citizens and volunteers toward the most impactful actions
Instead of replacing humans, AI in CityIQ acts as a decision-support system, helping communities and first responders react faster and more effectively.
The AI layer is designed to be modular and extensible, allowing future integration of:
NLP for incident text understanding
Computer vision for photo/video-based damage detection
Predictive risk analysis for urban safety
This practical, human-centered use of AI aligns strongly with the goals of the AI track.

### Time Gambit
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/time-gambit-d9a1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/r-baruah/Time-Gambit) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/0j84Z4XA--s?si=ZKsKFYf857YIlpkZ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devfest%205.0%20Goa-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devfest5goa.devfolio.co)

> The "Physics-Informed" Agentic AI Scheduler

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional scheduling tools are passive "databases of time." They don't understand context, energy levels, or the difference between "Deep Work" and a "Quick Sync." Users are forced to manually play Tetris with their own time, leading to fragmentation and burnout.

Time Gambit is an autonomous Agentic AI System that treats your schedule like a chessboard. Instead of a simple chatbot, it uses a sophisticated Router-Solver Architecture to:

- Negotiate with the user via a mobile-native interface (Telegram) to capture intent.
- Clarify ambiguity (e.g., asking "Is this a 30-min sync or a 1-hour deep dive?") before acting.
- Solve the time-slot optimization problem using "Physics-Informed" constraints (treating working hours and breaks as inviolable laws).
- Execute verified actions directly to Google Calendar.

**Challenges we ran into**

Time Gambit is not just a wrapper around an LLM; it is a Deterministically Constrained, Probabilistically Reasoning Agent. We built it to solve the specific problem of "Hallucinated Scheduling"—where AI assistants promise meetings that physically cannot happen.

🧠 System Architecture: The Router-Solver Pattern
We implemented a Stateful Multi-Agent Graph using LangGraph to decouple "Talk" from "Action":

🔵 Router Agent (The Gatekeeper):
Analyzes user intent (Schedule vs. Query vs. Chat). It prevents the expensive logic engine from running on simple queries.

🟢 Clarification Agent (The Investigator):
If a user says "Book a meeting," this agent halts execution and asks targeted questions: "With whom and for how long?" It maintains conversation state until all variables are resolved.

🟡 Solver Agent (The Physics Engine):
This agent acts as the execution layer. It converts natural language to ISO timestamps and solves for constraints (USER_WORKING_HOURS, LUNCH_BREAKS) before calling the Google Calendar API.
🤖 Kairos (The Interface):

We built Kairos (@Kairosengine_bot), a "Auth-First" Telegram bot. It acts as a secure bridge, forwarding authorized messages to the backend router. It features a BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) architecture, allowing privacy-focused users to bring their own API keys or use the hosted default.

⚡ Key Innovations
Physics-Informed Scheduling: The agent treats time constraints (like lunch breaks) as hard physical laws, not suggestions.
Auth-First Barrier: No commands are processed without OAuth 2.0 verification via Google.
Hybrid UX: Mobile-first interaction via Telegram for speed, coupled with a Next.js dashboard for rich administration.

### Adaptive Learning Intelligence Platform
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/learnmatevidya-b54f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/venkatayaswanth-IIITan/Adapactive-Learning-Intelligence-Platform) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1biFzykbEDPQ1WWAeX7kvhsIhOK_4jo2p/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=108080404503770390256&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Code%20Kalari-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://code-kalari.devfolio.co)

> LEARNMATE VIDYA-AI

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most existing learning platforms focus on delivering content and tracking completion, but they fail to understand how a student actually learns. They treat all learners the same, offering fixed paths, static recommendations, and one-time feedback regardless of whether a student is struggling, improving, or burning out.

As a result, students often face:

inefficient study patterns,

inconsistent learning habits,

cognitive overload or burnout,

and a lack of meaningful guidance on how to improve, not just what to study.

The core problem is not a lack of resources, but a lack of adaptive learning intelligence. Learning platforms rarely observe behavior deeply, learn from feedback, or adjust guidance over time. Students are left without a system that evolves alongside them.

This project addresses that gap by building a closed-loop, behavior-driven learning system that continuously observes student activity, derives insights, adapts learning strategies, and refines itself based on evidence—making personalization ongoing, explainable, and grounded in real behavior rather than assumptions.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the first roadblocks we encountered was realizing that tracking only high-level actions, such as sessions joined or resources viewed, was not enough to understand how a student learns. Early versions of the system produced shallow insights because the data lacked behavioral depth. We overcame this by redesigning our logging strategy to capture atomic learning events with contextual metadata. This shift allowed us to reconstruct learning behavior more accurately during analysis, without locking ourselves into premature assumptions.
Another significant roadblock appeared when we noticed that the adaptive loop worked well for the first iteration but began to repeat itself after that. The system was adapting based only on the current learning state, which caused recommendations to converge too quickly. To address this, we introduced a learning trajectory layer that records how learning states evolve over time. This enabled the system to detect plateaus and resistance to certain strategies, allowing subsequent iterations to remain meaningfully adaptive instead of repetitive.
Another significant roadblock appeared when we noticed that the adaptive loop worked well for the first iteration but began to repeat itself after that. The system was adapting based only on the current learning state, which caused recommendations to converge too quickly. To address this, we introduced a learning trajectory layer that records how learning states evolve over time. This enabled the system to detect plateaus and resistance to certain strategies, allowing subsequent iterations to remain meaningfully adaptive instead of repetitive.
Another challenge arose when updating learning guidance too frequently caused the system to feel unstable. Immediate reactions to individual tasks made recommendations fluctuate more than intended. We overcame this by introducing task-level feedback aggregation, where multiple task outcomes are evaluated together before updating the learning state. This allowed the system to adapt based on evidence rather than short-term noise.
Finally, presenting the system within limited time constraints became a roadblock during demonstrations. The depth of the workflow made it difficult to explain quickly. To handle this, we refined our abstraction layers and focused on communicating the closed-loop nature of the system rather than individual features, ensuring that the core idea remained clear even when time was limited.

> One Platform. Smarter Urban Decisions.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

UrbanX is an AI-based coordination platform designed to help city departments plan infrastructure work together instead of in isolation.

The problem we targeted is simple—but extremely common.

A road is repaired.
The next week, another department digs it up again.
Then another follows.

The result is chaos: delays, wasted money, traffic disruption, and frustrated citizens.

This happens because there is no single shared system where departments can see each other’s plans and coordinate before work begins.
So we tried building one.

What I’ve Built So Far

UrbanX currently includes:
A centralized dashboard for city departments
A live map view showing ongoing and planned projects
A citizen complaints module linked to locations
Project conflict detection logic (time + location overlaps)
Supabase for database and authentication
Backend APIs to manage project data
A basic machine learning model to predict project risk
A UI that has started to feel like a real product, not just a prototype

**Challenges we ran into**

While building UrbanX, I faced several technical challenges that strengthened my problem-solving skills.

- ESLint & Project Structure: A nested folder structure caused TypeScript parsing errors. I resolved this by fixing ESLint path configurations and adding proper ignore rules.
- Performance& Bundle Size: Large build sizes triggered Vite warnings. I optimized performance using code splitting, lazy loading, and manual chunking.
- Map Integration: React Leaflet integration caused dependency and rendering issues, which I fixed through version alignment, proper cleanup logic, and custom map handling.
- TypeScript Strict Mode: Strict checks exposed type and lint issues. I resolved these by adding strong typings, interfaces, and type guards.
- API & Auth Handling: Managing Google Maps APIs and Supabase authentication required careful async handling, error management, and protected routing.
- UI Consistency: Tailwind was customized to maintain consistent design, responsive layouts, and correct map overlay behavior.
These challenges helped turn UrbanX into a stable, production-like prototype.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/brain-works-4870) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/prathamb9/brain_works) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://brain-works-e58o.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/GLR7w3ZbDPo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackNITR%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknitr7.devfolio.co)

> Bridging the Gap Between AI Prediction and Clinica

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The "Black Box" Trust Deficit: Traditional AI models can predict a tumor with high accuracy, but they fail to explain why. Without visual evidence, clinicians hesitate to trust a machine's diagnosis, fearing the AI might be reacting to image noise or artifacts rather than actual tissue anomalies.

Radiologist Fatigue & Error: A single patient scan contains hundreds of MRI slices. Manually reviewing every slice is mentally exhausting for radiologists, leading to "alert fatigue" and increasing the risk of missing small, early-stage tumors.

Subjectivity in Diagnosis: Distinguishing between tumor types (e.g., Glioma vs. Meningioma) can be subjective. Junior doctors or general practitioners in remote areas may lack the specialized expertise to classify complex cases accurately.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge: The "Clever Hans" Effect (AI looking at the wrong place but guessing right).
Solution: We debugged the Grad-CAM layers (Fixed the High threshold 190+) to ensure the heatmap aligns with the actual tumor, not just the background.
Challenge: Shape Mismatches during testing.
Solution: Standardized the input pipeline to enforce strictly 128x128 resolution across training and testing phases.

### AI hallucination detector
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-hallucination-detector-49d1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/kifa-7/ai-hallucination-detector/tree/main) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/mPRWYDfDt8Q) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20Space%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-space-1.devfolio.co)

> Detecting false information in AI output

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![NLP](https://img.shields.io/badge/NLP-333333?style=flat-square) ![Generative AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Generative%20AI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Prompt Engineering](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prompt%20Engineering-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit for user interface](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit%20for%20user%20interface-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sentence Embeddings for semantic similarity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sentence%20Embeddings%20for%20semantic%20similarity-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In the context of generative AI systems, it has been noticed that they generate responses that come across as very convincing but sometimes consist of incorrect or even forged information, which has been termed as hallucinations
AI content, where students as well as developers are increasingly turning to content generated by artificial intelligences, currently does not provide a simple opportunity to check its accuracy.
This can cause inaccuracies and poorer decision-making and trust for these systems in Generative AI models.

**Challenges we ran into**

The first challenge was detecting hallucinations reliably because AI output can differ even when it is correct.
Building a process for distinguishing natural variation from true inconsistencies involved trial and error with different formulations of the prompt and thresholds for semantic similarity.

Another issue was to maintain accuracy and performance since there are more AI responses to produce.

This issue was handled by reducing the variations of the prompt and optimizing the logic for comparison to ensure the system remains responsive.

Working alone on this project, it was difficult to accomplish everything related to prompt engineering, semantics, and UI design on such short notice, However, it was beneficial to break the solution down into modular elements which helped in efficient development as well as testing of these elements.

**Generative AI**

The project is a direct fit in the Generative AI category as it aims to improve the reliability and authenticity of AI-generated output.
The proposed system incorporates large language models to create different responses based on the variations of the prompt. It utilizes semantic similarity analysis to identify inconsistencies and hallucinations.
By providing a hallucination risk score to the outputs of AI, the project responds to a significant challenge in using Generative AI in the real world.
