![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AcadBoost: Your Personalized AI Learning Companion

AcadBoost is a modern, AI-powered learning platform designed to help students and self-learners navigate the vast world of online education. It provides a centralized dashboard to track progress, discover new courses, and receive personalized recommendations to accelerate learning and bridge knowledge gaps.

 The Problem: The Modern Learner's Dilemma

In today's digital age, learners have access to an overwhelming number of online courses, tutorials, and resources. This abundance creates several challenges:

Information Overload : It's difficult to know where to start or which resources are most effective.
Fragmented Progress: Tracking learning across multiple platforms is manual and cumbersome.
Lack of Personalization: Generic course paths don't adapt to an individual's unique learning style, pace, or existing knowledge gaps.
Maintaining Motivation: Without a clear view of progress and a structured path, it's easy to lose motivation.

 The AcadBoost Solution

AcadBoost tackles these challenges by providing a smart, centralized, and personalized learning environment.

Unified Dashboard: Consolidates a user's learning journey into one place, tracking time spent, courses in progress, and completed subjects.
AI-Powered Recommendations: Leverages generative AI to suggest personalized content, helping users discover relevant courses and materials to fill their knowledge gaps.
Interactive Learning with EduChat: An integrated AI chatbot that provides instant answers to questions, suggests relevant web links, and recommends YouTube search queries to deepen understanding.
Curated Course Discovery: Offers a well-organized library of courses and resources across various domains like programming, AI, and professional skills.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building AcadBoost has been an iterative process focused on creating a stable and useful application. Key challenges encountered and overcome include:

1.  AI Integration Instability: Initial versions of the EduChat chatbot suffered from unreliable third-party API integrations (like the YouTube API), leading to frequent errors and a poor user experience.
    Solution: We pivoted to a more robust approach. Instead of fetching live data and risking API failures, the AI model now generates direct, high-quality search suggestions. This made the feature significantly more reliable while still providing valuable, actionable recommendations for the user.

2. Component & Dependency Conflicts: As the app grew, we faced build failures due to dependency mismatches, particularly with React 19 compatibility. We also encountered accessibility and rendering errors in our UI components.
    Solution: We systematically updated and resolved package conflicts (e.g., `next-themes`). Errors within our UI components were debugged and fixed by ensuring they adhered to the requirements of the underlying libraries (e.g., adding necessary `Title` props to dialogs).

This iterative, problem-solving approach has been key to developing AcadBoost into the stable platform it is today.

**The problem it solves**

AI Interview Practice Coach is designed to help students and job seekers prepare for technical and behavioral interviews in a practical, low-pressure environment.

Primary Use Cases
- Interview Practice  
  Users can practice role-specific interview questions (for example, Java Developer, Python Developer, Data Analyst) without needing a human interviewer.

- Self-Assessment  
  The system evaluates answers and provides structured feedback, helping users understand their strengths and gaps.

- Confidence Building  
  Practicing in a simulated interview setting reduces anxiety and improves communication before real interviews.

How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier
- No dependency on mentors or mock interview panels; feedback is available instantly.
- Faster preparation cycles, allowing users to practice multiple questions in a short time.
- Clear improvement guidance that highlights exactly what needs to be improved.

Safety and Accessibility
- Low-risk environment with no judgment or pressure.
- No personal data collection, making it safer for users.
- Beginner-friendly interface that works on any modern browser.

Who Benefits
- College students and freshers  
- Self-learners preparing for technical roles  
- Anyone looking to improve interview performance through practice  

In Short
This project simplifies interview preparation by turning it into an interactive, guided, and repeatable practice experience, helping users become more confident and better prepared for real-world interviews.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges during development was managing environment variables and API keys securely. Initially, the application failed to run because the API key was not being detected, which led to repeated runtime errors. I resolved this by learning how environment variables work, removing sensitive keys from the codebase, and properly configuring them locally and during deployment. This also helped me understand secure coding practices.

Another challenge was GitHub repository rule violations caused by accidentally committing secret files. GitHub blocked the push to protect sensitive data. I fixed this by removing the tracked secret files, updating the `.gitignore`, and resetting the commit history to ensure no sensitive information remained in the repository. This experience improved my understanding of version control and security.

Deployment was another hurdle, as free hosting platforms have specific requirements for ports and runtime configuration. The application initially failed to run online due to incorrect server settings. I overcame this by updating the application to bind to the correct host and port required by the platform and carefully checking deployment logs.

Finally, working as a solo participant was challenging in terms of time management and decision-making. To overcome this, I limited the project scope, focused on core functionality, and followed a step-by-step execution plan. This helped me successfully complete a fully working and deployed project within the hackathon timeline.

**Best Innovation**

Track: AI / Machine Learning

This project uses AI-driven evaluation to simulate mock interviews. 
It generates role-based interview questions and analyzes user responses to provide instant feedback and improvement suggestions, making interview preparation more effective and accessible for freshers.

### TrustBridge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trustbridge-28ec) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Namish1234/trustbridge-platform) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://medium.com/@namishshukla2/building-trustbridge-a-technical-deep-dive-into-alternative-credit-scoring-5e72d7404f56) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/9il4ihGuYYk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hackxios%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackxios2k25.devfolio.co)

> Alternative Credit Scoring Platform

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OAuth](https://img.shields.io/badge/OAuth-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

There are always new people entering the adult world, and some existing ones, that don't have a credit history. This forces them to take on less credit limit and more interest rate, than they can be eligible for.

Trust Bridge solves this, by giving you a score, not based on your past credit history but based on your current cashflow, investments and other financial investments. This would help unlock your true credit potential.

Trust Bridge solves this by shifting the focus from history to health.

- A New Logic: Instead of asking "Have you borrowed before?", we ask "Are you financially healthy now?"

- The TrustScore: We generate a verifiable score based on your 12-month bank statements and investment portfolio.

- Real Utility: This score allows freelancers and students to access institutional-grade credit cards, personal loans, and even rental agreements at fair market rates, completely bypassing predatory lenders.

We are leveraging the RBI Account Aggregator framework to turn data into dignity, ensuring that a young Indian's financial future is defined by their current discipline, not their lack of a paper trail.

**Challenges we ran into**

The "Rich Student" Algorithm Flaw The biggest hurdle wasn't writing the code, but getting the logic right for our specific users.

Early in development, we realized our scoring algorithm had a major flaw: it was penalizing responsible behavior. We initially weighed "Average Bank Balance" very heavily. However, we realized that many savvy Gen-Z users (our target audience) don't keep money idle in savings accounts—they invest it immediately into Mutual Funds or Stocks.

The Fix: A student with ₹2,000 in their bank account but ₹50,000 in a portfolio was getting a lower score than someone who just let cash sit idle. This was the opposite of what we wanted!

We had to completely rewrite our evaluation engine to include an "Asset Multiplier." We integrated logic to detect transfers to known investment platforms (like Zerodha or Groww) and treat them as assets rather than expenses. It was a tricky logical puzzle to solve without making the system too complex, but it was essential to ensure we were actually rewarding financial literacy, not just punishing low balances.

**Best Innovation**

We have made the entire front and backend, from Ideation, Planning and Implementation in the Kiro IDE, along with all the twicks. We have contributed towards making an innovative approach, and targetting a real world problem that can have a meaningful impact on society.

The impact we want to bring forward, is financial inclusion for everyone, and for people to secure low interest loans even if they don't have a credit history.

> "AI that understand learners,not just clicks"

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chart.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chart.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project solves the problem of static and one-size-fits-all online learning systems that fail to adapt to individual learners’ needs. Traditional platforms cannot recognize when a learner is confused, overwhelmed, or disengaged, which often leads to frustration, poor understanding, and high dropout rates. The system addresses this by continuously observing user behavior and adapting the learning experience in real time, making complex topics simpler when needed and offering more advanced material when the learner is ready. This makes learning easier by reducing cognitive overload, smarter by personalizing content without manual configuration, and safer by preventing learners from getting stuck or silently giving up. It creates a more supportive, tutor-like environment for learners while also helping educators and platforms improve engagement, retention, and overall learning effectiveness.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges in building this project was accurately interpreting user behavior and mapping it to meaningful learning states such as “engaged,” “slightly confused,” or “highly confused.” Early versions of the system often misclassified users because single signals like scroll speed or time on page were too noisy and inconsistent on their own. This led to unstable adaptations and poor user experience. To overcome this, I combined multiple behavioral signals and introduced threshold-based logic and smoothing techniques so that state changes only occurred when consistent patterns were detected over time. Another challenge was ensuring that real-time UI adaptations did not feel abrupt or disruptive to the learner. This was solved by adding gradual transitions and small UI changes instead of sudden content replacements. Finally, managing continuous observation without impacting performance required careful optimization, such as limiting event listeners and batching updates efficiently. Overcoming these challenges helped make the system more stable, responsive, and reliable in practice.

**Best Innovation**

This project fits strongly into the Best Innovation track because it rethinks how intelligence and personalization can be introduced into digital learning systems. Instead of relying on heavy machine learning models, complex infrastructure, or centralized data processing, the project explores a lightweight, agentic approach where the system continuously observes user behavior and adapts the learning experience in real time. This represents a shift from traditional static EdTech platforms to dynamic, responsive, and context-aware learning environments. The innovation lies not only in what the system does, but in how it does it — demonstrating that meaningful adaptivity and personalization can be achieved through careful system design, behavioral signals, and real-time feedback loops. As an MVP, the project serves as a proof of concept for a new class of intelligent user interfaces that behave like tutors rather than content delivery systems. This approach opens new possibilities for scalable, privacy-friendly, and user-centric AI-driven applications, making it a strong candidate for the Best Innovation category.

### Inji Offline Verify
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/inji-verification-suite-7f95) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SartMa/inji-offline-verify/tree/oid4vp) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QUmlcgZ6P1wahS_SAG4IDgrg2-DtuhGBpJyAMJ9u-84/edit?usp=sharing) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/qLVGWTRLmqQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hackxios%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackxios2k25.devfolio.co)

> Revolutionizing digital identity verification

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Inji Offline Verify Platform solves the critical challenge of verifiable credential verification in remote locations with unreliable network connectivity. Traditional verification systems require constant internet access to validate digital credentials, making them impractical for field workers in areas with poor connectivity. 

This platform addresses this through an offline-first architecture that pre-caches cryptographic materials (public keys, revocation lists, JSON-LD contexts) enabling complete verification without network dependency. The solution provides dual verification modes: offline QR scanning for cached credential validation, and online OpenID4VP integration that implements the standardized OpenID for Verifiable Presentations protocol. 

The OpenID4VP feature allows field workers to generate QR codes that wallet holders can scan to securely submit their credentials using the cross-device flow, where the verifier creates a session, the wallet retrieves presentation definitions, submits verifiable presentations, and results are polled in real-time. Both verification methods store results locally and sync to a central Django backend when connectivity returns, providing organizations with complete audit trails while ensuring no verification opportunity is lost due to network limitations.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our primary challenge was implementing a truly offline-first architecture. Although an Inji Verify SDK already existed, it delegated most of the verification logic to the backend and exposed only frontend components for integration, which did not meet our requirements.

We initially examined the Inji Verify backend, but it was implemented almost entirely in Kotlin and Java, whereas our stack required a TypeScript-based solution to align with the existing codebase. As a result, we reimplemented the required functionality in TypeScript.

Additionally, the Inji Verify service relied heavily on verification suites that were not compatible with TypeScript. To address this, we evaluated alternative implementations and ultimately adopted the Digital Bazaar verification suites, which proved to be fully compatible and integrated seamlessly into our application.

**Best Innovation**

We cracked the biggest problem in digital identity: what happens when the internet dies? Most credential verification systems are useless without connectivity, but our platform pre-downloads all the crypto keys and verification data so you can validate digital IDs completely offline. 

The innovation is in our "smart caching" approach - we figured out how to maintain the same cryptographic security guarantees whether you're online or in the middle of nowhere. Plus, we built dual verification modes: instant offline QR scanning for cached credentials, and cutting-edge OpenID4VP integration that lets wallet apps submit credentials using the latest W3C standards. 

Field workers can now verify identities in disaster zones, remote areas, or anywhere with spotty internet, with blazing-fast 74ms verification times. When connectivity returns, everything syncs automatically. This isn't just another verification app - it's a complete rethink of how digital identity can work in an offline-first world, making trusted verification truly universal regardless of network infrastructure.

**AWS**

We used Kiro IDE to help define the requirements for integrating the OpenID4VP protocol and to finalize a clear design plan. Kiro demonstrated a strong understanding of our existing codebase and proposed a well-structured plan for integrating OpenID4VP, which is a more secure and standardized approach to credential verification than our earlier QR code–based system.

Kiro generated a detailed task list that we followed step by step during implementation. It proved highly effective at understanding our requirements and producing functional, relevant code. After Kiro established a solid baseline implementation, we introduced minor improvements of our own, which significantly reduced development time.

We also leveraged Kiro’s agentic capabilities by defining hooks to automatically add new test cases whenever a file was saved. This provided an efficient, continuous testing workflow compared to manually writing tests. The approach was time-saving and allowed us to validate our code instantly, catch issues early, and avoid harder-to-debug problems later in the development cycle.

> Turning government forms into conversations

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![fast.ai](https://img.shields.io/badge/fast.ai-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Government forms are often long, confusing, and written in complex legal language.

For many people, filling out forms for taxes, identity verification, visas, or employment becomes stressful and error-prone. A single misunderstanding can lead to rejected applications, delays, or the need to pay expensive agents just to complete basic paperwork.


Bureaucracy Breaker removes this friction by turning rigid government PDF forms into a simple, guided 

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/52f4affb263a4cd1bc3afaacbeabebd0/2ebc48c9-391d-4f4a-a199-f496b19b14b8.jpeg)


How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

**Conversational Guidance**
Instead of staring at a complex PDF, users answer one clear question at a time—like talking to a helpful government clerk.

**Built-in Explanations**
Each question includes a short explanation, helping users understand why the information is needed and where to find it.

**Error Reduction**
Answers are validated step by step, reducing incorrect or missing information that can cause form rejection.

**No Technical Knowledge Required**
Users don’t need to understand form layouts, checkbox rules, or internal field names.

**Privacy-Friendly**
Forms are filled programmatically without sharing data with third-party agents or human intermediaries.


*In One Line**

Bureaucracy Breaker turns confusing government forms into simple conversations—making paperwork human again.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into:**
Building a system that works with real government PDF forms introduced challenges that don’t appear in toy examples or sample datasets. Some of the most important hurdles are described below.

**1 Government PDFs Are Not Standardized:**
Not all PDFs behave the same way. Some government forms expose roper AcroForms fields, while others appear fillable but contains no extractable fields at all. This initially caused empty field extractions and unexpected failure.
How I solved it 
Added PDF validation and graceful fallbacks.
Ensured the system does not crash when a PDF has no fields.
Clearly separated “unsupported PDFs” from system errors.

**2  Checkbox and Radio-Button Behavior in Real Form**:
One of the most challenging issues came from forms like the W-9, where a single logical question is implemented as multiple checkbox fields under the hood. Treating each checkbox as a separate question caused repeated questions and blocked progress.
How I solved it:
Identified checkbox groups using shared base field names
Collapsed multiple checkbox fields into a single conversational question
Skipped sibling fields after one selection
This required understanding how government PDFs encode radio-button behavior.

**3 AI Reliability Under Hackathon Constraint :**
 AI-generated output can be unpredictable especially under rate limits or quota issues. At times, AI responses failed or returned unexpected formats.
How I solved it:
Designed AI logic with strict fallbacks
Ensured the system continues working even when AI fails
Treated AI as an enhancement, not a dependency
This made the system robust and demo safe.

**Best Innovation**

Why Bureaucracy Breaker Fits the Best Innovation Track
Bureaucracy Breaker introduces a new way of interacting with government forms by** converting static, confusing PDFs into guided conversational experiences**.

Instead of treating form filling as a mechanical task, the system reframes it as a dialogue—asking one clear question at a time, explaining what each field means, and validating answers before moving forward. This reduces user error, eliminates guesswork, and removes the need for costly intermediaries.

The innovation lies in combining:

Real-time PDF field extraction from government forms
AI-driven, context-aware question generation
Field-level validation and progressive disclosure
Automatic reconstruction of a fully completed government PDF

Unlike traditional form fillers or OCR tools, Bureaucracy Breaker works directly with existing government PDFs, requiring no changes to government systems and no retraining of users.

This approach makes bureaucratic processes more accessible, safer, and easier—especially for non-technical users, first-time applicants, and individuals unfamiliar with legal terminology.

By bridging rigid government infrastructure with human-centered AI, Bureaucracy Breaker demonstrates a practical, impactful innovation suitable for real-world adoption.

**AWS**

Why Bureaucracy Breaker Fits the Kiro Prize Track

**The problem it solves**

**The problem PadhaKU: Learning, Reimagined for Everyone solves**

PadhaKU is a learning platform where the interface adapts to the student, not the other way around. It has standard features like a dashboard that pulls live data from classrooms, but its core is different:

Magic Learn: This is not an answer generator. It's an accessible whiteboard. A student can solve a math problem by drawing it in the air. Using MediaPipe, we track their hand gestures, digitize their work, and our AI focuses on understanding their problem-solving process. This is kinesthetic learning, and for a motor-impaired student, it's their notebook.

Gesture-Based Quizzes: Students can take entire quizzes using only hand gestures - pointing to select an answer, giving a thumbs-down for a hint. This removes the physical barrier of traditional input devices.

AI as a Support Tool: Our AI Course Generator creates structured learning paths, and our voice assistant, AskSensei, provides instant help. The goal is to unblock students, not think for them.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges we ran into**

The Kitchen Sink Trap: Early on, we had five small projects instead of one platform. We pivoted to connect everything through a unified user journey.

Gesture Reliability: Different lighting conditions and accidental triggers required weeks of tweaking to make gestures intuitive and reliable.

Pedagogical Integrity: We constantly asked: "Are we building a better way to cheat, or a better way to learn?" This forced us to focus on process analysis rather than just answers.

**Best Innovation**

## Why PadhaKU Deserves Best Innovation

**PadhaKU reimagines education by removing barriers between learners and knowledge.** While most EdTech platforms add accessibility as an afterthought, we built from first principles: what if learning was completely hands-free? Our gesture-based DrawInAir system (30 FPS hand tracking with MediaPipe) enables motor-impaired students to draw math problems in mid-air and receive AI-powered solutions—proving that designing for the most constrained users creates superior experiences for everyone.

**Innovation isn't about using the newest technology—it's about solving real problems.** We innovate across seven dimensions: (1) **Accessibility-First Design** with gesture + voice controls, (2) **AI as Learning Companion** with context-aware, persistent intelligence across Magic Learn, Course Generator, and AI Mentor, (3) **Transparent Gamification** using formula-based points that make progress visible, (4) **Technical Excellence** with dual database connectivity (100% network compatibility), smart gesture locking, and API key rotation, (5) **Systemic Integration** where features amplify each other in a closed-loop ecosystem, (6) **Universal Design** where constraints breed creativity, and (7) **Measurable Impact** with quantifiable metrics (30 FPS tracking, 95% AI success rate, zero-cost 24/7 tutoring vs. $50-100/hour human tutors).

**The result? An education platform that works for everyone because it was designed for those who need it most.** In a world where EdTech means "putting textbooks on iPads," PadhaKU asks: What if physical disabilities didn't limit learning? What if tutors were always available? What if courses matched your exact needs? What if progress was visible and rewarding? Each innovation solves a real barrier. Together, they create an education platform that's not just better—it's fundamentally different. **That's innovation with purpose. That's PadhaKU.**

**AWS**

## How Kiro Transformed Our Development Process

**PadhaKU demonstrates the most creative use of Kiro by treating it not as a documentation tool, but as the architectural foundation of our entire development methodology.** While most teams use Kiro to document finished work, we used Kiro to think through, validate, and systematically construct a production-grade EdTech platform before writing a single line of code. Our `.kiro/` folder contains 5,000+ lines of structured documentation including formal requirements using EARS patterns (79+ acceptance criteria), design documents with correctness properties (12 formal specifications that became executable tests), implementation tasks with requirement traceability (15+ discrete tasks), and complete Git workflow documentation (40+ commits in chronological order).

**Most teams document what they built. We used Kiro to plan what to build.** Our requirements documents weren't written after the fact—they were created before coding and guided every implementation decision. For example, using EARS patterns, we caught ambiguities early: "user-friendly interface" was rejected as vague and replaced with "WHEN a gesture is detected, THE System SHALL provide visual feedback within 100ms." Our design documents defined correctness properties like "*For any* valid password, hashing then verifying should return true" which became our test suite and drove optimization work. The task documents provided clear roadmaps where each task referenced specific requirements (e.g., "Implements Requirements 1.1, 1.2, 3.3"), and our Git workflow documentation proves authentic planning—40+ commits in conventional format matching our task order exactly.

**The result? A systematic development methodology that proves planning depth, execution quality, and creative Kiro usage.** Our `.kiro/` folder serves multiple audiences: developers get requirements/design/task roadmaps, stakeholders see feature completeness and competitive advantage, judges see authentic planning process and systematic thinking. We achieved 100% requirement traceability (every feature maps to requirements), zero architectural rework (design validated before implementation), and production-grade reliability (correctness properties caught edge cases). Beyond basic documentation, we used Kiro creatively: correctness properties as executable specifications, Git workflow as learning resource, innovation thesis using Kiro structure, architectural decisions documented with rationale, and knowledge preservation for future development. **That's not just using Kiro—that's making Kiro the foundation of everything we do.**

## ⚠️ Challenges Faced During Development

- **Real time video and socket stability**  
  Managing Socket.IO events alongside live video classes led to sync and reconnection issues under poor network conditions.

- **AI engagement accuracy vs performance**  
  Balancing real time computer vision inference with acceptable latency and server load required multiple optimizations.

- **Frontend performance bottlenecks**  
  Heavy animations and dashboards initially caused frame drops and higher load times on low end devices.

- **State management complexity**  
  Handling classroom state quiz state and live engagement data together increased frontend complexity.

- **Deployment coordination**  
  Synchronizing environment variables and communication between frontend backend and ML services across platforms was error prone.

- **Privacy and compliance concerns**  
  Ensuring student images were processed securely and not stored required careful API and data handling design.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Smart Farming Platform is an innovative solution designed to empower farmers by integrating artificial intelligence, data analytics, and modern web technologies into everyday agricultural practices. At its core, the platform provides a comprehensive dashboard that enables farmers to manage their crops, detect diseases, monitor market prices, and receive weather‑based advisory, all within a single, user‑friendly interface. By combining multiple features into one ecosystem, the project aims to enhance productivity, reduce risks, and support informed decision‑making in farming communities.

One of the key features of the platform is **crop management**. Farmers can register their farms, add details about their crops, and track their growth stages. The system allows users to record planting dates, expected harvest times, soil type, and farm size. This structured data not only helps farmers stay organized but also enables the platform to generate tailored recommendations. For example, based on soil pH or crop type, the system can suggest best practices for irrigation, fertilization, and pest control.

Another highlight is the **disease detection module**. Using image analysis powered by machine learning, farmers can upload photos of their crops to identify potential diseases. The platform processes the image, extracts features, and predicts whether the crop is healthy or affected by conditions such as leaf spot, rust, or blight. In cases where the model cannot provide a confident prediction, a rule‑based fallback ensures that farmers still receive useful guidance. This feature reduces reliance on manual inspection and helps farmers take timely action to protect their yield.

The **market analysis component** addresses one of the most pressing challenges in agriculture: price volatility. Farmers often struggle to access reliable information about current market rates. The platform integrates real‑time market data, allowing users to search for crop prices by region or state. By presenting this information in charts and lists, the system helps farmers decide when and where to sell their produce for maximum profit. This transparency empowers farmers to negotiate better deals and avoid exploitation.

Weather plays a critical role in farming, and the platform’s **weather advisory system** ensures that farmers are prepared for changing conditions. By entering their location and crop type, users receive forecasts along with actionable advice. For instance, if heavy rainfall is predicted, the system may recommend drainage measures or adjustments in irrigation schedules. This proactive guidance helps farmers minimize losses due to unpredictable weather patterns.

The platform also emphasizes **accessibility and usability**. With a clean interface, responsive design, and support for local languages, it ensures that farmers from diverse backgrounds can benefit. Features such as offline archives allow users to access essential information even without an internet connection, making the tool practical in rural areas with limited connectivity.

In summary, the Smart Farming Platform is more than just a web application; it is a digital companion for farmers. By integrating crop management, disease detection, market insights, and weather advisory into one cohesive system, it bridges the gap between traditional farming and modern technology. The project’s vision is to create a sustainable, data‑driven agricultural ecosystem that empowers farmers to make smarter decisions, improve productivity, and secure better livelihoods.

> Kideney Monitoring

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is often detected late because regular monitoring depends on blood tests, which are invasive, costly, and not easily accessible for frequent screening. This leads to delayed diagnosis and higher health risks, especially in low-resource settings.

How This Project Helps

This system enables non-invasive kidney health screening using ECG and vital signals combined with machine learning.

What it can be used for:

Early detection of potential kidney health risks, Regular monitoring without repeated blood tests, Tracking kidney health trends over time, Remote screening and telemedicine support.

By making kidney monitoring easier, safer, and more accessible, the system helps people take action before serious damage occurs

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

One of the main challenges was hardware–software alignment. The original design included bioimpedance-based fluid measurement, but due to sensor reliability and time constraints, bioimpedance data could not be used consistently. To overcome this, the ML pipeline was redesigned to rely only on stable ECG-derived features, vital signs, and demographic inputs, while keeping bioimpedance as a planned future enhancement.

Another challenge was handling noisy physiological signals, especially ECG data affected by motion artifacts and electrode placement. Instead of using rigid rule-based logic, a machine learning approach was chosen, which allowed the system to learn patterns statistically and remain robust to minor signal variations.

We also faced a data availability challenge, as real clinical kidney datasets are difficult to access due to privacy and ethical restrictions. This was addressed by generating physiologically realistic synthetic data for model training, ensuring the system could be demonstrated and validated as a working prototype.

These challenges helped shape a more modular, realistic, and scalable design.

### CrowdSense
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/crowdsense-03a3) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aviralshastri/crowdsense/tree/main) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/fU6k3iagQmU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Technocrats%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://technocrats-hackathon.devfolio.co)

> AI that sees the crowd before it forms.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![YOLO](https://img.shields.io/badge/YOLO-333333?style=flat-square) ![TCN (deep learning)](https://img.shields.io/badge/TCN%20(deep%20learning)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Cities today face a serious challenge when it comes to understanding and managing crowd movement in real time. CCTV cameras are installed everywhere, but they only record video and humans cannot manually monitor hundreds of screens at once. This results in delayed responses during festivals, protests, public gatherings, traffic congestion and emergency situations. There is no unified system that combines camera footage, sensor data and weather information to measure crowd density accurately. There is also no prediction system that can warn authorities before a crowd becomes uncontrollable. Because of this, police departments often react late, which increases the chance of stampedes, mismanagement and safety risks.

Civilians also face problems in crowded cities. They currently rely on guesswork or normal navigation apps that show only traffic and not the actual crowd or safety level of an area. People have no guideline to choose a safer and faster route based on real crowd conditions, environmental readings or predicted congestion.

Our project solves this gap by converting normal CCTV cameras into an AI powered monitoring network that detects people, measures the density of every area and predicts future crowd levels using TCN models. We combine camera analytics with sensor readings like noise, temperature, air quality and PIR based human activity so that the crowd calculation is more reliable. We also include real time weather information to understand outdoor conditions more accurately. This blended intelligence helps authorities take action early instead of reacting late.

The police control application provides a live city map with color coded crowd zones in red, yellow and green along with camera feeds, sensor readings and automatic alerts for barricading or team deployment. The civilian app works like a smarter navigation system that not only finds routes based on distance but also checks predicted crowd levels and weather conditions to guide users safely and comfortably.

In simple words, the project solves the problem of delayed awareness, poor real time crowd intelligence and the absence of a predictive safety system for both authorities and citizens. It creates a safer, smarter and more manageable city environment by turning raw surveillance data into live actionable intelligence.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was combining data from multiple sources in a synchronized and meaningful way. The CCTV person detection model works in continuous frames, while sensors like PIR, noise and temperature produce data at different intervals. Ensuring that each data stream aligned correctly for accurate prediction required careful timing logic and a stable data pipeline.

Another major challenge was handling the behaviour of the PIR sensor. PIR sensors produce interrupts in a very unpredictable pattern because of their internal timing and retriggering limitations. At first, the PIR was missing multiple triggers while other sensors were being read. I had to redesign the interrupt logic and remove blocking delays to make the system respond consistently in real time.

Integrating TCN based prediction was also challenging. The model needed well formatted and preprocessed data from both the camera and sensors. Preparing training samples, reducing noise in the dataset and making the model generalize to different crowd patterns took significant experimentation.

Another challenge was optimizing person detection on camera feeds. CCTV quality varies a lot, and factors like low light, glare and crowded scenes made detection accuracy fluctuate. I had to fine tune thresholds and apply preprocessing to get stable results.

The final challenge was ensuring the whole system works in real time. Predicting crowd behaviour, updating map colors, processing video and reading sensors must happen quickly and without lag. Achieving a balance between accuracy and speed required multiple rounds of optimization.

### PadhaKU: Learning, Reimagined for Everyone
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/padhaku-learning-reimagined-for-everyone-4066) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://padhaku.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/d2tfpHemvrI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Technocrats%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://technocrats-hackathon.devfolio.co)

> AI-Powered Learning Platform for All Students

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

PadhaKU is a learning platform where the interface adapts to the student, not the other way around. It has standard features like a dashboard that pulls live data from classrooms, but its core is different:

Magic Learn: This is not an answer generator. It's an accessible whiteboard. A student can solve a math problem by drawing it in the air. Using MediaPipe, we track their hand gestures, digitize their work, and our AI focuses on understanding their problem-solving process. This is kinesthetic learning, and for a motor-impaired student, it's their notebook.

Gesture-Based Quizzes: Students can take entire quizzes using only hand gestures - pointing to select an answer, giving a thumbs-down for a hint. This removes the physical barrier of traditional input devices.

AI as a Support Tool: Our AI Course Generator creates structured learning paths, and our voice assistant, AskSensei, provides instant help. The goal is to unblock students, not think for them.

**Challenges we ran into**

The Kitchen Sink Trap: Early on, we had five small projects instead of one platform. We pivoted to connect everything through a unified user journey.

Gesture Reliability: Different lighting conditions and accidental triggers required weeks of tweaking to make gestures intuitive and reliable.

Pedagogical Integrity: We constantly asked: "Are we building a better way to cheat, or a better way to learn?" This forced us to focus on process analysis rather than just answers.

### Barter Swap
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/barter-swap-8a6d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Doot-Foundation/zec_mina_barter) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co)

> Cross-Chain Escrow Based Bridge

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project enables atomic swaps between Mina and Zcash bridging a programmable smart
contract chain with the most private cryptocurrency that doesn't support smart contracts.

Privacy-First Escrow for Zcash

Zcash lacks programmable logic for escrow. Traditional solutions require wrapped tokens with trusted
custodians or centralized exchanges that destroy privacy. This system uses ephemeral escrow instances that
preserve Zcash's shielded architecture: sealed keys per-trade (each swap gets a dedicated instance
starting at port 9000), lightwalletd-only detection (escrow addresses never touch zcashd), and minimal
metadata leakage (only encrypted memo fields on-chain).

The middleware coordinates atomically: both MINA deposit (on-chain zkApp verification) and ZEC funding
(off-chain shielded note detection) must succeed before locking. No bridges, no wrapped tokens, no custody
risk.

Mina + Zcash: The Perfect Privacy-Programmability Alliance

Mina is the world's most advanced ZK-native blockchain the entire chain is a single ~22KB recursive
proof. This makes it uniquely positioned to handle privacy-preserving cross-chain logic that other
platforms can't match.

For Mina users: Finally access real privacy without centralized exchanges. Trade MINA → ZEC and hold funds
in Zcash's battle-tested shielded pools. Mina's zkApps provide programmable guarantees, Zcash provides
transaction privacy together they offer what neither can alone.

For Zcash users: Access Mina's rich zkApp ecosystem (DeFi, NFTs, identity protocols) without abandoning
privacy. Exit to shielded ZEC anytime via swaps. This is Zcash's gateway to programmable smart
contracts while maintaining shielded transactions.

This lets Mina spread its wings into privacy-enabled value transfer not just privacy in computation
(zkApps already do this), but privacy in cross-chain swaps. Mina proves it can bridge transparency and
opacity better than any EVM chain.

POC Simplifications vs. Production Potential

The current POC uses shortcuts for rapid testing: unified operator token across all trades, simple
sequential port allocation, and a single middleware instance. Production-ready architecture would enable
per-trade cryptographic API keys, distributed middleware (anyone can run the polling coordinator),
multi-signature operator controls, and enhanced memo encryption schemes.

With proper implementation, this could become the leading escrow service for Zcash offering
smart contract guarantees (timeouts, refunds, conditional claims) to a chain that fundamentally can't
support them natively.

Beyond Mina: Blockchain-Agnostic Design

While built with love for Mina's zero-knowledge architecture, the middleware is fundamentally
blockchain-agnostic. Any chain exposing queryable endpoints or RPCs can integrate. Replace the Mina client
with Ethereum RPC, Solana JSON-RPC, or Bitcoin electrum servers the escrowdv2 ZEC side remains
unchanged. This is a privacy-preserving escrow protocol, not a Mina-only bridge.

**Challenges we ran into**

The single biggest time sink was zcashd and lightwalletd syncing. Before I could even start testing atomic
   swaps, I had to wait hours for initial blockchain sync. This wasn't a one-time setup either — every
  configuration change, every parameter tweak meant restarting services and praying they'd sync correctly.
  Most of my development time wasn't spent writing code; it was spent figuring out what works and what 
  doesn't through endless docker exec and curl trial-and-error sessions.

  The documentation around Zcash RPC is sparse and scattered. Simple questions like "do I use account
  numbers or addresses in z_sendmany?" required reading through GitHub issues from 2019. The
  AllowRevealedAmounts privacy policy error? Only discovered after multiple failed transactions and diving
  into zcashd source code. Every curl command in CURL.md represents hours of debugging.

  Then came the worst possible timing: during the final days of the hackathon, lightwalletd completely 
  corrupted. The database became unreadable, the service refused to start, and there was no way to recover
  it. I had to nuke everything and rebuild from scratch — full blockchain resync, full wallet rescan, hours
  of waiting while the submission deadline approached. This meant re-testing the entire escrowdv2 funding
  verification flow when I should have been polishing features.

  Mina Compilation Delays

  On the Mina side, the challenge wasn't infrastructure — it was compilation speed. Every single change to
  the smart contract or offchain state required 2-3 minutes of recompilation before I could even know if my
  fix worked. Debugging became agonizingly slow: write one line, wait 3 minutes, see it fail, repeat. This
  isn't a Mina flaw (ZK circuits are complex), but it turns rapid iteration into a patience test.

  The offchain state settlement proofs added another 5-6 minutes per test cycle. When you're hunting a bug
  that requires multiple contract calls to reproduce, you're looking at 15+ minute feedback loops.
  Traditional smart contract development gives you sub-second compilation; zkApps demand planning every
  change carefully because you won't know if it works until you've waited long enough to make coffee.

  The Breaking Point

  There was a moment — somewhere around 3 AM during the final 48 hours — where everything failed 
  simultaneously. Middleware couldn't connect to escrowdv2. Port allocation was throwing collisions despite
  the allocator showing free ports. ZEC transactions were getting mined but escrowdv2 wasn't detecting them.
   Mina settlement proofs were timing out. The logs made no sense. Every fix broke something else.

  I genuinely considered scrapping the entire integration and submitting a simplified mock version. The
  circular debugging was maddening: fix the port allocator, breaks the API key flow. Fix the API keys, now
  lightwalletd can't find the notes. Fix the memo encoding, now zcashd rejects the privacy policy. It felt
  like playing whack-a-mole with a system that actively resisted coherence.

  The solutions however came from a pretty popular term "KISS": unified operator token (no per-trade key generation),
  sequential port allocation (no hash-based logic), and accepting that the POC doesn't need production-grade
   complexity. Once I stopped fighting the architecture and embraced "make it work first, optimize later,"
  the pieces finally clicked. But those dark hours of everything failing taught me more about distributed
  system debugging than any tutorial ever could. 


Finally, there's still a lot to be done, things to be fixed, but I am pretty happy with what I have with me right at this moment. And no one can take that from me.

Bonsoir Elliot.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

The project introduces escrowdv2, a privacy-preserving smart contract like protocol on Zcash enabling trustless atomic swaps with cross-chain assets. The Zcash-side escrow implements deposit verification, confirmation tracking, and atomic refund/forward mechanisms ensuring ZEC remains under user control throughout the swap lifecycle. Users can trade ZEC privately using shielded z-addresses while the escrowdv2 contract enforces trade integrity through on-chain state verification (deposited, confirmed, locked, refunded, forwarded). This creates unstoppable private DeFi infrastructure where Zcash acts as the privacy layer and value settlement chain, advancing ZEC's utility beyond simple transfers into programmable privacy-preserving trading.

**Privacy Infrastructure & Developer Tools**

The project delivers escrowdv2, a reusable Zcash escrow protocol for building privacy-preserving cross-chain applications. The contract provides foundational primitives (deposit verification, multi-signature coordination, atomic settlement) that developers can integrate into bridges, swaps, or DeFi protocols requiring Zcash privacy guarantees. Complete with state machine design (deposit → confirm → lock/refund → forward), the infrastructure enables trustless coordination between Zcash and external chains while preserving shielded transaction privacy.

Includes developer documentation, integration patterns, and testing utilities for building on Zcash making it easier  to leverage ZEC's privacy technology in cross-chain DeFi applications.

> Private Perpetual Platform

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anchor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anchor-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arcium](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arcium-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Traditional on-chain perpetual futures protocols expose all trading activity to the public ledger, creating significant problems for traders:

- **Front-running**: MEV bots exploit pending trades by observing order flow in the mempool
- **Copy-trading**: Sophisticated strategies are immediately visible and can be mimicked without consent
- **Targeted liquidations**: Attackers can identify large positions and manipulate prices to force liquidations
- **Information leakage**: Competitors gain insights into trading strategies and positions

**Arcium Shoot** solves these problems by encrypting all position data (side, size, leverage, entry price, liquidation price) using Multi-Party Computation (MPC). Traders can open and manage perpetual positions with complete privacy while maintaining verifiable on-chain integrity.

### What Makes It Safer and Easier

**Safety Benefits:**
- Position details remain encrypted throughout the entire lifecycle
- No information leakage to front-runners or competitors
- Verifiable computation through MPC ensures positions can't be manipulated
- Protocol enforces leverage limits and risk parameters even on encrypted data

**Ease of Use:**
- Standard perpetuals UI - traders don't need to understand cryptography
- Client-side encryption happens automatically via Arcium SDK
- Gas costs remain reasonable (encrypted operations optimized for Solana)
- Familiar trading experience with added privacy layer

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. MPC Callback Framework Integration

**The Problem:**
When implementing the encrypted computation callbacks for `calculate_pnl` and `close_position` operations, callback transaction execution was failing with error code 6204 during MPC callback finalization. This meant that while the MPC computation completed successfully, the results couldn't be written back to the blockchain.

**Root Cause:**
The callback structures were missing required account parameters that needed to be passed from the main instruction to the callback handler. Specifically:
- The `CalculatePnlCallback` struct was missing the `position` account that needed to be updated after MPC computation
- Callback registration was using empty account arrays `vec![]` instead of properly registering which accounts needed to be modified
- Account context wasn't being properly propagated through the callback boundary

**How I Solved It:**
1. Added the position account field to the CalculatePnlCallback struct
2. Updated callback registration to explicitly pass the position account with proper mutability flags, creating a CallbackAccount struct with the position's public key and writable permissions
3. Updated the callback handler to properly utilize the passed account context, following the same pattern as the working init_position_callback implementation

This fix enabled proper state updates after encrypted computation, allowing the protocol to function correctly.

### 2. Encrypted Data Serialization Across MPC Boundary

**The Problem:**
Position state needs to be encrypted client-side, sent to Solana, passed to Arcium's MPC network for computation, and results returned to Solana for storage. Each step requires careful cryptographic handling:
- Encryption must use fresh nonces to prevent replay attacks
- Ciphertexts must be exactly 32 bytes for efficient storage
- Key exchange must happen securely between user and MPC nodes

**How I Solved It:**
Implemented a robust cryptographic pattern:
- **x25519 key exchange** for public key agreement between parties
- **Rescue cipher** for symmetric encryption (MPC-friendly)
- **Fresh nonce generation** for each encryption operation to ensure uniqueness
- **Proper serialization/deserialization** of 32-byte ciphertexts between TypeScript client and Rust program

This ensures position data remains confidential while being computable by the MPC network.

### 3. Arcium proc-macro2 Dependency Conflict

**The Problem:**
Standard Rust dependency resolution pulled `proc-macro2` v1.0.97 from crates.io, but Arcium's SDK requires a custom fork with specific modifications. This caused compilation failures because the macro expansion behavior was incompatible.

**How I Solved It:**
Applied a Cargo patch in the workspace configuration to override the dependency and point to Arcium's custom fork on GitHub. This forces all crates in the workspace to use Arcium's fork, ensuring compatibility across the entire dependency tree.

- **Institutional traders** can deploy strategies without revealing proprietary signals

**4. Clarity - Explanation of Privacy Benefits**

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Zcash has a critical "privacy paradox" in analytics: existing block explorers only show transparent transactions, leaving shielded transaction holders with zero visibility into their own private holdings. This creates several problems:

### The Privacy Analytics Gap

**For Individual Users:**
- No way to generate tax reports for shielded transactions (compliance nightmare)
- Can't track transaction history without running a full node
- Viewing keys provide decryption ability but no tools to use them

**For Developers:**
- Extremely limited SDK and API options for Zcash (unlike Ethereum's robust ecosystem)
- No standardized privacy health metrics
- Difficult to build applications that leverage shielded pools

**For The Ecosystem:**
- Lack of analytics tools hinders adoption (users want visibility without sacrificing privacy)
- No real-time monitoring of network privacy metrics
- Privacy features remain underutilized due to poor developer experience

### What inZight Does

**inZight** is the first comprehensive analytics platform that bridges public network insights with private viewing key analytics, solving the privacy paradox:

1. **Viewing Key Analytics** (Industry First)
   - Import your viewing key to see your shielded transaction history
   - Private balance queries across Sapling and Orchard pools
   - Memo field decryption for shielded payments
   - Your data never leaves your control (client-side decryption)

2. **Network-Wide Privacy Metrics**
   - Privacy Health Score tracking shielded pool adoption
   - Shielding Velocity measuring transparent → shielded flows
   - Real-time pool distribution (Transparent, Sprout, Sapling, Orchard)
   - Historical trends and anomaly detection

3. **Developer SDK** (20+ TypeScript Methods)
   - Full Zcash RPC client abstraction
   - TypeScript-first with comprehensive type safety
   - Works with zcashd or Zebra nodes
   - Complete API documentation

4. **Real-Time Updates**
   - WebSocket connections for live block and transaction updates
   - No polling required (efficient architecture)
   - React Query integration for automatic cache invalidation

### How It Makes Tasks Easier and Safer

**Easier:**
- Beautiful web UI (no command-line required)
- One-click viewing key import
- Automatic transaction categorization
- Export functionality for tax reporting

**Safer:**
- Client-side key management (keys never sent to server)
- Direct RPC connection to your own Zcash node (no third-party trust)
- Open-source and auditable
- Privacy-preserving by design

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Zcash RPC Client Implementation from Scratch

**The Problem:**
Unlike Ethereum (which has ethers.js, web3.js, viem), Zcash has virtually no production-ready TypeScript RPC clients. The existing tools either:
- Don't support viewing keys
- Only work with zcashd (not Zebra)
- Lack proper TypeScript types
- Use outdated RPC methods

I needed a complete RPC client that supports viewing key operations (`z_importviewingkey`, `z_listreceivedbyaddress`), network statistics, and both consensus node implementations.

**How I Solved It:**
Built a comprehensive 418-line TypeScript RPC client from the ground up with methods for blockchain info, block retrieval, viewing key import, balance queries, transaction history, network statistics, pool distribution, and 15+ additional operations.

**Key Technical Decisions:**
- Implemented proper error handling with retry logic for network failures
- Used Axios with connection pooling for performance
- Added request/response logging for debugging
- Supported both zcashd and Zebra (different RPC method names)
- Proper handling of zatoshi amounts (multiply by 1e-8 for display)

**Result:** 10/10 RPC integration tests passing, real blockchain queries working

### 2. Viewing Key Cryptographic Operations

**The Problem:**
Viewing keys in Zcash are not simple public keys - they're complex cryptographic objects that require:
- Proper import format validation (Base58Check encoding)
- Different handling for Sapling vs. Orchard viewing keys
- Secure storage (never log or expose in errors)
- Asynchronous blockchain scanning for historical transactions

Additionally, the viewing key import process can take minutes for wallets with many transactions (node must scan entire blockchain from import height).

**How I Solved It:**
Implemented a robust viewing key management system:

1. **Format Validation**: Verify Base58Check encoding before sending to node
2. **Asynchronous Imports**: Import returns immediately, scanning happens in background
3. **Progress Tracking**: Poll operation status to show import progress
4. **Error Recovery**: Handle import failures gracefully with user-friendly messages
5. **Security**: Viewing keys are stored encrypted in PostgreSQL (using node's built-in encryption)

The implementation validates the viewing key format, starts an asynchronous blockchain scan, and returns immediately without blocking the user interface.

### 3. Database Schema Design for Time-Series Analytics

**The Problem:**
Zcash blockchain data has unique characteristics:
- Dual pools (transparent + shielded) require different schemas
- Time-series data (network stats, pool distributions) needs efficient querying
- Shielded transactions have encrypted memos (variable-length binary data)
- Historical snapshots needed for trend analysis

**How I Solved It:**
Designed an 11-table PostgreSQL schema with TimescaleDB for time-series optimization:

**Key Tables:**
- `blocks` - Block headers with shielded transaction counts
- `transparent_transactions` - Public UTXO-based transactions
- `shielded_transactions` - Sapling/Orchard shielded transfers
- `pool_snapshots` - Hourly value distribution across pools (TimescaleDB hypertable)
- `network_metrics` - Privacy Health Score and Shielding Velocity over time
- `viewing_keys` - Encrypted storage with last sync height
- `user_alerts` - Configurable alerts for threshold crossings

**Optimizations:**
- TimescaleDB hypertables for automatic partitioning by time
- Indexes on `(block_height, pool_type)` for fast range queries
- JSONB columns for flexible shielded transaction metadata
- Composite indexes for common query patterns

**Status:** Schema created and tested, full integration in progress (not required for MVP)

**Zcash Data & Analytics**

## How This Fits the Bounty

**Bounty:** Zcash Data & Analytics - Advanced Block Explorer with Viewing Key Support

### Specific Bounty Requirement

> "Build an advanced Zcash block explorer that empowers users to view their own shielded transactions without compromising privacy. The explorer should allow users to bring their own viewing keys to decrypt shielded transactions entirely client-side, ensuring that sensitive transaction data never leaves their device. The explorer should additionally allow a user to show up with their viewing key and see all transactions related to that user."

### How inZight Meets Every Requirement

#### 1. ✅ Advanced Zcash Block Explorer
**Requirement:** Build an advanced block explorer

**Implementation:**
- Complete block explorer functionality with real-time blockchain data
- Network statistics dashboard showing shielded pool distribution
- Latest blocks and transactions view
- Block height tracking and chain state monitoring
- Support for both zcashd and Zebra nodes via RPC client

**Evidence:** 10 API endpoints (`/api/v1/blocks/latest`, `/api/v1/network/stats`, etc.) + 5 complete web pages

#### 2. ✅ View Shielded Transactions Without Compromising Privacy
**Requirement:** Empowers users to view their own shielded transactions without compromising privacy

**Implementation:**
- **Viewing key import**: Users import their Sapling/Orchard viewing keys
- **Shielded balance queries**: `z_getbalanceforviewingkey` RPC integration
- **Transaction history**: `z_listreceivedbyaddress` shows all shielded transactions
- **Memo decryption**: Decrypt encrypted memo fields for shielded payments

**How Privacy Is Preserved:**
- Viewing keys enable read-only access (cannot spend funds)
- No link between viewing key and spending authority
- Transaction metadata decrypted locally only

**Evidence:** `server/services/zcash-rpc.ts` lines 200-350 implement viewing key operations

#### 3. ✅ Bring Your Own Viewing Keys
**Requirement:** Allow users to bring their own viewing keys

**Implementation:**
Users can import their Sapling or Orchard viewing keys through the API endpoint. The system validates the Base58Check format, imports the key to the connected Zcash node, and starts a background blockchain scan to find all related transactions.

**User Flow:**
1. User pastes Sapling or Orchard viewing key (zvk... or zxviews...)
2. System validates format client-side
3. Key imported to user's own node (or self-hosted)
4. Blockchain scanning begins from import height
5. All matching transactions displayed in dashboard

**Evidence:** Viewing key import form in Analytics page + RPC client implementation

#### 4. ✅ Decrypt Shielded Transactions Entirely Client-Side
**Requirement:** Decrypt shielded transactions entirely client-side, ensuring sensitive data never leaves device

**Implementation:**
The frontend decrypts shielded transaction outputs in the browser using the viewing key and ephemeral keys from the blockchain. All decryption happens locally without any server roundtrip.

**Privacy Guarantees:**
- Viewing keys stored encrypted in browser's localStorage only
- RPC calls go to user's own zcashd/Zebra node (not centralized server)
- Decryption logic runs in browser JavaScript (no server roundtrip)
- Memo fields decrypted client-side using viewing key

**Self-Hosting Option:**
Users can run inZight frontend locally and point to their own Zcash node using Docker and environment variables for complete control over their data.

**Evidence:** Frontend components never send viewing keys to backend + local storage encryption

#### 5. ✅ See ALL Transactions Related to Viewing Key
**Requirement:** Allow user to see all transactions related to that viewing key

**Implementation:**
The system queries all addresses derived from the viewing key and retrieves every transaction received by those addresses. Results are sorted chronologically by block height to provide a complete transaction timeline.

**Transaction Details Shown:**
- ✅ Amount received (in ZEC)
- ✅ Sender address (if transparent input)
- ✅ Block height and confirmation count
- ✅ Transaction ID (txid)
- ✅ Decrypted memo field
- ✅ Pool type (Sapling vs Orchard)
- ✅ Timestamp and transaction fee

**Evidence:** Analytics page displays complete transaction history with filtering and sorting

#### 6. ✅ Stays True to Zcash's Cypherpunk Ethos
**Requirement:** Provide transparency while staying true to Zcash's cypherpunk ethos

**Cypherpunk Principles Honored:**

**A. Self-Custody:**
- No custodial wallet features
- Users maintain full control of keys
- Optional self-hosting (no mandatory centralized service)

**B. Privacy by Default:**
- No user accounts or registration
- No tracking or analytics
- Viewing keys encrypted in local storage
- Open-source code (auditable by anyone)

**C. Trustless Architecture:**
- Direct RPC connection to user's own node
- No third-party APIs for sensitive operations
- Client-side cryptography only

### Privacy is Normal
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/privacy-normalization-f345) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/DisturbedCoin/status/1996677133284851842?s=20) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Zypherpunk-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://zypherpunk.devfolio.co)

> Privacy is normal

![Capcut](https://img.shields.io/badge/Capcut-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People don't connect their daily transactions to surveillance consequences until it's too late. 

This video makes that connection real through specific human stories. 

It normalizes privacy by showing it through four relatable characters making everyday choices - a woman taking a pregnancy test, an artist wanting to donate, a teenager seeking mental health resources, a parent struggling financially. None of them are doing anything wrong. 

They just want privacy for their decisions. 

The video shows how surveillance erodes their freedom to choose authentically, then demonstrates how privacy-preserving technology restores it. Privacy isn't positioned as paranoid - it's positioned as normal. Essential. Human.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was showing surveillance consequences without being preachy or fear-mongering. I needed viewers to feel the loss of privacy through the characters' emotional shifts, not through technical explanations. 

Getting the tone right in voiceover was critical - intimate and conversational, not corporate or announcer-like. I also had to figure out how to visualize abstract concepts like data collection and shielded transactions in ways that felt cinematic rather than technical or scary.

**Privacy-Focused Content & Media**

This is structured as four interconnected character stories following transformation arcs. 

Each character loses agency under surveillance, then regains it through privacy. 

The video uses emotional storytelling -intimate close-ups, parallel editing, montage crescendos - to make privacy viscerally matter. 

Rather than explaining why privacy is important, it shows what happens when you don't have it and what becomes possible when you do. 

The meme that sticks: privacy is freedom. It's built for shareability and emotional resonance, not technical explanation.

**Private Focused Content & Media**

The entire video centers on how exposed transaction data creates real consequences. 

- A prenatal vitamin purchase triggers algorithmic targeting. 
- A donation reveals political beliefs to employers. 
- Financial struggles become permanent records that sabotage job prospects. 
- Mental health searches get sold to insurance companies. 

The video then shows how private transactions -shielded, anonymous - are the concrete solution that restores freedom.

It educates viewers that private transactions aren't about secrecy; they're about the right to make choices without your financial life becoming a permanent judgment against you.

**Privacy-Focused Content & Media**

This video normalizes privacy by showing it as something ordinary people need for ordinary reasons. 

- A pregnant woman wants to share her news on her own timeline. 
- An artist wants to support causes they believe in. 
- A teenager wants to understand herself. 
- A parent wants dignity. 

None of these are suspicious activities - they're just human. 

The video demonstrates that privacy isn't about hiding; it's about sovereignty over your own decisions. It positions privacy-preserving technology not as paranoid, but as a basic tool for living authentically.
